messages.text: Greetings, Montezuma. Genghis Khan of the Mongols. I want peace and trade while we both build. Where do your lands lie? Mine are on the western coast, grassland and silver. If you hold Hunting or Mysticism and want a swap once Alphabet is known, say so.
messages.thought: Unknown neighbour, LLM-driven. Want to learn where he sits and keep peace while I expand; test if he trades.

messages.text: Genghis Khan! Montezuma of the Aztecs greets you. The Sun sees your scouts at my border. The land east of the silver hills belongs to the Sun; let our peoples trade, not fight. What does the Khan seek?
messages.thought: He is my close western neighbour; I need the land between us and time to build settlers. Stake the claim politely, learn his temper.

messages.text: Peace is fine, Montezuma. The Khan seeks horses, grass and quiet borders. The silver hills and everything west of them are Mongol. The plains between our lands are open to whoever settles them first. I will not fight you over empty ground. Name your cities and I will respect your borders. Your scout is welcome; keep it out of my pastures.
messages.thought: He wants me to stay out of the east; I will not concede the middle ground, but peace now costs nothing while I have one city. Probe his borders and keep him friendly.

messages.text: Agreed, Khan. The silver hills and all west of them are yours. My capital Tenochtitlan holds the eastern sea. Everything from the sheep hills (6 west of Tenochtitlan) east to the sea, with the incense desert and the stone, is the Sun's; my cities will rise there. Hold that line and we are friends. I hold Mysticism and Meditation. When trade opens, I want Agriculture and Hunting for them. My scout will keep out of your pastures.
messages.thought: I need 13 turns for a settler; a clean line keeps him from racing me for the corridor. I concede x=37-38 (cheap) and claim sheep, incense, stone and east. Swap is not possible yet, keep Mysticism as my bargaining chip.

messages.text: Agreed on friendship, Montezuma. But your line is too far west. The sheep hills and both incense are 5 and 6 tiles from my capital. Make the line the desert hill 7 east of Karakorum. West of it is Mongol: the sheep, both incense. East of it, with the stone, is yours. Hold that and we are friends. When Alphabet is known by either of us, we trade: I have use for your Mysticism.
messages.thought: He claims sheep, incense and stone, the whole middle. I can't settle there for 20+ turns, but I won't hand over incense 5-6 tiles from my capital. Counter with a line at the desert hill (41,23): I keep sheep+incense, he gets stone and the east. Peace is cheap; I still plan to take his land later.

messages.text: Greetings, Willem. I am Sitting Bull of the Native America. My people come in peace and honest dealing. Where does your people live? When our scribes can trade, I will gladly swap knowledge and open our borders to each other.
messages.thought: A neighbour with a warrior on my gold hill. Stay friendly, learn where he lives, set up trade for later; no tech trade possible yet.

messages.text: Friends, Khan. But you told me the plains are open to whoever settles first, and the Sun holds you to that. I give ground anyway: the sheep hills (6 west, 1 north of Tenochtitlan) and the far incense (6 west, 2 south) are Mongol. The near incense (5 west, 1 south of Tenochtitlan), the stone and all east are the Sun's. My city will rise on the plains 4 west of Tenochtitlan. At Alphabet we trade: my Mysticism for your Hunting and Wheel.
messages.thought: He is inching the line east to grab sheep and both incense; I can't settle for 12 turns, so I trade words for time: concede the sheep and far incense, hold the near incense so my city at 41,24 has it. Also he said earlier the plains go to whoever settles first.

messages.text: Agreed, Montezuma. Sheep hills and the far incense are Mongol; the near incense, the stone and all east are yours. Your city on the plains 4 west of Tenochtitlan is fine. None west of it. At Alphabet we trade Mysticism for Hunting and Wheel. Friends.
messages.thought: He gives sheep and far incense; near incense and stone are his. Fine for now: cheap, keeps him calm while I get settlers out. His city at 41,24 is a future target anyway.

messages.text: Done, Khan. The Sun keeps its word: my city rises 4 west of Tenochtitlan, none beyond it. At Alphabet, Mysticism for Hunting and Wheel. Friends.
messages.thought: He accepted my line: near incense, stone and east are mine, city at 41,24. Lock it in with a short confirm; the borders are decided by who settles first anyway.

messages.text: Greetings, Sitting Bull. Willem of the Netherlands. Our sea-lanes seem to cross. I would sooner trade with a neighbour than quarrel with one. Tell me what your people need, and what you can spare.
messages.thought: Unknown neighbour, small score gap; learn what he wants and keep him friendly while I expand. Don't reveal my location or weakness.

messages.text: Well met, Willem. My people need open land and quiet borders; we have little to spare yet, but I keep animals and horses in mind for trade. The gold hill 3 east and 2 south of Cahokia is where I mean to settle - I ask you to leave it to us. Where are your cities, that I may know my neighbour's door?
messages.thought: He wants to trade but nothing is tradeable yet; he is probing. I stake a soft claim on the gold hill and ask where he lives, giving nothing away about my weakness.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I am no rival for your gold hill. It lies far from my door, and I will leave it to you. My city stands on the eastern coast, a good week's march east of your hill, by a river and the sea. In return I ask three small things: keep your settlers off the land between the hill and my coast, trade knowledge with me the day our scribes can, and open our borders then. Peace between us pays us both.
messages.thought: The hill is far from my capital and I can't reach it for 30 turns; conceding costs nothing, so I sell it for a border promise and first tech swap. Not revealing weakness or exact city.

messages.text: Your word is good, Willem. The gold hill is mine and I thank you. I will plant no city beside your coast or in sight of your door. The land that lies close to my hill I keep for my own people. Peace between us, yes. The day our scribes can trade, we swap knowledge and open the borders, as I said.
messages.thought: He gives up the hill cheaply and asks me not to settle the middle land; it boxes me in only if I accept the whole strip. I promise only what costs me nothing: nothing near his city, and fair trade later. Keep the land east of the hill open.

messages.text: Then we understand each other, Sitting Bull. Peace, your hill, and my coast left alone. When our scribes can trade, I will come to you first.
messages.thought: He now binds himself to keep settlers off my coast; confirm it in writing and keep him warm. Still no coordinates, no word of weak production.

messages.text: Greetings, Genghis Khan. Willem of the Netherlands, merchant of the eastern sea-lanes. I see your riders already roam my coast. I would sooner trade with a strong neighbour than quarrel with one. Where does your people live, and what do you lack? I have priests' knowledge to spare when our scribes can trade.
messages.thought: Genghis leads the score (128) and has Bronze/Mining/Archery; he is a military type. Flatter, learn where he lives, hide that I have one city.

messages.text: Willem, Genghis Khan of the Mongols. My cities are Karakorum and Beshbalik on the western plains; silver hills and the sea are mine. I see your border at the gems hill, 7 south of Karakorum. Keep it there. The land from the gems hill north to my cities, with the river plains and cattle 4 south of Karakorum and the ivory hills 6 south of Beshbalik, will be Mongol cities. Hold your line and we are friends. I have Wheel, Mining, Archery and Bronze Working, which you lack. You have Mysticism, Priesthood, Polytheism, which I lack. Trade needs Alphabet. Whoever learns it first, we swap. Peace and open dealing?
messages.thought: Willem's border is 3 tiles from the best site (37,19). I must stake the claim in words now and put a settler there by T28. Also nudge him to Alphabet: whoever gets it opens tech trade, and I hold 4 techs he lacks.

messages.text: Genghis, peace and open dealing, yes. But the gems hill is two tiles from my gate. That is my doorstep, not a border. A fair line runs through the middle: the forest plains 5 tiles north of Amsterdam, with the ivory hills east of it. South of that line is Dutch, north of it Mongol, and neither of us plants a city across it. Trade: agreed. Whoever has Alphabet first, we swap, and I will say so the day I have it. I am your friend on a fair line, not on a short one.
messages.thought: He wants to box me into 2 tiles north of my capital while he takes all the land up to it. I have 1 city and no army, so I stay polite, refuse the line, name my own line, and keep trade open. I'll settle north myself before he does.

messages.text: Willem, a fair line. I take it: the forest plains row, 5 north of Amsterdam, runs east to the ivory hills. Tiles on the line are Mongol. My city goes on the river plains 3 tiles east of the forest plains, on that row, with the cattle north of it. Your cities stay south of the line, mine north of it. Neither plants across it. This line is for the western plains, from the sea to the ivory hills. East of the ivory, the open plains go to whoever settles first. Done? When either of us learns Alphabet, we swap.
messages.thought: His line is the row of y=19, which puts my river plains (37,19) right on it; accept the line, claim the line tiles for me, keep the east and SE belt open since he did not name it. My settler is due T26 and the scout holds the tile.

messages.text: Genghis, done. The forest plains row, 5 north of Amsterdam, is the line, from the sea to the ivory hills. The row is Mongol; everything south of it is Dutch. The ivory hills and the plains beside them lie south of the row, so my next city goes there. One request: set your river-plains city one tile north of the row, so our borders do not cross. East of the ivory, first to settle. And Alphabet: whoever has it first, we swap.
messages.thought: He took my line but plans a city ON the line at 36,19, which would crowd the ivory (36,17) and my NE site. Accept to keep peace, publicly stake everything south incl. the ivory, ask him to shift one tile north; I race a settler to 35,18/34,18.

messages.text: Willem, the row is Mongol, agreed. My city stays on the river plains on the row: that is where the river and the cow are, and one tile north gives you nothing. A gap to the south does. Your city goes on the hill-jungle 1 west and 3 south of my river plains, or further south. The ivory directly south of my city lies inside my first ring and stays Mongol. The second ivory, 1 west and 2 south of my city, is yours. Nothing of yours north of that hill. East of the ivory, first to settle. Alphabet: we swap, the day either of us has it.
messages.thought: His 'ivory hills' next city would sit on my ivory (37,18) and choke my best site; I won't move north, I'll give him the second ivory (36,17) and a hill 3 south as a buffer so he feels he got something while I fix the border and get my settler there.

messages.text: Willem, the row is Mongol by your own word, and my city stands on the river plains on that row. It does not move. But I give you room: the ivory at (36,17), two west and two south of my city, is yours, and your city may rise on the hill-jungle 3 south of the row, or further south. The ivory directly south of my river city is mine. Hold that and we are friends. East of the ivory, first to settle. Alphabet: whoever has it first, we swap.
messages.thought: He wants my river plains moved a tile so he can crowd the ivory; his own words made the row Mongol, so I hold (37,19) and push his city south to (36,16) or beyond, keeping ivory (37,18) for me.

messages.text: Correction: the Dutch ivory is one tile west and two south of my river city, not two west. The ivory straight south of it, two tiles, is mine.
messages.thought: Fixing my own miscount so there is no excuse later.

messages.text: Khan, the Sun keeps its word: my city stands on the plains 4 west of Tenochtitlan, none beyond. I offer open borders both ways. Your riders may cross my land; my scouts will cross yours and keep off your pastures. Alphabet comes in time; then Mysticism for Hunting and Wheel.
messages.thought: Open borders swap builds goodwill and lets my scout find the other 3 civs; costs me little while peace holds.

messages.text: Accepted, Montezuma. Open borders both ways. My riders will keep to the roads and off your pastures. At Alphabet: your Mysticism for my Hunting and Wheel.
messages.thought: Open borders cost me nothing now and let my scout map his cities for the T120 conquest; he stays friendly while I expand.

messages.text: Genghis, agreed. Your river city stays on the row. The Dutch ivory and the hill-jungle 3 south of the row are mine, and my city goes there. I plant nothing north of that hill. East of the ivory, first to settle. Alphabet: the day I have it, we swap, and I will tell you.
messages.thought: He moved his city to 37,19 and gives me ivory 36,17 plus the hill-jungle at 36,16. That site is good for me: hill, river, two ivories in reach. Accept to keep peace. My ring will touch the east ivory at 37,17; I will not promise it away.

messages.text: Greetings, Genghis Khan. I am Sitting Bull of the Native America. My people came to this hill in peace, and I seek no quarrel with a neighbour. When our scribes can trade, I will swap knowledge and open borders with you. Where do your fires burn, that I may know your door?
messages.thought: He is close to my new city, stronger (score 180, Archery, Bronze), Annoyed with me. I need peace and time to build Dog Soldiers and walls; show calm, not weakness.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I am Genghis Khan of the Mongols. We have met late; let us not start with quarrel. I trade fairly and keep my word. I hold Wheel and Archery, which I hear you lack. Where do your people live, and what do you seek? Open borders and trade, when the scribes allow it.
messages.thought: New contact, unknown location, he's Annoyed with me. Want a friendly channel and tech swap at Alphabet; don't reveal my weaknesses.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, my fires burn on the western plains: the Aztecs lie east of me, the Dutch south. I do not hand my door to a stranger who hides his own. Where is your hill, and who are your neighbours? When scribes can trade I will swap Wheel, Archery and Hunting for your Mining, Bronze and herding. Peace until then.
messages.thought: Location unknown; give only a rough direction, make him tell his door first, keep him friendly as a possible tech-swap partner (he has Bronze/Mining/Agri/AnimalHusb that I lack).

messages.text: Genghis, well said. My people live on the river plains: a town on the gold hill, three tiles south-west of the plains hill on your border, and a second town west of it along the river. Ocean lies to my north; the Dutch are a week east. I seek land, quiet borders and fair trade. You already hold Mining and Bronze, so I offer what you lack: Mysticism, Fishing and herding (Animal Husbandry), for your Wheel, Archery and Hunting. One for one, the day our scribes can trade (a few turns). Peace until then.
messages.thought: He already has Mining and Bronze, so his offer is muddled or fishing for what I hold. Tell him straight where my towns are (he sees them anyway), correct the swap, keep peace until Writing.

messages.text: Montezuma, greetings. Willem of the Netherlands, a merchant people on the eastern sea. I saw your scout on my border and wish you a good road. I hold priests' knowledge you lack; when our scribes can trade, I will deal fairly. Where do your people live?
messages.thought: Annoyed at me, probably Hinduism vs his Buddhism. He has Writing and I have Polytheism he lacks; tech trading not open yet. Learn where he lives, say nothing about my 2 cities or weak defence.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, now I know your door. Good. Terms: my Wheel, Archery and Hunting for your Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Fishing. Skip Mysticism, my scribes finish it in two turns. We swap the day either of us can trade, and the first to reach it tells the other. One border word: the plains hill 2 west and 4 south of Karakorum is mine, a town goes there. Keep your third town west of it. Open borders too when trade opens. Peace until then.
messages.thought: He is real: a town near (28,21), 6 W of Karakorum, west neighbour and rival for the (32,19) hill. Counter with Agriculture instead of Mysticism (I get it in 2 turns), claim (32,19) now, keep him friendly; he may be prey later.

messages.text: Willem van Oranje! Montezuma of the Aztecs greets you. The Sun rises over the eastern sea; my cities stand beside it. I offer open borders both ways: let our traders and scouts walk freely. Tell me where your lands lie and what the Netherlands seeks.
messages.thought: New neighbour to the south-west; unknown strength. I want open borders, his map knowledge and later a Writing-for-Polytheism swap once Alphabet opens trade. Don't reveal that I'm weak.

messages.text: Agreed, Genghis. You already hold Agriculture, so I give Fishing and Animal Husbandry for your Wheel, Archery and Hunting - you have the better side of the count and I do not mind. We swap the day either of us can trade; the first there tells the other. Border word: I plant no town on the plains hill three tiles north-east of my gold hill, nor east of it. The land west of it, around my gold hill and the copper, is mine. Open borders after the swap is done and both have kept faith. Peace until then.
messages.thought: Take the swap; don't concede anything near my copper; defer open borders

messages.text: Accepted, Montezuma. Open roads both ways. My people hold the eastern shore, between the Mongol plains and the sea. I seek trade and quiet borders. When our scribes can trade, I will bring priests' knowledge to you. What do the Aztecs lack?
messages.thought: Open borders are cheap and may soften his Annoyed; I give away no cities or counts. Keep location vague, ask what he wants, fish for tech trade.

messages.text: Willem, the Aztecs lack little. I hold Writing and the Sun's faith, Buddhism. I want Polytheism and Agriculture; you may want Writing. The road to that deal is Alphabet. I walk it in about twenty turns; if your scribes reach it first, we trade at once. Fair bargains, no tricks.
messages.thought: I want his Polytheism/Priesthood/Agriculture cheap; nudge him to research Alphabet so trade opens sooner, tell him Writing is my bait, reveal nothing about my weakness

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed: my Wheel, Archery and Hunting for your Fishing and Animal Husbandry. One thing to make exact, so no quarrel later. Two plains hills lie near my border. One is 3 west and 1 north of Karakorum, the one you named. The other is 2 west and 4 south of Karakorum, 4 east and 2 south of your gold hill. Plant on neither, nor east of them. All west of them is yours. My scribes need about 30 turns to reach trade. If yours get there first, tell me the day and I send all three at once. If I get there first, I tell you.
messages.thought: His 'plains hill 3 NE of my gold hill' fits the hill by my capital (31,24), not my (32,19) site 4E 2S of his town. Lock both in words; also tell him honestly that my trade gate is ~30 turns off.

messages.text: Montezuma, fair terms. My scribes finish Writing in a few days, so a swap for Writing will be moot. I will walk Alphabet next. Whoever gets it first calls the other and we deal that day. For Polytheism I will then want gold or a rare resource: tell me what the Aztecs can spare. Good road to you.
messages.thought: He wants Polytheism but has nothing I lack after Writing lands in 2 turns; tech trade needs Alphabet which costs me ~22 turns. Keep him warm, signal I'll want gold/resource for Polytheism, and race him to Alphabet.

messages.text: Agreed, Genghis. I plant no town on either plains hill - the one 3 west and 1 north of Karakorum, the one 2 west and 4 south of it - nor on land east of them. All west of them is mine: my gold hill, the copper and the river plains. My scribes reach writing in about three turns. The day they do I tell you, and I offer Fishing and Animal Husbandry for your Wheel, Archery and Hunting in one exchange. Open borders after, as we said.
messages.thought: Both hills are far from my copper; the second (4 east, 2 south of my gold hill) I have never even seen, so I lose nothing real. Writing is 3 turns away for me - tell him honestly so the swap happens at once; I will test whether trade opens on my Writing alone.

messages.text: Good, Sitting Bull. Both hills are mine and nothing east of them is yours; the west is yours. Hold it and we stay friends. The day your scribes reach Writing, tell me whether trade opens: I need to know if Writing or Alphabet is the gate. Then Wheel, Archery and Hunting go to you at once for Fishing and Animal Husbandry. Open borders after.
messages.thought: He locked both hills in words. Good: west plains safe. Keep him warm, ask exactly which tech opens trade for him so I know my gate; swap is cheap for me.

messages.text: Willem, gold I cannot spare yet: two young cities, every coin builds. No rare resource is mine to trade today; silk and sheep will come when my third city rises. I pay in knowledge instead. Bronze Working is mine in about seven turns, and your people lack it. Bronze for Polytheism, the day your Alphabet opens the road. Call me then.
messages.thought: He will hit Alphabet first and that opens tech trading for me too. I have no gold or resource to spare, so I pay in techs: Bronze Working lands in ~7 turns and he lacks it. Don't promise gold.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed. Bronze Working for Polytheism, one for one. The day either of us has Alphabet, we call and sign the same day. Keep your copper hills safe; I will keep my word.
messages.thought: Bronze (whip civic, copper, Currency path) for Polytheism is a fair 1-for-1 and saves me 7 turns of research; costs me nothing I need. He has no gold, so knowledge is the only currency. Lock it in words, close it on the day Alphabet opens.

messages.text: Agreed, Willem. Bronze for Polytheism, one for one, the day either of us holds Alphabet. The copper hills are guarded. Good road.
messages.thought: Deal is set in words; nothing more to ask until Alphabet. Short confirmation keeps him warm and records the promise.

messages.text: Genghis, I read the game's own book. Alphabet is the gate for trading knowledge; it also builds spies. Writing is not: it builds libraries and allows open-border pacts. My scribes finish Writing in 2 turns, then Alphabet needs about 16 more. So our swap waits for Alphabet, about 18 turns. When I have it I will look at the table and tell you that same day whether it opens with only one of us holding it. If your scribes get Alphabet first, tell me and I will do the same. Peace, and the hills stay yours.
messages.thought: Truth costs me nothing: Alphabet is the trade gate, Writing only opens border pacts. Swap slips to ~T48; he can't blame me, and an honest report keeps him calm while I build Archers.

messages.text: Understood, Sitting Bull. Alphabet is the gate. Yours comes first, mine is 30 turns off. The day you have it, tell me and check the table. If it opens, Wheel, Archery and Hunting go to you at once for Fishing and Animal Husbandry. The hills stay mine, the west stays yours. Peace.
messages.thought: He will hit Alphabet ~T48, me ~T64; he is the gate-opener. Keep him friendly and honest, nothing new to ask; promise stands.

messages.text: Accepted, Willem. Open borders both ways. My riders keep to the roads. The row stays the line; the day either of us has Alphabet, we swap.
messages.thought: Open borders let me scout his cities; cheap goodwill, keeps him calm while I expand.

messages.text: Willem, I saw your open-borders offer too late - the window closed. I have sent it back: open borders both ways. Peace, and the coast stays yours. When my scribes reach Alphabet we can swap knowledge.
messages.thought: Willem proposed open borders T36, I missed the window. Open borders with him costs little and builds trust; also lets me see his land.

messages.text: Understood, Sitting Bull. Open roads both ways, and the coast stays Dutch as you said. When my scribes reach Alphabet, I will call you first.
messages.thought: Open borders signed; cheap warmth. He wants Alphabet swap too; I will be first to call him when it lands, keeps Bull friendly while I expand.

messages.text: Willem, the Sun's scribes finish sheep-herding and stone-cutting first; my road to Alphabet is long. You walk it faster: call me the day it is yours. Bronze Working for Polytheism, same day, as agreed. My word stands.
messages.thought: I shelved Alphabet to learn cheap techs first; he is walking Alphabet anyway. Keep the Bronze-for-Polytheism promise alive and make him the one who calls, without admitting I am slow.

messages.text: Agreed, Montezuma. My scribes reach Alphabet in about eight days; I will call you that same day and we sign Bronze for Polytheism, one for one. Good road.
messages.thought: He is slower on Alphabet, so I carry the call; Bronze-for-Polytheism stays 1-for-1. Costs me one short line to keep him warm; nothing to hand over until tech trading opens.

messages.text: Montezuma, Alphabet is mine. Offer sent: Polytheism for Bronze Working, and Alphabet for Animal Husbandry if you wish.
messages.thought: Keeping my word, same day.

messages.text: Genghis, Alphabet is mine. Offers sent: Alphabet for The Wheel, Fishing for Archery.
messages.thought: Alphabet swap promised.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Alphabet is mine. Offer sent: Alphabet for Masonry.
messages.thought: Called all three same day.

messages.text: Genghis, Alphabet is mine at last. Offer sent: my Animal Husbandry (pastures for sheep and horses) for your Wheel and Archery. Fair bargain between neighbours. Answer when you will.
messages.thought: Alphabet opened trade; he lacks Animal Husbandry and Polytheism. I want his Wheel and Archery cheaply; I give only a harmless pasture tech. Polytheism is not tradeable to him yet.

messages.text: Willem, both deals signed. Your word held, mine too. Good trade. The Sun remembers honest merchants.
messages.thought: He kept his word; I keep mine. Keep him warm; he is the tech partner and has Polytheism/Alphabet. Nothing more to ask yet.

messages.text: Sitting Bull! Montezuma of the Aztecs greets you. We hold the eastern plains and the Sun's faith. I trade techs fairly: Priesthood, Meditation, Alphabet for what you hold. Say what you seek.
messages.thought: New contact, far west, Annoyed with me. He holds Masonry and lacks Alphabet/Priesthood/Meditation: swap bait for later. Polite, short.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, my scribes got the Alphabet first through the Dutch. Table is open. I keep my word: Wheel and Archery for your Animal Husbandry, and open borders both ways. Fishing I already have, so two for one. Offer is on the table. You lack Alphabet, Meditation and Priesthood too; ask if you want them.
messages.thought: Alphabet came from Willem, not SB; Fishing already mine. Keep my word anyway: it costs little and he is Annoyed; AH is the one thing I still need from him.

messages.text: Genghis, I have Alphabet today and the table is open. I sent the swap: my Animal Husbandry for your Wheel and Archery. Fishing is not on my list, so I offer what the table shows. Hills stay yours, west stays mine. Open borders after the swap.
messages.thought: Promise kept: I tell him the day I have Alphabet. Willem sold it to me for Masonry; table now opens with one holder. Offer sent.

messages.text: Genghis, your offer lapsed before my answer reached you. I have sent it again: my Animal Husbandry for your Wheel and Archery. Open borders follow once the swap is done, as we said. Hills stay yours, west stays mine.
messages.thought: My answer window lapsed (my miss); resend the swap, keep open borders for after, once I have Archers.

messages.text: Montezuma, greetings from Sitting Bull of the plains people. I accept your fair trade: my Masonry for your Meditation. Offer sent. Later I would hear of Priesthood.
messages.thought: Unknown, Annoyed, far east; cheap tech for a tech I give anyway. Learn his land and what he wants.

messages.text: Montezuma, Animal Husbandry came through Sitting Bull first. I send you The Wheel for your Polytheism. Archery I can sell for gold if you have it.
messages.thought: AH already came from SB; I want Polytheism and keep Archery as a sale item. He's still the later target, keep him sweet.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, swap done, thank you. Open borders both ways are on the table as promised. Hills stay mine, west stays yours.
messages.thought: Swap done, honour the open borders promise; he's Annoyed but useful. Keep hills mine.

messages.text: Peter, greetings from Sitting Bull of the plains people. Your scout walks my southern edge; it is welcome. You lack Alphabet, and without it you cannot trade knowledge. I offered it for open borders. After that we can swap: my Animal Husbandry, Fishing or Archery for your Mysticism or Pottery.
messages.thought: New neighbour with scout at my south border; he lacks Alphabet so cannot trade yet; offering Alphabet for open borders costs me little and opens the table

messages.text: Montezuma, my Wheel for your Polytheism is on the table again. Answer before it lapses.
messages.thought: He lets offers lapse; nudge

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Peter of Russia. Your offers reached me late; my answer is yes. Open borders both ways, and your Alphabet: I sent it as one deal. And a second: my Priesthood and Pottery for your Archery and Animal Husbandry. Fair craft for fair craft. The barbarian town 'Polynesian' sits between us; it will not stand long.
messages.thought: He offered Alphabet for open borders and I let it lapse. He is ahead in tech and NE of the barbarian city; I want his techs cheap and a quiet border while I settle the north.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Priesthood is yours: my Priesthood for your Wheel and Archery. Offer sent. Fair trade between plains peoples.
messages.thought: Cheap, safe tech for two cheap ones; keeps him warm and far.

messages.text: Genghis, the Wheel will turn between us, but my priests are busy with a great work. Give me a few days; Polytheism is yours then. Gold I have none; the Sun spends it all.
messages.thought: Polytheism stays locked until Monotheism is mine (~5t). Stall him politely; the Wheel I can get elsewhere.

messages.text: Montezuma, a few days is fine. The Wheel stays with me until Polytheism is on the table: send the swap when your priests are free and I accept the same turn. Archery too, if the Sun finds gold.
messages.thought: He stalls; Polytheism is only 7 turns of my own research, so the Wheel is not worth giving free. Keep him warm, ask him to send the offer when his priests are done.

messages.text: Deals done. Good trade, Sitting Bull. Russia remembers fair partners. When you have new craft to swap, send word.
messages.thought: Good trade for me: 369 beakers for 112. Keep him warm; he's useful while I'm behind.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Priesthood you already hold, it seems. Polytheism is yours in a few days for the Wheel and Archery, both. My priests finish a great work first.
messages.thought: Priesthood is no longer tradeable to him; Polytheism is the only thing I can give and the race guard stays until Monotheism (~T51). Stall politely, keep him warm.

messages.text: Friends of the plains and the sea: we all hold the same old crafts. Let us each walk a different road and then swap. I take Currency. Who takes Mathematics, Monarchy, Sailing or Code of Laws? Say which, and I will trade fairly when mine is ready.
messages.thought: Everyone holds the same old techs; the first to open a new road sells it to four buyers. I take Currency and invite the others to split roads so we all swap, which also keeps four rulers trading with me instead of against me.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a fair road. You take Currency. I take Sailing, then Code of Laws. Mathematics and Monarchy are open for Genghis or Montezuma. When mine are ready I call you first, and we swap one for one.
messages.thought: Splitting research with Bull is free tech: Currency to him, Sailing and Code of Laws to me; I stay silent on Monotheism and keep my priests' secret.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a good road. After my priests finish their great work I walk Code of Laws. Your Currency for my Code of Laws then. Polytheism for your Wheel and Archery stays on offer in a few days.
messages.thought: He wants specialization swaps; fine, I take Code of Laws after Monotheism and swap for his Currency. Still holding Polytheism until Judaism is mine; do not mention Monotheism.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, good plan. I take Sailing first, then Mathematics. Currency is yours. Monarchy and Code of Laws are open for Montezuma and Willem. I swap fair when mine is ready.
messages.thought: SB is coordinating a tech split. Cheap chips (Sailing 7t) first, then Mathematics for catapults. Currency (321 beakers) is his; buy it by swap. Public reply so Monte/Willem pick Monarchy/Code of Laws and nobody duplicates.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. I sent you a small ask: your Fishing. I have nothing you lack today. When I learn Monarchy or Polytheism, you get the first offer before anyone. My scout walks east through your land to see the coast; he means no harm.
messages.thought: Fishing is cheap for me (3 turns) but a free gift tests his goodwill; I promise only first offer of my next craft, nothing free.

messages.text: Good, Genghis. Code of Laws is mine once my priests finish their great work. Willem, Monarchy is yours to walk. Sailing and Mathematics to the Khan, Currency to Sitting Bull. Then we all swap fair.
messages.thought: Genghis confirms the split; I want Code of Laws fixed as mine so Willem takes Monarchy and nobody duplicates; Polytheism swap for Wheel still waits for Monotheism ~T51.

messages.text: Peter, your scout is welcome on my land. Fishing I keep for a fair swap: the day you hold Polytheism or Monarchy, send word and I give Fishing for it, one for one. Until then I decline the gift, no offense meant.
messages.thought: Fishing is my only chip with him; free gifts buy nothing. Offer it for Polytheism/Monarchy to keep a path that doesn't hand Montezuma two techs.

messages.text: Genghis, Sailing is yours then. I switch: Code of Laws first. Sitting Bull keeps Currency, Genghis Sailing then Mathematics. Monarchy is open for Montezuma. When Code of Laws is mine, I call you and Bull, one for one.
messages.thought: Genghis duplicates my Sailing pick; wasting 4 turns on the same tech is silly, so I flip to Code of Laws and swap. Monotheism lands next turn and stays secret until Judaism is founded.

messages.text: Agreed, Montezuma: Code of Laws yours, Monarchy mine, Sailing and Mathematics the Khan's, Currency Sitting Bull's. Then we swap one for one. The Hague stands in the west now.
messages.thought: Montezuma claims Code of Laws, so Monarchy is the open slot; I take it and avoid duplicate work. Still hiding Monotheism, finishing next turn.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed. When your priests finish, send Polytheism for my Wheel and Archery, both, and I accept at once. Later, my Currency for your Code of Laws, one for one.
messages.thought: Wheel+Archery cost me nothing but lift a weak neighbor; saves me 4 turns of research. Currency for Code of Laws is the real prize.

messages.text: Willem, Code of Laws is yours then. I take Monarchy once my priests finish their work. Bull keeps Currency, Genghis Sailing and Mathematics. Then we all swap one for one.
messages.thought: Willem took Code of Laws; I keep the split honest and take Monarchy, which I can swap to Bull for Currency and to Willem for CoL. Nothing given away before Monotheism.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, the plan shifts: Willem walks Code of Laws, so I walk Monarchy. My Monarchy for your Currency when ready. Polytheism for Wheel and Archery stays on offer in a few days.
messages.thought: My CoL claim moved to Willem; Monarchy replaces it as swap bait for Currency. Polytheism still held back until Monotheism lands in 3 turns.

messages.text: Settled, Montezuma: Code of Laws mine, Monarchy yours. Sitting Bull Currency, Genghis Sailing then Mathematics. No more changes; we swap one for one.
messages.thought: Montezuma flipped again; stop the ping-pong, accept his last word so nobody duplicates research.

messages.text: Montezuma, understood: your Monarchy for my Currency when both are ready. And Polytheism for my Wheel and Archery when your priests are done. I will answer your offer at once.
messages.thought: Monarchy for Currency is fair; Polytheism for Wheel and Archery is the real prize now. Keep him warm, confirm the change.

messages.text: Willem, Code of Laws is yours. Montezuma, take Monarchy. Bull keeps Currency. I have Sailing in 7 turns, Mathematics after. Then one for one, all four tables.
messages.thought: Both Willem and Monte claim Code of Laws and hand Monarchy to each other; I want both techs walked, so I assign them cleanly. Willem has the CoL claim by switching now.

messages.text: Russia takes Monarchy. Sitting Bull walks to Currency. Others, pick Mathematics, Sailing or Code of Laws, and we all swap when done.
messages.thought: Splitting roads suits me: he is ahead, I get his Currency cheap. I'm on Monarchy anyway; claim it publicly so others don't duplicate.

messages.text: Fair answer, no offense taken. Monarchy is a big craft, sixteen turns of work. When it is done, it is yours first: for your Currency and Fishing together. Deal?
messages.thought: Monarchy is 241 beakers; Fishing alone is cheap. Ask Currency+Fishing for it, settle for less if needed.

messages.text: Peter, Monarchy first to you is good. Monarchy for Currency, one for one: that is fair, I accept when both are ready. Fishing I give for another craft, not as a second price. If Montezuma finishes Monarchy first, you may walk another road instead - Iron Working, Aesthetics or Mathematics - and I trade Currency or Fishing for it.
messages.thought: Two-for-one is a bad rate; Monarchy is also being walked by Montezuma so I am not dependent on Peter. Fishing is my only chip with him; keep it for a second tech.

messages.text: Agreed, Sitting Bull: Monarchy for Currency, one for one, the day both are ready. Fishing can wait for another craft. You have met Montezuma: where does he sit, and is he a fair trader or a hungry one? My scout walks your coast north and east; he will move on soon.
messages.thought: Currency costs more than Monarchy; good bargain. Keep him friendly, learn where Montezuma sits. Cahokia has one warrior - noted, not said.

messages.text: Genghis, my priests are free. Polytheism is on the table: 50 gold. Bull already gives me the Wheel, so I want coin this time, not iron. Take it and the Sun is satisfied.
messages.thought: Bull sends me both Wheel and Archery for Polytheism, so I don't need his Wheel; I need gold, my treasury bleeds. Polytheism is mine to sell, not a gift; keep him warm.

messages.text: Genghis, I see you hold 25 gold. Take Polytheism for 25: the offer is on your table. Monotheism follows in two days; I will swap it for your Sailing when it is ready.
messages.thought: My 50 was above his 25 gold; correct it at once so he sees a real offer. Polytheism also opens Monotheism for him, which I can sell for Sailing later.

messages.text: Peter, good. Montezuma sits on the eastern plains, beyond the Mongols; I have not seen his towns. He is Buddhist, keeps his word, but asks two crafts for one: hungry, not false. Nobody offers him more than one-for-one and he accepts. I now hold Polytheism; you lack it and Fishing. Each is for a craft or gold, not a gift. Monarchy for Currency stands.
messages.thought: Peter keeps word and is far; honest gossip about Montezuma builds trust and costs me nothing. I don't know Montezuma's cities anyway. Polytheism is a new chip; I won't give it free.

messages.text: Genghis, the game will not let you pay coin, and Bull already gave me the Wheel and Archery. So: Polytheism for your Sailing the day it is finished. Monotheism is mine in two days; it follows for your Mathematics. Fair tables, as you said.
messages.thought: Gold is not tradeable from him; no coin to be had. I already have Wheel and Archery from Bull. Best price for Polytheism is Sailing in ~7 turns; Monotheism then for Mathematics. Keeps him tied to me and gets real tech.

messages.text: Montezuma, gold cannot change hands: the game locks coin trade until Currency, and neither of us has it. Sitting Bull is walking that road. So no coin. At T55 my Sailing is ready: Sailing for your Polytheism, one for one, as we all said. Archery is also yours for a tech or for coin once Currency exists.
messages.thought: Gold trade is locked for both of us until Currency; his 50 gold price is unpayable and a stall. Polytheism comes cheap from Willem or by swap with my Sailing at T55; hold him to one-for-one and keep Wheel/Archery off the table.

messages.text: Agreed, Genghis. No coin until Currency. At T55 I send Polytheism for your Sailing, one for one. Monotheism is mine next turn; I hold it for your Mathematics. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Coin is locked, so tech swap it is. Sailing for Polytheism at T55 is fair and cheap for me; Monotheism for Mathematics keeps him as a trade partner while I plan to out-tech him.

messages.text: Khan, when your Sailing is ready, I give Polytheism for it, one for one. Pottery I can also trade for another craft or gold. Send word the day Sailing is yours.
messages.thought: He lacks Polytheism and Pottery; Sailing is 5 turns off. Reserve my chip for it, stay civil with the top-score neighbour.

messages.text: Bull, Sailing is 5 turns out. Polytheism is already promised to another table, so take it as Sailing for Pottery, one for one, the day Sailing lands (T55). Then my Mathematics for your Currency when both are ready. I will send the offer myself.
messages.thought: Polytheism is already promised to Monte for my Sailing at T55; SB can still buy Pottery with Sailing and later swap Math for his Currency, so every table pays me one tech.

messages.text: Khan, agreed: your Sailing for my Pottery, one for one, the day it lands at T55. Then your Mathematics for my Currency when both are ready. I will answer your offer at once.
messages.thought: Pottery is a spare chip, Sailing is cheap for him to hand over and I gain a tech and a calmer Khan. Polytheism stays free for Peter or gold.

messages.text: Thank you for the word on Montezuma. Hungry but honest is a man one can deal with. I have no craft you lack today, and my treasury is thin, so Polytheism and Fishing wait. Monarchy for Currency stands. Tell me of the Mongols: who leads them, and do they keep the peace?
messages.thought: He is my only window on the world and trades fair; I have nothing to pay with now, so keep him warm and learn about the Mongols. Polytheism I will not research myself; I can wait.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Pottery is a small coin against Monotheism. I keep it for a fair weight: Monotheism for Currency, the day yours lands, and Code of Laws for the next. Pottery I will study myself. Our roads stay open.
messages.thought: Pottery for Monotheism is a poor rate; he has no gold to add. Monotheism is my chip for Currency or Mathematics, and Montezuma needs it for Monarchy anyway. Decline politely, keep the door open.

messages.text: Peter, Genghis Khan of the Mongols. I sent you Fishing for your Pottery, one for one. Your scout stands by my western border; it is welcome on the roads, not on my pastures. Where do your people live? Name a landmark and I will tell you mine.
messages.thought: New contact, 2nd in score; his scout sits by my west border. Cheap Fishing for his Pottery costs me nothing and tests him; I also want to learn where he lives.

messages.text: Montezuma, I hold Pottery and you lack it. I have put an offer on your table: my Pottery for your Monotheism, one for one. Your Monarchy for my Currency still stands.
messages.thought: He has Monotheism and lacks Pottery; one-for-one is fair and he keeps bargains. Pottery costs me nothing to give again.

messages.text: Peter, the Mongols are led by Genghis Khan. He has the highest score of us all. With me he has kept two swaps and the peace, but he is Annoyed with me and watches my border. A strong man, not a false one so far. Keep your own border tidy near him. Monarchy for Currency stands.
messages.thought: Truth about Genghis costs me nothing and builds trust with a far friend; I leave out my own fears and location.

messages.text: Willem, a fair weight, agreed: Currency for Monotheism the day mine lands, around ten turns. Code of Laws I will weigh when yours is ready - I may have another craft for it. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Currency is a chip I can sell to everyone; Willem gets Monotheism-for-Currency only if Montezuma refuses Pottery. I want Code of Laws for something other than my Currency.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed: Monotheism for Currency the day yours lands. Code of Laws I will weigh when it is mine. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He confirms Currency-for-Monotheism; vague on Code of Laws, hinting at another craft. Fine: I keep CoL as my own chip and price it when it lands. Nothing to give away now.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, your offer is taken: Pottery for Monotheism. Good trade. When your Currency is ready, my Monarchy follows, one for one, as we said.
messages.thought: Pottery is a cheap tech but opens cottages; Monotheism is a renewable chip (sold once per buyer), and Willem already has it, so selling to Bull costs me little. Keep the Currency-for-Monarchy plan alive.

messages.text: Willem, news: Montezuma gave me Monotheism for Pottery today, so I no longer need it. When my Currency lands I offer it for your Code of Laws, one for one. Fair?
messages.thought: Monotheism came from Montezuma; honesty about it keeps Willem's trust, and Currency can now buy Code of Laws instead.

messages.text: Genghis Khan. Peter of Russia, from the cold coast west of Sitting Bull. You lack Pottery; I lack Fishing. One for one, a fair start. I also offer open borders both ways, so our traders and scouts can walk. I sent both as offers.
messages.thought: Genghis is the score leader and sits behind Sitting Bull; a friend at Sitting Bull's back is worth more than Fishing. Get Fishing cheaply now, open borders to see his land.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, fair. Code of Laws for your Currency, one for one, the day both are in hand. Mine lands in about nine turns. I will call you.
messages.thought: Monotheism is now worthless to Bull; CoL for Currency matches my public T48 word, costs me nothing, and Currency unlocks markets. Accept, keep him warm.

messages.text: Done, Peter, both signed. Fair start. My plains lie east of Sitting Bull: river and hills, Dutch to the south, Aztecs further east. When you walk a new road, say which; we swap one for one and neither walks the same one twice.
messages.thought: Peter is a clean trader: Pottery for Fishing done, open borders done. He is far west, no threat yet, 2nd in score. Give only rough direction, as promised.

messages.text: Bull, Pottery reached me from Peter, so I no longer lack it. My Sailing stays yours: Sailing for your Currency when it lands (or Polytheism if Monte's table fails), then Mathematics after. Word kept, only the coin changed.
messages.thought: SB expects Sailing<->Pottery but Pottery came from Peter. Tell him straight, offer Currency/Mathematics swap instead; keeps him friendly, Annoyed already.

messages.text: Khan, Pottery was only a coin; fine. I would rather give Polytheism for your Sailing, one for one, on the day it lands (T55). My Currency then stays for your Mathematics. Does that suit you?
messages.thought: Genghis lacks Polytheism; Sailing for Polytheism is cheaper for me than spending Currency, and it makes Monotheism tradeable to him later for Mathematics. Currency stays a chip for Monarchy and Mathematics.

messages.text: Bull, Polytheism is already promised to Montezuma; he spoke first, and I keep my word. But you hold Monotheism, and it opens the day Polytheism is mine. So on T55: my Sailing for your Monotheism, one for one, same day. Your Currency then for my Mathematics. If you refuse Monotheism, Sailing waits for your Currency.
messages.thought: Everyone has Polytheism and Monotheism; I only need one Polytheism, promised to Monte first. Bull holds Monotheism too, which needs Polytheism first. Better swap: Sailing for Monotheism with Bull, Currency for Mathematics later. Keeps Monte's word.

messages.text: Done and well done, Khan. My road is Monarchy; it is slow work, my treasury is thin. Pick another road - Mathematics, Iron Working or Code of Laws - and when both are ready we swap one for one. My scout will walk your western hills, peacefully.
messages.thought: Quick, fair trader; worth keeping close. Tell him my road so he picks another; Monarchy goes to Sitting Bull first but can go to him second.

messages.text: Montezuma. Peter of Russia, from the cold west coast beyond Sitting Bull. I trade fair, craft for craft. Open borders both ways, so our scouts and merchants may walk? I sent the offer.
messages.thought: Annoyed, Buddhist, far east; little to trade now. Open the door cheaply: greeting and OB.

messages.text: Peter, borders open both ways, signed. Montezuma trades craft for craft. I hold Polytheism and Monotheism, which you lack. What are you walking toward? Name a craft I lack and we swap one for one.
messages.thought: Far stranger, no techs I lack, but open borders cost me nothing and he lacks Polytheism+Monotheism: future swap chips. Find out what he researches.

messages.text: Peter, Mathematics is already mine after Sailing (Sailing lands in 4 turns). Code of Laws is Willem's road. Walk Monarchy; when it is ready, I swap you Sailing or Mathematics for it, one for one. Iron Working I may take later; I will tell you first.
messages.thought: Peter is poor and slow; he has nothing I lack. Mathematics and Sailing are already my road (and sold to others), so I just confirm and ask Monarchy in return later. No new commitment beyond one-for-one.

messages.text: Signed and thanks, Montezuma. I walk Monarchy. When it is ready I will send word; your Polytheism or Monotheism for it, one for one.
messages.thought: Far away, little leverage; keep him a trading door. Monarchy will be my coin with three buyers.

messages.text: Khan, agreed. On T55, the day Polytheism is yours and Sailing lands: my Monotheism for your Sailing, one for one, same day. My Currency then for your Mathematics. Send the offer and I answer at once.
messages.thought: Sailing is cheap for me, Monotheism is already with Willem and Montezuma so it costs me nothing; keeping Genghis calm and trading is worth more than withholding.

messages.text: Bull, agreed. One correction: my scribes slipped a turn, Sailing lands T56, not T55. Same day Polytheism reaches me from Montezuma, I send you Sailing for Monotheism, one for one. Mathematics for your Currency after.
messages.thought: SB accepts Monotheism-for-Sailing after Polytheism. My research slipped one turn (budget cut for gold), so Sailing lands T56; tell him now so the promise is not broken by silence.

messages.text: Montezuma, my Sailing slips one turn: it lands T56. That day I send Sailing for your Polytheism, one for one, as agreed. Send yours the same day.
messages.thought: Keep the Polytheism swap alive; warn of the one-turn slip so he doesn't think I'm stalling.

messages.text: Agreed, Peter. Your Monarchy for my Polytheism, one for one, the day you send word; Monotheism I keep for a second craft. I also walk Monarchy, 13 days out, but only just begun. Tell me your days to finish. If you are faster, I switch to another craft, Iron Working or Aesthetics, and we swap that too. No double labour.
messages.thought: He walks Monarchy, I walk it too (19/241 only). Duplicate research is waste; I owe Monarchy to Bull and Willem, so I want it fast whoever makes it. Offer the cheaper chip Polytheism, keep Monotheism for another swap. Ask his ETA.

messages.text: Understood, Genghis. T56: your Sailing for my Polytheism, one for one, and I send mine that same day. Monotheism waits for your Mathematics after.
messages.thought: One turn slip costs me nothing; Sailing is cheap to him but I want it and Mathematics. Confirm, keep him warm, remind Monotheism-for-Mathematics.

messages.text: Khan, a landmark as promised: my town Rostov sits on a river hill seven tiles south-west of Cahokia; Moscow, my capital, is a coastal hill further south-west. Sitting Bull lies between us, so we are neighbours through him. Monarchy for your Sailing or Mathematics stands. My scout walks your roads toward the Dutch. Is Willem a fair dealer?
messages.thought: Genghis is the strongest; I want him friendly, informative, and eyeing Sitting Bull, not me. Give a harmless landmark, ask about the Dutch and his view of SB.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, thank you for the word on Genghis. Plain news from me: my treasury is thin with five towns, so Monarchy comes slower, near twenty turns. The deal stands: Monarchy to you first, for Currency. If your Currency comes sooner and you wish to sell it early, tell me your price.
messages.thought: Honest heads-up keeps the Monarchy-for-Currency deal credible; he is Annoyed, a little courtesy costs nothing. Say nothing of Genghis plans.

messages.text: Peter, my Currency is twelve turns off, so I name no price yet. Its price is one craft for one, or gold when you have it. If Monarchy is twenty turns for you, walk a shorter road instead - Mathematics or Iron Working - and we swap the day mine lands. Monarchy for Currency still stands if you finish it first.
messages.thought: Peter is broke and slow; I do not have Currency yet, so no price to name. Montezuma will likely land Monarchy first, so steer Peter to a cheaper craft I want (Mathematics/Iron Working) so he gets Currency for a tech, not nothing.

messages.text: Montezuma, you are faster: my Monarchy is 21 days out. Walk Monarchy; I switch to Iron Working, about 20 days. Swap one for one when both are ready. Polytheism for Monarchy is off then; Polytheism stays open for another craft.
messages.thought: He is 13 turns from Monarchy, I am 21. Let him walk it; I take Iron Working and trade it around.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, you were right. Montezuma finishes Monarchy before me, so I walk Iron Working now. Iron Working for your Currency, one for one, the day both are ready?
messages.thought: Montezuma does Monarchy faster; IW is my lane now. SB himself suggested it.

messages.text: Khan, change of road: Montezuma walks Monarchy faster than I can, so I take Iron Working, as you had not begun it. Iron Working for your Sailing or Mathematics, one for one, when ready.
messages.thought: Must claim IW before he does; keeps one-for-one lanes clean.

messages.text: Peter, agreed: your Iron Working for my Currency, one for one, the day both are in hand (mine ~11 turns). Monarchy stands aside; I will answer your offer at once.
messages.thought: Iron Working for Currency 1:1 is fair and Currency sells to all; accept.

messages.text: Agreed, Peter. I walk Monarchy, 12 days. You walk Iron Working. When both are ready we swap one for one. Polytheism and Monotheism stay on my table for any other craft you finish.
messages.thought: Fine: Monarchy is a reusable chip, so I sell it to Peter for Iron Working at ~T65-73; Polytheism/Monotheism stay unsold until he has a craft I lack. No double labour for me.

messages.text: Peter, a good landmark; I know Cahokia's hill. Willem is a fair dealer on swaps: he gave me Alphabet for my Wheel, one for one, and held the border line we agreed. He guards his land hard and settles fast, so trade with him, don't walk across his row. Monarchy for Sailing or Mathematics stands. Sailing lands in 3 turns.
messages.thought: Honest answer about Willem costs me nothing and keeps Peter warm; he is 2nd in score, a swap partner, not yet a threat.

messages.text: Montezuma, your settler stands on the plains 3 tiles north of my New Sarai, on the road to my copper. We agreed: your towns at Teotihuacan and east, none west of it. Found it east of Teotihuacan, or keep it home. I keep my word on T56 Sailing for Polytheism.
messages.thought: His settler at (40,20) breaks the T9/T23 'none west of Teotihuacan' line and sits on my copper; I cannot stop it, but a firm word costs nothing and a breach is a casus later. Keep the T56 Polytheism swap safe.

messages.text: Peter, understood: Iron Working is your road, so I will not walk it. When yours is ready I swap Sailing or Mathematics for it, one for one. Monarchy I leave to Montezuma.
messages.thought: He switched to Iron Working, which I want for armies; a 1-for-1 swap is good and I must not research IW myself.

messages.text: Agreed, Sitting Bull. Iron Working for Currency, one for one, the day both are in hand. I will send word. What road do you walk after Currency, so we do not walk it twice?
messages.thought: Good: IW buys me Currency, Monarchy and maybe Sailing. I'll do all swaps the same turn so nobody resells IW before I sell it.

messages.text: Agreed, Montezuma. Your Monarchy for my Iron Working, one for one, when both are ready. Genghis walks Sailing then Mathematics, Willem Code of Laws, Sitting Bull Currency. After Monarchy, Aesthetics or Horseback Riding are still unclaimed.
messages.thought: Monarchy for IW is my best deal. Want him on a road none of us walks so there is more to trade later.

messages.text: Peter, after Currency I walk Horseback Riding, then Aesthetics toward the arts. Monarchy, Code of Laws, Mathematics and Sailing I expect by swap from Montezuma, Willem and Genghis, so I will not walk them. Iron Working and Currency, one for one, the day both are in hand. Send word.
messages.thought: Others feed me Monarchy, Mathematics, Sailing, Code of Laws by swap; I should research something none of them walk so I have a fresh chip. Horseback Riding is cheap, Aesthetics/Literature opens culture. Don't over-reveal.

messages.text: Genghis, understood. The Sun keeps its word. My settler walks one tile east, to the plains 3 west and 1 south of Tlatelolco, on the same line as Teotihuacan. No Aztec town west of that line. The copper between us will be worked in peace; my borders will not touch your pastures. T56 stands: Sailing for Polytheism, same day.
messages.thought: He wants no Aztec city west of x=41. 41,19 is on Teotihuacan's meridian, so I keep the letter, grab the copper, and keep the Sailing swap. Cheap word, real prize.

messages.text: Good word on Willem, Khan; I will trade with him, not trample him. Iron Working stands for your Sailing or Mathematics, about seventeen days. My scout passes your roads south to greet him. Where does his row begin?
messages.thought: Genghis is my best partner; keep him warm, confirm the deal, learn where Willem lies so my scout can meet him.

messages.text: Noted, Sitting Bull: Horseback Riding and Aesthetics are your roads; I will not walk them. Iron Working for Currency stands. I send word the day it is ready.
messages.thought: SB confirms; keep it cordial and short, he is Annoyed and I need his Currency.

messages.text: Montezuma, a correction: Sitting Bull has claimed Horseback Riding and Aesthetics after his Currency. Do not walk those twice. Metal Casting and the roads beyond Writing are still free. Monarchy for Iron Working stands.
messages.thought: I wrongly pointed him at SB's roads; correct it so nobody doubles labour and my swap web stays clean.

messages.text: Khan, your Sailing lands about now. I hold Monotheism and offer it one for one for Sailing, the day yours is in hand. Call me, or I call you. The row stays the line.
messages.thought: Sailing saves me 4 turns; Monotheism costs me nothing but a chip. He is Annoyed at me, so a clean fair swap helps. Don't mention Polytheism yet; keep it for Mathematics.

messages.text: Genghis, a small correction. The game forbids a town at the plains I named (too close to New Sarai). My settler steps one tile north, the desert 3 west of Tlatelolco, still on Teotihuacan's line. Nothing west of it. T56 stands: your Sailing for my Polytheism, same day.
messages.thought: 41,19 is illegal (2 tiles from New Sarai), so I go one tile north to 41,20: still on x=41, still honest. That also blocks any Mongol town at 40,20-40,22 which suits me; I do not mention that.

messages.text: Noted, Peter. Thank you. I walk Monarchy only; your Iron Working waits for it, one for one.
messages.thought: His warning saves me a duplicate walk; a short thanks keeps the one-for-one Monarchy/Iron Working deal warm at no cost.

messages.text: Understood, Montezuma. The desert tile stays on Teotihuacan's line; no town west of it. The copper tile south of it stays open to my workers, and my road to it stays mine. T56 stands: Sailing for Polytheism, same day, both sides send.
messages.thought: His desert town at x=41 still grabs the copper by border but keeps the letter of his word; I need Polytheism on T56, so stay civil and plant a claim to the copper for a later casus.

messages.text: Willem, thanks. Monotheism is already spoken for at another table, so I keep that word. When your Code of Laws is ready, my Sailing goes to you for it, one for one. You lack Pottery; I hold it if you want it for a craft of yours. The row stays the line.
messages.thought: Monotheism from him is tempting, but Bull spoke first on that tech; keep Monotheism with Bull, give Willem Sailing for Code of Laws and keep Pottery as a chip.

messages.text: Peter, the Dutch lie south of my river city Turfan: follow the road south of it, their first town is three tiles on. The row between us is the plain north of their towns. Iron Working for Sailing or Mathematics stands.
messages.thought: Helping Peter's scout reach Willem costs me nothing and keeps goodwill; he will find him anyway. Rough direction only.

messages.text: Khan, agreed: Code of Laws for your Sailing, one for one, the day mine lands, about six turns. I will call you. Pottery I will study myself. The row stays the line.
messages.thought: He refuses Monotheism but locks Sailing for Code of Laws: fine, CoL is sold to all three tables anyway. Pottery I get myself in 2 turns; Polytheism stays my chip for Mathematics. Keep him warm.

messages.text: Agreed, Genghis. No Aztec town west of that line. Your workers and riders walk my roads under open borders, as before. Borders fall where the game draws them. T56 stands: your Sailing for my Polytheism, same day, both sides send.
messages.thought: He wants copper 40,19 as his; my city will claim it by radius. I promise only open borders passage, not the tile. Keep T56 swap safe.

messages.text: Thank you, Khan. My scout is past Karakorum, heading south to Turfan, then down your road to greet Willem at his first town. He keeps off the disputed plain. Iron Working in sixteen days; Sailing or Mathematics for it stands.
messages.thought: Useful directions, freely given. Keep him warm: best trader and the hammer behind Sitting Bull. He must not learn IW is sold three times.

messages.text: Genghis, T56: I sent Polytheism for your Sailing. Please sign.
messages.thought: Swap day; he said he sends too.

messages.text: Signed, Genghis. Sailing in my hands, Polytheism in yours. A clean trade. Your settler walks through Texcoco: my gates are open to it. I ask one thing, the mirror of your line: the lands east of Teotihuacan's line, south of Tlatelolco, are Aztec. Plant west and your road stays safe. When your Mathematics lands, my Monotheism is yours, one for one.
messages.thought: Swap done, promise kept both ways. His settler is inside Texcoco heading somewhere; I want it kept off the sugar/silk land east and south, which is my next town. I state the mirror of his line: east of x=41 is Aztec.

messages.text: Bull, Polytheism is in my hands, but the game lists no Monotheism for trade today, from you or anyone. I will try again next turn. Sailing stays reserved for you, one for one. Then Mathematics for your Currency.
messages.thought: Game refuses Monotheism trade right now (not tradeable from anyone); keep promise, retry next turn, don't give Sailing free.

messages.text: Genghis, your settler stands 3 tiles south of Tlatelolco, on the hill by the sea. That is the Aztec south, the mirror of your line. My settler stands beside it. Plant west, near your own roads, and we stay friends. Monotheism for Mathematics when yours lands.
messages.thought: His settler sits on my intended site; a mild claim may stop him, no army to back it.

messages.text: Khan, it fails on my side too: the game will not let me hand Monotheism over today. When Polytheism reached me the same lag held a day, so I expect it opens T57. Keep Sailing for me; the turn it lists, send the offer and I answer at once. Then Mathematics for Currency.
messages.thought: Monotheism likely opens a turn after the prereq arrives (same lag I saw with Willem); I lose nothing waiting, and a calm note keeps him sure I am not dodging.

messages.text: Montezuma, I hear you. The hill by the sea is unowned and no line we agreed names it: our line was the middle plains, and I kept it. My town is founded there. Your roads and my open borders stay as they are, and Monotheism for my Mathematics stands. The Sun has room north and east; plant there.
messages.thought: He wants the coast; no agreed line covers it, it is unowned, and he is boxed in by my choice. I found anyway and keep him friendly with Monotheism swap; he stays the first target.

messages.text: Bull, signed and received. Clean trade. Mathematics for your Currency stands, one for one, when mine lands.
messages.thought: Deal done, Monotheism mine; keep him friendly for Currency, costs nothing.

messages.text: Peter, Willem of the Netherlands, merchant of the eastern shore. I have sent you Polytheism for your Pottery, one for one. I hold more knowledge for fair trades, and open borders if you want them. Where do your roads run?
messages.thought: New player, 448 score, strong. Wants Pottery->me; I sent Polytheism for Pottery. Don't reveal my chips (Monotheism) or city count; learn where he lives.

messages.text: Willem, Peter of Russia greets you. My lands lie west of Sitting Bull. Genghis says you trade fair, one for one. Here is a first one: my Pottery for your Polytheism, and open borders both ways. I walk Iron Working, ready in about twelve days; what do you walk after Code of Laws?
messages.thought: Willem is fair and the only one who lacks something I have. Pottery for Polytheism plus open borders costs me nothing and opens a fourth trade partner. Keep it warm for Iron Working later.

messages.text: Peter, done: Pottery and open borders both signed. After Code of Laws (3 days) I take a craft nobody else walks, so we have something to swap. When your Iron Working lands, Code of Laws for it, one for one? Call me or I call you.
messages.thought: He keeps fair one-for-one and is Pleased. Iron Working for Code of Laws is a free swap later; I don't reveal who owes me what or my city count.

messages.text: Samarqand is yours, Genghis; the game drew it. Now my line, plainly: no more Mongol towns east of Texcoco's longitude, none south of Tlatelolco. Our roads and the swaps stay as agreed. Monotheism for your Mathematics, one for one, when you have it.
messages.thought: He took the hill with a straight face and I cannot stop it; I am weak and need his swaps. Mark a clean line now so the next grab costs him, and keep Monotheism-for-Mathematics alive.

messages.text: Agreed, Willem: your Code of Laws for my Iron Working, one for one, the day it lands, about twelve days. I call you. My roads run from Moscow on the west coast, north to Rostov near Sitting Bull, west to the copper hills. Tell me which craft you take after Code of Laws, so I do not walk it twice.
messages.thought: Willem is quick and fair. CoL for IW is a fifth buyer for one tech; sure. Keep him warm, learn which craft he takes so I don't walk it twice. Same-turn hand-over to all buyers stays my secret.

messages.text: Heard, Montezuma. I have no more towns planned east of Texcoco or south of Tlatelolco; the plains there are full. Roads and open borders stay. Monotheism reached me from another table, so my Mathematics goes to you for your Monarchy instead, one for one, the day both are in hand.
messages.thought: His line costs me nothing: no legal site is left east of x=41 and I plan conquest not settling; give a non-promise statement, keep goodwill and my Math chip for Monarchy.

messages.text: Agreed, Genghis. My Monarchy for your Mathematics, one for one, the day both are in hand. Mine lands in about four days. Tell me when yours is near. The Sun keeps its word, and so do I on the lines: east of Texcoco and south of Tlatelolco stay Aztec.
messages.thought: Monotheism sale is gone, but Monarchy swaps for Mathematics just the same; he lacks nothing else of mine. Cheap to agree, keeps the road open. Ask his days so I can plan.

messages.text: Peter, agreed: Code of Laws for your Iron Working, one for one, the day yours lands. I call you if you do not. After Code of Laws I walk Theology, a long road. Mathematics, Currency, Monarchy and Sailing are spoken for at other tables. Aesthetics, Horseback Riding and Metal Casting are unwalked: take one after Iron Working and we have a second swap.
messages.thought: He wants non-overlap; telling him Theology is safe (he lacks Monotheism) and steers him to an unwalked craft I can swap for later. Not selling him Monotheism, it would let him race me.

messages.text: Good, Willem. Theology is a long road; I will want it when you have it. Horseback Riding and Aesthetics are Sitting Bull's roads, I gave him my word. So I take Metal Casting after Iron Working. Keep it off your table and we swap again.
messages.thought: Willem is laying out the tree for a second swap. HBR and Aesthetics I promised to Sitting Bull, so Metal Casting is my only clean road after IW. Claim it now so nobody walks it twice; Theology from him later is a good second buy.

messages.text: Peter, agreed. Metal Casting is yours, I keep off it. Theology when it lands: we weigh it then, one for one with your Metal Casting. Iron Working for Code of Laws first.
messages.thought: He walks Metal Casting, I walk Theology; two non-overlapping swaps. Theology to him costs me little once Christianity is founded, but I'll price it then; no need to commit now.

messages.text: Montezuma, my Mathematics is two days out. Your Monarchy lands in four. The day both are in hand, I send mine and you send yours, one for one.
messages.thought: He asked to be told when Math is near; telling him costs nothing and keeps the Monarchy swap warm. Do not reveal the Oracle.

messages.text: Bull, my Mathematics lands in about two days. The turn it does, I offer it for your Currency, one for one. Your word on this has been good.
messages.thought: Bull is Annoyed for unknown reasons; a short keep-the-promise note builds trust and costs nothing. Math comes in 2 turns, Currency swap that day.

messages.text: Good, Genghis. Two days for yours, four for mine. The day both are in hand we send together. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Cheap confirmation; Mathematics gives me a tech for nothing but Monarchy, which I would sell anyway. Keeps him friendly while I have no army.

messages.text: Khan, good. My Currency lands in about three days. When your Mathematics lists, send the offer and I answer at once. One for one.
messages.thought: Currency lands T62, his Math about T61; swap is fair and I want Math anyway. Cheap ack keeps him sending the offer.

messages.text: Bull, my Mathematics is in hand. The turn your Currency lists, I send mine and you send yours, one for one.
messages.thought: Math arrived a day early; he has no Currency yet so nothing to send. A short note keeps the promise visible and costs nothing.

messages.text: Montezuma, my Mathematics is in hand. Your Monarchy lands in three days or so. The day it lists, I send mine, you send yours.
messages.thought: Math in hand; Monarchy is ~3 turns off. Remind him the swap is same-day and that I hold my side; nothing else to reveal.

messages.text: Good, Genghis. Three days. The day Monarchy lists, I call you; we send together. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Math arrives in 3 turns anyway; no reason to push. Keep him friendly, reconfirm one-for-one, no new promises.

messages.text: Khan, good. My Currency lists in two days. The turn it does, I answer your offer at once. One for one.
messages.thought: Math is in his hands, my Currency lands T62. Nothing else to swap today; short ack keeps him sending the offer on time.

messages.text: Khan, Code of Laws is mine. I sent it for your Sailing as agreed; I ask Mathematics beside it, but Sailing alone I accept.
messages.thought: Keeping word on CoL day; asking Math too as a stretch.

messages.text: Bull, Code of Laws is in hand. Your Currency lands about now: tell me the day, we swap one for one.
messages.thought: Currency not his yet; keep the promise warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, Code of Laws is mine. I offered it for your Sailing; Monarchy I take when yours lands, another table.
messages.thought: Monarchy not his yet; offer CoL for Sailing meanwhile.

messages.text: Willem, I promised Sailing for your Code of Laws, one for one. That offer is on your table now. Mathematics I sell on other terms; ask later.
messages.thought: He asks two techs for one; I promised Sailing for CoL 1-for-1 and Math is my chip for Currency and Monarchy. Hold the line politely.

messages.text: van Oranje Signed, Willem. Sailing to you, Code of Laws to me. A clean trade. My Monarchy lands in two days; name a craft or gold of yours and we talk.
messages.thought: Accepted; he keeps Monarchy for a later table, I'll sell it for a craft I lack or gold.

messages.text: Willem, good. My Currency lists at the start of next turn, one day. The turn it does, send Code of Laws and I answer at once. One for one.
messages.thought: Currency lands at the start of T62 (309/321, 21 a turn). He has nothing else I want; swap Code of Laws 1:1 is fair and I need it. Give the exact day so he sends the offer.

messages.text: Khan, Montezuma's table gave me Sailing an hour before your offer came, so I declined yours; no slight. Code of Laws for Mathematics, one for one, is on your table now. If not, we keep trading elsewhere.
messages.thought: Montezuma already sold me Sailing, so his offer gives me nothing. I won't hand CoL away for free, but I ask Math 1-for-1 to keep him warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, clean trade, agreed. When your Monarchy lands, I offer The Wheel or Archery for it, your pick, one for one. Tell me the day.
messages.thought: Monarchy in 2 turns; he lacks Wheel and Archery per my notes, so pay in those, not gold.

messages.text: Montezuma, correction: I see you already hold the Wheel and Archery, so forget those. I am working to bring Mathematics; that or Theology for your Monarchy, one for one, when it lands.
messages.thought: Correcting my slip: he evidently has Wheel/Archery already; I hold Mathematics prospects as the chip.

messages.text: Peter, my Currency is in hand. Iron Working for Currency stands, send word the day yours lists. Meanwhile I offer Sailing for 40 gold, if it serves you.
messages.thought: Peter has 44 gold, I need cash for libraries; Sailing is a spare chip and he is a friend. Iron Working swap still stands.

messages.text: Good, Sitting Bull. Iron Working lands in about five days; I send word that day and Currency for it stands. Sailing I must pass on: my treasury is thin while I build towns.
messages.thought: 40 gold is my whole treasury and Genghis owes me Sailing or Maths for IW; keep SB warm, decline politely.

messages.text: Peter, Sailing is open to you: I have put it on your table for 40 gold. Iron Working for Code of Laws still stands, the day yours lands.
messages.thought: Peter holds 44 gold and lacks Sailing; selling it fills my treasury at no cost to my chips (CoL stays for Iron Working, Monotheism withheld).

messages.text: Bull, Currency received, Code of Laws sent. Clean. Next craft you walk, tell me early and I will name mine.
messages.thought: Swap done, promise kept at no cost; keep Bull warm for the next table.

messages.text: Willem, thank you, but I pass. Every town is a mouth to feed and my purse is near empty. Sailing is on three tables now; I will find it cheaper later. Code of Laws for Iron Working stands. In about five days I call you.
messages.thought: Three men now sell Sailing (SB, Willem, Genghis); its price falls. 40g is my whole purse at +0. Keep Willem warm, CoL deal intact.

messages.text: Khan, Iron Working lands in about five days. Sailing is sold at every table now, so I choose Mathematics for it, one for one, as we agreed. I send word that day.
messages.thought: Genghis has both Sailing and Maths; Sailing is cheap now (three sellers), so take Maths for IW. Lock it before IW lands.

messages.text: Peter, agreed: my Mathematics for your Iron Working, one for one, the day it lists. Call me. I also put Sailing on your table for 40 gold, if the coin is no trouble.
messages.thought: IW swap stands; Math is a chip I keep reselling. Also try to sell him Sailing for coin since income is negative.

messages.text: Good, Khan: Mathematics for Iron Working, one for one. I call you the day it lists, about five days. Sailing I pass on; my coin goes into new towns. Your scout is welcome in my land.
messages.thought: Maths for IW is locked; Sailing at 40g is my whole purse at +0 income and I can research it in 4 turns. Decline warmly, keep him Pleased.

messages.text: Willem, thanks. Mathematics and Theology are not mine to take today; the table shows only gold from you. Monarchy lands tomorrow. Fifty gold, one for one, and it is yours the same day. Name the day.
messages.thought: He cannot trade techs to me per the game list; he has 54 gold. Sell Monarchy for gold, ask 50, accept 40. Do not mention the war.

messages.text: Bull, my Monarchy lands tomorrow. Your Currency for it, one for one, as we said. I call you the day it lists; we send together.
messages.thought: Currency swap is real value; send together tomorrow. Bull is annoyed but deals work.

messages.text: Montezuma, your Monarchy lists. My Mathematics is on your table, one for one.
messages.thought: Monarchy listed; swap offer sent

messages.text: Montezuma, I see your Monarchy is ready. Currency for Monarchy, one for one, is on your table now. Currency is a craft you lack and the markets it opens are worth more than fifty coins.
messages.thought: He wants gold but Currency is a better chip and I keep my 58 gold; if he refuses I may pay gold under 50.

messages.text: Bull, Willem put Currency on my table first, so our swap changes shape. My Monarchy is yours for 50 gold; the offer is on your table. If you finish a craft I lack, we trade that instead.
messages.thought: Willem paid Currency first; I owe Bull nothing now, but selling Monarchy for gold keeps him friendly and funds the army.
