Bull, Willem put Currency on my table first, so the swap changes shape. My Monarchy is yours for 50 gold, offer is on your table. Name another craft instead if you finish one I lack.

messages.text: Khan, I must pass. Forty-five gold is every coin I own, and my new towns eat more than they pay. Monotheism sits at every table now; I will take it later for a craft, not coin. Mathematics for Iron Working stands: four days, I call you.
messages.thought: 45g is my entire purse at -3/turn; paying it disbands my units next turn. Monotheism is on every table and 6 turns of my own research: worth little. Decline warmly, keep the Maths deal and his goodwill.

messages.text: Done, Genghis. Your Mathematics is mine, my Monarchy is yours. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Swap done, Math in hand. Keep him warm and calm; war is ~T72, no hint. Done, Genghis. Mathematics received, Monarchy sent. The Sun keeps its word.

messages.text: Signed, Willem. Currency for Monarchy, one for one. Well bargained. When Theology or Mathematics-level craft of yours lists, call me.
messages.thought: Currency for Monarchy is a good deal, far better than 55 gold. Keep him friendly.

messages.text: Willem, thanks for the clean swap. I see your Settler 3 tiles east of Mesa Verde, just south of the hill that lies 2 tiles south of Poverty Point. A town on that hill would sit on my gold hill's doorstep. You asked me to keep my towns off your coast, and I have. I ask the same: plant elsewhere on your side of the plains. My sentry walks to that hill to keep watch.
messages.thought: His settler stands next to the hill at 28,19 that crowds my gold hill; I cannot stop it by force and do not want a quarrel with my cleanest partner, so I ask plainly and put a sentry there.

messages.text: Montezuma, good. The day Monarchy lists, call me and we swap one for one. I would also swap open borders with you, if you wish.
messages.thought: Monarchy for Currency is clean; nothing to ask beyond acknowledging, and open borders with him would help trade.

messages.text: Bull, our words crossed. Monarchy is listed and yours: 50 gold, the offer is on your table. Currency already reached me from another hand, so I want gold, or Aesthetics or Horseback Riding when you finish one, one for one. Open borders both ways: also on your table, sign it.
messages.thought: His message crossed mine; he thinks swap is still Currency. Restate cleanly: gold 50 now, or Aesthetics/Horseback later. Open borders is harmless, far west.

messages.text: Bull, the hill is not my site. My town goes on the grass one tile south of it, on my own coast, inside my border already. I build nothing on the hill. Mesa Verde took the shore I asked you to leave; this is what remains for me. Your gold hill stays yours.
messages.thought: 28,18 is my own land and the last legal coastal slot; he can't stop me and won't fight over it. Give him the hill in words (costs nothing, I never wanted to build on a hill under his gold), stay firm on the tile south of it.

messages.text: Willem, thanks. The grass south of the hill is yours, the hill and the gold hill stay mine. Good neighbours. Monarchy lands in my hands next turn; I will tell you the day I can swap it.
messages.thought: He yields the hill and keeps his word; a short thanks costs nothing and keeps my best neighbour warm.

messages.text: Bull, good neighbours. Monarchy I already hold, so keep it for your own people. Tell me the craft you walk after it, and I will name mine, one for one.
messages.thought: He will hold Monarchy, which I already have, so there is no swap there; better to say so now than let him plan around it. Keep him warm, ask his next craft early.

messages.text: Montezuma, Monarchy and open borders received, thank you. Horseback Riding lands in about six days. I call you first; I trade it for a craft I lack, or for gold.
messages.thought: Bought Monarchy fair; he has 97 gold and nothing I lack. Horseback Riding in 6 turns is my chip: sell it for gold if he has no craft. Keep him warm, no promises beyond 'I call you first'.

messages.text: Willem, my Monarchy is in hand but not yet on the table. If you lack it, tell me next turn and we talk: a craft you hold, or gold.
messages.thought: Monarchy just landed and is not yet tradeable; he holds 62 gold. Early warning costs nothing and he asked for it.

messages.text: Good, Bull. My Construction lands in about eight days, yours in six. Swap one for one the day both list. If I am short, I pay thirty gold for Horseback.
messages.thought: Horseback is cheap for me but a swap saves gold for the army; my Construction lands ~T72, his Horseback ~T70. Lock a 1:1 swap, fallback small gold.

messages.text: Willem, understood, keep your Monarchy. I walk Horseback Riding now (about six days), then Aesthetics. Name yours and we swap one for one.
messages.thought: He holds Monarchy already, so no sale; he asked my next craft, telling him early keeps our clean swaps going.

messages.text: Bull, my craft is Theology, about seven days. Theology for your Horseback Riding the day both are in hand, one for one. Aesthetics after that I will weigh.
messages.thought: Bull walks Horseback ~T71, my Theology lands ~T72; 1-for-1 fits and gives me a craft I'd otherwise research. Christianity founding is mine first, so I name it only when done.

messages.text: Peter, I offer Monarchy for 38 gold, if it serves you. Iron Working for Currency still stands when yours lists.
messages.thought: He has 38 gold and wanted Monarchy; selling it for all his gold fills my treasury and keeps Iron Working/Currency swap intact.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed. Horseback Riding lands in about five days; Construction for it, one for one, the day both list. If you are late, I take 40 gold for Horseback, not 30.
messages.thought: Construction for Horseback 1:1 is fair and I get a craft; if he is late, 30 gold is too low, I ask 40.

messages.text: Agreed, Bull. Construction for Horseback, one for one, the day both list. Call me first; I do the same.
messages.thought: Deal is as I wanted: 1:1 swap, he calls me; Construction lands ~T72, Horseback ~T70 so I may be a couple of days late, 40 gold fallback is acceptable but I'd rather swap. Keep it short.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I pass on coin: 38 gold is every coin I have. But hear this. Monarchy now sits at every table, and Iron Working at none but mine. Iron Working lands in three days. Give me Currency and Monarchy for it, and you hold iron first of all your neighbours. If not, Currency for Iron Working stands, as agreed.
messages.thought: 38g is my whole purse at -2/turn; paying it starts disbanding. Monarchy is now on every table (all four hold it), so its price is falling; my Iron Working is the only rare craft left. Ask high: Currency + Monarchy for IW. If he refuses, 1:1 for Currency stands and Montezuma pays Monarchy.

messages.text: Peter, Currency for Iron Working, one for one, stands as we agreed the day yours lists. Monarchy is a separate trade: I take 25 gold for it, or a craft later. You choose.
messages.thought: He wants two techs for one and will not spend coin; Monarchy is cheap now but not free. Iron Working is not worth more than Currency to me. Hold the agreed 1:1, sell Monarchy small.

messages.text: Montezuma, Theology lands with me in about five days. You asked me to call you. I sell it for 100 gold, same day it lists. Tell me if the price suits you.
messages.thought: He holds 109 gold and likes me; Theology lands ~T71 and is my chip for coin since he already owns everything else I have. Price early, ask a little more than I'll take.

messages.text: Willem, Theology is welcome, but 100 coins is a Sun-priest's price. My Construction lands in about six days, yours in five. Swap one for one the day both list, as we did with Currency. If I am a day late, I pay 60 gold for Theology. Agreed?
messages.thought: 100 gold is steep while I arm for the Mongol war; Construction lands 1 day after his Theology, so a 1:1 swap is natural; he has liked 1:1 trades before. Fallback 60 gold.

messages.text: Done, Sitting Bull: Monarchy for 25 gold, a fair price. Iron Working lands tomorrow. I put Currency for it on your table that day, one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: 25 gold for 241 beakers and Hereditary Rule is a bargain; now I keep IW-for-Currency to the letter, he is my nearest neighbour and still Annoyed.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed: Theology for Construction, one for one, the day both list. If you are late, 75 gold, not 60, and I send it anyway when you can pay.
messages.thought: Construction saves me ~6 turns of research, worth more than 100 gold; his fallback of 60 coins is thin but only if he's late. Accept, and ask for 75 if he's late.

messages.text: Montezuma, Monarchy came to me by another hand, so our old bargain needs a new price. Iron Working lands tomorrow, and still nobody but me holds it. For it I ask Sailing and Monotheism. If that is too rich for you, Monotheism and 30 gold. Tell me which, and I put it on your table.
messages.thought: Monarchy is bought, so Montezuma's slot is free: IW is the only rare craft on the board, ask two techs or a tech plus gold; I need the coin most.

messages.text: Khan, Iron Working lands tomorrow. I put it on your table for Mathematics that day, one for one, as we agreed. Be ready to sign.
messages.thought: Keep the Khan warm and ready to sign the moment IW lists; 1:1 Maths as agreed.

messages.text: Willem, Iron Working lands tomorrow. I put it on your table for Code of Laws that day, one for one, as we agreed.
messages.thought: Willem is fair but Cautious; keep the CoL deal exact and on time.

messages.text: Peter, fair that Monarchy reached you elsewhere. Monotheism for Iron Working, one for one, the day it lists. Sailing I sell separately, for gold. Put Monotheism-for-Iron Working on my table.
messages.thought: Monarchy-for-Iron Working fell through because he got Monarchy elsewhere; Monotheism is my chip but Iron Working is only 6 turns for me; one for one is fair, Sailing extra is too rich.

messages.text: Peter, ready. Mathematics for Iron Working, one for one, the day it lands. Call me and I sign at once.
messages.thought: IW not tradeable yet; keep the Math<->IW promise, it is cheap and gets me IW toward copper/catapult plan.

messages.text: Agreed, Willem. Theology for Construction, one for one, the day both list. I call you the moment mine lists; if I am late, 75 gold. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Deal is exactly what I wanted: 1:1 swap, 75 gold fallback acceptable. Confirm briefly, keep him warm; I call him the day Construction lists (~T72).

messages.text: Signed, Khan. Iron for Mathematics, as agreed. Good doing business with a man who signs fast.
messages.thought: Clean 1:1 swap done; keep the Khan warm, he is the one to watch.

messages.text: Signed, Willem. Code of Laws for Iron Working, done as agreed. When my Metal Casting is poured, we talk Theology.
messages.thought: Willem kept his word; Theology-for-Metal Casting is the next thread.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Iron Working for Currency is on your table now, one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: Keeping my word to the letter with my Annoyed neighbour.

messages.text: Montezuma, Monotheism for Iron Working is on your table now, one for one. Sailing: if you take 15 gold, say so.
messages.thought: He agreed 1:1; Monotheism will save me 5 turns of research. Sailing only if cheap.

messages.text: Signed, Peter. Iron Working is mine, Monotheism is yours. Sailing and Currency I still sell for gold, when your coffers fill.
messages.thought: Deal done as planned: Iron Working in hand, Monotheism cost me nothing. Keep him warm; Sailing only when he has gold.

messages.text: Peter, 15 is a beggar's price and your coffers hold two. Sailing is 40 gold, or 3 gold a turn from you. Put either on my table when you can pay.
messages.thought: He has 2 gold, so 15 is a bluff of poverty. Sailing costs me nothing to give, but I want real gold; leave a door open with a gold-per-turn option.

messages.text: Fair words, Montezuma. My coffers are thin this season and Sailing can wait. When they fill, or when I have a new craft for your table, I come to you first.
messages.thought: No coin to spare until Hereditary Rule is paid for; Sailing can wait. Keep him Pleased and leave the door open for a craft swap instead of gold.

messages.text: Montezuma, Horseback Riding is in my hand. I call you first. Construction for it, one for one, the day yours lists.
messages.thought: Calling first as promised; keep the 1:1 swap

messages.text: Willem, Horseback Riding is in my hand. Theology for it, one for one, the day yours lists.
messages.thought: Calling first as promised

messages.text: Bull, good. Theology lists in two days. The day it does, I send it for your Horseback Riding, one for one. Aesthetics after, I will weigh.
messages.thought: Horseback is a cheap chip but a fair swap keeps Bull warm; Theology lands in 2 turns, I promised 1-for-1; no reason to haggle.

messages.text: Good, Bull. Construction lists in three days. I call you the moment it does: one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: He just repeats the swap; keeping him warm costs nothing, and it pins the date so he does not sell Horseback elsewhere first.

messages.text: Khan, I decline: my purse is thin and Construction is already promised to reach me elsewhere. Another day, another craft.
messages.thought: Construction arrives from Montezuma for Theology tomorrow, so 50 gold is waste; keep him polite, reveal nothing of Theology yet

messages.text: Montezuma, I will be plain: Genghis put Construction on my table and I took it. I do not need yours now. Horseback Riding is still yours for 50 gold, today. If you prefer a craft you hold that I lack, name it.
messages.thought: Construction came from Genghis today, so I no longer need his; be honest and sell Horseback for gold, he has 153.

messages.text: Montezuma, you took a one-pop border town with no word. I offered you peace on your table. Take it and keep what you took. Refuse, and my next envoys ride with iron.
messages.thought: I'm all warriors; I need ~15 turns of peace to get swords and catapults, then Texcoco is mine anyway. Peace now is the cheap way to buy time.

messages.text: Montezuma signed lines with me at T59 and struck my town with no word at T70. Remember who breaks his word when you sign yours with him.
messages.thought: Four neighbours at open borders with Montezuma; I want them to see him as the one who strikes without warning, and maybe cut him off. I don't ask for war, only distance.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear you. I hold peace with you and keep my word to those who keep theirs. Your war is yours; my doors stay open to you as before.
messages.thought: He wants me wary of Montezuma and maybe in his war; I stay neutral and keep selling to both, but I want Genghis calm, not offended.

messages.text: Montezuma, I hear you have drawn the sword on the Khan. Bold. What is the quarrel? Russia stands outside it for now, but my ears are open, and so is my door. Sailing my own shipwrights will find this season, so keep it. When I have a new craft, your table is still the first I visit.
messages.thought: His war on the Khan is the best news this season: the score leader bleeds. I won't fight Genghis with warriors, but I'll hear what he'd pay, and keep him Pleased. Sailing I research myself in 3 turns; tell him so he is not left waiting.

messages.text: Khan, word reached me that the Aztec bites at your heels. Russia has no part in it; our trade stands as before. If you sell Construction for coin later, tell me your price.
messages.thought: Genghis is the score leader and my long-term threat; I want him busy in the east. Reassure him so he looks away from me, and keep the door to his Construction open.

messages.text: Willem, a new faith rises in your land. A good day for you. Metal Casting is on my anvil now; when it is poured, I come for Theology as we said.
messages.thought: He founded Christianity; he is Cautious to me. A short warm word keeps the Theology-for-Metal Casting door open; nothing to trade today.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I have no horses to ride, and 30 gold is nearly all my purse. For Horseback Riding I pay 15 gold. If that suits you, put it on my table.
messages.thought: HBR leads nowhere for me and I have no horses; 30 of my 35 gold is too much. He comes down when refused; 15 is my price, and I'm content if he says no.

messages.text: Montezuma, Theology is in my hand. Send me your Construction the day it lists and I send mine, one for one, as agreed. A question: the Khan keeps two warriors in the towns beside my border. A second front costs swords. What would the Sun pay a friend who marches on the day he names?
messages.thought: Genghis's southern towns hold two warriors each; a paid second front is worth gold if Monty pays, and I learn his appetite before I commit. Do not name a date.

messages.text: Paid, Bull. Horseback Riding is mine. Honest dealing: when I finish a craft you lack, you hear it from me first.
messages.thought: Paid his 50 for a tech worth 150 beakers; keeps my best gold buyer warm. No promise left open.

messages.text: The quarrel is land, Peter. The Khan planted a town on my road and sat on my doorstep. I answered. His border towns hold two warriors each. Stand outside, or take your share. My table stays open.
messages.thought: Peter probes before choosing a side; give him the land reason and the soft-target hint, nothing of my force.

messages.text: Genghis speaks of broken words. I have kept every swap I signed with Bull, Willem, Peter and the Khan himself. Ask them. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Genghis smears me to the court; my deals with the others are all kept, so I answer with the record, not with a threat. Does not offer him peace.

messages.text: Peter, you ride no horses and I will not squeeze a thin purse. 15 is too little, 30 too much. Take it at 22 gold; it is on your table now.
messages.thought: He pays little; Horseback costs me nothing to give, but I do not give for nothing. Meet in the middle at 22 and keep him friendly; he is far away and honest.

messages.text: Willem, Monte broke his lines with me and took a town. His Samarqand sits 44,17 = the city of Samarqand (Aztec). Strike him with me: I take Texcoco and the copper, you take what you reach first. His workers walk your borders too. Say yes and I send Construction as thanks.
messages.thought: Willem is cautious and broke, but a Dutch front on Monte's flank would split his stack; I give him bait (Samarqand) I can't take soon anyway.

messages.text: Willem, Construction lists tomorrow. I call you the same day: Theology for Construction, one for one. As for marching: I pay no gold. I pay spoils. Every town your swords take is yours to keep, Turfan and any other. My axes take New Sarai within days. Name your day and strike when you are ready; the Khan's warriors cannot hold two fronts.
messages.thought: Willem would happily let me bleed Genghis while he grabs a town; his offer to march is cheap for him if I pay. I pay in spoils only, never gold, and the swap stays 1:1 tomorrow.

messages.text: Khan, I decline. I trade with all and strike none today. Keep your Construction; keep your quarrel with the Sun.
messages.thought: He is my target; Theology would feed him wonders and he is annoyed at me anyway. Stay neutral in words, keep him unwarned.

messages.text: Montezuma, spoils will do. What my swords take stays mine, Turfan first. I name my day when the swords are ready; do not name yours. Construction tomorrow, Theology the same day.
messages.thought: Spoils cost him nothing, but a written claim that Turfan and what I take stays mine is useful; give no date, keep him from taking Turfan first.

messages.text: Khan, 35 is every coin I hold, and I have just spent some. I put Construction for 3 gold a turn on your table instead: steady coin for your war chest. Sign if it suits you.
messages.thought: Construction is worth ~300 beakers; 35 lump would empty me to 0. 3 gold a turn gets it now and I can end it after 10 turns. Paying him a trickle is fine; it won't decide his war.

messages.text: Signed at 22, Sitting Bull. A fair meeting in the middle.
messages.thought: He met me halfway gracefully; thank him, keep the neighbour warm while I take Polynesian.

messages.text: Peter, my price for Construction is 35 gold. The offer is on your table. Sign it and the tech is yours the same turn. Colosseums and the Great Wall come with it.
messages.thought: He has exactly 35 gold; Construction will be common soon, so sell now; small coin, but it keeps him paying me and not Monte.

messages.text: Willem, understood. Construction stays for sale: 30 gold, any day you want it. If the Sun's armies cross your border, my door is open.
messages.thought: He refuses war and swaps; he will get Construction elsewhere. Leave one cheap door open for coin, no more begging.

messages.text: Land is a quarrel I understand, Montezuma. With me you kept every word, and I say so to anyone who asks. Russia stands outside this season; my soldiers have work at home. Strike well. If the season changes, you hear it from me first.
messages.thought: I want him to keep the Khan busy for a long time. I won't join with warriors and Genghis's armies a few steps from Yakutsk; keep the door half open, give nothing away.

messages.text: Peter, signed. Construction is yours; 3 gold a turn is received. Horses and Sailing come later at fair price.
messages.thought: 3g/turn is small but steady; keeps Peter paying me and out of Monte's pocket. A short thanks keeps him warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, thank you for the gold. I hold Theology now. It is on your table for 100 gold. You said you hear from me first; here I do the same.
messages.thought: He has 106 gold and paid 50 for Horseback; Theology is a fair sale at 100, I will take 80 if he counters.

messages.text: Genghis, I hold Theology. It is on your table for 75 gold. Fair price, peace stays as it is.
messages.thought: He has 78 gold, is top score and annoyed, but Theology is no weapon; gold is useful and a fair deal keeps him calm.

messages.text: Willem, I hold Construction. It is on your table for 45 gold, one fair meeting. Aesthetics follows in three days.
messages.thought: Construction is cheap to give, he has 47 gold; take it all but 2, he is a neighbour I want calm.

messages.text: Montezuma, 100 was too much for you. Theology for 75 gold: a middle price. It is on your table now.
messages.thought: He refused 100; he has 106 and just paid 50 for a tech, so 75 should clear. Better 75 than nothing.

messages.text: Bull, keep your gold price: Theology is already mine, I swapped for it today. No hard feelings. Calendar comes in nine days. I call you first, as I said.
messages.thought: Bull sells me a tech I already own; he doesn't know I swapped with Willem. No gold wasted, keep him warm and honest, tease next craft (Calendar) so he keeps calling me first.

messages.text: Bull, my thanks: Construction already reached me, so keep your 45 gold in my debt's absence. When Aesthetics lists, send word. My next craft, Philosophy, lands in a dozen days; I would trade it for Aesthetics, one for one.
messages.thought: Construction is already mine via Monty; I have no craft he lacks right now, and gold is for swords. Keep him warm, keep Aesthetics open for a Philosophy swap later.

messages.text: Received, Khan. Construction is already at work in my cities. Good dealing. When my shipwrights finish Sailing I need no horses yet; but if you have a craft I lack later, name your price early.
messages.thought: A short warm word keeps the score leader Pleased and looking east. I take no side in his public quarrel with Montezuma; I won't vouch either way in public.

messages.text: Willem, no debt between us. Aesthetics lists in three days. Philosophy for Aesthetics, one for one: agreed. You call me the day Philosophy lists, I put Aesthetics on your table at once.
messages.thought: Philosophy for Aesthetics 1:1 saves me twelve turns of research; his Philosophy is later than my Aesthetics, so I hold Aesthetics until his lists or he asks. Fair and cheap.

messages.text: Montezuma, no hard feelings. Aesthetics lists in three days. When your Calendar lists, I would trade Aesthetics for it, one for one. I will not walk Calendar myself; you call me first, I answer at once.
messages.thought: Calendar in nine days from him; I can trade Aesthetics for it and skip researching Calendar myself. Keep him friendly, no cost to me.

messages.text: Agreed, Bull. Aesthetics for Calendar, one for one. Calendar lists in about nine days; Aesthetics sooner on your side. Whoever lists second calls the other the same day. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Aesthetics for Calendar 1:1 costs me nothing and saves 8 days of research; he gets a tech he won't walk. Accept in words, deal when both list.

messages.text: Bull, 75 is too much while the Sun's axes stand at my gate. Keep Theology for me; at 35 gold I sign the same day.
messages.thought: 75 gold is all my war chest for a tech I can research in 13 turns; he overprices because he knows I'm at war. Keep him warm, no insult, leave the door open for a lower price later.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Khan puts peace and 50 gold on your table. Keep Samarqand. Sign, and your stack at the hill north of New Sarai goes home with coin.
messages.thought: He declined a bare peace; gold may tempt an LLM that wants coin, and the stack at New Sarai cannot be stopped by me this turn. Cheap insurance.

messages.text: Genghis, I come down to 45 gold for Theology. It is on your table. Peace stays as it is.
messages.thought: He has 80 gold and wants it for war, but Theology costs me nothing to hold; 45 is above my floor 40 and shows a second price is firm.

messages.text: Khan, New Sarai is mine now. The Sun takes a fair price for peace: the whole of your purse, 80 gold. It is on your table (#19). Sign, and the axes stay home. Wait, and they march on.
messages.thought: New Sarai fell; he pays for peace from weakness. I want his last 80 gold and 10 quiet turns to build catapults; I plan to strike again ~T84. Bluff of finality is fine.

messages.text: Bull, the Sun took a town of mine. Gold goes to swords this week. Theology at 35 gold still signs the same day I can spare it.
messages.thought: 45 still too much while Monte took New Sarai; I won't beg but keep the door open at 35 so he sees I'm still a buyer.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear the war in your words. 35 gold it is, on your table now. Sign the day your purse allows; Theology does not spoil. Peace stays as it is.
messages.thought: He has only 30 gold; 35 vs my floor 40 is small, and a sale to the neighbour beats losing it to Willem's swap. Close it and keep goodwill.

messages.text: Genghis, a correction: the game will not let me put 35 on your table while your purse holds 30. The day you hold 35, send word and I put it there at once. Theology keeps.
messages.thought: Correction: game refuses a 35 offer while he holds 30. Be plain about it so he is not misled.

messages.text: Peter, the Khan lost New Sarai and asked for peace; I signed. Your earlier wish stands: Sailing for 25 gold, all your purse. It is on your table now.
messages.thought: He has 25 gold; Sailing is cheap trade fodder, and every sale keeps him warm; the offer is on his table.

messages.text: Willem, New Sarai is mine. The Khan begged peace and paid; I signed for a while to heal and forge catapults. My word on Turfan stands: every town your swords take is yours. Strike when your day comes.
messages.thought: Peace with Genghis binds me ten turns; Willem still fights if he wants; his Turfan spoils keep Genghis busy and I stay honest.

messages.text: A town taken and peace on your terms, Montezuma. Well struck. Sailing I must leave on your table: my shipwrights launch in three days, and my purse is for soldiers now. Keep your coin and I keep mine. When I pour Metal Casting, yours is the first table I visit.
messages.thought: Sailing lands in 3 turns by my own beakers; 25 gold is my whole purse and buying it would waste what's already sunk. Decline warmly. The war ended too soon for me - Genghis lost a town but is free again. Keep Montezuma Pleased; he's the winner now and rich.

messages.text: Montezuma, New Sarai suits you; hold it well. Heal, forge your catapults. My swords are not yet ready, and I will not name the day. The spoils of Turfan are mine alone, as you said.
messages.thought: Peace between Monty and Genghis means my front is alone; fine, Turfan is a pop-6 city with an archer and warriors. Keep Monty warm, reveal no date.

messages.text: Genghis, your purse allows it now. Theology for 35 gold is on your table, as I said. Sign when you wish. Peace stays.
messages.thought: He holds 49 gold now; I keep my word at 35, goodwill with the strongest neighbour is worth more than 10 gold.

messages.text: Bull, my purse holds 49. I put 35 gold for Theology on your table. Sign it and we are square.
messages.thought: He is rich and wants coin; buying Theology at 35 saves 9 turns of research. Keep him warm for a later war request.

messages.text: Genghis, Theology is yours and the gold is received. Fair meeting. Peace stays as it is.
messages.thought: He paid 35; goodwill with the strongest neighbour, and he cannot hurt me while his war eats him. Short thanks, no more.

messages.text: Bull, Theology received, we are square. Good dealing. I will have another matter for you in a few turns.
messages.thought: Theology bought; he is rich and cooperative. Keep him warm; I will ask him to join the war on Monte around T80.

messages.text: Montezuma, Aesthetics is mine. You hold much gold. I offer Aesthetics for 110 gold now, and then our Calendar swap is released on both sides. If you prefer the swap as we said, say so and I keep my word. The offer is on your table.
messages.thought: He holds 197 gold; Aesthetics for gold now beats Calendar later. If he refuses I keep the swap. Honest about it.

messages.text: Peter, your purse grows. Sailing for 36 gold is on your table: ships and fishing boats for your coast. Theology waits for the next refill.
messages.thought: His purse is 38; Sailing at about his purse. Patient, sell tech by tech as the purse refills.

messages.text: Bull, keep your gold price. I keep the swap as we said: Aesthetics for Calendar, one for one. Calendar lists in four days; I call you the same day. The Sun does not pay twice for what it already traded.
messages.thought: He tries to turn my free 1:1 swap into 110 gold; Aesthetics is minor for me and gold runs -5/turn. Four days wait costs nothing; keep the swap.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, my shipwrights launch tomorrow; Sailing I keep my coin for. Theology interests me. When my purse refills, I hear your price - but I count low, as you know.
messages.thought: Sailing lands tomorrow by my own beakers; 36g would be thrown away. Theology is interesting later, but Willem promised it for Metal Casting; still, a second seller keeps his price honest. Keep him warm, name a low anchor.

messages.text: Peter, you asked for Theology. It is on your table for 40 gold, near your purse. Sailing I leave aside; ships you build yourself.
messages.thought: His purse is 44; Theology at 40 is near what he can pay and he asked for it. Patient, plain.

messages.text: Peter, Theology at 40 stays on your table; your purse now holds it.
messages.thought: Theology offer pending at 40; purse 49, keep it open.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, 40 is every coin I can spare, and my soldiers eat too. 30 gold for Theology is on your table now. Fair coin, paid today, for a book I could copy myself in twelve days.
messages.thought: Theology (402 beakers, leads to Paper) for 40g is already cheap and frees my Metal Casting for other tables; but he has come down every time I pushed. 30 is fair. If he holds at 40, I still take his #18 before it lapses end of T77.

messages.text: Peter, 30 gold, signed. Theology is yours. Sailing waits on your table whenever your purse is full again.
messages.thought: 30 is fair for a friend far away, and it costs me nothing; goodwill matters more than 10 coins. Sailing next when purse refills.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, received. Your scribes write a good book and you sell it at an honest price. Sailing I already have; keep it. Also: barbarian archers prowl south of the copper hill near my Rostov. My soldiers are clearing them out; if they wander toward Cahokia, you know who is hunting them.
messages.thought: Good buy at 30; he keeps coming down. Keep him warm while my soldiers take the barbarian town on his side of the woods; promise nothing on Metal Casting (Montezuma's table is first).

messages.text: Peter, keep your Sailing; you are ahead of me there. Good hunting on the barbarians. I have founded a seventh town to the west and my own archers watch it. When your purse is full, I will have a new book to show you.
messages.thought: He asks nothing; Sailing sale is dead. Keep goodwill, hint Aesthetics later without promising a price. His purse is 24.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a seventh town: you build fast. Two barbarian archers are dead by the copper hill; tomorrow my men walk into their town by the rice fields. That town will be Russian, so your Spiro has a quiet neighbour, not bandits. Your new book: I guess Aesthetics. Keep it warm; when my purse fills I come to hear the price.
messages.thought: His new book is Aesthetics (I promised not to walk it, so he is my only seller). My purse is for the Moscow settler now; buy later, low. Spiro sits 5 tiles from Polynesian: say plainly the barbarian town is mine before he eyes it.

messages.text: Bull, Aesthetics at 60 is dear while I buy swords. 40 gold is on your table. Sign it and we are square again. The other matter I spoke of waits a few turns more.
messages.thought: 60 for a 241-beaker tech is fair but he dropped Theology 75->35, so I test 40 first; #21 stays open as fallback. War ask on Monte comes later, before I strike.

messages.text: Montezuma, Calendar received, Aesthetics is yours. Our word is kept on both sides. I have another book, Literature; I will put it on your table with a price tomorrow.
messages.thought: Swap kept both sides; I want his 192 gold for Literature but the game won't let me offer it this turn. Plant the seed, no price yet.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, 28 gold, signed. Aesthetics is mine and my purse is empty again. Good book, fair price. Next time I come to you, not you to me.
messages.thought: Fair price, 241 beakers for 28. Purse is empty now; tell him so he stops pitching for a while, keep him Cautious-to-Pleased.

messages.text: Bull, the Sun thanks you. Put Literature on my table with your price. I walk it myself in five days, so I pay little, and I prefer a swap with my next craft: Metal Casting or Philosophy, whichever lists first. You are the first I call.
messages.thought: Bull has every tech I own and wants gold; Literature is 5 days of my own research, so I will not overpay; I keep him friendly (his attitude is Annoyed) and make clear I prefer a swap with my next craft.

messages.text: Genghis, 40 gold received and Aesthetics is yours. We are square. When you name the other matter I will hear it; I promise nothing before I know what it is.
messages.thought: He bought cheap and hints at a request; probably a war ask against Montezuma or land. Let him name it; promise nothing.

messages.text: Bull, we are square. The matter: Montezuma. He took two of my towns while we spoke of peace. His axes sit at my border and yours is the next road west. When I march on Texcoco, I ask you to declare war on the Sun the same week. Take what you can reach; I keep what I retake. Say yes or no. I will name the day.
messages.thought: Bull is rich (232g) and has war:Montezuma tradeable; his joining costs me nothing and splits Monte's attention, but he promises nothing blind. Name it now, keep the date vague, offer shared spoils, no gold.

messages.text: Montezuma, Literature: my price is 70 gold, or one for one with Metal Casting when your scribes finish it. The scrolls will not move on this sun; tomorrow I put it on your table. Choose gold or the swap.
messages.thought: He wants Literature cheap or swapped. I take 70 gold or a 1:1 for Metal Casting; the game will not list the trade until the day turns, so I tell him the price now and keep my promise tomorrow.

messages.text: Montezuma, a small offer is on your table: 40 gold for your Calendar. In four turns I hold Philosophy; the Sun's coffers may find it worth a look.
messages.thought: Calendar unlocks my spices and dye (health/happy) and costs me 5 turns of research; 40 gold is cheap. Hinting at Philosophy sale in 4 turns to plant a gold buyer, no war talk yet.

messages.text: Bull, 70 is a king's price for a scroll Peter's library already holds. I offer 35 gold, or the swap: I move Metal Casting to the front now, ten days, one for one, and you are the first I call. Put whichever you choose on my table.
messages.thought: Literature only gives National Epic (Peter has the Great Library) and a bought tech can't be resold; 70 is too much, 35 is fair, the swap is the better road and costs me nothing real.

messages.text: Willem, 40 gold is small for a craft that opens a calendar of feasts. Philosophy is the coin I want: Calendar for Philosophy, one for one, the day yours lands in four days. Call me and I send Calendar the same hour. Is it agreed?
messages.thought: Philosophy is 18 turns of my labour; he hints at a swap, so I take it one for one and keep 40 gold off the table.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed: Calendar for Philosophy, one for one, the day mine lands. I call you then. Take my 40-gold offer as withdrawn.
messages.thought: Calendar for Philosophy 1-for-1 costs me nothing I need to hold back and keeps a gold-rich buyer friendly; I'd rather keep my 40 gold.

messages.text: Montezuma, 35 is too little and Metal Casting costs me only six days of my own work. Middle road: Literature for 50 gold is on your table now. Sign it and Drama follows when it is ready.
messages.thought: He pays 35 for a scroll he can walk in 5 days; the swap for Metal Casting is worth little since I can research it in 6. I split: 50 gold, written on his table. Cheap but real income; 191 purse.

messages.text: Genghis, I have weighed it. My answer is no: I will not declare war on the Sun. My towns are young and my people want peace; I keep it with all. But I sell no swords or iron to Montezuma, and I tell you what I see on my border. Our open road stays open.
messages.thought: I will not fight a distant Aztec war for his gain; Montezuma pays me and Genghis is the one who could hurt me. A firm no without insult, and a small gift of words: no arms to Montezuma.

messages.text: Willem, Calendar is on your table for 40 gold, a good book for your cities. The Aesthetics-for-Philosophy word between us still stands.
messages.thought: Calendar for 40 is a small cash sale; Aesthetics stays reserved for his Philosophy.

messages.text: Bull, understood. Peace between us stands, and I thank you for the border word. Literature at 50 is dear while I buy swords: 30 gold is on your table. Sign it and we are square.
messages.thought: He refused the war, fine; he still sells cheap. Keep him friendly, don't reveal army timing.

messages.text: Genghis, 30 received, Literature is yours. We are square. Drama comes soon; when your purse fills, I will tell you the price.
messages.thought: 30 is cheap but his purse is small and I want him calm; Literature is harmless to me. Keep him buying, leave Drama for when his purse refills.

messages.text: Montezuma, 50 received, Literature is yours. Drama is almost ready; I will bring it to your table with a price.
messages.thought: He paid 50, fair. Drama is nearly done; sell with a price, swap only for something I cannot make cheaply.

messages.text: Bull, signed: Literature for 50 gold. The Sun pays a fair price once. Drama lists in about six days; you are the first I call, and I ask the price you set today: 50 gold.
messages.thought: 50 gold buys me 5 turns of research (~185 beakers) and keeps an Annoyed neighbour friendly; gold otherwise sits idle. I break my own 35 cap knowingly. I will sell him Drama at the same price to recoup.

messages.text: Bull, thank you, but my gold stays home this week. Calendar is spoken for in my own bargain. Philosophy lists in three days; I call you the hour it does, Aesthetics for Philosophy, one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: He keeps dropping his Calendar price (40 then 30); I keep my Monty promise and take Calendar on the Philosophy day; stay friendly, he is first prey but I tell him nothing.

messages.text: Montezuma, 50 received and the word holds: Drama is 50 gold, the same price. It finishes tomorrow; I put it on your table that day.
messages.thought: 50 is fair for a scroll he walks in six days; I confirm and sell tomorrow when it is mine, so he keeps coming to me first.

messages.text: Willem, a fair trader gets first word: Aesthetics is on your table for 40 gold. Poets and sculptors, ready today. Metal Casting I pour in a week; we talk then.
messages.thought: Aesthetics cost me 28; Willem is the only one without it. Sell it for 40, settle 30. Keep Metal Casting talk alive for a tech swap later.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Calendar for 8 gold: that is a neighbour's price, and I will remember it. The bandit town by the rice fields falls tomorrow; then your Spiro and my soldiers share a quiet border.
messages.thought: 8 gold for Calendar is a gift in all but name; he is courting me while Spiro grows. Thank him warmly; Polynesian falls tomorrow.

messages.text: Khan, by tomorrow my coin for Construction reaches 30 gold, near the 35 you first asked. I close that line then, bill paid. Next swap one for one, as we began. What do you walk now?
messages.thought: The 3 gpt line eats a third of my surplus; cancel at T81 when allowed, but announce it so it reads as a paid bill, not a broken word.

messages.text: Peter, my thanks, but my gold stays home: Aesthetics reaches me by barter within the week. When your Metal Casting is poured, we talk, as you say. A fair trader gets first word from me too.
messages.thought: Aesthetics is already promised to me by swap (Bull, Philosophy day T83); 40 gold would be wasted. Keep Peter warm for Metal Casting<->Theology; don't reveal Philosophy date.

messages.text: Bull, 50 gold for Drama, same price, same word. Put it on my table the day it lists and I sign. My scribes turn to other work meanwhile.
messages.thought: Drama at 50 gold saves me ~200 beakers; I move my labour to Paper now (progress per tech is kept, so no loss if he fails) and pay when it lands

messages.text: Montezuma, 50 received, Drama is yours. The word held on both sides. When your scribes finish Philosophy or Metal Casting, call me first and we speak of a swap.
messages.thought: 50 gold for Drama is fair and keeps my best customer coming first to me. Next craft: Philosophy or Metal Casting swap.

messages.text: Peter, a neighbour's price, yes: Calendar was small because your purse was empty. I put Literature on your table at 5 gold, all your purse holds. Good hunting at the rice-field town.
messages.thought: Peter is a friend with an empty purse; Literature for 5 is nearly a gift but it buys goodwill and costs me nothing.

messages.text: Genghis, Drama is on your table at 40 gold. A good book for your cities. Sign it and we are square.
messages.thought: He haggles to 60 percent; Drama at 40 is on his table. Keep him buying, nothing more.

messages.text: Willem, understood. I wait for your call when Philosophy lists. Aesthetics is held for you, one for one.
messages.thought: Wait for Philosophy; no new ask.

messages.text: Bull, Drama is mine already through my own offer: 50 gold paid, the word kept. I decline your duplicate table. I call you first when Paper lists.
messages.thought: Drama is already mine via my own offer #23; his #22 is the same deal twice. Decline the duplicate, keep him friendly.

messages.text: Bull Bull, Drama at 40 is dear while I buy swords. 27 gold is on your table. Sign it and we are square.
messages.thought: Drama is cheap if haggled; 27 keeps my purse near 40 for the Texcoco strike.

messages.text: Khan walks no new road, Peter: you hold no tech I lack. You lack Literature. Four gold a turn on your table, and it is yours. The Construction line closes at 30; bill paid.
messages.thought: He lacks only Literature; he has no tech for me, only trickle gold. Take steady coin; Literature to him costs little, and he stays friendly.

messages.text: Montezuma, understood: one table, one price, the word kept. I turn my scribes to Music, not Paper, so that when your Paper lists we can trade one for one.
messages.thought: He gets Paper himself; I swap Paper for Music, not race him. Keep him first-caller.

messages.text: Peter, Literature is no longer mine to sell: the game says you hold it. Then we owe each other nothing. Close the Construction line at 30. When one of us learns something new, we talk again.
messages.thought: Literature vanished from the table - he got it elsewhere. Nothing to sell; keep him warm, no obligation.

messages.text: Bull, agreed. Paper for Music, one for one, the day my Paper lists in about twelve days. I call you first.
messages.thought: Music for Paper 1:1 costs me nothing and saves me 11 turns of research; confirming keeps him sweet. Promise is the one I already made (call him first on Paper).

messages.text: Genghis, 27 received, Drama is yours. We are square.
messages.thought: 27 is low but it is his usual 60 percent; keeps him calm and paying.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Literature for 5 gold: I owe you a good word, and here it is. The rice-field town is Russian since this morning; the bandits are gone, your Spiro has a quiet neighbour. The plunder refilled my purse a little: 15 gold for your Drama, if you like the coin.
messages.thought: Literature for 5 was a gift to buy goodwill while Spiro and Polynesian share a border. He sits on 351 gold, richest at the table. Try Drama cheap; keep him warm, the north border must stay quiet.

messages.text: Willem, understood: your gold stays home. One last word before Metal Casting: Calendar and Aesthetics together, 30 gold, both today. If your barter comes first, no harm done. Metal Casting in six days; you hear from me.
messages.thought: He refused 40 for one book; he lacks both Calendar and Aesthetics and has 66 gold. A cheaper bundle tests whether he wants coin-free barter only. Keep Metal Casting talk alive.

messages.text: Peter, 15 received, Drama is yours. A neighbour's price again. When your purse fills, Sailing still waits for you.
messages.thought: 15 gold from a thin purse is fair for a book that costs me nothing; he stays a friend and a buyer. Peter, 15 received, Drama is yours.

messages.text: Peter, done: Calendar and Aesthetics for 30 gold. A fair price, fairly asked. When your Metal Casting is poured, call me; I will have something to put against it.
messages.thought: 30 gold for two techs is a bargain; it frees Philosophy to be sold for gold to Bull (393 gold) and Monty/Peter instead of swapped for techs I now own. Keep Peter warm for Metal Casting.

messages.text: Willem, two more books on your table: Literature and Drama, 35 gold for both. Libraries that remember, theatres that keep the people quiet. Metal Casting in four days; your counter-piece is welcome then.
messages.thought: He lacks Literature and Drama, I bought both for 20. He has 40 gold; ask 35, settle 25-30. Keeps the trade habit warm before Metal Casting.

messages.text: Bull Sitting Bull, your shelf and mine hold the same books now. Two tribes walking the same road is waste. I walk Metal Casting, then Philosophy. Take a different road, Paper or Feudalism or Music, and we swap one for one when both are done. Which do you walk?
messages.thought: We are both at the frontier now: he has no book I lack, I have none he lacks. A research split doubles both our speeds and keeps him buying from me instead of arming. I want Philosophy myself; let him take Feudalism or Paper.

messages.text: Montezuma, my word holds: Metal Casting pours in four days, and your table sees it first. Keep some coin warm. What road do you walk now?
messages.thought: Keep the T68/T74 promise visible: his table first for Metal Casting. He has 88 gold; prime him so he holds coin for it. Ask 60, settle 40-45.

messages.text: Peter, I walk Music, five days. When your Metal Casting is done and my Music is done, we swap one for one. I will call you the day it lists.
messages.thought: Music is my road; Metal Casting from him for Music is a clean 1:1 and he keeps his word. Also I will not give Music free.

messages.text: Peter, the Sun walks the border road: the Khan's elephants camp on my copper and I hold my gates. My scribes finish Paper in eleven days. Your Metal Casting for my Paper, one for one, the day mine lists; coin is thin here, the swap is my price. If you pour first, put it on my table with a price and I weigh it. Paper is yours at that swap or for gold, your choice.
messages.thought: Peter holds 180 gold and every tech I have, so he is a buyer only for Paper (11 days) and I want Metal Casting cheaply by swap; I must not reveal the Beshbalik plan, only that the Khan's border is my road.

messages.text: Philosophy has listed. Aesthetics and Calendar reached me by another hand, so I offer Philosophy for gold: Bull 250, Peter 150, Sun 80. Offers are on your tables.
messages.thought: Philosophy for gold; swap words bent, say it plainly

messages.text: Willem, I see you walked Aesthetics yourself, so our one-for-one has nothing to carry. I have no hard feelings. If you want gold for Philosophy name a low price; otherwise we trade again when a new craft lists.
messages.thought: He already owns Aesthetics, so the swap is void; I won't pay gold for Philosophy at 7 turns of my own work. Keep him friendly.

messages.text: Willem, 250 is dear: that is nearly my whole year's profit. I decline for now. If Philosophy is still unsold when others have passed on it, name a price near 50 and I will look again. I have Music coming in four days; we may trade then.
messages.thought: 250 gold for a tech I can walk in 7 turns is robbery; Peter/Montezuma will not pay it either. I keep my gold, stay polite.

messages.text: Bull, fair. Gold is the coin: Philosophy for 200, and I drop my 250. Fresh offer is on your table. Name your counter if 200 pinches; I deal quickly with a neighbour.
messages.thought: Bull holds ~362 gold and asked me to name a low price; he can pay. Test 200, floor ~140. Philosophy sold to a prey neighbour costs me little; gold funds the Mesa Verde strike.

messages.text: Willem, 80 is dear while I buy swords. 45 gold is on your table for Philosophy. Sign it and we trade again.
messages.thought: Philosophy is worth ~640 beakers but 80g is dear while I arm; he is broke (9g), so he will take coin. Haggle to ~half, resell to SB/Peter.

messages.text: Willem, 200 still pinches too hard. My counter is 50 gold for Philosophy. If that is too low, keep it; I will trade when Music lists.
messages.thought: 200 is still four times what I'd pay; hold the line at 50-60, he has a 9-gold purse and no other buyer.

messages.text: Bull, 50 is too low; I keep Philosophy for now. When your Music lists, Philosophy for Music, one for one. Call me the hour it does.
messages.thought: Bull offers 50 gold but Music lands for him ~T87; a Philosophy-for-Music swap is worth ~6 turns of my research, far more than 50 gold. Keep Philosophy for the swap; do not sell cheap

messages.text: Genghis, 45 is near. Others have bids on my table too. Make it 55, all you hold, and I sign today. Otherwise I answer by next turn.
messages.thought: Genghis has only 56 gold, bids 45; Peter (166g) and Monty (86g) bids are still pending and I must not let him resell Philosophy before they answer. Ask 55, hold #21 until T84

messages.text: Willem, Philosophy is a good book, but 150 is my whole purse. In two days Metal Casting pours: that is the counter-piece you promised. Metal Casting for Philosophy, one for one, on that day. And after it? I walk Feudalism next. Take another road and we swap again.
messages.thought: 150 gold is nearly my whole purse and he has 9 gold: he needs barter. Metal Casting in 2 days is the counter-piece he promised. Swap 1:1, and ask his next road for a research split.

messages.text: Montezuma, my word holds: Metal Casting comes to your table first, in two days. Coin is thin with you, so take it on credit: Metal Casting the day it pours, your Paper the day it lists. I pour first, your word is the payment. You kept it on Iron Working; I trust it now. Hold your gates.
messages.thought: Waiting until T94 risks Willem or Sitting Bull reselling him Metal Casting first. A forward swap locks him in and builds trust with my eastern ally against Genghis. He kept his word on Iron Working.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed. Metal Casting pours in two days and waits for your Music. Call me when it lists.
messages.thought: Keep him warm and the split alive; Cautious neighbour on my north border. Nothing more to say.

messages.text: Willem, agreed: Music for Philosophy, one for one. Music lists in four days; I call you the hour it does and put it on your table.
messages.thought: Music for Philosophy 1:1 is a good swap: I save 7 turns of research and Music is cheap for me. He has no gold anyway. Agree and keep it.

messages.text: Peter, agreed: Metal Casting for Philosophy, one for one, the day yours pours. Call me and I send it the same hour. Feudalism next: noted, we swap again.
messages.thought: Metal Casting for Philosophy 1-for-1 is better than 150 gold I could never get from his purse; keeps Theology as a later chip

messages.text: Willem, 55 is on your table. All I hold. Sign it and we trade again.
messages.thought: 55 is fair for Philosophy and I resell it; the strike needs no gold. Closing it fast stops Bull buying first.

messages.text: Genghis, 55 signed. Philosophy is yours. We trade again when a new craft lists.
messages.thought: 55 is all he had; takes his sword money, Philosophy is non-military. Word kept: I said 55 signs today.

messages.text: Montezuma, my offer of 80 gold for Philosophy still stands on your table. A copy has now gone east to other hands; the price will not rise.
messages.thought: Monty holds 86 and has not answered my 80; Genghis could resell cheaper, so nudge him honestly: copies are spreading

messages.text: Willem, good. Two days, then I call, and the books cross the same hour. Fair dealing, as always.
messages.thought: Deal is set; a short ack keeps him bound and warm. I call him T85 with the offer.

messages.text: Willem, I decline Philosophy at 80: the Khan's elephants, swordsmen and three catapults camp two tiles from my copper, and my coin goes to walls. No offence. If he breaks the peace on me, his stack leaves Turfan thin. Turfan stays yours, as we said. I will call you the day.
messages.thought: Philosophy at 80 is poor value with gold 86 and -2/turn. A shared enemy is worth more: if Genghis attacks me, his Turfan empties and Willem could take it. Telling Willem the stack exists is true and costs nothing.

messages.text: Montezuma, walls first, I understand. Then 60 gold for Philosophy, and it is on your table when your coin allows. Keep your eye on that stack.
messages.thought: Monty declines 80 but holds 83; a lower price may still sell. Philosophy loses value as it spreads; 60 gold is a Swordsman rush. Keeps him warm as the Genghis counterweight.

messages.text: Peter, agreed. Metal Casting on credit when it pours; my Paper follows the day it lists, in about nine days, one for one. The Sun pays its debts. The gates hold.
messages.thought: Credit Metal Casting for Paper is a good price for me; Paper is self-researched so resellable; keep it simple and keep the word, he trusts credit.

messages.text: Montezuma, done. Tomorrow the metal pours and it crosses to you the same day. Your Paper in nine days closes the account. Hold the copper; the Khan tests gates, he does not break good ones.
messages.thought: Deal bound on his word. I give MC tomorrow when it pours; Paper ~T93-94 is my payment. A short ack and a word on Genghis keeps him warm.

messages.text: Willem, the Sun thanks you. 60 is more than a scholar's tool is worth to me now: my coin buys walls and spears while the elephants sit on my copper. 30 gold is on your table for Philosophy. If it suits you, sign. If not, keep it; I will not chase it.
messages.thought: Philosophy is not on my path (Education needs only Paper); it is score and a wonder, worth little while walls and gold matter. 30 is a fair probe; he dropped 80 to 60 in a day, so he will fall again. No hurry.

messages.text: Montezuma, split the difference: 45 gold, Philosophy is yours the hour you sign. I have put it on your table. Your 30 I keep in hand until tomorrow; if 45 is too much, I will look at it again then.
messages.thought: 30 is thin but Philosophy is non-military and he's my counterweight; the 45 offer is on his table, 30 stays on mine until tomorrow. Nothing lost by waiting a turn.

messages.text: Willem, signed at 45. The Sun pays its price once and does not forget it. Paper lists in about nine days; you are first I call. Watch Turfan: the Khan's swords sit on my copper, not on his walls.
messages.thought: 45 for ~500 beakers is cheap; deal done, keep him friendly and aimed at Turfan; he has 67 gold, I can sell him Paper later.

messages.text: Montezuma, 45 signed, Philosophy is yours. Spend it on walls; the stack at your copper bears watching. I will hear you the day you name it.
messages.thought: Monty paid 45 for Philosophy; 23 is moot. Gold now ~157. Quiet thanks keeps him warm as Genghis counterweight.

messages.text: Khan, something new, as you said: Metal Casting poured today. Forges, more hammers. Your purse holds 19; it is on your table for that. Talk when you learn the next thing.
messages.thought: He has 19 gold and nothing I lack; MC will reach him by resale soon anyway, so take his coin first.

messages.text: Willem, the metal is poured. Metal Casting for Philosophy is on your table, as agreed. Send yours and the account is square. Feudalism next for me.
messages.thought: Keeping my word on time; want Philosophy today.

messages.text: Montezuma, Metal Casting is yours as of this hour. Your Paper when it lists closes the account.
messages.thought: Credit given; Paper ~T93-94 is the bill.

messages.text: Peter, signed. Metal Casting for Philosophy, one for one, the account is square. Feudalism next: call me.
messages.thought: Promise kept, cheap; Metal Casting is mine now.

messages.text: Peter, 19 signed. Metal Casting is mine. When I learn something new, we talk again.
messages.thought: Metal Casting for 19g is cheap (8 turns of research); keep him warm, say nothing of the strike.

messages.text: Willem, received, square as you say. Feudalism is mine, about fourteen days. Take Machinery or Compass meanwhile and we swap one for one when both are done. Which road?
messages.thought: Philosophy in hand, fair deal closed. A research split with him is the cheapest way to my next books; Monte walks Paper, SB Music, me Feudalism.

messages.text: Peter, Compass: it lists in two days. Compass for Feudalism, one for one, when yours is done. I will call you.
messages.thought: Compass is already 2 turns from done; a free 1-for-1 for Feudalism costs me nothing.

messages.text: Peter, Metal Casting received. The Sun thanks you. My Paper closes the account the day it lists, in about eight days.
messages.thought: Metal Casting received on credit; cheap courtesy keeps his trust and the Paper debt stays mine.

messages.text: Willem, the Khan's whole army, two elephants, two swordsmen, three catapults, now stands on the hill north of New Sarai. That is every blade he had at Turfan. When your swords are ready, his walls are empty. The day is yours.
messages.thought: Whole Khan army is 1 tile from New Sarai, so Turfan is thin; nudging him to move costs me nothing and diverts Genghis.

messages.text: Peter, Music is listed. Offer is on your table: Music for Metal Casting, one for one.
messages.thought: Keep word, swap now.

messages.text: Willem, Music is listed. It is on your table for Philosophy, one for one.
messages.thought: Keep word.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, signed. Music for Metal Casting, square. The split worked; let us do it again. I walk Feudalism, about twelve days. Take Machinery or Civil Service and we swap one for one when both are done. Which?
messages.thought: Promise kept, Music in hand. Every rival already has Music so nothing to resell. Another split is the cheapest book I can get; Feudalism can be sold twice (Willem already).

messages.text: Bull, the game shows Philosophy already sits in your books, so our swap cannot carry. Music for 40 gold instead: it is on your table. Take it or we part friends.
messages.thought: He already owns Philosophy (resold), so the swap cannot run; Music is cheap to me, 40 gold is fair, and the promise stays honest.

messages.text: Willem, true, Philosophy came to me by another road, so no swap. Fair is fair: Music for 70 gold. The offer is on your table. Meet me near 60 and it is done.
messages.thought: Philosophy came by my Scientist, so the swap is void as he says. His purse is 122; 40 is low, aim 70 and settle near 55.

messages.text: Peter, good. I take Machinery, eight days. You walk Feudalism; when both are done we swap one for one. I call you the day it lists.
messages.thought: Machinery is cheaper and leads to Engineering/Guilds; Divine Right can wait. Keep the swap loop with Peter going.

messages.text: Montezuma, seen. The stack stands two tiles from Turfan and moves faster than my swords. If it crosses onto your walls, I move that same day. Hold your hill.
messages.thought: Stack is 2 tiles from Turfan, can be home in one turn; I will not walk into that. Keep him warm, promise nothing.

messages.text: Willem, I do not need 40 gold as much as a craft. You hold Compass: Music for Compass, one for one. It is on your table. If you prefer gold, 60 and it is done.
messages.thought: Compass is a real tech worth ~5 turns of my research; better than 40-70 gold. He can give it, so offer 1:1.

messages.text: Peter, Machinery is my road, eight days. Civil Service I leave. We swap when both are done.
messages.thought: Already told him Machinery; confirm briefly.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed. Machinery for Feudalism, one for one. Mine is about eleven days off, so yours will wait a little for it. When both are listed, we sign the same hour.
messages.thought: Good: Machinery comes to me for a book I already sell to Willem. SB is Annoyed with me though; keep the deal crisp and kept. Feudalism ~T98, his Machinery ~T95: he waits a few days for me.

messages.text: Bull, a craft for a craft suits me. Compass for Music, and 50 gold on top for the trouble: that is on your table. If 50 is too dear, your one-for-one stands and I will sign it tomorrow.
messages.thought: Compass-for-Music is fair, but he holds 311 gold and wants Compass badly; ask 50 on top, keep #27 as fallback. Say nothing of Mesa Verde.

messages.text: Willem, Music and fifty gold for Compass is too much; Compass is a small craft, four days of my work. One for one is on your table, or Music for 60 gold. Either, and it is done.
messages.thought: Compass is a small craft; paying Music plus 50 is robbery, he values his Compass dearly. Hold the 1:1 line; gold alternative stays.

messages.text: Genghis, I have Music, new and untouched by your people. I put it on your table for Divine Right, one for one. Your purse is thin; a craft for a craft suits us both.
messages.thought: Divine Right is 13 turns of my work and he has no buyer with gold; Music has no purse behind it for him (18 gold). Swap is cheap for me and he gets a craft.

messages.text: Bull, Music for Divine Right is fair. Add 40 gold for the haste and it is signed today. Offer is on your table.
messages.thought: He wants Divine Right; 40g on top is cheap for him with 311g. His proposal #25 stays open as my fallback.

messages.text: Willem, the Khan's stack is dead: three swordsmen and three catapults, on the field beside New Sarai. Turfan has no army behind it now. My catapults reach its gates in two days. If your swords stand there first, the city is yours when it breaks. If not, I take it, and the first Paper that lists is yours as a gift. Name your day.
messages.thought: Stack dead; I mean to take Turfan myself because his swords are too slow; give him a short deadline plus a free Paper so the word is bent honestly, not hidden.

messages.text: Genghis, agreed: Music and 40 gold for Divine Right. Signed. We are square.
messages.thought: 40 gold for 13 turns of research is cheap; keep him friendly.

messages.text: Montezuma, Compass is on your table for 40 gold. My Music still waits for your Paper, one for one. Call me the day it lists.
messages.thought: Silent since T81; his purse is 44. Compass sale is cheap, keep Music for the Paper swap he walks. Montezuma, I put Compass on your table for 40 gold. Music I hold for your Paper, one for one.

messages.text: Willem, Compass for Music is signed, square. I put Divine Right on your table for 90 gold. Your purse can carry it.
messages.thought: Compass signed as promised. Divine Right is a real craft; 90 is fair, he has 126.

messages.text: Bull, Compass for 30 gold. The Aztec stack sits on my border and my purse is for swords. Offer is on your table.
messages.thought: 45 is his usual ask; 2/3 haggle has worked every time. Compass saves me 7 turns of beakers at war time.

messages.text: Montezuma, I have declared on the Khan and my sword stands in the ivory jungle just south of Turfan. Know this: the walls are not empty. Inside I count a war elephant, two swordsmen, an archer and three warriors. Your catapults must break seven, not four. Strike when you are ready; I walk in over what you leave, as you offered. More swords follow.
messages.thought: Khan rebuilt: Turfan has Elephant, 2 Swordsmen, Archer, 3 Warriors; my one sword is alone at its gate. Need Monty's catapults to do the breaking; keep him committed and the capture promise alive.

messages.text: Peter, I learned something new: Divine Right. 80 gold and it is yours. Offer is on your table.
messages.thought: Peter holds 123g and lacks Divine Right; he sells fair and buys fair. Ask high, expect ~2/3.

messages.text: Willem, peace holds. Divine Right is new to you: 80 gold and it is yours.
messages.thought: He declared war then took peace in the same turn; sell him Divine Right for gold to keep him warm and fund the war.

messages.text: Genghis, Compass for 30 gold is signed. We are square. Keep your purse for your swords.
messages.thought: 30 is two thirds of my ask; gold has no better sink and he stays friendly while at war with two. Signed.

messages.text: Montezuma, you are the last court without Music. It is on your table: Music for 40 gold. War is loud; songs keep the men in line. I hear you march on the Khan again. Russia stays at home, but I wish the gates well.
messages.thought: Monte is the only one without Music; my purse bleeds 16 a turn, so any coin helps. Others could sell it to him too, so I name 40 but would take 30. His war on the Khan suits me: keeps the Khan busy.

messages.text: Bull, Divine Right interests me. Seventy gold, on your table. If not, I will look at your ninety tomorrow.
messages.thought: Divine Right at 90 is fine but Bull always accepts near his price; try 70 first, sign #28 tomorrow if he holds.

messages.text: Montezuma, a correction. The Khan answered my declaration with an instant peace, and the treaty binds me for now. My sword is back on my side of the line. Turfan is yours to break; if it falls, it is yours to keep. The Paper gift you spoke of I will gladly take when it lists, or trade a craft for it. Hold your hill.
messages.thought: Genghis's AI gifted instant peace after my declaration; I cannot hit Turfan now and its 7 defenders are too many anyway. Tell Monty plainly so he does not wait on my sword; keep Ning-hsia plan secret.

messages.text: Khan, good book, but 80 is more than my purse can spare this season. I pass for now. Feudalism lists in about nine days: then we talk, book for book or coin.
messages.thought: Divine Right is low on my road and 80 is two-thirds of a bleeding purse. Decline politely, keep him warm for Feudalism ~T97.

messages.text: Willem, seventy for Divine Right is signed. We are square. Another craft comes, you will hear of it.
messages.thought: Signed at 70; he is the weakest neighbour and pays on time. Keep him friendly, nothing more.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, thank you, but no this season. Compass is already promised to me, and Divine Right waits until my purse is fuller. Our Machinery for Feudalism stands: about nine days.
messages.thought: Compass comes free from Willem for Feudalism; Divine Right is off my road and now has two sellers, so its price will fall. My purse bleeds; I keep it. SB is Annoyed: decline warmly, point to our Machinery deal.

messages.text: Peter, fair. Keep your purse. Divine Right for Feudalism, book for book, the day it lists. I also hold Compass: 30 gold whenever you have it. No hurry on my side.
messages.thought: He is thin on gold but will get Feudalism first; a book swap saves me ~10 turns of beakers and costs me nothing. Keep Compass as the coin item.

messages.text: Khan, your stack lies dead on the grass beside New Sarai. My catapults stand two tiles from Turfan's gate. Peace is on your table: Music, Divine Right and your 37 gold. The Sun does not sell peace cheap. Sign, or I come.
messages.thought: He lost his stack and I cannot break Turfan's seven defenders now; if he pays two crafts and his purse for peace I win twenty turns of research. The catapult line is true: they stand two tiles from his gate.

messages.text: Khan, Divine Right is already in my books, bought elsewhere. The peace suits a merchant. Bring me a craft I lack and we talk.
messages.thought: He sells what I already bought; reply costs nothing and keeps his guard down while my swords gather at the hill by Ning-hsia.

messages.text: Khan, agreed. Divine Right for Feudalism, book for book, the day mine lists, about nine days. I call you. Compass is already spoken for, so keep your 30 for the war.
messages.thought: Divine Right is ~1000 beakers I'd never research; free for a book I sell anyway is pure gain, and if I don't sell him Feudalism, Willem or SB will. Longbows on his side keep the Aztec war a stalemate, which is what I want: long. Compass comes free from Willem; I won't say from whom.

messages.text: Montezuma, Compass is on your table for 35 gold. Music still waits for your Paper, one for one. Call me the day it lists.
messages.thought: His purse is 45; Compass costs me nothing more to sell, and 35 is close to what he can carry.

messages.text: Montezuma, 40 was too rich for a man at war, I see it. Music for 30, on your table now. A fair price, and the Paper account still stands as agreed.
messages.thought: He has 45g and is at war; 40 was my opening. 30 is my real price; any seller could undercut me, so close it now before SB or Willem does.

messages.text: Montezuma, the gate of Turfan is stone and sword. Peace for gold only, or come and count your catapults.
messages.thought: He wants my techs and gold; I will not pay while Turfan holds. A short line keeps him guessing.

messages.text: Montezuma, signed. Music is yours, 30 received. Paper when it lists, and we are square again.
messages.thought: 30 gold in a thin season is good; keep him warm for the Paper day and for gold buys of Feudalism later.

messages.text: Khan, gold only, then. Forty from your purse, and the catapults go home. Sign it on your table. The Sun sells peace once at this price.
messages.thought: I want peace for his coin and a quiet decade; I cannot break Turfan today, so I price peace as if from strength and say nothing of my plans.

messages.text: Montezuma, your purse is thin: Compass for 20 gold, on your table. I see you already hold Music; when your Paper lists, I will trade you Divine Right for it, one for one.
messages.thought: His purse is 21, so my 35 could not be carried; Compass costs me nothing, take what he can pay. He already holds Music, so my Music-for-Paper promise is void.

messages.text: Bull, Music is already in my hand; Peter sold it for 30. So my Paper has a new price. It lists in three days. I ask Compass and Divine Right for it. Say yes, or name your number. You are first I call.
messages.thought: Music is mine now, so the 1:1 swap is moot; I tell him honestly and ask two crafts for my Paper: Compass and Divine Right are the ones I lack; he will counter but it costs nothing to ask.

messages.text: Peter, Music bought at 30; the Sun is content. Your Paper closes the account the day it lists, in three days. As agreed.
messages.thought: Thank him, keep the debt promise visible, and keep him friendly; he is the richest buyer of my Paper later.

messages.text: Montezuma, forty is my whole purse. I weigh it. My answer comes with the next dawn.
messages.thought: Elephant has no moves left; next turn it hits his stack at 89% if it stays on open grass. Stall so he keeps the stack in place and keeps the offer open.

messages.text: Montezuma, good. Three days, Paper, and the account is closed. After that I have Feudalism coming: castles and longbows, fit for a man at war. We talk price when it lists.
messages.thought: He is keeping time on the Paper debt; good. Short thanks, keep him warm, and set up Feudalism for gold later.

messages.text: Montezuma, my window shows Compass already in your hand, so only Divine Right is left between us. Divine Right for Paper, one for one, signed the hour your Paper lists. That is my number. If I am wrong about Compass, tell me.
messages.thought: Compass shows in his tech list already; Divine Right is my only real coin and costs me nothing. I want Paper 1:1 and will not set a 2-for-1 precedent.

messages.text: Montezuma, Ning-hsia on the hill is mine, taken today. The Khan keeps sueing for peace the moment a blade is drawn: weak, not strong. If your catapults still point at Turfan, I am near. Paper lists for me tomorrow; we can swap a craft.
messages.thought: Wants: Monty to keep pressure on the Khan so his Turfan stack stays pinned; no promise from me.

messages.text: Willem, Feudalism lists in about five days; your Compass for it, one for one, the same hour, as agreed. I saw you crossed swords with the Khan and made peace the same day. A short war. Was it worth the trouble?
messages.thought: Willem drew on the Khan and made peace the same day; I want to know why and keep him warm for the Compass swap. Nothing to sell him until Feudalism.

messages.text: Peter, it paid: the Khan's hill town at Ning-hsia is mine, for two swords. Compass for Feudalism, one for one, the same hour: agreed. Call me when it lists.
messages.thought: Keep Peter warm; he asked whether the war paid. Truth: it paid, a city for two swords; do not reveal more.

messages.text: Bull, you read me right: Compass is mine, bought from you at 20. Thank you. Paper lists tomorrow and you are first at my door. Divine Right is also offered by others, so I will ask Divine Right plus some of your gold for it. Say what you can add; I will not make you wait.
messages.thought: Bull holds 341 gold; Willem also sells Divine Right, so I can ask Bull for gold on top and keep 1:1 as the fallback. Be honest about Compass.

messages.text: Willem, Paper lists tomorrow. Plain words: Turfan did not fall, so the gift I spoke of is not due. Paper is a trade. I ask Divine Right for it, and I stand ready to carry the Buddhist faith to your cities, if you wish it. Name your day.
messages.thought: Turfan did not fall, so the Paper-as-gift condition is void; I tell him plainly and ask a fair trade: Divine Right he holds and I lack. He has 112 gold, so maybe a little gold too.

messages.text: Montezuma, thank you. I add no gold: Divine Right is the heavier craft and it already stands for your Paper, one for one. Sign it the hour Paper lists, or keep Divine Right from the others if you can. If you want gold for it, name a small one and I will hear it.
messages.thought: He tries 2-for-1 again, asking gold from me for a cheap tech. Divine Right costs me nothing and is worth more than his Paper; I add no gold. If he refuses I research Paper myself in 6 turns.

messages.text: Montezuma, Paper lists for me tomorrow as well, so a swap would only trade one book for the same book. Divine Right I will sell: fifty gold, on your table now. Your Buddhist missionaries are welcome to pass my roads; I keep no state faith, so nothing to bargain there.
messages.thought: He wants Divine Right for free-ish via a Paper swap I do not need; I sell for his gold and keep Buddhism talk polite.

messages.text: Willem, a hill town for two swords is cheap work. Well done. I call you the day Feudalism lists. If the Khan's other towns stand as thin as that one, I'd like to hear it. Russia listens.
messages.thought: Willem bleeding the Khan is good for me: Genghis is my nearest chaser in score. Encourage him, learn how thin the Mongol garrisons are, commit to nothing.

messages.text: Bull, Willem broke his peace with me three times in four days and took Ning-hsia while I held a peace deal. He signs and strikes. Nijmegen sits two tiles from your Mesa Verde, The Hague beyond it. Strike him with me and the cities fall to whoever reaches them.
messages.thought: Willem just took Ning-hsia in a surprise war; SB sits next to Nijmegen and Hague. A third power on Willem splits his army. SB refused the Monte war but Willem is a different matter. Bait: Nijmegen is closest to him.

messages.text: Bull, agreed in principle: Divine Right for my Paper, signed the hour it lists, tomorrow. You said to name a small number: twenty gold on top. If twenty is too much, say so and the swap stands one for one. You are first at my door.
messages.thought: Divine Right 1:1 is free for me since Paper costs me nothing more; I still name a small gold since he invited it. Keep him warm, Paper goes to him first.

messages.text: Willem, well taken: Ning-hsia is a fine prize, and the Khan bleeds. Fifty is more than Divine Right is worth to me while another door opens one for one, so I decline today. My catapults sleep under a peace treaty until it runs out; I will send word before they march. My missionaries will gladly walk your roads when the first ones are ready.
messages.thought: Fifty is dear when Bull offers the same tech for my Paper at no cost. Decline politely, keep him friendly: he is at war with Genghis and a useful distraction.

messages.text: Montezuma, our peace is paid and I keep it. Willem keeps no peace: he signed with me, then struck Ning-hsia the same dawn. His Swordsmen are in my west and his south is open. Rotterdam sits three tiles from New Sarai. Your catapults need a wall to hit. Take Rotterdam, I take Utrecht; the rest to whoever reaches it.
messages.thought: Willem just broke peace and took Ning-hsia. Pointing Monte's doom stack at Rotterdam instead of Turfan is the best thing that could happen; Utrecht and Ning-hsia I take myself. If he refuses, nothing lost.
