messages.text: Peter, Willem broke peace with me and took Ning-hsia. He signs and strikes. Our Divine Right for Feudalism stands. Name your day, the war needs pikes, and cut Willem from your trade if you can.
messages.thought: Peter is far; can't help militarily, but he is the Feudalism swap and the biggest score. Tell him Willem broke peace and ask to sell Feudalism early or embargo Willem. Keep it short.

messages.text: Khan, the swap stands: Feudalism lists in about five days, and I call you that hour for Divine Right. But Russia cuts no one from its trade. I stayed out of Montezuma's quarrel and I stay out of Willem's. Your war is yours to settle.
messages.thought: I keep the Divine Right swap and won't embargo Willem: his Compass deal is mine too, and I take no side in their war. Neutral, short, keep him warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, I see Paper on your shelf. The Metal Casting account: I put the request on your table, Paper for the debt. Sign it and we are square. Feudalism comes in about four days, for a fair price.
messages.thought: Monte has Paper listed now; collect the MC debt politely, then sell him Feudalism for gold.

messages.text: Montezuma, twenty is small, but Divine Right is the heavier craft and I keep to one for one. Your Paper lists tomorrow; I sign the same hour, Divine Right for Paper. I will call at your door first thing.
messages.thought: 20 gold is nothing, but he offered one-for-one as fallback; DR is heavier than Paper and I resell Paper, so I pay no gold and keep my line.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear you; a peace signed three times and broken three times is marked. But my towns are builders and I carry no catapults yet. I will not march this season. Press him in the east and keep his swords there. If Nijmegen still stands on one Warrior when my machines are ready, you will hear it from me before the rest do.
messages.thought: Nijmegen holds one Warrior and I would love it, but my archers cannot take it fast and Willem's swords would return; keep Genghis pressing Willem in the east, buy time, promise nothing, leave the door open.

messages.text: Bull, Paper is in my books today. One hundred fifty on your table. A fair price for a craft that opens Education and Civil Service. Name yours if you prefer.
messages.thought: He sits on 329 gold and lacks Paper; sell dear, he resells fast so I ask high and settle near 100.

messages.text: Peter, Paper is in my books. A hundred gold on your table. Compass for Feudalism stands as agreed; call me the day it lists.
messages.thought: He holds 116, lacks Paper; selling him Paper is cheap cash, no military use. Compass stays reserved for Feudalism swap.

messages.text: Khan, the peace I signed I keep to its last day. I write no carve-ups on paper. Press Willem hard in the west. What falls to my catapults, I keep.
messages.thought: He wants my catapults on Willem so his own west is safe; fine, Willem is weak and near, but I pledge nothing and claim whatever I take. Keep him fighting Willem while my peace with him runs out.

messages.text: Willem, thank you, but no. Paper is already owed to me from an old account, and a hundred is most of my purse. Compass for Feudalism stands, one for one: about four days, I call you that hour.
messages.thought: Monte owes me Paper for MC; 100g would empty my purse (116). Decline politely, keep the Compass swap warm, don't name Monte.

messages.text: Willem, one hundred fifty is too dear for Paper; I have it elsewhere for a swap. A new craft lists tomorrow. If you want to trade craft for craft, say so then.
messages.thought: 150 is robbery for a craft I can swap for; keep him warm, hint at Machinery swap next turn without committing

messages.text: Peter, signed. Paper is yours, the account is closed. The Sun pays its debts. Name Feudalism's price when it lists; I buy cheap, as before.
messages.thought: Debt closed by deal #32, I kept my word. Now ask the Feudalism price when it lists; keep him pleased.

messages.text: Montezuma, received. The account is square, and the Sun keeps its word. I remember that. Feudalism lists in about four days; for you, 35 gold, first offer.
messages.thought: Monte paid in full and on time: an honest debtor, worth a fair Feudalism price (~35 open, 30 floor). Thank him, flag the price early.

messages.text: Bull, signed: Divine Right for Paper. Fair and quick. When Machinery is mine, you are first at my door again.
messages.thought: Got Divine Right 1:1; keep Bull warm, he is rich and will buy Machinery later.

messages.text: Peter, good. The Sun remembers too. When Feudalism lists I take it, but my purse is thin: thirty, and I sign the same hour. Name it then.
messages.thought: Debt closed, he is warm. Feudalism is wanted for pikemen/castles; haggle gently from 35 to 30 without souring him. No need to over-talk.

messages.text: Peter, Divine Right is on your table for 60 gold. Tomorrow my Machinery lists; we sign it for your Feudalism, one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: Divine Right is his only missing craft; 60 is fair for his purse of 106; Machinery lists next turn for the Feudalism swap.

messages.text: Peter, Machinery is listed. It is yours for Feudalism one for one when your Feudalism lists; or 50 gold today if you prefer.
messages.thought: He may not have Feudalism yet; hold swap but test sale

messages.text: Montezuma, Machinery lists. You are first at my door: 55 gold.
messages.thought: Promised first at door; sell cheap

messages.text: Willem, Machinery is ready: 60 gold, on your table.
messages.thought: keep warm, sale

messages.text: Bull, you call first and I hear it. Fifty-five is high for a craft I already half-own. Forty gold, signed this hour. If not, I take your fifty-five tomorrow.
messages.thought: Machinery is worth ~490 beakers to me; 55 is cheap, but Bull drops prices when I haggle. Try 40 once, keep #34 open as fallback.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, no to Divine Right, thank you: my purse is for courthouses this season. I see Machinery on your shelf. Feudalism lists in two days; that hour I put it on your table for Machinery, one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: DR comes free from Genghis for Feudalism; 60g would gut my purse. Keep the Machinery swap; he seems to think Feudalism lists tomorrow, it's 2 days.

messages.text: Montezuma, thirty it is. You paid on time, the Sun gets a friend's price. Feudalism lists in two days; I put it on your table that hour.
messages.thought: He holds 93g, not thin; but 30 was my floor and he is my one honest creditor. Take 30, bind him.

messages.text: Montezuma, forty, signed. You were first at my door and I keep that. Next craft I make, you hear first again.
messages.thought: 40 beats nothing; he is thin on gold and has always paid. Keep him warm for Education later.

messages.text: Peter, I hear you. Feudalism lists, Machinery goes across the same hour, one for one. Courthouses are wise.
messages.thought: He wants swap; fine, but I should keep Feudalism free of 50g sale; patience.

messages.text: Bull, forty paid, Machinery in my hand. The Sun remembers who answers first. My next craft, Civil Service, is a dozen days off; you hear it first, and at a price that fits your purse.
messages.thought: Bull is my richest buyer; keep him warm cheaply, promise only what costs nothing

messages.text: Montezuma, good. My next craft is Education, about twelve days. When your Civil Service lists, we swap one for one, same hour.
messages.thought: Civil Service swap for Education is a clean 1:1 and costs me no gold; both land around T106.

messages.text: Bull, agreed. Civil Service for Education, one for one, same hour, whoever lists first calls the other. The Sun keeps its word.
messages.thought: Education would cost me 31 turns of research; a 1:1 swap for Civil Service is a bargain and Bull is my richest partner. Cheap promise, keeps him warm.

messages.text: Khan, no on Compass, thank you: it comes to me by other trade. Feudalism lists tomorrow. That hour it goes on your table for Divine Right, one for one, as agreed.
messages.thought: He is cutting Compass price (70->45): wants my coin before Feudalism floods. Willem gives Compass free for Feudalism. Decline, keep him warm for the DR swap tomorrow.

messages.text: Peter, Compass dropped. Feudalism tomorrow, Divine Right the same hour, book for book. Call me.
messages.thought: Compass sale failed, fine. Feudalism tomorrow is what matters; keep him warm and the swap exact.

messages.text: Peter, Feudalism is on your shelf. Machinery for Feudalism, one for one, offered now.
messages.thought: Swap on the table, hold him to it.

messages.text: Willem, Feudalism listed. It is on your table now for Compass, one for one, as agreed. Sign when you wake.
messages.thought: Swap day. Keep him fair and fighting the Khan; not telling him Feudalism goes four ways.

messages.text: Montezuma, Feudalism is on your table: thirty gold, as agreed. A friend's price for a man who pays.
messages.thought: My one honest creditor; friend's price as agreed.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, signed. Machinery for Feudalism, word kept both ways. Civil Service is my next road; tell me yours and we split again.
messages.thought: Swap done, word kept both ways. Keep the border quiet and the door open for the next split.

messages.text: Khan, signed: Divine Right for Feudalism, book for book. Good trade.
messages.thought: Swap done. He's my main score rival; keep him Pleased and busy with Willem.

messages.text: Peter, signed. Compass for Feudalism, one for one, as agreed. Good dealing.
messages.thought: Fair 1-for-1 swap as promised; Feudalism gives Pikemen vs elephants, and keeps Peter warm.

messages.text: Peter, signed: Feudalism is mine at thirty. A friend's price, a friend's word. The Sun remembers.
messages.thought: Feudalism bought at the agreed 30; keep Peter warm, he is the top scorer and a cheap seller.

messages.text: Peter, word kept both ways, thank you. My road is Education, about eleven days. When it lists, I would swap it for your Civil Service, one for one. Compass is still on my shelf: thirty gold, if your purse allows.
messages.thought: Peter keeps word; Civil Service from him for Education 1:1 is a free tech, but Montezuma also holds a claim; I will settle that when it lists. Compass at 30 is small money, try again.

messages.text: Peter, a correction: Compass is already in your books, ignore my thirty gold. Education for Civil Service, one for one, still stands. Whoever lists first calls the other.
messages.thought: My Compass line was wrong: he already has it. Correct it briefly to keep his trust; Education<->Civil Service stands.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed: your Education for my Civil Service, one for one, the hour both are listed. Mine is about nine days. Compass I have now, thank you.
messages.thought: Education for Civil Service is a good split: Education leads to universities, my road. CS ~T104, his Education ~T106. Compass I already got from Willem; don't name him.

messages.text: Willem, good dealing indeed. My next book is Civil Service, about eight days. Education is already walked by another. What is your road? Engineering, Optics or Guilds and we split again, one for one.
messages.thought: Want his next book for my Civil Service; private, so I stay the hub and he and the Khan don't swap with each other. Don't name SB.

messages.text: Khan, Civil Service is my road, about eight days. What do you walk next? If it is Engineering, Optics or Guilds, we trade book for book again when both list.
messages.thought: Score rival, but a 1:1 swap is even and someone would resell him CS anyway. Find his road to avoid duplicates; keep him Pleased.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Sun pays well. Civil Service lists in about eight days. Tell me your road: if you walk a book I don't, we swap one for one and your purse stays full.
messages.thought: Honest buyer at ~30g; learn his road, maybe a swap instead of coin from his thin purse.

messages.text: Peter, Civil Service lands for me in five days, before your eight. Do not walk it twice: take Engineering instead, and Civil Service crosses to you the day yours pours, one for one. I will walk Guilds or Optics after, and we split that too. Walk Engineering and I call you at once.
messages.thought: He plans Civil Service which I finish in 5 turns; duplicating wastes his book. Steer him to Engineering (Pikemen vs elephants for me). He is score leader but 1-for-1 swaps help me as much as him.

messages.text: Peter, I do not walk Civil Service after all; you have it in eight days. My road is Optics, twelve days, then Guilds for the Knights. When you list Civil Service and I list Optics, book for book. After Civil Service take Engineering and we keep trading clean, no duplicates.
messages.thought: Peter walks Civil Service; duplicating it wastes beakers. Optics is cheap (12t), resellable to Bull for gold, and swaps 1:1 for his Civil Service. Guilds (Knights) after. Steer him to Engineering so we never duplicate.

messages.text: Peter, the Sun walks the water road: Optics, Caravels, whales. Eleven days. You walk Civil Service, I will not duplicate it. When Optics lists, we swap one for one, same hour, and both purses stay full. Name the hour you list Civil Service; I will be at your door.
messages.thought: Peter and Bull have identical tech lists; my only edge is a craft neither walks. Optics, then swap it for Civil Service; keep my plans against Willem to myself.

messages.text: Bull, change of road, told early. Peter lists Civil Service in eight days, so I walk Optics instead: eleven days. The deal stands in the same shape: my craft for your Education, one for one, same hour, whoever lists first calls. Optics is yours at that price, no one else has it.
messages.thought: Peter lists Civil Service in 8 days and Bull will likely buy it from him, so my Civil Service would be worthless to Bull. Optics is unique; offer the same 1:1 for Education and tell him early, honestly.

messages.text: Willem, done. I walk Engineering from today, about twelve days. Civil Service for Engineering, one for one. Better still: send Civil Service the day yours pours, and Engineering crosses to you the hour mine lists. My word has held on every book we traded. Either way, deal. Then you take Guilds or Optics and we split again.
messages.thought: Good split: no duplicate, he lands CS T101, I walk Engineering (804 beakers, the book nobody else walks). Ask CS on credit at T101 so I can use it for SB's Education; fallback 1:1 at T108. Don't name SB or the Khan.

messages.text: Khan, agreed, and sooner than you asked: I walk Engineering from today, about twelve days, the same as your Optics. Engineering for Optics, book for book, the hour both list. Civil Service comes to me by other trade; no duplicates on our road.
messages.thought: Score rival, but Optics for Engineering is fair and someone would resell him Engineering anyway. CS comes from Willem, his enemy: don't name him, don't promise CS to the Khan yet.

messages.text: Montezuma, understood. Optics for Education, one for one, same hour, whoever lists first calls. My Education is about ten days.
messages.thought: Optics instead of Civil Service removes my conflict with Peter; one for one is fine.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, my road has turned: Civil Service comes to me by other trade, so I walk Engineering now, about twelve days. Our split stands: your Education for my Civil Service or my Engineering, whichever you lack, one for one. Whoever lists first calls the other.
messages.thought: My road changed; tell him before he hears it elsewhere, and keep the promise in spirit: Education for whichever of CS/Engineering he lacks. Don't name Willem.

messages.text: Willem, my word kept: my catapults stand at Rotterdam's gate. War, from this hour. Give the city or lose it.
messages.thought: My catapults are at his door; I keep my word to warn him the same hour.

messages.text: Peter, good. Engineering walks, Civil Service lands for me T101. When yours pours we sign both the same hour, one for one. I will not send first, nor will you. Deal.
messages.thought: Engineering is 12 days; I won't hand over first, but the same-hour swap keeps it fair.

messages.text: Montezuma, you break an open road and a long friendship over one hill town. Peace is on your table. Rotterdam is not for sale, and its walls will cost you more than it is worth.
messages.thought: He betrayed the peace; stall and seek peace while I whip defenders.

messages.text: Willem, peace has a price: Rotterdam. Open the gate, or the catapults open it. The Sun does not walk back from a hill it has stood under.
messages.thought: He offers white peace; I want Rotterdam and Utrecht, not peace. Keep door open: the price is the hill town.

messages.text: Peter, agreed. Engineering for Optics, book for book, the hour both list. Then Guilds is mine.
messages.thought: He commits Engineering for my Optics, clean swap and no duplicates; a one-line yes costs nothing and keeps him warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, the water road is a good road. Mine has turned: Civil Service comes to me by other trade, and I walk Engineering now, about eleven days. When your Optics lists, I swap you Engineering or Civil Service for it, one for one, whichever you lack. Both purses stay full.
messages.thought: Monte walks Optics (~T107), as does Genghis; I need it only once, so keep both sellers and take the better deal. Tell him my road changed so he isn't waiting on CS.

messages.text: Peter, agreed. When Optics lists I take Engineering for it, one for one, same hour. Civil Service I will walk or buy myself. Name the hour yours lists, I will be at your door.
messages.thought: Engineering is the pricier craft and unique to him; Civil Service I can research myself in ~9 turns or buy cheap. Take Engineering for Optics, keep the swap 1:1, say nothing of Willem.

messages.text: Peter, understood. My Education lists in about nine days. I take Civil Service first, then we see about Engineering. One for one, the hour both are listed.
messages.thought: He keeps shifting roads but the 1:1 stands; Education ~T106, I take whichever of CS/Engineering I lack first, and I do not give Education early. Keep him warm.

messages.text: Khan, enough blood between us. The Sun's catapults stand at my gate today; Turfan is as close to New Sarai as Rotterdam is. Take my peace on your table. Ning-hsia stays mine, Tabriz stays yours. Then ask yourself what the Sun does when Rotterdam is his.
messages.thought: Monty's stack is at my gate; a second war with Genghis is a luxury I cannot afford. Peace with Genghis frees Ning-hsia swords, and a Khan-Sun war would pull Monty's stack away. He is Furious but wants peace.

messages.text: Montezuma, the hill has stood under many suns. My walls rise and my bowmen string, and I have asked the Khan for peace: your Turfan neighbour has long memories of your catapults. Name gold, not a city, and we both keep what we built.
messages.thought: He wants Rotterdam, no gold sweeteners yet. I tell him the cost and hint the Khan/me peace is coming, to make his stack uneasy. The stack is real; my defense is in progress.

messages.text: Peter, the Sun broke an open road and a long friendship this morning and set four catapults before Rotterdam. A prince who does that to me may do it to you. Sell him no craft while this lasts, and tell me if you hear his plans. Civil Service for Engineering still stands, same hour, one for one.
messages.thought: Peter likes wars among others, but a Sun that eats neighbours is a risk to him too. Cheap ask: sell Monty nothing, and tell me what he sees.

messages.text: Bull, Montezuma has declared war on me over Rotterdam. I do not ask your sword, only your caution: sell him nothing that makes catapults. Your road and mine stay open, and my gold is good for any craft you list.
messages.thought: Bull is rich and cautious; I want him to stop feeding Monty, and maybe sell me a craft for gold later. No promises.

messages.text: Montezuma, good. One honest warning: another ruler walks Optics too, about the same day. If you turn to Guilds, Engineering crosses for it one for one, and Optics you get from me cheap after. If you keep Optics, our swap stands. And Willem: what did he do to the Sun? Russia stays out and trades with all.
messages.thought: Two rulers walk Optics and both promised it to me; I need it once. Give Monte the choice of Guilds (I gain a book); keep my word if he stays. Ask about his war on Willem for intel; Russia stays out.

messages.text: Willem, I hear you. I have no new craft on my shelf now; the next lists in about nine days. I will not hurry to arm anyone against a neighbour whose road stays open to me. I keep my word to those who keep theirs.
messages.thought: He asks me to starve Montezuma of catapult tech; Montezuma already holds Machinery from me, and I plan to hit Nijmegen myself. Give warm words, no promise I will not keep.

messages.text: Willem, deal. I see the Sun has come at you too. Russia stays out of it and trades with all; Civil Service for Engineering stands. After Civil Service: Optics, Guilds and Education are all walked already. Printing Press is open. Walk it and we split again.
messages.thought: Willem now fights the Khan and the Sun; I want him standing and bleeding the Khan. Reassure neutrality, keep the deal, steer his next road off Optics/Guilds so no duplicates.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed. Your Education for my Civil Service, one for one. Civil Service lands for me about the same day as Engineering; I call you that hour.
messages.thought: SB wants CS for Education; CS reaches me ~T108 with Engineering. Keep him warm (Annoyed), keep the promise.

messages.text: Peter, thanks for the honest word. I keep Optics: nine days. Our swap stands, Engineering for Optics, one for one, same hour. If the other ruler lists first, I buy Optics from you cheap as you say. Willem holds a hill my border needs; I warned him first. Nothing against Russia.
messages.thought: Warning is probably honest, but I am a third through Optics and Guilds is 17 turns; keep the swap, tell him little of Willem.

messages.text: Willem, a hard morning. What I promised the Sun before his march, I keep, as I keep my word to you. Nothing new goes to him while he marches on you. What I hear of his plans, you hear. Civil Service for Engineering stands.
messages.thought: Willem must stand and bleed the Khan. My Engineering swap with Monte predates his ask and I keep it (Willem gets Engineering too, so even). Promising nothing NEW to Monte is cheap: he is poor. Intel promise costs nothing; I share only what serves me.

messages.text: Montezuma, Engineering pours in about ten days. I call you that hour. And tell me: Optics or Guilds? Both roads end at my door.
messages.thought: Reliable partner; keep him warm and push him to Guilds so I collect a fifth book. Do not mention Willem asked me to embargo him.

messages.text: Peter, thanks. A word kept in a hard hour is worth more than gold. What did you promise the Sun, and does he ask you for anything now: gold, a craft, passage? Tell me what you hear of his catapults. Civil Service for Engineering stands, same hour, nobody sends first.
messages.thought: Peter keeps the Sun cut off and offers intel; useful. I ask what he promised Monty (to see what leverage exists) and keep CS-for-Engineering warm without feeding him anything.

messages.text: Peter, Optics. Nine days, then I knock on your door with it. Engineering for Optics, one for one, same hour. Call me the hour yours pours.
messages.thought: He asks again what I already answered; Optics is a third done and Guilds is 17 turns away. Keep the swap, short answer.

messages.text: Willem, I thank you for the offer, but I do not sell my sword for eighty gold. I keep my road open with Montezuma as with you. I am not at war with him, and I wish you strength at the table.
messages.thought: 80 gold buys a war with my Optics customer and a rival who could later help against Willem; I plan to hit Nijmegen anyway, so keep him warm and say nothing true.

messages.text: Willem, no. Russia does not sell its sword, and the Sun is my customer as you are. A war of words from me helps you little and costs me every road east. Your questions: I promised him one book swap, made before his march, nothing since. He asks me nothing now: no gold, no craft, no passage. He told me he wants a hill on his border with you, nothing more. Of his catapults I hear nothing. Civil Service for Engineering stands, same hour.
messages.thought: Sixty gold buys neither a war nor my broken word to Monte; my trade hub earns far more and a far war gains Russia nothing. Keep Willem warm: answer his T98 questions honestly and pass on Monte's stated aim, as promised.

messages.text: Khan, peace with 50 gold is on your table. Ning-hsia stays mine, Tabriz and Turfan stay yours. The Sun's catapults stand at my gate today and your Turfan is as close to his New Sarai. Sign, and look east.
messages.thought: I need the elephant at Nijmegen's wall to stop; peace plus 50 gold is cheap next to a lost city; Monty is the common enemy.

messages.text: Peter, 60 gold sits on your table for war on the Sun. A request, not a demand; if Russia stays out, I understand. Civil Service lands in 3 days for me, then the swap with your Engineering, same hour.
messages.thought: A war declaration is a long shot; but asking costs nothing and shows him I pay for help. Keep Engineering swap warm.

messages.text: Bull, I put 80 gold on your table for war on the Sun, who has set four catapults at my gate. A request only. Whatever you decide, my road to you stays open and my gold buys your next craft.
messages.thought: 80 gold for his declaring war on Monty is a long shot; he is rich and cautious; fine to ask.

messages.text: Willem, my answer on the Sun stays no. Better news: a great mind in Moscow put Education on my desk; it lists in about four days. Take Education for your Civil Service instead of Engineering, the hour mine lists, one for one. You get a bigger book a week sooner. Engineering still comes after, for your next book or coin.
messages.thought: He asked again with the same 60g; my no stands. Better: a great mind put Education 4 days away. Swap it for his CS on ~T103 instead of Engineering T113: I get CS 10 days sooner, he gets a bigger book sooner. He cannot resell it to his two enemies, only to SB who walks it anyway.

messages.text: Peter, accepted. Civil Service lands for me in 3 days; Education lists for you in about 4. The hour yours lists, we sign both, one for one, nobody sends first. I walk Guilds after Civil Service, and Engineering we settle for coin or for Guilds when yours pours. Good dealing.
messages.thought: Education for CS one-for-one is a better swap than Engineering: saves me 5 turns and he needs CS anyway. He keeps refusing the sword, so keep him warm; take Guilds next, ask Engineering later for coin or a book.

messages.text: Willem, I saw Nijmegen fall. Hard news. Our deal stands: Education for Civil Service the hour mine lists, two days. One more thing. Two wars at once eat a country. The Sun is my customer; I can carry words to him. Is there a price for peace with him? He spoke to me of a hill on your border. Tell me what you would give and what you will not, and I carry it.
messages.thought: Nijmegen fell: Willem is bleeding on two fronts and I need him standing against the Khan. A peace with the poor Sun frees him to face Genghis alone; I can carry words. Education deal stays T103.

messages.text: Montezuma, a word as a friend. The Khan took Nijmegen from Willem yesterday. Each Dutch city he eats makes him stronger on your border too; you have fought him twice. Your hill is worth less than a fat Khan. If you want peace with Willem on good terms, I can carry the word. Our Optics for Engineering swap stands.
messages.thought: Plant the seed: Genghis is the one who grows fat on Willem; Monte has fought him twice. Peace with Willem frees Willem to bleed the Khan, and keeps Monte my customer. No trade offered (my promise to Willem holds).

messages.text: Sitting Bull, news, and plain. A great mind in Moscow gave me Education; it lists in two days. So your Education is no use to me now, and our old split must change. Civil Service also comes to me in two days, sooner than I said. It is yours that day: for 120 gold, or for the next book you walk, one for one, if nobody else walks it. Your pick. What do you walk after Education?
messages.thought: Lock SB to MY Civil Service before Willem sells him his (CS lands for Willem T102). His Education is useless to me now; be honest about it and ask gold: he holds 295. Ask 120, settle ~80.

messages.text: Genghis, I see Nijmegen is yours now. It stands three tiles from my Mesa Verde; I hold the peace with you and expect the same. My Education lists in about four days. You will be first at my door for it.
messages.thought: Nijmegen went to him before my chariots were ready; he is the strong neighbour next to Mesa Verde, so keep him calm and fed with trade, and advertise Education to refill my purse.

messages.text: Khan, peace is signed and Ning-hsia is yours; my border will be quiet. Look east: the Sun keeps five catapults and five axemen at New Sarai, closer to Turfan than to me. Civil Service lists for me tomorrow; you hold gold, I hold the book. Name a fair price.
messages.thought: I paid with Ning-hsia (a pop-2 city) for peace; I will retake it when stronger. Meanwhile keep him calm, point him at the Sun, and tease Civil Service for his 184 gold.

messages.text: Peter, kind of you, but it is done: peace is signed with both the Sun and the Khan this morning. Civil Service lands tomorrow; Education when yours lists, same hour, one for one. Then we talk Engineering.
messages.thought: Peace is already done at a cost; no need to tell Peter the price (he is the score leader and sells to the Sun). Keep the swap on track.

messages.text: Peter, understood, thank you for telling me early. I take the book swap, not the gold: after Education I walk Guilds, about seven days. Civil Service for Guilds, one for one, the hour both are listed, if nobody else walks it first. If you walk it first, tell me and I change.
messages.thought: Education is worthless to Peter now; gold is tight (-18/t), so take the book swap, not 120 gold. Guilds is a real next craft.

messages.text: Montezuma. Willem signed peace with you and with me in the same dawn, and he has broken every peace he ever gave me. Utrecht stands on one Longbowman and three Warriors, three tiles from your catapults. I will not walk in your road there. Turfan is not a road: its walls are thick and its swords many. Choose where your catapults hunt.
messages.thought: His 15-unit stack at New Sarai is 3 tiles from Turfan; I want it aimed at the Dutch, not me, and I want him to think Turfan is costly.

messages.text: Khan, my catapults have gone home from the Dutch hill; peace is signed there. The Sun offers open roads both ways and trade in techs when mine lists. Answer the offer on your table.
messages.thought: I need open roads for missionaries and to see Turfan; he suspects my stack, so sound peaceful and offer trade.

messages.text: Willem, peace is signed and the gold taken. The hill stays yours. Let the roads open again: trade and my priests may walk both ways.
messages.thought: Peace paid 60 gold; I want open borders so missionaries pass and trade resumes, while his hill stays untouched for now.

messages.text: Montezuma. No open borders while five catapults sit three tiles from Turfan. Move them toward Willem's gate and we open the roads the same day. Peace stands on my side.
messages.thought: Open borders would let his 5 cats and 5 axes walk to Turfan's gate at peace and declare the same hour; I refuse, but keep it polite so he stays on the Dutch road.

messages.text: Bull. Nijmegen is a border town and I hold the peace with you. When Education lists, I come first. My Optics lists in five days: Optics for Education, book for book.
messages.thought: Bull is Annoyed about Nijmegen; keep him calm and line up Education for Optics book for book, no gold if I can avoid it.

messages.text: Montezuma, peace is signed and I honour it. Roads open when the Sun's catapults are back from my gate; a stack three tiles from Rotterdam is no neighbourly sight. Send them home and we talk trade.
messages.thought: Open borders would let his five catapults walk to Rotterdam's gate under peace and strike the moment it lapses; he wants priests and a view of my defences. Refuse politely and make the stack's withdrawal the price.

messages.text: Genghis, plain words: Montezuma holds an older word from me, Optics for Education, whoever lists first. One Optics is all I need. If yours lists first, I swap with you, book for book, and he pays gold. If his lists first, I take his, and you buy Education for gold, a fair price, about forty. Either way you are first at my door the hour it lists, about four days. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Optics can only be taken once; Montezuma's claim is older, so whoever lists Optics first gets the swap and the other pays gold. Honest and keeps both buyers warm; I need the gold anyway.

messages.text: Bull. Agreed. If my Optics lists first, book for book. If the Sun's lists first, I buy Education, but forty is high: thirty. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Bull wants one Optics and a clean order; fine. If Monte lists first I buy Education, but I haggle his forty down to thirty as usual.

messages.text: Genghis, the book for book stands if yours lists first. If the Sun's lists first, thirty-five and we are square. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He haggles to 60% as always; splitting at 35 costs nothing and I only sell if Montezuma's Optics lists first. Keep him warm, he is the strong neighbour at Nijmegen.

messages.text: Bull. Understood. Book for book if my Optics lists first; if the Sun's lists first, we talk price then. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Bull holds 35 as his floor if Monte lists first; fine, I will counter at 30 only when it happens. Keep him calm, nothing more to give today.

messages.text: Khan, look at the map: New Sarai is walled in by your land and the Dutch. My catapults cannot walk out without your road. Open borders, and the same hour all five go east to Samarqand, seven tiles from Turfan. Not to Willem's gate: my peace with him is signed, and I keep it. The offer is on your table.
messages.thought: My stack is walled into New Sarai by his land and Willem's; it cannot leave without a road. Honest truth is also my best argument: open the road, catapults go east, away from Turfan. I won't walk to Willem's gate.

messages.text: Willem, my catapults cannot leave New Sarai: your land and the Khan's wall the city in. Open the roads and all five walk east to Samarqand that same day, far from Rotterdam. Peace stands; the offer is on your table.
messages.thought: Same trap for him: the stack can leave through his one jungle tile only with OB. Tell him plainly: roads open, catapults go east, away from Rotterdam.

messages.text: Peter, thanks. Peace with Willem is signed already; the hill stays his. The Optics for Engineering swap stands: I call you the hour mine lists.
messages.thought: Peter fishes for a role as broker and wants me peaceful toward Willem; nothing to gain, keep the swap warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, I see the tiles: my land lies between New Sarai and Samarqand. The last time my roads stood open, your catapults stood at Rotterdam by morning. Peace stands, my word with it. Open roads wait until the Sun has no stack at my gate, or a longer peace is signed. Your priests may ask me again then.
messages.thought: His boxed-in claim is true (my land at 41,17 and 42,17 lies between New Sarai and Samarqand) but open borders is how his stack reached my gate on T97; I cannot cancel for 10 turns and peace may lapse ~T111. Keep him boxed, polite, no.

messages.text: Willem, I heard you. Three of my five catapults are ash this morning; the other two cannot walk out without your road. Open the road: those two go east to Samarqand, or burn if you prefer. The Axemen stay as New Sarai's walls, nothing more. When this peace lapses I will ask for another.
messages.thought: He fears the stack more than anything; three catapults cost me 100 hammers and prove I can shrink it. Next step is the open road so missionaries walk to Rotterdam.

messages.text: Khan, I will not aim at Willem: my peace with him is signed. So I burned three of my five catapults this morning; two remain, walled in at New Sarai. Open the road and they go east to Samarqand, far from Turfan. Peace stands on my side. The offer is on your table.
messages.thought: He wants my catapults aimed at Willem; I cannot satisfy both neighbours, so I shrink the stack and keep Turfan and Rotterdam equally out of reach. Missionaries need his road.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I do not walk Guilds. But I hear two other rulers walk it already, so it will be cheap and common soon. Printing Press: nobody walks it. Walk that instead, and Civil Service is yours for it. I hand Civil Service over in two days, the day it lists, on your word; you pay with Printing Press when it lists. You have kept every deal with me, so I trust you first this time.
messages.thought: Honest about Guilds: three rulers walk it, his would be a wasted week and our swap would fail. Steer him to Printing Press, which nobody walks: a unique book for my cheap CS. Lock him by handing CS on T103 on credit; he keeps his deals, and Willem would otherwise sell him CS first.

messages.text: Montezuma, three catapults lost is a poor week. The answer stays no: open roads ride on a longer peace. Ask me for another peace when this one runs down and I will listen, roads with it. Meanwhile I offer you Civil Service for 110 gold; it is on your table.
messages.thought: Two catapults 3 tiles from Rotterdam still threaten me, and open borders lock for 10 turns past the lapse at T111; his shrinking stack suggests he is short of coin, so I sell him CS to drain it and keep the hint of a renewed peace.

messages.text: Montezuma. No open borders. A road through my land is a road to Turfan, and I do not sell that. Your way east is the jungle at the Dutch edge, not my road. Peace stands on my side.
messages.thought: Open borders would put 12 units on my road at Turfan's gate; his 'burned three catapults' shows he feels my walls, but the stack is still there. Refuse again, politely, keep peace, point him at Dutch jungle route.

messages.text: Peter, agreed. Civil Service to me the day it lists; Printing Press to you the day I list it, one for one. I walk Education first (3 days), then Printing Press, about 8 days after. My word is good: you will hold it the hour it lists.
messages.thought: Printing Press is a tech nobody else walks, so I can sell it on afterwards; Civil Service costs him nothing and I'd research it anyway. Keeping my word to a trusting top-scorer keeps the swap network alive.

messages.text: Willem. 170 is a thief's price. Forty, and I read the book. Otherwise I walk it myself.
messages.thought: 170 for a 6-turn tech is robbery from a peace-breaker; but a price signal keeps him calm and Utrecht strike stays hidden. Say 40 and no more.

messages.text: Khan, 170 was my opening, 40 is your insult. Meet me: 115 gold, and the book is on your table now. You have 196 in the chest; a Khan does not haggle for a mule's price.
messages.thought: He holds 196 gold and is bluffing about walking it himself (Civil Service is ~10 turns of his research); a split price near 115 still beats nothing, and the gold buys my Knights.

messages.text: Willem, Civil Service at two hundred and thirty is too dear for me; I decline, with thanks. But in two days my Education lists, a craft you do not have. Put one hundred and fifty gold on the table that day and it is yours. You are first at my door, as before.
messages.thought: 230 for Civil Service is robbery and Peter hands it to me for a book; but his purse is 159 and Education lists in 2 days: pre-sell it for real gold, I need cash at -22/turn.

messages.text: Willem, Civil Service bought at 65: fair trade, thank you. I will ask for a longer peace when this one runs down, roads with it.
messages.thought: He sold me Civil Service at 65 and wants a longer peace; fine, I need his roads at T110 for missionaries. Be courteous, promise only to ask.

messages.text: Willem, peace on both fronts: good work, a country needs to breathe. Education lists tomorrow; the hour it does, we sign: Education for Civil Service, one for one. Engineering after, for Guilds or coin. One ask: you have seen the Khan army up close. If he masses on any border, mine included, tell me.
messages.thought: Peace on both fronts keeps Willem alive; the swap is tomorrow. Ask for his eyes on the Khan, who is now free and next door to me.

messages.text: Khan, Education lists in Moscow tomorrow. It builds universities and opens the road past the middle ages. Yours the hour it lists, for 120 gold. Our Engineering for Optics swap stands; my Engineering pours in about eleven days.
messages.thought: Education will spread within days (Willem tomorrow, SB walks it); sell it to the Khan now for his gold before someone sells it cheaper. Ask 120, accept 90. Don't name Willem.

messages.text: Montezuma, glad the war is done. Education lists in Moscow tomorrow: universities, and the road beyond. Yours the hour it lists, for 80 gold, a friend price. Optics for Engineering stands; mine pours in about eleven days.
messages.thought: Monte war is over, so my promise to Willem no longer binds. Sell him Education at a friend price before SB or Willem can resell it. Ask 80, accept 50.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, done. Civil Service to you tomorrow, the hour it lists; Printing Press to me when yours lists. One more: Education also lists for me tomorrow. Take it for 40 gold and save yourself three days; Printing Press comes sooner to us both. Your pick.
messages.thought: SB is 3 days from Education; selling it to him small saves him beakers and brings my Printing Press 3 days sooner. CS goes tomorrow on his word as agreed.

messages.text: Peter, glad of the friend price, but my purse is thin after buying Civil Service. I bid 50 gold for Education when it lists; if you say no, I take it from another table for Optics. Optics for Engineering stands, one for one, same hour. Four days, then I knock.
messages.thought: Education at 80 is cheap per beaker but my purse is 62 and Bull swaps it for Optics free ~T107; haggle to ~50, keep the Engineering swap warm.

messages.text: Peter, thank you, but I keep my own Education: it lists in two days and the work is mostly done. Civil Service tomorrow, Printing Press to you the hour I list it. Our word stands.
messages.thought: 1102 of 1447 beakers are already in Education; buying it would likely waste them to save one day for 40 gold. Decline kindly, keep the CS-for-PP deal firm.

messages.text: Montezuma, 50 gold it is. Education to you the hour it lists tomorrow. Optics for Engineering stands.
messages.thought: 50 is my floor and he could get it elsewhere for Optics; take it and keep him my customer.

messages.text: Peter, your Education is listed, I see it. Civil Service for Education, one for one, is on your table now. On the Khan: today I see only two War Elephants near Ning-hsia and Nijmegen, no mass on any border I watch. I will tell you if that changes. Engineering after, for Guilds or coin.
messages.thought: He is first reliable partner; send swap now, tell him honestly what I see of the Khan (no massing) to keep goodwill; reveal nothing of my targets.

messages.text: Peter. 120 is too much. My Optics lists in two days: Optics for Education, book for book, the hour it lists. Engineering I will take later, for Guilds or small coin.
messages.thought: 120 gold is the price of a fool; my Optics lists in two days and he wants it for his Engineering anyway. Move the swap to Education now, Engineering later for something else.

messages.text: Willem, 170 for Civil Service is still too dear; I decline, with thanks. Tomorrow my Education lists. Keep your gold for it: 150, and it is yours the hour it lists.
messages.thought: 170 gold for a craft Peter gives me for a book; his purse is 169, and my Education lists tomorrow: I want his gold for that, not for CS

messages.text: Peter, Education is in my hands and the 50 gold is yours: honest trade, thank you. Optics for Engineering stands, one for one, same hour. Optics lists in three days; I knock.
messages.thought: Education arrived the same hour, 50 gold well spent; keep Peter warm for Engineering and later a Buddhist city; say nothing of the Palace.

messages.text: Bull, change of table: I bought Education from Peter, so our Optics for Education swap has nothing to swap. Optics lists in three days. I sell it to you for gold, or swap for your next craft. Name your price.
messages.thought: Education no longer needed from Bull; I told him a 1:1 swap, so say plainly that it changes; Optics becomes a sale or a swap for his next craft.

messages.text: Bull, my thanks: Education reached me by another road, so keep your craft. Civil Service stands on your table at 170, a fair step down from 230. You hold the gold, I hold the book. My road to you stays open.
messages.thought: I already hold Education through Peter, so his 150 ask is moot; his 251 gold is the target for Civil Service, which he declined at 230. Step down to 170 and keep the road warm.

messages.text: Khan, done: Optics for Education. I send Education now, today, on your word, so you start universities sooner. Optics to me the hour it lists. Engineering later, for Guilds or small coin, as you say.
messages.thought: Education is spreading (Willem and Monte hold it now); lock the Khan to my table before they resell it. Send now on trust, he has kept every deal; Optics in 2 days is worth more than his gold. Engineering later for Guilds.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Civil Service is on my desk, but the scribes cannot hand it over until tomorrow. It goes to you tomorrow, first thing. Printing Press to me when yours lists, as agreed.
messages.thought: The game will not let me pass a book on the same day I received it; CS goes to him tomorrow T104. Do not name Willem as the source.

messages.text: Willem, signed and done. Thank you for the eyes on the Khan; keep them open. Engineering pours in about nine days. Guilds for it, one for one, if yours lists by then.
messages.thought: Swap done cleanly. Keep him as my eyes on the Khan; Engineering ~9 days for Guilds.

messages.text: Sun, understood. I need Optics little, but I will not refuse it. The day it lists, I pay thirty gold. Or, if you prefer a craft, my Printing Press for your Optics, book for book, in about nine days. Your pick; you are first at my door either way.
messages.thought: Optics costs me 480 beakers but he needs gold; 30g is a fine price for a spare craft, and the Press swap is my fallback. He holds Civil Service already but Peter hands it free tomorrow, so I do not show interest.

messages.text: Peter. Education received, thanks. Optics is yours the hour it lists, tomorrow. Engineering later for Guilds, as agreed.
messages.thought: He sent Education first on my word; Optics lists tomorrow and I must hand it over the hour it lists. Keeps him warm, Engineering later is cheap.

messages.text: Bull. A change, told early: Education came to me from another hand today. My Optics lists tomorrow. If you still want it, name gold: it is worth a hundred. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: I got Education from Peter already, so book-for-book with Bull is void; I tell him first, honestly, and offer Optics for gold since he needs it for Monte's old deal.

messages.text: Bull, the craft. Printing Press for Optics, book for book, the same hour. Optics lists in two days; I hold it until your press pours, about nine days, and I knock. The Sun keeps this one.
messages.thought: Printing Press is worth far more than 30 gold and I need it anyway; the swap is the better deal. Waiting 9 days to hand over Optics costs me little; other buyers (Genghis, Willem) can pay gold meanwhile.

messages.text: Peter, agreed: Guilds for Engineering, one for one, the hour both are listed. Guilds comes in about six days. I keep my eyes on the Khan.
messages.thought: Fair swap partner; Guilds lists in ~6 turns, Engineering ~9. Confirm so the same-hour swap happens. Reveal nothing on the Khan beyond what I see.

messages.text: Agreed, Sun: Printing Press for Optics, book for book, the same hour. Knock when my press pours, about nine days.
messages.thought: Free tech swap in 9 days instead of 30 gold now: fine, I lose nothing, and he gets nothing from me until the Press pours.

messages.text: Genghis, a hundred for Optics is too dear for me; my book swap with the Sun stands. In about seven days my Printing Press lists, a craft nobody else walks. If you want it, you are among the first at my door, and the price is the one you set on crafts: near a hundred. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He wants 100 for Optics; I have a free swap with Montezuma for it, so I need none. His Education came from another hand, so his gold is the only thing left to harvest: the Press is my product for him.

messages.text: Peter, Civil Service has reached me, thank you. Printing Press goes to you the hour it lists, about seven days. My word stands.
messages.thought: He kept his word and gave CS first; I must keep mine on PP in 7 turns. Say thanks, no new ask.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, good. Your word has always been good. One thing, neighbour to neighbour: your settler stands on the hill two tiles from Polynesian. A city there chokes mine and yours both. There is open land elsewhere; I would take it kindly if he walked on.
messages.thought: He keeps his word; acknowledge it. His settler on the hill by Polynesian will squeeze my city; ask plainly, no threat, he may move it.

messages.text: Bull. Keep your swap with the Sun. Printing Press at a hundred is dear; at thirty-five I take it the hour it lists. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He will not pay a hundred and has the Sun's Optics coming; my Optics is worth little to him. Printing Press at near a hundred is too dear. Anchor low, keep him warm, do not beg.

messages.text: Peter, I hear you. Your friendship is worth more than that hill: my settler turns back and walks to the coast near my own cities, four days lost. A kind word is answered with a kind word; if you wish to ease the walk, send a hundred gold, and I thank you. Printing Press comes to you the hour it lists, about a week.
messages.thought: Hill (15,23) is a poor site, and Peter is my best partner and top scorer; yielding costs little. But a favour deserves a price: he holds 193 gold and I bleed 25 a turn. I also hide that PP may come sooner via Liberalism.

messages.text: Genghis, thirty-five is too little for a craft nobody else walks. But tomorrow I have another for you: Civil Service, which you lack. Seventy gold, tomorrow, the hour it can be traded. Printing Press in about a week, eighty. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He lowballs 35 for PP; I have another sellable craft he lacks: Civil Service (not tradeable until tomorrow). He holds 177 gold; I need gold. Anchor high, expect ~55%.

messages.text: Willem, no craft on my table today. In about a week Printing Press lists, which nobody else walks. One hundred gold, and you are among the first at my door. Peace and open roads stand.
messages.thought: Willem has 164 gold and lacks nothing now; PP in a week is the next thing I can sell him. Plant the price early; he haggles to ~60%.

messages.text: Bull. Civil Service: I walk it myself in five days, so forty is its price to me. Forty tomorrow, the hour it trades, and Printing Press at thirty-five still stands. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Civil Service costs me five turns of research, worth about forty gold; seventy is dear. Counter low, keep him warm, he already dropped Printing Press from 100 to 80 in a day.

messages.text: Bull, thank you for the notice. Printing Press is a quiet craft; seventy gold, paid the hour it lists, as with Machinery. If it must be eighty, say so then. Peace and roads stand on my side.
messages.thought: Printing Press is 1286 beakers (11 turns) for me; 100g is already cheap but he took 60-70 from me before, so open at 70 and settle at 85 at most. Keeps him as a regular seller.

messages.text: Bull. A change, told early: my own scholars finish Printing Press in two days, so I do not need yours. Civil Service at forty still stands the hour it trades. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: My Great Scientist gave me Printing Press nearly done; I no longer need his PP. Telling him early, keeping the CS 40g offer.

messages.text: Genghis, then let us not trade coin for what we both walk. Civil Service for your Printing Press, book for book, the hour your Press lists in two days. If it does not list, forty gold for Civil Service still stands. Ignore the fifty I sent today. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: If his Press really lists in two days, swapping Civil Service for it beats 40 gold: I can pay Peter and Montezuma sooner and use my free tech on something dearer. If he bluffs, I fall back to 40 gold for CS on T107 and lose little.

messages.text: Bull. Civil Service at fifty: signed. Fair dealing. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Fifty is a fair price for four turns of research and keeps him warm; his prices drop daily so he is eager. Nothing more to ask now.

messages.text: Genghis, fifty received, fair dealing. When your Press lists in two days I will buy it at thirty-five, the price you set on it yourself, paid the hour it trades. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He pays fair; his Press lists in 2 days. Buying it at his own price of 35 lets me pay Peter and Montezuma sooner and spend my free tech on something dearer. Cheap for me, no risk.

messages.text: Bull. Plain words: I took your fifty before I read your newer line. An oversight, not a slight. By your own fallback the price was forty; if you hold to it, send ten back. Civil Service is mine, Printing Press I walk myself. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: I accepted his 50g before reading his newer 'ignore the fifty' line; overpaid 10g over his own fallback. Say it plainly, ask the ten back (cheap test of his goodwill), keep him warm; no PP sale needed since he lists his own PP.

messages.text: Genghis, you are right: my own line said forty. Ten gold sent back. Square. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Ten gold is cheap to keep his trust; my own line said forty, and he told me plainly. He walks his Press himself, so no purchase is assured.

messages.text: Khan, Optics received. You keep your word, and I remember it. Engineering pours in about five days; Guilds or a little coin for it, as we said.
messages.thought: He paid Optics the hour it listed: an honest trader, keep him sweet but don't arm him. Engineering later for Guilds or coin.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, thank you for turning him back. A hundred is a king ransom for a walk. Forty gold is yours the day he founds his city by your coast, as a housewarming. Printing Press as agreed.
messages.thought: He charges me for doing what costs him little. 100 is half my purse; a token paid on the deed keeps my nearest neighbour calm and the hill free.

messages.text: Montezuma, Optics at 110 is dear; I have a counter of 60 gold on your table. A fair price keeps the trade going. The peace stands on my side.
messages.thought: Optics at 110 is double what it is worth to me; he has only 54 gold, so he wants to cash in. 60 keeps him a customer while the peace runs down.

messages.text: Peter, your word is kind. My second settler has founded a small town on the iron hill three tiles south of Spiro; the one for the coast lands in two days. The forty is welcome when it does. Printing Press comes to you the hour it lists, three days or so.
messages.thought: Nacogdoches is inland on the iron hill, not the coast; the true coast city (21,19) founds in ~2 turns. Remind him of his 40 gold gently without nagging; keeps him warm and pays a bit.

messages.text: Willem, a middle price: Optics for 80 gold, on your table now. Your 60 stays open until I hear. The peace runs down in five days; I will come to you for a longer one, roads with it, as you said.
messages.thought: Optics costs me nothing more to sell; 60 is his floor, 80 my try; I keep #40 open as fallback and want goodwill for the longer peace plus roads at T110.

messages.text: Montezuma, thank you for coming down. Optics is four days of my own research, so I can wait. Seventy gold is on your table now; at that price I take it today. Of the longer peace, we will speak when the day comes.
messages.thought: Optics is four turns of my own research, so 80 is a courtesy price; 70 keeps him selling and cash-short, and I want him a customer through the lapse.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, good. I see your settler on the coast hill east of Spiro. The forty goes to you the day the town stands. Printing Press when it lists, as agreed.
messages.thought: He is honest so far; his coast settler stands at 21,19, close to Rostov but on his land. Pay the 40 when it founds, as promised; keep him calm until PP arrives.

messages.text: Montezuma, I see my sixty was taken and Optics is mine: the account is closed, nothing more is owed on it, and my 70 and 80 talk was moot. Good trading. When the peace runs down we will speak.
messages.thought: My 60 was taken already; Optics is mine. Close it cleanly so he does not expect 80 or 70, and keep him warm for the peace talk.

messages.text: Willem, Optics already sits in your hands: your 60 gold was taken, deal done. Fair trade, thank you. The peace runs down in four days; I come to you then for a longer one, roads with it.
messages.thought: He already has Optics for 60 (his own counter #40); his 70 message is stale. Keep goodwill for the longer peace plus roads at T110.

messages.text: Peter, my Printing Press is in hand and trades tomorrow. I give it to you the hour it can pass, as promised. My coast town founds at the start of tomorrow's turn; the forty is welcome then.
messages.thought: PP is in my hands; tradeable tomorrow. Paying Peter first keeps my word and my best partner warm; the coast city founds at turn start so his 40 gold is due tomorrow.

messages.text: Sun, my Printing Press is in hand sooner than I said. It trades tomorrow. Press for your Optics, book for book, the same hour: knock tomorrow.
messages.thought: Swap PP for Optics 1:1 tomorrow as agreed; he has 127 gold but I keep my word. Tell him early so he knocks tomorrow.

messages.text: van Oranje Willem, my Printing Press lists tomorrow, earlier than I thought. Eighty gold, paid the hour it trades; you are first at my door.
messages.thought: He offered 70, said say 80 then. Purse 112; ask 80, accept 70 at the table.

messages.text: Khan Genghis, your Printing Press for fifty: signed, fair dealing. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Bought his Press at 50 (dearer than 35 but I save beakers and can spend the free tech on a dearer craft). Keep him warm; no more to ask.

messages.text: Bull. Fifty received, Printing Press is yours. Square. If something about me irks you, say it plain. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He paid my floor-plus price fast; cheap goodwill to keep him buying and to learn why he is Annoyed. Nothing owed.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, good. Tomorrow then: your book to me, my forty to your new town. A fair day for both of us.
messages.thought: He is keeping both ends; pay the 40 when I see the town tomorrow, take PP, and the scientist's target shifts off PP.

messages.text: Bull, good. Press for Optics, book for book, the same hour. I knock tomorrow when it pours.
messages.thought: The swap is agreed both ways; I only confirm so he knows I will knock tomorrow and the Optics stays reserved for him.

messages.text: Bull, eighty is fair and I will pay it the hour Printing Press trades. If you prefer, my Guilds lists in two days: Guilds for Printing Press, one for one, no gold either way. Name your choice; my table is open.
messages.thought: 80 for 1286 beakers is cheap, but a swap for Guilds (lists in 2 days) saves my reserve; either way I get PP. Offer him both; he decides.

messages.text: Bull, your press has poured. Optics for Printing Press, book for book, on your table now.
messages.thought: Keep the swap as agreed.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I see Printing Press can pass now. I put the paper on your table: sign it and the book is mine. Your settler still stands on the coast hill; the forty goes the hour the town stands.
messages.thought: PP is listed now; I put the deal on his table so he only signs. Settler still on 21,19 unfounded: 40g on founding, not before.

messages.text: Sun, the Press already pours today. I sent Printing Press for Optics, book for book: open the table and take it.
messages.thought: PP already lists today; pouring early shows good faith and gets me Optics a day sooner. He keeps swaps.

messages.text: Willem, I choose the book: Printing Press for your Guilds, one for one, the hour yours lists in two days. If it slips past three days, eighty gold stands instead. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Guilds resells to three buyers and saves me four turns of beakers; better than 80 gold. Fallback to gold if it slips. Gold is tight but Peter's forty and Nationalism sales cover it.

messages.text: Bull, agreed: Printing Press for Guilds, one for one, the hour my Guilds lists. I expect it within a day or two and will call you the same hour. Peace and roads stand on my side.
messages.thought: Swap saves me 80 gold and Guilds is already on the way; PP lists for me tomorrow anyway. Keep him warm, no new promise beyond the swap.

messages.text: Bull, the Press is on my table, the Optics on yours. Clean trade. The Sun comes to your door for the next craft.
messages.thought: Swap done; Press is mine. Keep him warm as a seller and buyer of the next craft, no further promise needed.

messages.text: Peter, Printing Press is yours, signed. The town stands now on the coast hill east of Spiro: I name it Nanih Waiya. The forty is welcome. A fair day for both.
messages.thought: PP owed for the CS he gave; paid at once. The town stands now, so his forty is due; he keeps his word.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, the book is in my hands and forty gold is in yours. Good luck to Nanih Waiya. You keep your word; so do I.
messages.thought: He kept both ends; I keep mine. 40 paid. A cheap price for a quiet border near Rostov.

messages.text: Peter, my Guilds is listed. On your table: Guilds for Engineering and Printing Press. If that is too much, Guilds for Engineering alone stands as agreed; say so and I will send it the same hour.
messages.thought: Ask for Engineering plus PP is a stretch but costs nothing; fall back to 1-for-1.

messages.text: Bull, my Guilds is listed. The swap is on your table now: Guilds for Printing Press, one for one. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Keeping the agreed swap; same hour as promised.

messages.text: Montezuma, Guilds is mine since today, the craft of the Knight. One hundred fifty gold on your table; I know your purse is full. The peace stands on my side.
messages.thought: He has 160 gold; Guilds gives him Knights but my hills+walls hold; the gold buys me Knights and Musketmen. Peace lapses in 2 days; trading keeps him warm.

messages.text: Willem, we shook on one for one: my Engineering for your Guilds, and that paper is on your table. Printing Press is a second book; it is yours for fifty gold, also on your table. Sign either or both.
messages.thought: He asks two books for one; we agreed 1:1. Hold him to it, sell PP separately for coin before the others resell it to him.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, you were first to Liberalism; well run. I have Engineering fresh from the forge: pikemen, castles, faster roads. Book for book, on your table now.
messages.thought: He beat me to Liberalism; free tech is gone. Buy it with Engineering before anyone else can; Liberalism is worth more, but Engineering is the one book he lacks.

messages.text: Khan, Engineering is ready, as promised. Sixty gold and it is yours; the paper is on your table.
messages.thought: Promised Engineering for small coin. 60 of his 184 is fair; trebuchets for the Khan worry me but he gets it in days anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma, Optics reached me by another road before yours could. Engineering is still yours at a friend price: forty gold. The paper is on your table.
messages.thought: His Optics came too late, I have it already. Keep the friendship: Engineering at a friend price.

messages.text: Peter. Engineering when it lists: forty gold from me the same hour. Guilds I reach in about twelve days; if you still want it then, we talk again. Steppe holds quiet.
messages.thought: I want Engineering cheaply; he is thin on gold and likes crafts, but Guilds is 12 turns off for me, so coin is my honest offer. Keeps the friendship warm.

messages.text: Peter, Astronomy is mine and trades today. I put it on your table for your Guilds and your Engineering, two books for one. If it is too much, tell me which you keep, and Liberalism is also for sale.
messages.thought: He is the top scorer and a friend, but two techs for one is good for me; Liberalism for gold after.

messages.text: Peter, I see your Guilds cannot pass until tomorrow. Today then: my Astronomy for your Engineering and ninety gold, on your table. Tomorrow Guilds for my Liberalism, book for book.
messages.thought: Guilds is not tradeable for him yet (new tech delay). Take Engineering plus gold today; Guilds for Liberalism tomorrow.

messages.text: Willem, Guilds received; a clean swap as always. Printing Press for thirty then, a neighbour price. On your table.
messages.thought: He took the 1:1, declined PP at 50. PP reaches him from others soon; 30 now beats nothing.

messages.text: Khan, meet me halfway: fifty and Engineering is yours today. If forty is your last word, send forty; I will not haggle a friend to the bone.
messages.thought: He bids 40 for Engineering; my 60 is on his table. I said small coin; 40 is acceptable if he holds firm.

messages.text: Willem, your Guilds can pass today. I put Printing Press for Guilds, one for one, on your table. Astronomy is also mine now: a hundred gold, if you want it after.
messages.thought: His Guilds lists now, so the swap can run today and I resell nothing to him yet; Astronomy 100 next since he holds 120.

messages.text: Genghis, two new crafts are mine and pass today: Astronomy and Liberalism. Both for a hundred and fifty gold. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: He holds 184 gold, nothing to give me in tech. Bundle for 150; he haggles to ~60%, accept >=90.

messages.text: Sun, Astronomy and Liberalism are mine and pass today, the next crafts I promised. Both for a hundred and fifty gold, on your table.
messages.thought: He holds 160 gold. Same bundle; accept >=90.

messages.text: Bull, honest word: Peter sold me Printing Press for thirty while we spoke, so I cannot take it from you. Your Astronomy you priced at a hundred; my Guilds is worth that to you. On your table: Guilds for Astronomy, one for one. If you would rather give Liberalism, say so. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: PP came from Peter for 30g, so Bull's swap is moot; Guilds should fetch his Astronomy (his own price 100g, 13 turns of my research). Honest about PP, keep him warm.

messages.text: Peter, Printing Press taken at thirty: signed and received. A clean trade again. I will list my next book to you first.
messages.thought: Thirty is a fair neighbour price; keep the 1-for-1 channel warm, he is score leader and sells honestly.

messages.text: Bull, thank you for the crafts. A hundred and fifty is dear for a purse that also feeds my wonders. Ninety gold, Astronomy and Liberalism both, on your table now.
messages.thought: 150 for both is steep; 40 was my bid for Astronomy alone. Counter at 90 for both, he has fallen on price before

messages.text: Willem, Guilds at a hundred and fifty is a king's price. Fifty gold on your table now, a fair price keeps the trade going. When the peace runs down I come to you for the longer one, roads with it.
messages.thought: Guilds at 150 is robbery; test a fair bid, and keep him warm before the peace talk at T111

messages.text: Peter. Forty gold for Engineering is on your table, my last word and my word kept. Take it and we stay friends. Steppe holds quiet.
messages.thought: He will take forty; 50 is a stretch and my word was forty. Keep it friendly, hold the price.

messages.text: Bull. Astronomy and Liberalism both: a hundred gold, one deal, paid the hour it trades. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Two techs for 150 is cheap vs 2700 beakers, but he drops prices if I wait, and I need gold buffer for the Dutch strike. Counter at 100.

messages.text: Willem, understood about the Press. Guilds for Astronomy, one for one: signed. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Guilds for Astronomy is fair; I need Guilds for Banking.

messages.text: Peter, Engineering for Liberalism: signed, thank you. I find Guilds through another hand, so no more owed either way. Astronomy stays for sale: a hundred gold, if you want it.
messages.thought: Took his Engineering for Liberalism; I now hold Guilds too, so the Guilds swap I floated is moot; Astronomy still for sale.

messages.text: Genghis, a hundred for Astronomy and Liberalism: signed. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: 100 is above my floor.

messages.text: Willem, Liberalism is the last craft I hold that you lack. Ninety gold, paid the hour it trades. On your table.
messages.thought: Willem has 90 gold and lacks Liberalism; he offered it himself. Sell at 90, accept 70.

messages.text: Peter. Forty received on your side, Engineering on mine. Square, and my word kept. Steppe holds quiet.
messages.thought: Engineering is mine for forty; thank him to keep him warm, nothing more owed.

messages.text: Montezuma, I set aside your fifty: Guilds is worth more, and your purse looks thin today. A hundred stands whenever you can pay it. Bull holds Guilds now too, so do not wait long. The peace stands on my side.
messages.thought: His purse fell from 120 to 30 mid-day; 50 was lowball, Guilds not for sale at that. Keep him warm, keep the price, wait for his purse; Bull now owns Guilds too so I should not wait too long.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Liberalism and Astronomy both in my hands, and you have my Engineering and eighty gold. A good day of trade between neighbours. Square.
messages.thought: Got Liberalism and Astronomy from him in one day for Engineering and 80g: a very good day. Keep him sweet; he is Cautious.

messages.text: Khan, forty received, Engineering yours. Square, friend. May the steppe stay quiet.
messages.thought: 40 is what he would pay; keep the Khan pleased and quiet while my east is thin.

messages.text: Willem, my purse is spent on other crafts today. Guilds will wait for me or I take it elsewhere. When the peace runs down we speak of the longer one, roads with it.
messages.thought: Purse is empty today; Bull also sells Guilds so I will shop there first. Keep Willem warm for the longer peace + OB at T111.

messages.text: Peter, square. Good dealing, as always between neighbours.
messages.thought: Square indeed; Peter is the top scorer but pays and keeps word. Keep him Pleased, nothing more to ask today.

messages.text: Bull, thank you for the Astronomy swap. Liberalism at ninety empties my purse with the Sun's peace running down. Sixty gold on your table, paid the hour it trades. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Liberalism is 7 turns of my research; 90 would drain my reserve before Monty's peace lapses. Try 60, keep the 90 as fallback; he is rich so he does not need gold, only a fair deal.

messages.text: Bull, fifty gold for Guilds, on your table now.
messages.thought: Guilds cheap, fifty is my bid

messages.text: Genghis, Guilds is mine to trade and yours to take: fifty gold, paid the hour it trades. On your table.
messages.thought: He has 55 gold; Guilds is cheap to give and gives me coin; accept >=35

messages.text: Willem, Liberalism is yours for sixty: signed. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Took 60, below my 70 floor, but his purse is empty and score is tiny; goodwill is worth more.

messages.text: Sun, Guilds for fifty: signed. The next craft I hold, you hear first.
messages.thought: 50 for Guilds is fair; Guilds is cheap to everyone.

messages.text: Bull, Guilds received, clean trade. When your next craft is ready, name it and a fair price; the Sun pays when the purse is full.
messages.thought: Bull is a cheap, reliable tech seller; keep him warm. No gold now, nothing to buy yet.

messages.text: Bull, Liberalism received, sixty paid: a clean trade. My next book is Gunpowder, in about five days; you are on my list. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Liberalism is already mine for 60 (not in his list any more). Keep him warm; he holds 509 gold, I will sell him Gunpowder when it lists in 5 turns.

messages.text: Khan, Guilds is ready now, not in twelve days. Fifty gold and it is yours today; the paper is on your table.
messages.thought: Everyone has Guilds but him; knights for the Khan worry me, but SB, Willem or Monte will sell it to him within days anyway. Take his gold first: 50 of his 55.

messages.text: Bull. Guilds: thirty-five gold, paid the hour it trades. Peter also offers it at fifty, so the price is falling. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: Guilds from two sellers at 50 each; bid 35 to the richer, Annoyed neighbour first, fall back to 50 if refused

messages.text: Willem, the peace runs down. I put open borders for open borders on your table: roads and caravans for both, and a longer peace after. Take it.
messages.thought: Need OB for the missionary; keep the peace long.

messages.text: Genghis, Guilds for thirty-five: signed. Peace holds on my side.
messages.thought: 35 for Guilds: cheap, but coin is coin and he stays quiet. Keep him Cautious, no more.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Banking comes to me tomorrow. Banks, and the Mercantilism civic. What book do you walk now? Book for book when yours lists, or one hundred fifty gold tomorrow. Your choice.
messages.thought: We are all level now; he is the rich one (509g). Line him up for Banking before anyone else walks it, and learn what he researches.

messages.text: Peter. Guilds reached me elsewhere at thirty-five; your fifty came a day late. Next craft, open at thirty-five and I buy the same hour. Steppe holds quiet.
messages.thought: He was late and dear; a polite note keeps the price falling next time, no gold owed.

messages.text: Willem, the Khan beats his drums at your gate again. Hold your walls. Gunpowder comes to me in about five days; you will have it first, for whatever coin you can spare. Tell me where his stacks march.
messages.thought: The Khan is back on him; if the Dutch fall the Khan sits on Yakutsk's doorstep. Willem must hold and bleed him. Gunpowder to him first is cheap insurance for me; I won't fight for him.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Khan marches on the Dutch again. If he swallows them, your New Sarai is the next meal on his road. Russia watches. Think on it.
messages.thought: Plant the seed: Monte fought the Khan before and borders him. A second front keeps the Khan from eating Willem whole. No promise from me.

messages.text: Khan, your quarrel with the Dutch is your own. Keep the fighting off Russian roads and we stay friends. Guilds can wait.
messages.thought: He is at war with Willem and refused 50 for Guilds; good, I will not arm his knights now. Draw a line around my land, stay friendly.

messages.text: Peter. Understood. My fight is on Dutch ground only; no Russian road is touched. Steppe holds quiet.
messages.thought: He is staying out; a short assurance keeps him a friendly seller of future techs and costs nothing. No Russian tile is in my war plans.

messages.text: Peter, I hear you. New Sarai stands on a hill with thirteen blades; the Khan will break on Dutch walls before he reaches mine. Russia watches, so do I. If Russia moves against him, tell me the day. Gunpowder is mine in seven turns: you hear it first, at a friend's price.
messages.thought: Peter wants me to bleed against the Khan while Russia watches; I will not fight for him. Fine for Khan to break on Rotterdam's walls. Keep Peter warm, hint at my first Gunpowder to sell.

messages.text: Willem, open borders signed: good. Roads and caravans for both of us. We are at peace and I mean to keep it; my traders will come to your gates.
messages.thought: OB is open; my missionary walks to Rotterdam. Keep him calm and trading; peace needs no renewal while no war stands.

messages.text: Montezuma, open borders signed. The Khan broke our ten-day peace the hour it ran out: his army stands at Utrecht, three tiles from your New Sarai. Samarqand and New Sarai were his once; he will want them back. Turfan stands behind him with its garrison at my gate. Strike while he is here. My roads are yours for the march. The peace stands on my side.
messages.thought: I took the roads because a Sun marching on the Khan helps me more than a Sun marching on Rotterdam; Rotterdam is walled, Utrecht is the soft spot. Ask him to hit Turfan.

messages.text: Khan, ten days of peace and you broke it the hour it ran out. Utrecht has walls, a hill and longbows; elephants do not climb walls. Peace is on your table on the old terms, no city, no gold. The Sun's army is three tiles from Turfan while yours stands at my gate. Think what that costs you.
messages.thought: He may crack Utrecht before Gunpowder lands; I need him to hesitate, not to know how thin I am. Offer peace plainly, no gold yet.

messages.text: Peter, thank you for the warning. The Khan declared on me today; his stack (3 elephants, 4 catapults, 4 foot) stands 1 tile north-east of Utrecht. Walls hold. If you can close your roads to him and sell him nothing, I remember it. Gunpowder lists to you first in about four days, as promised.
messages.thought: Peter trades with everyone; he will not fight, but cutting Khan's roads and silver costs him little and me much. Intel on the Khan stack is not a secret I need.

messages.text: Bull, the Khan broke his peace with me today and marches on Utrecht. He holds Nijmegen, two tiles from your hill. If you will close roads to him, his purse and his patience shrink. Gunpowder is still on my list for you in about four days.
messages.thought: Bull has OB with the Khan and a stack at Poverty Point; asking him to cut roads and press Nijmegen costs me nothing and splits the Khan. I keep Nijmegen for myself only if I can; no promise.

messages.text: Willem, the road is open and I walk it in peace. New Sarai stands on its hill with a full guard; any Khan who comes to my gate finds blades, not gold. I do not march on promises. Hold Utrecht: Dutch walls are the best anvil the Sun could ask for.
messages.thought: He wants me to bleed against the Khan. Rotterdam now holds Buddhism - my goal is met there. I march for no one, but keep him hopeful and the Khan busy at Dutch walls.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Banking is listed today, as I said. One hundred fifty gold and it is yours this hour. The paper is on your table.
messages.thought: He is rich and will get Banking from others within a day; take 150 now.
