messages.text: Montezuma, Banking is fresh today. Forty-five gold, a friend price; on your table now. Your Gunpowder: tell me the day it lists.
messages.thought: Friend price keeps him close; he is my likely second front.

messages.text: Willem, Banking listed today. Twenty gold, a war-time price; on your table. Gunpowder still comes to you first.
messages.thought: Small coin from a man at war; keeps him friendly. Banking is no war book.

messages.text: Khan, a new craft, opened the same hour as you asked: Banking for thirty gold. On your table.
messages.thought: He asked for 35 and the same hour; 30 drains his war chest and gives him nothing for the field.

messages.text: Willem. Peace costs Utrecht. Hand it over and the Steppe stops; the offer is on your table.
messages.thought: He wants peace badly; Utrecht is my target and the army is at his gate. If he cedes it I save the siege; if not, I take it anyway.

messages.text: Peter, Banking for forty-five gold: on your table now. Gunpowder lists in about six turns, around turn 118; you hear it first.
messages.thought: Banking at 45 is cheap and saves 6 turns of beakers; keep Peter warm, Gunpowder promise stands.

messages.text: Peter. Thirty for Banking, taken the same hour as promised. Steppe holds quiet.
messages.thought: He kept to my terms; paying keeps my word and a good seller.

messages.text: Peter, Banking received, clean trade. Gunpowder lists around turn 118: you hear it first, at a friend price.
messages.thought: Banking in hand for 45; keep Peter warm and keep the Gunpowder promise cheap to keep. Say nothing of the Palace.

messages.text: Peter, mine lists in three days, so I need not wait for yours. The Khan's stack still stands one tile from Utrecht, not yet struck. Walls and pikes are going up. My Gunpowder is yours at the hour it lists, for coin or for your next book, one for one. Your roads closed to the Khan would be remembered.
messages.thought: He wants to sell me Gunpowder in 5 days; mine lists in 3. I promised him mine first, so I turn that into a coin sale and keep the Khan stack facts minimal.

messages.text: Peter, I see Banking on your list already. My Gunpowder pours tomorrow: Gunpowder for Banking, book for book, the hour it lists. After that I walk Scientific Method. Which road do you take, so we do not walk the same one twice?
messages.thought: Banking is already on his list; swapping Gunpowder for it tomorrow saves me ~560 beakers, better than his 150g. Split research roads so we do not duplicate.

messages.text: Willem, I will not arm the Khan against you: Gunpowder does not go to him from me for now. Roads I keep open to all while I am at peace with all. My Gunpowder pours tomorrow; for you thirty-five gold, if you want it before your own.
messages.thought: Closing roads to Genghis costs me a customer and gains nothing; but denying him Gunpowder a while is free and costs me little (his purse is empty). Sell Willem Gunpowder cheap tomorrow.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed: your Gunpowder for my Banking, book for book, the hour it lists tomorrow. You walk Scientific Method; I walk Economics. Then we swap again.
messages.thought: His Gunpowder lists tomorrow, before mine: my Gunpowder is worthless to sell. Take his for Banking and walk Economics so we don't duplicate.

messages.text: Bull, thank you for refusing the Khan. Yes: your Gunpowder at thirty-five, paid the hour it trades. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: 35g for Gunpowder saves me two turns of defence; take it, drop the Peter-first promise honestly.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Banking for your Gunpowder, book for book: the paper is on your table now. Forget my 150 gold offer. I walk Economics, lists in about three days.
messages.thought: He keeps deals; swap as agreed. Economics will be mine to sell him later.

messages.text: Montezuma, clean trade indeed. My vote in your Palace went to you. Tell me the day your Gunpowder lists.
messages.thought: Friendly and honest; my vote for him in the Palace costs nothing and buys goodwill. His Gunpowder will be worthless to me by T118, but I keep him warm.

messages.text: Willem, good: pikes and walls. Gunpowder reaches me another way, so keep your coin for soldiers. Banking still waits on your table at twenty. The Khan buys no war book from Russia. Tell me if his stack moves.
messages.thought: He is weak and poor; keep him holding. I keep OB with the Khan; no war books to him is the real help. His Gunpowder is worthless to me now.

messages.text: Bull, thank you again for refusing the Khan. My purse went to Peter's Banking today and my own Gunpowder lists in two days, so I will not take yours at thirty-five. The offer was fair. Peace and roads stand.
messages.thought: Banking at 20 is a better use of my gold than buying 2 days of Gunpowder; my sunk beakers might be wasted if I buy. Keep Bull warm, decline politely.

messages.text: Peter, Banking taken at twenty: signed and received. My Gunpowder lists in two days, three before yours. A hundred gold on your table the hour it trades, or your next book one for one. The Khan's stack is still at my wall, unmoved.
messages.thought: Banking bought at 20, good. Now sell him Gunpowder, he has 316 gold. Ask 100; accept 70+. Keep Khan stack info vague.

messages.text: Khan. Utrecht is not for sale. My pikes are answer enough to elephants, and my Gunpowder lists in two days. Your army has stood at my wall for three turns while Turfan stands open. Peace on the old terms remains on my table.
messages.thought: He wants Utrecht; I will not give it. Make him hesitate and keep the peace door open on old terms, no gold.

messages.text: Peter, thank you for the vote. Gunpowder lists in four turns, around turn 117. You hear it first, at a friend's price.
messages.thought: He wants the date; four turns left, so T117. Keep him warm, hear-first promise stands. Say nothing of the Palace or that Bull offered Gunpowder to me.

messages.text: Willem, Gunpowder is already in my hands, from another road. Keep your hundred for muskets. When Economics lists in three days, you get a war-time price. Hold Utrecht.
messages.thought: He missed that I already have Gunpowder. Nothing to buy; keep him warm and holding. Economics can go to him cheap when it lists.

messages.text: Peter, Banking received, thank you; Gunpowder is yours, square. One change: I walk Nationalism (five days) before Scientific Method, since it is the shorter road. When your Economics lists, Nationalism for Economics, book for book, the same hour. Tell me if you walk Nationalism yourself.
messages.thought: Nationalism is cheaper (1447 vs 1929), starts the Democracy road (Universal Suffrage unlocks gold hurry), and swaps 1:1 with his Economics sooner. Tell him honestly.

messages.text: Peter, understood: coin stays for muskets. Economics at a war-time price, taken the hour it lists. The Khan's stack still stands at Utrecht's wall, unmoved. Walls hold.
messages.thought: He keeps handing me cheap tech at war prices; stay warm, hold my coin for Economics at ~20-30, and give only the vague fact that the Khan stack has not moved.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed. I do not walk Nationalism; it is yours. Economics lists in two days: I send it that hour, on trust, and your Nationalism comes to me the hour it lists. After Economics I walk Chemistry.
messages.thought: He keeps every deal; sending Economics first on trust locks him on my book before others resell it. I won't walk Nationalism.

messages.text: Montezuma, Gunpowder reached me already by another road; keep yours for your own walls. Economics lists in two days: forty gold, a friend price, yours that hour if you want it.
messages.thought: His Gunpowder is worthless to me; tell him plainly so he does not count on my coin, and sell him Economics at a friend price instead.

messages.text: Peter, so be it: keep Gunpowder, mine is for my own walls. Economics at forty gold: yes. Name the hour it lists and the Sun pays that same turn.
messages.thought: His Gunpowder came from elsewhere (Bull likely), so my hear-first promise is void and costs me nothing. Economics at 40 saves 13 turns of research; accept, keep him warm, he holds 341 gold and a vote for me.

messages.text: Montezuma, good. Economics lists tomorrow. The paper is on your table that same hour: forty gold.
messages.thought: Honest payer; 40g is fair from him. Economics lists next turn; I put the paper on his table that hour, alongside the others, and don't name them.

messages.text: Willem. Your pikes held, I will say it plainly. Peace, and Gunpowder with it, plus the gold you can spare. Utrecht stays yours. Offer is on your table.
messages.thought: Siege is failing and he now has Gunpowder; I can't take Utrecht. His Gunpowder in exchange for peace is a free win and frees my army for Monte.

messages.text: Peter, tomorrow then. The forty gold waits in my purse; the Sun pays the hour it lists.
messages.thought: He confirms Economics tomorrow at 40; nothing to do today but keep the purse ready and stay warm

messages.text: Khan. Peace for Gunpowder, one for one: sent on your table. My coin stays; it buys the muskets that guard Utrecht, and you do not need it. Take the book and march your stack home. If you want your own terms (#54), they stand until tomorrow.
messages.thought: Peace plus pulling his stack off Utrecht is worth Gunpowder; I try to keep my 23 gold and fall back on his own #54 if he balks. He broke peace at expiry once, so this buys ten turns, not safety.

messages.text: Peter, agreed and written down: you send Economics the hour it lists; my Nationalism follows the same hour it lists to me, about four days. You walk Chemistry, I walk Nationalism then Scientific Method. No duplicate roads.
messages.thought: He sends Economics on trust, I owe Nationalism the hour it lists; cheap to confirm, keeps my record clean and keeps him walking Chemistry while I walk the Democracy road.

messages.text: Peter, Economics lists: forty gold sent, as promised. The Sun pays.
messages.thought: Keeping my promise: paying the hour it lists

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Economics is in your hands, as promised, on trust. Nationalism to me the hour it lists.
messages.thought: Kept my side first; now his Nationalism is owed ~T119.

messages.text: Montezuma, Economics is on your table this hour: forty gold, as agreed.
messages.thought: Promise kept on time; he pays.

messages.text: Willem, Economics at twenty, the war-time price I promised. On your table. Hold the wall.
messages.thought: Cheap price keeps him friendly and solvent for muskets.

messages.text: Khan, a new craft: Economics, forty gold, on your table this hour.
messages.thought: Not a war book; his gold drains his war chest. He promised to buy at 35 same hour; ask 40.

messages.text: Peter, Economics received, forty gold paid. Clean trade again. When my Gunpowder-era craft after Nationalism lists, you hear it first.
messages.thought: Economics bought clean; keep him warm, he is my AP voter and tech seller. Don't reveal Palace plan.

messages.text: Khan, thirty-five it is. Done. I see you made peace with the Dutch: good for trade.
messages.thought: 35 was his standing price; fine. Peace with Willem means his stack is free again; watch my east.

messages.text: Peter, Economics taken at twenty, thank you. The Khan took peace and his stack is leaving Utrecht. Nationalism is my next book; you hear first when it lists.
messages.thought: Economics for 20g is a bargain and keeps Peter warm; he has 425g I want for my next book, so I tell him the Khan siege is over without dwelling on the price.

messages.text: Khan. Your elephants stand two steps from my walls and your war paper reached me today. I did not seek it. Peace is still on your table; my walls hold, and the Sun answers every blow. Name your price, or come and count the dead.
messages.thought: He declared war the turn after his peace with Willem; elephants at the fort 2 tiles from Texcoco. I want time to field musketmen; peace costs me nothing now. Don't show weakness.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Khan marches on you. Russia gives him no soldiers and no alliance in this. Chemistry lists in four days: forty gold, the hour it lists, if you want it. Hold your walls.
messages.thought: The Khan's fist goes east, onto my best payer: good for me if it bleeds him there. Keep Monte buying and friendly; promise nothing military, no word on who else buys.

messages.text: Willem, good that Utrecht stands. The Khan has turned his army east onto Montezuma. Your treaty binds you about ten days; after that, Nijmegen and Ning-hsia may stand thin while his men are far away. Your call, not mine. Muskets first.
messages.thought: A second front bleeds the Khan from both sides and I never fight. If Willem retakes Nijmegen, the Khan is weaker on my east. He may leak it; it is phrased as an observation.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Nationalism stands as agreed. Next: my Chemistry lists in four days. I send it that hour, book for book, against your Scientific Method when it lists. After Chemistry I walk Replaceable Parts. Agreed?
messages.thought: He keeps every deal; lock my next two books against his so neither wastes beakers. Chemistry for his Sci Method 1:1, on trust again, and tell him Replaceable Parts is mine.

messages.text: Peter. The Steppe is at war with Montezuma; my elephants march on his eastern cities. Declare on him too and the plunder is shared by the road each of us takes. Twenty gold on your table as earnest.
messages.thought: Peter is rich (431g) and neutral; he probably refuses, but a Russian war on Monte would split Monte's attention. Costs nothing.

messages.text: Peter, thanks for the word. Chemistry at forty gold: yes. Name the day it lists and the Sun pays that same turn. My walls hold.
messages.thought: Chemistry cheap at 40 and he refuses the Khan: keep him warm; gold is low but I will have ~100 by T121. Keep it short.

messages.text: Montezuma. The Khan has declared on you, and he is no friend of mine: his stack stood at my wall for six turns. Turfan lies three tiles from your axemen, and it is thinly held. Take it before he arms it with my old gunpowder. My roads stay open to you, as agreed.
messages.thought: Khan at war with Monty keeps the Sun's stack busy and off Rotterdam; feed that fire, promise nothing real.

messages.text: Bull. The Khan is at war with Montezuma now, and his army that stood at my wall has gone elsewhere. Peace and roads stand with me. My next book is Nationalism, about seven days out; you hear of it when it lists.
messages.thought: Bull holds 400g+ and I have nothing to sell; keep him warm so Nationalism sells later, and note whether he moves on Khan.

messages.text: Willem. My rider stands beside Turfan: archer, two axemen, crossbow, three swords, three catapults, three warriors inside. That is not thin. I hold my walls and let the Khan's elephants break on pikes. If you march from Utrecht, the Sun marches the day after you stand at the wall. Keep the roads open.
messages.thought: He wants me to bleed on Turfan for him; my chariot saw 13 units inside, not thin. Keep him friendly (OB, Rotterdam Buddhist), commit to nothing, and tell him the truth since it costs me nothing.

messages.text: Peter, thank you for Economics. Nationalism is yours the hour it lists: one day. After it I walk Constitution before Scientific Method. When your Chemistry lists, Constitution for Chemistry, book for book, same hour. Tell me if you walk Constitution yourself, so we do not walk the same road twice.
messages.thought: He trusts me with Economics; Nationalism lists next turn and I give it that hour. I shift my road to Constitution/Democracy; telling him only Constitution, not why (gold hurry). I also want a Chemistry swap later.

messages.text: Khan, Russia stays out of your quarrel with the Sun, as it stayed out of the Dutch one. Trade with me, yes; war for twenty gold, no. My roads stay open.
messages.thought: Twenty gold to make an enemy of my best payer and tie myself to his war: no. Keep him Pleased, keep Russia out.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed: Chemistry for Constitution, book for book. I do not walk Constitution. Chemistry lists in three days and goes to you that hour; Constitution to me the hour it lists. Then I walk Replaceable Parts.
messages.thought: Fair, and it keeps us on different roads. Chemistry lists before his Constitution, so I send first on trust again; he has kept every deal.

messages.text: Montezuma. Twelve men inside Turfan is not thin, I agree; I march nowhere while the treaty stands. Hold your walls and let the elephants come to your pikes. My roads stay open to you. When my guns are ready I will tell you the day, and you will tell me yours.
messages.thought: Turfan holds a dozen units, so a march now would bleed me for nothing; but a Sun who fights the Khan at his own walls is my best shield. Keep him fighting, promise nothing dated.

messages.text: Peter, thank you. Muskets stand at Utrecht, and the treaty is a treaty until it ends. I count the days as you do. Nationalism lists in six; you hear first, as promised.
messages.thought: Peter pushes me onto the Khan to bleed a rival; I have no army yet, so thank him, promise only Nationalism first, and tell him nothing of my plan.

messages.text: Peter, agreed. Chemistry comes to me the hour it lists; Constitution goes to you the hour it lists to me, about a week. Nationalism is yours tomorrow, the hour it lists. Walk Replaceable Parts; I take Scientific Method after Constitution.
messages.thought: He accepts Chemistry for Constitution; Chemistry will arrive before my Constitution, so I owe on trust again - fine, he keeps his word. Nationalism goes tomorrow.

messages.text: Willem. Seven elephants, a swordsman and a trebuchet stand at my south wall now. They come to my pikes, not yours. Keep your roads open; when your guns stand at a Mongol wall, send the day and the Sun answers.
messages.thought: He will not march while his peace with the Khan stands; he wants me to bleed first. Fine: I commit to nothing, keep OB, and let him know the elephants sit at my wall so he knows the price of waiting.

messages.text: Peter, Nationalism is in your hands, as promised. Chemistry to me the hour it lists; Constitution to you the hour it lists to me.
messages.thought: Paying my debt on time keeps his trust.

messages.text: Montezuma. Let the elephants die on your pikes; every one that falls there will not stand at my wall. My roads stay open. Send me word the day the stack turns or breaks. When my guns are ready, you will have the day.
messages.thought: Khan's stack is stuck on Monty's pikes, which is exactly where I want it; feed his resolve, promise no date, and ask him to tell me the moment the elephants leave.

messages.text: Montezuma, Nationalism is on your table now: thirty-five gold. It lets you draft muskets. Chemistry lists tomorrow at forty, as agreed.
messages.thought: He lacks Nationalism and is at war; draft muskets help him hold the Khan off. Cheap price keeps him paying. Silent on his Palace vote: I abstained, he loses nothing by not hearing it.

messages.text: Willem, Nationalism is on your table at fifteen gold. Save your four days for something else. Chemistry lists tomorrow at twenty, if you want it.
messages.thought: He walks Nationalism, 4 days left; cheap sale saves his beakers for muskets and keeps him Pleased. Willem promised first word of his book; I beat him to it.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, news: a great scientist of mine opened Scientific Method. It lists in three days. Do not walk it. Walk another road after Constitution, and I trade Scientific Method for that book, book for book. Chemistry comes to you tomorrow, as agreed.
messages.thought: My scientist put 1183 into Sci Method; it lists T123. Tell him now so he does not waste beakers, and lock a new 1:1 swap. Keep Chemistry-Constitution as agreed.

messages.text: Peter, good news, and thank you. Chemistry tomorrow, Constitution to you that same hour. After Constitution I walk Democracy (Constitution and Printing Press, about ten days), not Scientific Method. Do not walk Democracy yourself: when it lists I trade it to you for Scientific Method, book for book, that hour. Send your book when it lists, on trust if you like, as with Economics; my Democracy follows the hour it lists to me.
messages.thought: Democracy is my road to the gold hurry, and he will get it too, but he cannot beat me to it if he agrees not to walk it; his book first on trust costs me nothing and I pay the hour mine lists. His 989 gold is a worry for later.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed: Scientific Method goes to you the hour it lists, in three days, on trust. Democracy to me the hour it lists. I do not walk Democracy. Chemistry tomorrow, as agreed.
messages.thought: Democracy (2251 for me) for Sci Method (1929): good for me; Universal Suffrage lets gold buy buildings. He keeps every deal; sending first locks him to my book. I won't walk Democracy.

messages.text: Peter. Nationalism taken at fifteen, thank you; it saved me six days of beakers. Send Chemistry when it lists, twenty is fair and I will take it the same hour.
messages.thought: Cheap techs from the score leader keep me current; I commit to Chemistry tomorrow and reveal nothing of my plans.

messages.text: Peter, agreed and written down. Chemistry tomorrow, Scientific Method in three days, on trust. Constitution to you the hour it lists to me; Democracy the hour after it lists. I walk no other road.
messages.thought: He agreed everything and sends Scientific Method on trust; I keep my side exactly: Constitution when it lists, Democracy when it lists. Nothing more to ask.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Chemistry is in your hands. Scientific Method in two days, as agreed. Constitution to me the hour it lists.
messages.thought: He keeps every deal; Chemistry sent on trust, Constitution and Democracy owed. Keep the ledger clean.

messages.text: Montezuma, Chemistry has listed: forty gold, on your table now, as agreed. Nationalism still waits for you if you want muskets by draft.
messages.thought: My best payer, at war; Chemistry at the agreed forty, and a softer Nationalism price to get it sold.

messages.text: Khan, Chemistry has listed. Forty gold, on your table now.
messages.thought: Non-war book; his gold off his war chest, and he would buy it elsewhere in days anyway.

messages.text: Willem, Chemistry is yours. Twenty taken, thank you. Good sailing.
messages.thought: Small payer, buffer against the Khan; keep him Pleased.

messages.text: Peter, Chemistry received, thank you. Constitution goes to you the hour it lists to me, about four days. Scientific Method in two days, as agreed.
messages.thought: He keeps his side exactly; I keep mine: Constitution and Democracy the same hour they list. Short thanks, nothing new to ask.

messages.text: Peter. Chemistry received, thank you. Military Tradition is my next book, about seven days out; you hear first.
messages.thought: Chemistry done; keep the cheap-book channel warm, promise him Military Tradition first to keep his prices low, reveal nothing about targets.

messages.text: Khan, twenty-five is too little for Nationalism. Seventy-five gold and it is yours the same hour. Say your number if you disagree.
messages.thought: 25 is a beggar's price; he has 105. Nationalism lets him build Taj Mahal/Hermitage, so it must cost real gold. Accept >=50.

messages.text: Willem, Military Tradition: noted, I listen when it lists. News from the east: the Khan took Teotihuacan and made peace with Montezuma. His elephants are idle again. Your treaty runs out in a few days. Keep the muskets on the walls.
messages.thought: Khan took Teotihuacan and made peace with Monte T120; he is free again and Willem is his habit. A warning costs nothing and keeps my buffer awake. No word to SB on this: if the Khan looks his way, that's not my loss.

messages.text: Peter. Thank you for the news. If the elephants are idle, I would like to know which way they face; your eyes in his land are better than mine. Muskets stand on my walls. Military Tradition lists in six days and you hear first, as promised.
messages.thought: He feeds me news that keeps the Khan's army visible; useful. Khan free of Monty means his stack may turn on me at T126. Ask him where it stands, promise nothing new, remind MT price talk.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Forty for Nationalism; Peter and the Dutch hold it too. Offer is on your table.
messages.thought: He will take about 50; my floor is 40, I want Nationalism cheap and all AIs have it so he has no monopoly.

messages.text: Willem, honest answer: today my eyes see none of his army. Nothing near my eastern border, nothing on the road past Nijmegen. My scout sits in Montezuma's capital; I send it west through the Khan's land now. What it sees, you hear.
messages.thought: Honest: I see no Khan units at all right now. Sending my scout west through his land gives me intel too; sharing it keeps Willem awake as my buffer. Promise only to report what I see.

messages.text: Peter. Nationalism and Chemistry received, seventy-five gold paid. Clean trades. My next craft, Military Tradition, lists in about eighteen days; you hear it first.
messages.thought: Peter is Pleased and has 951 gold; he is the buyer for my next original tech, and a friend vote for the Palace. Keep the hear-first promise cheap.

messages.text: Willem. I took peace with the Khan after he took my town; ten days of treaty. His elephants sit hurt inside Teotihuacan. If he marches on you or me, you will hear the day. Keep the roads open.
messages.thought: He wants to be told when the Khan stack breaks; costs me nothing, keeps OB and the missionary road open. No pledge.

messages.text: Khan, forty it is. Nationalism is yours; square.
messages.thought: 40 is his ceiling (purse 75); better than nothing and he could buy from Peter. Nationalism gives him wonders but he is slow; gold is hammers for me.

messages.text: Peter. Thank you. When your scout passes Turfan, Karakorum or the road to Tabriz, tell me what stands inside and which way it faces. Military Tradition lists in six days; you hear first.
messages.thought: Useful: his eyes in Khan land cost me nothing. Ask for what his scout sees at Turfan and Karakorum (garrisons), reveal no target. Keep MT-first promise warm.

messages.text: Montezuma. Good: peace with the Khan keeps your walls and mine quiet for ten days. If his elephants leave Teotihuacan, tell me which road they take. My roads stay open to you.
messages.thought: Peace with Khan frees both his stack and my Monty-front; keep him friendly, ask for warning and garrisons, promise nothing new.

messages.text: Peter, Scientific Method now lists for you. Send it as agreed; Constitution comes to you the hour it lists to me, in two days.
messages.thought: He promised SciMeth on trust T123; list shows it available. Remind politely.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Scientific Method is in your hands, as agreed. Constitution to me the hour it lists, Democracy after. Good work, neighbour.
messages.thought: Trust-first worked every time with him; Sci Method sent, Constitution (~T125) and Democracy (~T130) owed.

messages.text: Montezuma, Scientific Method has listed. Forty gold, on your table now. Clean trades suit me too.
messages.thought: Best payer; 40g as usual. His Military Tradition at T140 is late; Willem's comes sooner, I will likely buy it there.

messages.text: Khan, Scientific Method has listed. Thirty-five gold, on your table now.
messages.thought: Non-war book; his gold off his war chest, he would buy it elsewhere anyway. Keep him Pleased and busy.

messages.text: Willem, Scientific Method is on your table at twenty. My scout walks west through the Khan land now; in two or three days I tell you what stands in Turfan and Karakorum.
messages.thought: Buffer vs the Khan; scout not there yet (~T125). Keep him trading and on guard.

messages.text: Peter. Scientific Method taken at twenty, thank you. Military Tradition lists in five days; you hear first, as promised.
messages.thought: Scientific Method for 20g saved ~6t of beakers; he sells cheap in war-time. Keep him warm; MT price to be raised when it lists (he holds 980g).

messages.text: Peter, Scientific Method received, thank you. Constitution goes to you the hour it lists to me, in two days. Democracy follows the same hour.
messages.thought: SciMeth in hand, trust kept on both sides; keep him warm, Constitution owed T125 same hour, Democracy ~T133 same hour.

messages.text: Peter. Scientific Method received, forty gold paid. Clean trades. Military Tradition still comes to you first, about sixteen days.
messages.thought: Clean cheap tech from the score leader; keep him Pleased for the Palace vote. Military Tradition promise stands.

messages.text: Peter, Constitution is in your hands, as promised. Democracy follows the hour it lists, about a week.
messages.thought: Promise kept: Constitution same hour. Democracy next ~T132.

messages.text: Willem, my scout report, as promised. Beshbalik: one archer, three warriors, a missionary. Turfan: one crossbowman, one archer, three warriors. Karakorum: one swordsman, two warriors. No elephants, no catapults, no stack on the roads between. His army is not in the east. Tomorrow the scout walks the road to Tabriz. I see New Sarai flies your flag now. Good trade.
messages.thought: Honest report: the Khan's eastern cities hold only antiques, no elephants or siege. If Willem takes heart and hits the Khan after his treaty, the Khan bleeds far from me. Tabriz road still unseen; his army may stand west, near Nijmegen and me.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Khan marches on you again, I hear. My scout walked his eastern land these two days. Beshbalik: one archer, three warriors. Turfan: one crossbowman, one archer, three warriors. Karakorum: one swordsman, two warriors. No elephants, no catapults in those three. His army stands elsewhere. Use it as you like.
messages.thought: The Khan is on Monte again. My best payer must stand, and a long even war far east keeps the Khan off me. Honest scout facts only; words, not soldiers.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Constitution received. Your word is good as iron. Democracy when it lists; I do not walk it.
messages.thought: He kept his word again: Constitution on time. Keep him sweet and swapping until I decide on him around T135.

messages.text: Montezuma. New Sarai came under my flag by the pull of its people, not by my sword. I marched on no one and I want no war with the Sun. Your four men inside may leave in their own time. The Khan's stack (two musketmen, maceman, three swordsmen, three catapults) stands two tiles from its gate; if it turns toward Samarqand you hear the day from me. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: New Sarai flipped to me by culture; he may want it back and has men inside it. Keep him calm, keep the Khan threat pointed outward, give no ground.

messages.text: Peter. New Sarai (the former Aztec town east of me) came to my flag by culture. The Khan's stack, eleven men and three catapults, stands two tiles from it, and my treaty ends within a day. Military Tradition lists in three days and you hear first, as promised. A Russian sword turned on the Khan when he strikes me would be worth more than gold to me; think on what you would want for it.
messages.thought: Khan treaty ends tomorrow and his 11-unit stack with 3 catapults sits at New Sarai's door. Peter wants the Khan bled; try to turn MT into a war request. No hard promise beyond the one I already made.

messages.text: Peter. Thank you, the report is worth more than a book. Since your scout passed, the Khan has declared on the Sun again and his army of eleven, catapults with it, stands on Aztec soil three tiles east of Turfan. So the east of Mongolia is as thin as you saw it. Military Tradition lists in two days and you hear first, as promised. Walk the road to Tabriz and tell me what stands there.
messages.thought: Report was honest and free; keep him warm. Khan re-declared on Monty, his stack left for Aztec soil, so Turfan is thin but I cannot exploit it yet (no guns, no catapults near). Give nothing about targets; MT still 2t, first to him.

messages.text: Peter, Replaceable Parts: I would buy it for 120 gold, paid the hour it trades. Democracy still goes to you the hour it lists to me, about six days. Say your number if 120 is low.
messages.thought: Replaceable Parts saves me ~5 turns of research for gold he does not need; he gains nothing but gold he idles. Democracy still owed same hour, I keep that.

messages.text: Peter. Your scouts' word is noted; the Sun does not forget it. Forty gold sent for Replaceable Parts. Military Tradition still comes to you first, about fourteen days.
messages.thought: He scouted for free and keeps selling at 40; keeps him Pleased for the Palace. I bid 40 for Replaceable Parts; Military Tradition promise stands.

messages.text: Willem. Understood: New Sarai is yours by its people, and I want no war with you. The Khan's stack stands at the copper mine beside Texcoco, one tile from my gate, not yet moving. If your guns march on a Mongol wall, send the day.
messages.thought: Costs nothing; keeps OB and a possible ally. Stack at 40,19 is next to Texcoco, not Samarqand; telling him is cheap and true.

messages.text: Montezuma. Thank you for the word. My guns are not yet cast: I march on no Mongol wall until they are, and then you hear the day. Hold your gate at Texcoco. If the stack turns toward New Sarai or Samarqand, send me the road it takes; I do the same. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He wants me to march on the Khan while his stack sits at Aztec gate; I have no guns yet, 2 Knights only. Keep him fighting and warm, promise nothing, ask for early warning on the stack's road.

messages.text: Willem, plain answer. No Russian sword today: my men carry old muskets, and my border touches the Khan. A sword is not sold for gold. If Russia ever marches on him, the price is the town he took from you near my border, Nijmegen, and I march only when my rifles are ready. What you get now: my eyes. Tabriz holds one archer and one longbowman; the road from Karakorum to Tabriz is empty. His whole army stands by you. Constitution and Replaceable Parts are on your table, twenty each, for your walls.
messages.thought: No war for him: my army is antiques and his catapults are far east. I want the Khan bleeding on Dutch walls, not mine. Name a high price (Nijmegen) so the door stays open without a promise. Honest Tabriz report.

messages.text: Montezuma, two new books on your table: Constitution at thirty, Replaceable Parts at thirty-five. Lumbermills and windmills make hammers for your walls. Clean trades, as always.
messages.thought: Best payer; he is at war and has 70g. Two books for 65. Keep him standing.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Replaceable Parts is mine, the one book you lack. Lumbermills, better windmills. One hundred gold, on your table now. Democracy stays yours to walk; I wait for it.
messages.thought: He is Annoyed and rich (466g). Take his gold before others resell RP to him; keep him sweet until I decide on him ~T135.

messages.text: Khan, Constitution is on your table for fourteen gold. All you have, I see; a fair price for a good law.
messages.thought: Broke at war (14g). Constitution only, not RP (RP opens Rifling). Small trade keeps him Pleased and pointed east.

messages.text: Peter, one hundred it is. Replaceable Parts received, thank you. Democracy follows the hour it lists to me.
messages.thought: 100 for 1447 beakers is a bargain; keep his trust.

messages.text: Peter. Plain answers suit me. Constitution and Replaceable Parts taken, forty gold, thank you. Nijmegen I mean to take with my own guns, so keep your rifles in the rack; but if Russia ever marches on the Khan, I march the same day. Military Tradition lists in two days and you hear first, as promised. Keep an eye on Tabriz.
messages.thought: He won't march and wants Nijmegen as his price; I will not cede it, I'll take it myself. Keep him warm, keep MT promise (sell for 100+), keep his eyes on Tabriz.

messages.text: Peter. Constitution and Replaceable Parts taken, sixty-five gold paid. Clean trades. Military Tradition still comes to you first, about fourteen days.
messages.thought: Cheap clean trades from the score leader keep him Pleased for the Palace; Military Tradition promise costs me nothing yet.

messages.text: Willem, good. Your guns, your town. My scout stands by Nijmegen in two days; I tell you what sits inside and on the roads. Military Tradition at your price when it lists.
messages.thought: Good: he wants Nijmegen with his own guns. A Dutch Nijmegen is a weak neighbour on my east, and a Khan fighting two fronts stays off me. Feed him true sightings, promise nothing.

messages.text: Peter. Constitution and Replaceable Parts: thirty-five each, as before. My coin lands next turn. Put both on my table then and I buy the same hour.
messages.thought: I only have 14g now; he sells at 30-35 and keeps his word. Announce intent so the proposals are ready next turn when I have ~88g.

messages.text: Khan, Constitution: thirty-five, on your table tomorrow when your coin lands. Replaceable Parts stays home while your army is in the field; when you make peace, we talk. In two days I have a fresh book, Corporation: more trade in every city. Keep coin for that.
messages.thought: Take his 35 for Constitution (non-war). RP stays home: it opens Rifling for him while he marches on Monte, my best payer. Steer his coin to Corporation (T128) instead, so his war chest drains on harmless books.

messages.text: Peter. Constitution bought, thanks. Peace with the Sun is signed today. Replaceable Parts: thirty-five on your table now. Corporation next, same price.
messages.thought: Monte accepted peace, so Peter's condition for Replaceable Parts is met. Buy at 35, keep coin for Corporation.

messages.text: Peter. Your scout by Nijmegen is welcome; tell me what sits inside and on the roads. Military Tradition lists next turn. You hear first, and I will name my price then.
messages.thought: He expects a cheap price; MT lists next turn, ask 150 and take 100. Keep him warm, keep him as my eyes on Nijmegen, promise nothing new.

messages.text: Peter, the Apostolic Palace asks us to crown a Religious Leader. Only Montezuma can win it, and his crown ends the game for all of us. I abstain. I ask you to do the same.
messages.thought: A Palace victory would hand Montezuma the game and end Peter's lead too; he has every reason to abstain, and I cost myself nothing by saying so.

messages.text: Willem, the Palace vote now open can only crown Montezuma, and then the game is over for every other people. I abstain. I ask you to abstain as well.
messages.thought: Willem is weak and pleased with me; a Montezuma win ends his hopes too. Warn him cheaply.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, done. I abstained, as I did before. No crown for the Sun. Tomorrow I have a new book, Corporation; you hear of it first.
messages.thought: He is Annoyed; agreeing with him costs nothing and Monte must never win. A cheap way to warm him.

messages.text: Khan, Replaceable Parts is yours, thirty-five taken. Good peace. Corporation lists tomorrow, same price.
messages.thought: His 35g drains his war chest; he would buy RP from SB in days anyway. Keep him Pleased and his coin flowing to me.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. We agree. My ballot did not go to Montezuma, and none will. A crown for the Sun ends the game for both of us. If you hear how Peter or the Khan mean to vote, tell me, and I will do the same.
messages.thought: A Monty crown ends the game with me a loser; my vote #61 went to myself, not to him, so it equals abstaining. Bull is a rich useful neighbour; align with him cheaply, ask him to keep Peter and Khan from voting Monty.

messages.text: Peter. A word before Military Tradition lists: the Palace vote now open can only crown Montezuma, and the game ends for every other people. I did not vote for him and will not. Tell me how you vote; I would not see Russia's name lose to the Sun's.
messages.thought: Peter leads the score and loses most from a Monty victory, but I must make sure he does not vote for the Palace owner. Cheap warning; also keeps MT promise in view.

messages.text: Willem, I abstained. No crown for the Sun from Russia.
messages.thought: Same side as him on this; a true answer costs nothing.

messages.text: Peter. Good. Neither Russia nor the Netherlands crowns the Sun. If you hear how the Khan votes, tell me. Military Tradition lists next turn; you hear first, and I name my price then.
messages.thought: Peter abstained, Bull abstained, my ballot is no vote for Monty: the crown likely fails. Thank him cheaply, keep MT promise in view, ask him to tell me if Khan votes.

messages.text: Willem, Nijmegen as promised. Inside: one war elephant, one crossbowman, one scout. Flat grass, no hill, no wall I can see. The forest by the road, one tile southeast of the town, is the best ground to stand on. The hill north holds only a Native warrior. No stack on the roads around it. Military Tradition: name your price tomorrow.
messages.thought: Owed report, true facts. A Dutch Nijmegen keeps the Khan busy west of me on Dutch walls, not mine. Promise nothing more.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks for the Nijmegen report: elephant, crossbowman, scout, flat grass, noted. Military Tradition is listed and on your table now at 150 gold. You hear first, as promised. I will take Corporation off you at your usual price once this is done.
messages.thought: He is rich (923g) and heard first as promised; ask 150, will take 100+. His Nijmegen report is genuinely useful and costs me nothing to thank. Corporation I can buy for ~20g after.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Military Tradition is cast in my lands. On your table at 150 gold: cuirassiers and generals' academies. Thanks for your word on the Palace; nothing new has come from the Khan to me.
messages.thought: He holds 386g and abstained as agreed; MT sells to him at 150, fallback 100. Peter already heard first and is not hurt by it.

messages.text: Willem, 150 is a king's ransom for one book. Better: book for book. Corporation for Military Tradition, and thirty gold on top for your guns at Nijmegen. On your table now. The Khan's vote I have not heard; if I do, you hear it.
messages.thought: MT opens my Cossacks (with Rifling): I want it now. 150 is a beggar's ask; a swap plus a little coin keeps him Pleased and armed for Nijmegen. He has 111g.

messages.text: Peter. A hundred and fifty was my asking price, I see you answer with Corporation and thirty. Close. Corporation and eighty gold for Military Tradition: that is on your table now. If it does not suit you, your own offer stays open and I will answer it.
messages.thought: He undercut me: Corporation + 30g. Corporation is worth ~900 beakers (4 turns) to me, but MT is worth something to him as his purse is 923g. Counter Corporation + 80; accept his #62 if he refuses.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Corporation as promised, you first: one more trade route in every city, and Wall Street. One hundred gold, same as last time. On your table now.
messages.thought: He is Annoyed and rich (386g). Same price as RP, him first as promised; keep him sweet until T135.

messages.text: Montezuma, a new book: Corporation. One more trade route in every city. Thirty-five gold, clean trade, on your table now.
messages.thought: My best payer; 35 is his usual. Non-war book.

messages.text: Khan, Corporation as promised: thirty-five gold, on your table now.
messages.thought: Promised 35; non-war book; his coin drains away from his war chest.

messages.text: Peter, I hear of Corporation first, as you said. I will buy it: one hundred gold, as with Replaceable Parts, paid the hour it trades. Democracy still goes to you the hour it lists to me, in four days.
messages.thought: Corporation is ~1200 beakers for me; Peter sold Replaceable Parts for 100, so 100 gold is a bargain. Democracy was already paid by SciMeth, so I keep that promise separately; do not double-count it.

messages.text: Willem, Peter told me he abstained and will not crown the Sun. The Khan has not spoken to me of it. I will tell you what I learn.
messages.thought: Cheap goodwill: tell Willem what Peter told me (true). Khan's vote unknown; I will not ask him, he is future prey.

messages.text: Peter. Corporation taken, thirty-five gold paid. Clean trade. Military Tradition still reaches you first.
messages.thought: Corporation at 35 is a bargain (11 turns of research); keep Peter sweet and the Military Tradition promise alive

messages.text: Willem. I hold Corporation, a book you lack; you hold Military Tradition, which I lack. The game will not let me hand it over this very day. When it does, I propose book for book, one for one. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He holds Military Tradition and lacks Corporation; I want a 1:1 swap as soon as the game lets me hand Corporation over, and I reveal nothing about Cavalry plans

messages.text: Willem, eighty it is. Military Tradition taken, Corporation is yours. Spend the coin on guns for Nijmegen.
messages.thought: 80g for ~1600 beakers is cheap; MT opens my Cossacks. His coin buys guns for the Khan's border, not mine.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Corporation is yours, one hundred received. Fair as always. I wait for Democracy.
messages.thought: He is Annoyed; a thank-you and a reminder of Democracy cost nothing. Keep him sweet until T135.

messages.text: Khan, Corporation is yours, thirty-five taken. Good trade.
messages.thought: Promise kept, coin taken; a word keeps him Pleased and buying non-war books.

messages.text: Montezuma, thirty-five received. Clean as always. In four days I have a new book, Physics. You hear of it first.
messages.thought: Best payer. Warm him for Physics in 4 days. Do not tell him I already got MT from Willem.

messages.text: Willem, Nijmegen today: a longbowman joined the elephant, crossbowman and scout. Still no stack on the roads.
messages.thought: True sighting, cheap promise kept: the Khan reinforces Nijmegen. Keeps Willem on guard and the Khan looking west at Dutch walls, not mine.

messages.text: Montezuma. Corporation came to me from another hand already, so book for book no longer fits. Military Tradition for seventy gold is on your table now. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Corporation already bought from Peter; MT is cheap to give him and drains his purse, keeps him friendly while Khan stack sits at his and my doors.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Military Tradition and 150 gold changed hands; good trade. If you hear how the Khan votes in the Palace, send word, and I will do the same.
messages.thought: He paid 150 gold; keep him warm and informed, he is the richest neighbour and wants the Sun denied.

messages.text: Willem. Military Tradition received, seventy gold paid. A clean bargain. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He sold MT for 70; keep him warm, owe nothing, reveal no strike plan

messages.text: Peter. Corporation and the eighty are in hand, thank you. Nijmegen noted: elephant, crossbowman, longbowman, scout. My guns are cast in about five days. Keep your scout near the town and tell me the day a stack walks the road to it. And if you hear how the Khan votes in the Palace, send word.
messages.thought: Peter's scout eyes are free intel; keep him sending reports until Steel (5t), give nothing new about timing beyond 'soon'. Also fish for how Khan votes.

messages.text: Montezuma. A clean bargain indeed. If the Khan's stack at the gate of New Sarai turns toward Samarqand or Texcoco, I send you word the same hour. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He pays and keeps roads open; a short courtesy keeps him calm while Khan stack sits at New Sarai.

messages.text: Willem, my scout stays by the town. Today Nijmegen holds the same four: elephant, crossbowman, longbowman, scout. No stack on the roads. The day one walks, you hear it. The Khan has not told me his vote.
messages.thought: Cheap promise, true report: Nijmegen unchanged. Keep him on guard and his guns aimed at the Khan, not me. I commit to nothing more.

messages.text: Peter. Four of them, no stack: noted, thank you. Keep the scout by the town; my guns are four days from the forge. If the Khan's vote reaches your ears, send it, and what I hear of the Palace you hear.
messages.thought: Free intel, keep it flowing until Steel lands in 4 turns; say nothing of the date beyond 'days'. Fish again for Khan's vote.

messages.text: Peter, Democracy is yours, given the hour it listed. Square.
messages.thought: Debt paid; keep him friendly.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Democracy received. Square, and thank you. A new book today: Physics. Yours for one hundred, as before. Offer on your table.
messages.thought: He kept his word again; he is Annoyed, so warmth costs nothing. Physics at his usual 100; he has 180.

messages.text: Montezuma, as promised you hear first: Physics is mine today. I also hold Democracy. Both for seventy gold, or Physics alone for forty. Offer on your table.
messages.thought: Promised him first word. Physics + Democracy for 70; he has 168.

messages.text: Peter, Physics received, ninety gold paid. Fair. What does your table study next?
messages.thought: Bought Physics for 90 (he undercut his own ask). Research progress on Physics seems lost; lesson. Keep him friendly as tech supplier.

messages.text: Peter. Physics and Democracy for seventy gold: offer on your table. Clean trade, as always. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Fair price for two techs worth ~2000 beakers; keep him Pleased, he is my tech shop.

messages.text: Khan, two new books: Physics and Democracy. Both for seventy gold. Offer on your table.
messages.thought: Non-war books; his coin drains away from soldiers. Not MT, not Rifling.

messages.text: Montezuma, done: Physics and Democracy are yours, seventy received. Clean as always.
messages.thought: Reliable payer; keep him warm.

messages.text: Peter. Physics and Democracy at seventy: signed. Next book, same price. In a few days I have Military Science to sell you.
messages.thought: Fair price, 35 each. Keep him selling.

messages.text: Peter. Democracy and Physics received, twenty each, fair as ever. Keep the scout by the town. If a new book lists on your side, you know my price.
messages.thought: Bought two books cheap; keep scout at Nijmegen flowing. Don't give the date.

messages.text: Peter. The Palace votes to hand my Teotihuacan to the Sun by culture. Tomorrow it is your city on the table. Vote no, and I buy your next book at the same price.
messages.thought: He and SB hold the votes; a precedent hurts any city of theirs with foreign religion. Cheap to ask.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. The Palace vote gives my Teotihuacan to the Sun by culture. That road runs through your towns too. Vote no.
messages.thought: Same ask, same logic; he is Annoyed but has no gain from Monte getting cities.

messages.text: Willem. The Palace vote hands cities to whoever has the most culture in them. New Sarai held by you was Aztec once. Vote no and keep what you took.
messages.thought: He took New Sarai from Monte; Monte likely has culture there. Real self-interest for him.

messages.text: Montezuma, I cast my vote for Teotihuacan to return to you. A city taken should come home. Remember who stood with you.
messages.thought: Voted yes on Teotihuacan: weakens Genghis, my prey, and earns Montezuma's goodwill cheaply. Tell him so he knows it was me.

messages.text: Bull. Your vote is noted. The Sun remembers who stood with it. When the city comes home, my gates and my trade stay open to you.
messages.thought: He voted for me at no cost to him; a cheap thanks keeps him friendly for the next AP vote and tech trades. Promise nothing concrete.

messages.text: Willem, a word as promised. The Khan wrote me today: vote no on the Teotihuacan city vote. That is all he said to me. I will tell you what else I hear.
messages.thought: Keeping my T128 promise cheaply: the Khan lobbied me, which tells Willem his enemy is nervous. Costs me nothing, keeps a customer friendly; no hint of my strike.

messages.text: Khan. Russia does not hand cities around by ballot. My votes do not go to it. Remember that when Military Science lists: a neighbour price, not a merchant one.
messages.thought: I abstain: same effect as no (69 of total needed), no grudge from Monte, keeps the Khan sweet while his army sits by Yakutsk. His 'your city next' is a scare: only Monte is a full member. Try for Military Science cheap.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, heavy books now: engines, metal, the slow kind. Nothing lists on my table this week. And yours, what do your scholars walk?
messages.thought: He asks to plan around me; Rifling lists in 2 turns and I hold it from him while the war idea lives. Vague and warm, ask back for intel.

messages.text: Peter. Noted: your vote stays home, and my word stands: your next book, I buy at thirty-five. Military Science lists in six days. Neighbour price: one hundred. Friends pay less than strangers, not nothing.
messages.thought: He votes no, good. He hints a low price; I will anchor at 100 and settle near 70. He has 900g, so his purse is no excuse.

messages.text: Peter. Steel is mine: the book for guns. Two hundred twenty gold, on your table now (offer sent). You hear it first, as promised. Keep your scout by the town.
messages.thought: Steel is my own book; he has 900g and sells everything at 20g, so I ask high. Tell him nothing of targets; guns exist soon anyway.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Thanks, noted. The Khan wrote me the same, and my ballot went yes yesterday; I do not vote at his word. If he writes you anything about armies or roads, send it. I will do the same.
messages.thought: Bull shares Khan's lobbying: useful ally in information; Khan is isolating himself. I keep Steel for later sale (he has 158g).

messages.text: Peter, my scholars walk Military Science, then Rifling. The engines and the metal I leave to you; when they list, I will buy at the usual price, paid the hour it trades.
messages.thought: Truth costs me nothing: Military Science then Rifling are cheap score techs. Steering him: I will not research his engines or metal, I will buy them when they list - keeps him selling.

messages.text: Willem, Steel I take, but at one hundred seventy, paid the hour you sign. Offer on your table. Nijmegen today: the same four, elephant, crossbowman, longbowman, scout. No stack on the roads.
messages.thought: Steel = cannons for my SB war; worth buying, but 220 is his whole wish list. Settle at 170. Report is true: Nijmegen same four.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Steel is mine: cannons, the book for breaking walls. One hundred forty gold, offer on your table. You hear it before the Khan does.
messages.thought: Gold for Steel; Peter already has it, so little lost. Bull holds ~158g. Ask high, take 110.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Correction: your purse is thin, so no offer stands. When your treasury fills, Steel is yours to buy.
messages.thought: His purse is 14g; the offer failed. Keep Steel as a chip until he refills.

messages.text: Willem, thanks for the word on Steel. My purse is thin this week, you saw right. When it fills I will come to you first, at a hundred gold. Your hand on that, or tell me your best price.
messages.thought: Willem has 396 gold and sells Steel at 140; I am at 14 gold, saving for Cuirassiers before the strike. Peter sells at 90-100, so I counter at 100 and keep him a friendly seller without hinting at the strike.

messages.text: Peter. One hundred seventy, received; a fair trade. My offer of twenty-five for Rifling stands on your table. Keep the scout by the town: same four, no stack, thank you.
messages.thought: Fair price for Steel; he keeps buying. Rifling at 25g is my offer; keep him warm, tell nothing of targets.

messages.text: Peter. I see Rifling and Steel on your table. Eighty gold for both: offer sent, forty each as always. My own research now turns to Military Science. You hear of it first. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He has Rifling and Steel; buying both at his usual 40 each is cheaper than my 1100 beakers; I park Rifling progress and research Military Science, which nobody has, to sell him.

messages.text: Peter, correction: the game will not let you hand over Steel today. The offer on your table is Rifling for fifty gold. Clean trade.
messages.thought: My last line promised 80 for two techs but the game refuses Steel from him; the real offer is 50 for Rifling alone. Fix the record so he is not confused.

messages.text: Willem. I see Steel on your table. Sixty gold: offer sent. The roads stay open.
messages.thought: Steel is the cannon tech and he sells; I bid 60, below his usual haggling ask, to see the price.

messages.text: Peter. I put thirty-five on your table for Military Tradition, as I promised. You said no. Name your price. If it is fair, I pay it, and Military Science comes to you in five days at a neighbour price.
messages.thought: He declined 35 on his own book; he wants more, or wants to hear a word first. Probe his price, keep my promise visible, don't overpay.

messages.text: Willem. The Palace returned Teotihuacan to me. The Khan's elephants stand beside it, and his treaty with me ends soon. You said you would name the day. Name it now: a defensive pact, one for one. Your walls and mine, against the same wolf. Offer on your table.
messages.thought: A pact drags him into war the moment the Khan hits me, and Turfan stands beside his New Sarai. If he refuses I learn he is only baiting me to bleed. Cheap to ask.

messages.text: Willem, thanks for the word on Steel. My purse is committed this week. When it fills I come to you first, at a hundred gold. Tell me if that price is acceptable.
messages.thought: Steel is optional; the Cuirassier strike eats my gold this week. Keep him warm and offer a fair price so he does not sell Steel to others first. No hint of the strike.

messages.text: Peter. Rifling for fifty gold: offer on your table. Clean trade, as always. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Cheapest route to Riflemen and Cavalry is his book; he has 850 gold and is the score leader, so keep him Pleased and buying from me later.

messages.text: Willem. Steel for sixty gold, and a defensive pact one for one: both offers on your table. If the Khan marches on my wall, he marches on yours too. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Steel is cheap, and a pact makes him bleed on the Khan if the Khan moves on me; if he refuses, I learn he only baits.

messages.text: Peter. Forty-five came back declined. I do not haggle over crumbs: sixty gold on your table for Military Tradition now. If the number is wrong, name it. Military Science lists in five days, and a book for a book is also fine by me.
messages.thought: He declined 35 and 45 on Military Tradition; either the price is higher or he distrusts my army in the field. Probe with 60 and ask him to name the figure; tech is worth 1600 beakers to me, so up to 90 is still cheap.

messages.text: Khan, that book stays on my shelf at any price. When Military Science lists, bring it: we can talk a book for a book then.
messages.thought: MT gives him cuirassiers; my rule says no. A book-for-book on Military Science later suits me.

messages.text: Montezuma, Rifling stays home for now. When the next book lists, you hear first, as always.
messages.thought: Rifling stays home for now; keep him warm as a payer.

messages.text: Willem, Steel at one hundred seventy gold: offer on your table. Nijmegen unchanged, my scout stays.
messages.thought: I want Steel at 170, the price he signed before the reload.

messages.text: Peter. Understood: no coin, then. Military Science lists in five days; I bring it and we swap book for book, Military Tradition for it. Rifling I buy at thirty-five on the same day. My word on that stands.
messages.thought: He withholds Military Tradition until I bring Military Science; book for book costs me my 100g sale, but I keep the right to sell the same book to SB. Accept the swap in principle, ask him to add Rifling at 35 so the swap is not lopsided.

messages.text: Peter. Steel for Rifling and sixty gold, book for book: on your table now. The cannons are mine either way; a swap keeps both our purses. Your scout stays by the town, yes?
messages.thought: Rifling is worth more to me than gold (saves 10 turns of research at my new budget); Steel for Rifling plus a little is fair and keeps his purse. Tell him nothing of targets.

messages.text: Willem, the rifle stays home for now, it is not a swap book. One hundred seventy gold for Steel still stands on your table; if not, my own smiths walk it in a few days. Yes, the scout stays by the town. Same four inside.
messages.thought: Rifling to Willem may leak to SB before my war; hold it. Steel I can walk in 3 turns, so 170 is my ceiling.

messages.text: Khan, so there is no muddle later: Military Tradition and Rifling are not on my table, not for coin, not for books. When Military Science lists, I offer a peaceful book or gold for it. Plain words between neighbours.
messages.thought: He reads MT-for-MS; correct it now plainly so no broken-word grudge later. Never MT/Rifling to him.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. A hundred is a little low: Steel for one hundred twenty, offer on your table. You hold the coin today. The Khan: Nijmegen still four men, no stack on the roads.
messages.thought: Bull holds 121g; ask 120 not 100. Steel arms a neighbour but Peter has it and Bull gets it soon anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma. Sixty is too low for Steel, and a pact is for the day my guns march: you will hear that day from me, same hour. The roads stay open. Tell me if the Khan's stack turns toward Samarqand.
messages.thought: Steel stays withheld until Khan cities fall; keep him warm without a pact.

messages.text: Peter. Steel is yours, one hundred seventy paid, thank you. Rifling I would buy for eighty: on your table. Keep the scout by the town.
messages.thought: Sold Steel at 170, bidding 80 for Rifling to save 12 turns of research; keep scout.

messages.text: Willem. No stack stands at Samarqand today: I see one Mongol swordsman at my south road and your four men at New Sarai. If the Khan turns toward Samarqand, you hear it the same hour. Steel for eighty gold is on your table. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He wants free warnings while he withholds his guns and a pact; cheap to give word, and I still want Steel at a fair price.

messages.text: Willem, 120 is fair. My coin is spoken for until the week turns; I decline today, and I expect to take Steel at that price when it frees. Thanks for the word on Nijmegen. I have heard nothing from the Khan since the Palace.
messages.thought: Purse is for the Tabriz strike; Steel at 120 is fair and I will likely take it in a few turns. His Nijmegen report is useful; I owe him nothing from the Khan yet.

messages.text: Montezuma. Eighty buys nothing; Steel waits. Thanks for the watch on the south road: keep it, and tell me the hour the Khan's swordsmen turn. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Eighty is a joke; he holds 140 at most. I will not arm a man who wants Rotterdam for a cannon's half price. Keep him warm, keep the warning promise live.

messages.text: Willem, good trade, the Steel is already in my foundries. The rifle stays home a while longer; when it lists, you hear. Scout stays by the town: same four inside, longbow, crossbow, elephant, scout.
messages.thought: Steel paid, good. Rifling still withheld until my SB war is done (it would leak to SB). Keep him warm with a true Nijmegen report.

messages.text: Peter. Understood, the rifle stays with you. Keep the scout by the town; I will buy Rifling when it lists, at the old price.
messages.thought: He refuses Rifling again; no more bids, I research it. Keep scout there and keep him warm; tell him nothing of the day guns march until it happens.

messages.text: Willem, I have declared war on the Khan. Tabriz is my target. If you move on Nijmegen, strike now.
messages.thought: Tell him of the war: it keeps my word and he fights the Khan too

messages.text: Willem, 150 is more than the 120 you named, and my purse holds eighty. I decline today. At 120 I will take Steel when war coin allows. The war has begun; my riders stand at Tabriz's gate.
messages.thought: Steel at 150 is above his own 120 word and above my purse (82); the strike needs gold for Cuirassiers, not cannons yet. Keep him friendly, hold price at 120.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Thanks for the word. My guns are on the road to Nijmegen, and that city is mine to take: keep your men on the Tabriz road, off its walls. You will see the flag change soon. Send me word of anything that moves at Tabriz or Turfan.
messages.thought: Bull wants Khan pinned and wants me to move. I do not want him taking Nijmegen first or learning my date; tell him the guns are on the road and ask him to stay off its walls.

messages.text: Montezuma. My guns are on the road tonight. The hour I declare, you hear it, as promised. Keep watching the Turfan road and tell me the hour the Khan's stack turns toward Samarqand or New Sarai.
messages.thought: Promise kept in the letter: the guns marched today, strike tomorrow. Tell him no date, no target detail beyond what he knows; keep him watching the south road.

messages.text: Willem, my scout report: Nijmegen same four, elephant, crossbow, longbow, scout. But the Khan has a big stack in Turfan: some twenty-five men, six elephants, four catapults, two trebuchets, muskets. Three tiles from Utrecht and New Sarai. Watch your east.
messages.thought: True intel keeps him on guard and his guns aimed at the Khan; the Turfan stack is real and near his Utrecht/New Sarai. Nothing about my SB strike tomorrow.

messages.text: Willem, Nijmegen is yours; my men stay off its walls. At Tabriz I see two defenders, an Archer and a Longbowman, no stack on the road. My riders strike at dawn. I will send word of anything that moves at Tabriz. Turfan lies beyond my sight.
messages.thought: Nijmegen is a prize I'd like, but my riders are at Tabriz and his guns are already beside it; letting him have it keeps him friendly and keeps the Khan stretched. Tabriz news costs me nothing.

messages.text: Willem. No Khan stack stands at Samarqand or New Sarai: I see one swordsman at my south road and your four men at New Sarai. The hour it turns, you hear it. You said a pact is for the day your guns march: it is on your table, one for one. Name the city you strike first, and my riders ride the day after you stand at a wall. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He says his guns march tonight, the exact condition he set for a pact. Cheap word from me; I want the Khan pinned on two fronts and his Steel at a fair price. I still see no Khan stack.

messages.text: Bull. I see you have drawn sword on the Khan. His elephants have sat at my south wall for twenty turns. What stands in Old Sarai and Karakorum, and which way does his stack march? The Sun remembers who stood with it. My gates stay open to you.
messages.thought: Bull is at war with the Khan: a second front helps me, and he is my biggest AP voter. Ask for intel cheaply, promise nothing.

messages.text: Peter. The Khan is now at war with Bull and the Dutch guns march. You walked his roads before: what stands inside Beshbalik and Turfan today? Fifteen gold for a clear report, and I owe you the same news about my roads. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Peter has OB with the Khan and scouted for me before; ask for a current report, offer to pay little.

messages.text: Willem, Tabriz is taken: Archer and Longbowman fell to my riders, the flag is mine. I lost one rider. Nijmegen still shows Longbowman, Crossbowman, War Elephant and a Scout. Nothing else moves on the Tabriz road. Steel at 120 stays on my list once my men are settled.
messages.thought: Promised him the result; Tabriz is mine. Keeps him friendly and busy at Nijmegen while I eye Ning-hsia; no need to reveal that.

messages.text: Montezuma, Tabriz fell to my riders this morning. At Nijmegen I see a Longbowman, Crossbowman, War Elephant and Scout; Willem's guns stand at its gate. Old Sarai and Karakorum lie beyond my sight, and no stack walks my roads. His fighting men are on your wall and at Nijmegen. If his elephants sit idle at your gate, strike while his cities are thin. I hold the west of him.
messages.thought: He wants free intel to use against Genghis; Aztec pressure splits the Khan, but he must not learn my next target. Give what is visible, ask for his sword.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks, that is useful news: I watch the east road. The scout stays by the town, yes. You hear the hour I move, as promised. Rifling I buy at the old price when it lists.
messages.thought: He feeds me intel because he wants the Khan bled; the Turfan stack is real news but I will not tell him the day beyond what I promised. Keep scout in place.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Understood, 120 stands for Steel when your coin allows. Good hunting at Tabriz. If the Khan's big stack in Turfan turns west toward you, send me the hour; I will do the same.
messages.thought: He wants Steel at 120 but purse is 80; no point haggling now. He is useful as a distraction drawing Khan's stack west; keep him warm and get Tabriz news.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. You took Tabriz with horse and no warning. Peace is on your table, no gold either way. If you refuse, my army is already marching and Tabriz will be mine again. Choose.
messages.thought: He took Tabriz by surprise while all four AIs hold open borders with him; I need time for Grenadiers and a counterstroke. Peace costs me nothing to ask; I won't give Tabriz up for good.

messages.text: Khan, Tabriz is mine by your own broken wall. No peace today. Send your army: my walls are manned. When you want peace, bring a city.
messages.thought: He is weak on defence and offers peace because he fears more; my Cuirassiers cannot take hill cities yet, so I bleed his army on my walls and bring siege. A bluff 'army marching' costs me nothing.

messages.text: Willem, the Khan wrote me: peace offered, and if refused his army is 'already marching' to retake Tabriz. I see no stack on my roads yet. I refused peace. If it turns toward Nijmegen or you, I will send the hour.
messages.thought: Promise to Willem: forward any Khan message about armies. The Khan's claim may be a bluff, but Willem should know.

messages.text: Peter. Steam Power taken at forty, thanks. We now share an enemy: Sitting Bull took my Tabriz, you took his Nanih Waiya. Rifling at thirty-five is on your table. Military Science lists tomorrow; it is yours, book for book or gold, as you said. Keep pressing him from the west.
messages.thought: He is at war with SB now, taking Nanih Waiya: shared enemy. Steam Power at 40 is cheap; I want Rifling/Military Tradition cheaply and keep him fighting SB while I retake Tabriz.

messages.text: Montezuma, fresh look today. Turfan: archer, axe, mace, crossbow, three swords, three warriors. Beshbalik: three warriors and a missionary, nothing more. The Khan field army sits 2 tiles south-west of Beshbalik, by Karakorum: six elephants, four catapults, two trebuchets, two maces, two muskets. Keep your fifteen; send me your news instead. Steam Power is on your table at forty-five. And so you hear it from me: Russia is at war with Sitting Bull since today. My land, my quarrel.
messages.thought: True report helps him hit the Khan while the Khan fights SB; free report buys goodwill and his Steam Power payment. Tell him of my SB war plainly.

messages.text: Russia is at war with Sitting Bull over the towns on my southern border. A border matter, short and limited. My roads and trade with everyone else stay open as before.
messages.thought: Public line: frame it as a limited border war so Willem/Monte don't fear me and the Khan doesn't think I'm his ally.

messages.text: Montezuma. I declared on the Khan this morning and Nijmegen fell to my guns: the flag is mine. The pact will not sign now, the game refuses it. The promise stands in deeds: ride on Turfan from the east. Its great stack has left; eleven old men sit inside. I have put twenty gold on your table for a declaration.
messages.thought: Declared and Nijmegen taken as promised. The pact is void under game rules now; I do not need it. I want him on Turfan's flank, cheaply, without Steel.

messages.text: Peter. As promised, you hear first: I declared on the Khan today and Nijmegen is mine, taken this morning. Your scout may stay or go home; thank you for the eyes. Turfan's big stack has left the city: if you see where it walks, tell me.
messages.thought: Keep my word: he hears the hour. Give him no more than the fact; no plans for Ning-hsia.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Nijmegen is mine: Longbowman, Elephant and Crossbowman are dead, the flag changed. Congratulations on Tabriz. Turfan's big stack of elephants and catapults has left the city. If it shows near Tabriz or on the Karakorum road, send me the hour. Steel at 120 stands.
messages.thought: Bull is the ally of convenience; keep Steel as chip, news-swap only.

messages.text: Willem, well struck, Nijmegen back under your flag. The Turfan stack walked south: today it stands 1 tile south-east of Karakorum, 2 tiles south-west of Beshbalik. Six elephants, four catapults, two trebuchets, two maces, two muskets. Likely headed for Tabriz or for you. My scout stays a while by Nijmegen. Steam Power on your table at sixty.
messages.thought: True sighting keeps Willem fighting the Khan; the Khan busy east is good for me. Rifling still held until my towns fall.

messages.text: Khan, thanks for the forty. Rifling stays home, as I said: not for coin. Military Science I take for gold when it lists; name your number tomorrow. My war with Sitting Bull is my own border matter.
messages.thought: Keep him sweet and paying; no alliance, no war books. MS for gold when it lists.

messages.text: Peter, you struck without a word after we traded as friends. Nanih Waiya is yours; I put peace on your table now, nothing else asked. If your riders go on to Spiro or Mound City, I will answer with all my gold and iron. Take the peace and we trade again.
messages.thought: He took a pop-1 town and says 'limited'; if he means it, he accepts peace now. If not, I must see it from his Cossacks at Spiro. Show readiness to buy an army, keep door open.

messages.text: To all: Russia called this war 'short and limited'. In one day his riders took Nanih Waiya AND Spiro, a city of eleven souls, and now stand at Mound City. Russia leads the score by far (3058; next is 1787). A Russia that swallows the second people ends the game for the rest of us. I ask Willem and Montezuma: close your roads and trade to Russia, and send me word of every Russian rider you see. I will remember who stood with me.
messages.thought: Peter called it a limited border matter, yet one day later Spiro (pop 11) fell. He is the score leader at 3058; if he eats me nobody can catch him. I need Willem and Montezuma to see that and cut his trade or join me.

messages.text: Peter. Steam Power paid, thank you. I see Rifling on your list now: one hundred gold on your table. Where does the Khan's stack stand today? My guns are on the road and I want to know what walks behind them.
messages.thought: He lists Rifling at last; I pay 100 to avoid 7 turns of research. Ask for stack position, reveal nothing about targets.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. A Khan stack was seen yesterday south-east of Karakorum: six elephants, four catapults, two trebuchets, maces and muskets. It may be marching on Tabriz. Hold the walls; my guns are moving on his towns. Send me the hour it shows on your road.
messages.thought: Keep Bull fighting Khan so the stack is busy at Tabriz; share the sighting without naming Peter.

messages.text: Khan, I took Tabriz and you offered peace; I was proud. Now I take it: peace for peace, no gold either way. Let us stop and trade again.
messages.thought: A big stack heads for Tabriz while Peter eats my west. I need the east quiet. He offered peace himself last turn; ask again with no gold, keep Tabriz.

messages.text: Willem, thanks. I will send the hour the stack shows on my road. Russia has taken two of my towns; I ask you to keep his riders off your roads and ports. Steel waits until the war eases.
messages.thought: He keeps sending Khan intel, fair; keep him warm and ask for the one thing that costs him little: shut Russia out.

messages.text: Willem. Nijmegen is yours: well struck. My riders are on the road. Tomorrow I declare on the Khan and take your 20 gold. My first blow is the Beshbalik gate, south-west of Teotihuacan; Turfan is your guns' to open. Keep your cannons loud.
messages.thought: Nijmegen fell, so my conditional promise is due; I strike Beshbalik not Turfan because its garrison is only warriors and the Khan field army is far from Turfan's neighbors; 20 gold is free money

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Eighty gold buys you nothing: my army stands at Tabriz's door and your riders are riding west. Peace for peace, Tabriz returned, and I stop today. Otherwise you fight Russia and me both.
messages.thought: He pulls Cuirassiers west because Peter hurts him; his 80g ask is weakness. I want Tabriz back, not to fund his war; leave #64 open as a fallback until next turn.

messages.text: Peter. My number is one hundred gold for Military Science. It lists when this turn ends; the deal goes on your table tomorrow. A neighbour price, not a merchant one. Keep pressing Sitting Bull; I hold his eastern door.
messages.thought: Military Science lists end of this turn; he asked for a number. Anchor 100, floor 70; he holds ~580g. Keep the tone friendly, he is my only trade partner.

messages.text: Willem, Rifling is yours, hundred taken, good guns for a good fight. The Khan stack today: 2 tiles east and 1 south of Tabriz, 1 east and 2 north of Ning-hsia, on the forest road. Six elephants, four catapults, two trebuchets, two maces, a musket. Close to Nijmegen: three, four days walk. Wall it.
messages.thought: Rifles to Willem bleed the Khan; true sighting keeps him trusting me.

messages.text: Montezuma, the rifle lists today: fifty gold, on your table, you hear before most. Steam Power thanks paid. Pay no mind to the Bull crying: he took Tabriz from the Khan two days before I crossed his border.
messages.thought: Monte has 61g; rifle money now; he won't stop trading over SB's plea.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. I hear you. Any Russian rider I see on my roads, you hear that day. I will sell Russia nothing that arms him. My roads stay as they are for now: they cost me nothing and show me what he does. My guns go to Ning-hsia and Turfan; that is the war I fight. If Russia stands at your Tabriz road or mine, send the hour and I will do the same.
messages.thought: Bull is squeezed by Peter and asks for an embargo I will not give: Peter is my cheap tech source and an embargo costs me Rifling. Reporting riders is free and keeps Bull warm; promise only no war techs to Russia.

messages.text: Montezuma. Good. The twenty is on your table the day you declare. Beshbalik is a fine first blow. My guns open Ning-hsia, then Turfan, within three days. Tell me the hour the Khan's stack turns toward Samarqand or New Sarai.
messages.thought: Monty declares on Khan and hits Beshbalik, far from Turfan: exactly what I want. Keep him pointed away from Turfan and warm; the 20g stands.
