messages.text: Sitting Bull, you hear it plain this time. Mound City is the last town I want. When it flies my flag, I take your peace the same day, nothing more asked, and trade opens again. Send your riders at me before that and the war goes on to Cahokia.
messages.thought: Mound City falls T142; then peace is real. Nacogdoches I give up unless he refuses.

messages.text: To all: Sitting Bull took Tabriz from the Khan the day before I moved, and now calls for help. My war is the three towns on my south border, Nanih Waiya, Spiro and Mound City, settled on my doorstep. When the third is mine I make peace. Trade and roads with all of you stay open.
messages.thought: Public reassurance so Willem/Monte don't embargo; the limit is true.

messages.text: Peter. Your look at Beshbalik and Turfan is received, with thanks; Steam Power is on my roads now, forty-five paid. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: His report is gold; he has OB with the Khan so I give no hint of the strike; keep him Pleased and his intel flowing

messages.text: Peter. Rifling in hand, thanks. I hear the stack stands near Ning-hsia; my guns and walls will meet it. Tell me tomorrow where it walks, and I keep paying fair for your news.
messages.thought: Rifling bought. Peter keeps feeding me Khan stack positions; keep him useful and warm, give nothing about my targets beyond what the stack will see anyway.

messages.text: Willem, the hour is now: the Khan's stack (6 elephants, 4 catapults, 2 trebuchets, 2 maces, a musketman) stands on the forest road tile 2 east and 1 south of Tabriz, one step from Ning-hsia. Ning-hsia itself shows only Longbowman, Maceman, Musketman. Your guns at the road tile 2 west of it are well placed. Russia also took my Spiro; keep his scouts off your roads.
messages.thought: Promise kept: tell him the stack's hour. Also steer his guns at Ning-hsia while the Khan stack stands outside it, and keep him fighting the Khan so the east stays busy.

messages.text: Khan, hear me once. Peter took two of my towns in two days and leads the score by 1300 over you. If you and I bleed each other, Peter eats us both. Peace for peace, no gold, and I trade with you again. Your stack at Tabriz's gate will cost you elephants; my walls are manned.
messages.thought: I want peace to free my army for Peter; Khan is Furious and his stack is 2 tiles from Tabriz. Pitch Peter as the common danger; do not give a city.

messages.text: Peter, you took Nanih Waiya and Spiro in two days and now name Mound City as the third. Mound City is twelve souls and my walls; you will pay for it in Cossacks. Take the peace I put on your table now: you keep Nanih Waiya, I keep Mound City, and the war ends with trade open. Spiro I will buy from you, name a price.
messages.thought: He wants Mound City (pop 12, my best western town) then peace. No. Stall, keep him talking while Pikemen/Cuirassiers arrive; make him believe cost is high.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, no. My word stands as I gave it: Mound City, then peace the same day. Spiro is not for sale. Put the same peace on my table when Mound City flies my flag and I sign it that hour.
messages.thought: Mound City falls tomorrow if the odds hold; I keep my word: peace the same day, not before. Spiro is not for sale.

messages.text: Khan, one hundred for Military Science is a fair neighbour price. Put it on my table tomorrow and I sign the same hour.
messages.thought: MS is 4 turns of my research (~2100 beakers); 100g is cheap, no haggle worth the grudge. Promise him nothing in the SB war.

messages.text: Willem. War on the Khan is declared; your twenty is taken. My riders stand at the Beshbalik gate, 3 tiles west-northwest of Teotihuacan, and strike at dawn. Your guns on Turfan and Ning-hsia, and the Khan's field army will turn from me. If his stack turns on New Sarai, you hear it the same hour.
messages.thought: He pays 20 and wants me to bleed for his guns; fine, my war is for land too. Tell him real positions, keep his guns loud.

messages.text: Bull. Your word arrived: I have drawn sword on the Khan today and my riders stand at the Beshbalik gate. I have seen no Russian rider on my roads. My gates stay open to you.
messages.thought: He wants me to cut Russia; I cannot afford a fight on two fronts and Peter sells me techs. Give him the war news only, no pledge.

messages.text: Khan, your elephants took Tabriz back. It is yours; I ask nothing for it. You said peace for peace once the city came home. The deal is on your table: sign it and we trade again.
messages.thought: Tabriz is gone and my riders with it; the Khan won his price by force. Peace now costs me nothing more and frees the west. He asked peace-for-peace with Tabriz returned: it is returned.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Thank you for the hour. Today I see a Mongol Maceman, a War Elephant and your captured Worker on the hill-forest road tile 1 south-east of Tabriz, 2 tiles north of Ning-hsia. The stack seems to be turning on Tabriz, not on me. Hold the gate and keep your riders inside. I will say if it turns my way.
messages.thought: His hour-is-now note is stale: the stack went to Tabriz's flank, not mine. Warning him costs me nothing and keeps the doom stack busy at his walls; goodwill banked.

messages.text: Montezuma. Your declaration is noted and the twenty is paid. My guns stand 2 tiles from Turfan's wall; they speak within three days. Keep the Beshbalik road busy and tell me the hour any Khan stack turns toward Samarqand or New Sarai. Steel still waits until a Khan city is mine.
messages.thought: He declared and took my 20g; good. Keep him fighting at Beshbalik, far from Turfan. Give him no date for Turfan beyond what's true.

messages.text: Willem. My riders stand at the Beshbalik gate and strike at first light; no Khan stack has turned on New Sarai or Samarqand, and I will send the hour if one does. Open Turfan, and when a Khan flag falls to either of us, Steel changes hands as you said.
messages.thought: He wants me to pin the Khan while his guns work; fine, it is my plan anyway. Steel is the real prize once a Khan city falls.

messages.text: Willem, the hour: the Khan's stack struck Tabriz this morning and took it back, killing my four men there. The elephants and catapults now stand IN Tabriz, 3 tiles east of my Poverty Point and 4 tiles from your guns at the grass road tile west of Ning-hsia. Ning-hsia may be thin now. I sent the Khan a peace offer; no answer yet.
messages.thought: Promise kept: tell him the hour. Also keeps the Khan stack off his guns and pins the Khan between three of us; peace with Khan is also pending, so I describe facts only.

messages.text: Montezuma, thank you. The Khan's big stack (6 elephants, 4 catapults, trebuchets) took Tabriz back from me this morning and now stands in that city, far from his home towns. Beshbalik and Karakorum may be lightly held; strike while his elephants are away. I have seen no Russian rider on my roads toward you either.
messages.thought: Montezuma at war with Khan is good for me: Khan stack is committed at Tabriz, far from his home. Give him true facts; Khan peace is pending but pressure helps get it.

messages.text: Bull. Your word is received. My riders stand at the Beshbalik gate and strike at first light. Keep his big stack busy at Tabriz as long as you can; tell me the hour it turns east. My gates stay open to you.
messages.thought: He wants the Khan pinned and bled while Russia is his problem; his word on the empty home towns is useful and costs me nothing. No pledge on Russia.

messages.text: Montezuma, a straight word: the Khan took Tabriz back, then signed peace with me this morning. Russia's riders are at Mound City, so I need every man west. I do not ask you to stop your war: his stack of elephants and catapults is in Tabriz, not at your gate. I will pass on what I see of Russia.
messages.thought: Honest about the peace: he will see it in relations anyway. Keep him friendly; he fights the Khan on his own account and still helps me by pinning the Khan.

messages.text: Willem, the Khan accepted peace with me this morning, Tabriz his again. I need every man against Russia at Mound City. Your war on him is yours; I will still tell you what I see of his stack from my border. Thank you for the watch.
messages.thought: Honest: Khan signed peace-for-peace. Willem fights on; Khan stack in Tabriz is not at peace with Willem. My promise to send hours about the Khan to Willem still holds where I can see it.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Mound City stays yours. I stop at two towns, not three. Peace is on your table today for eighty gold. Nanih Waiya and Spiro stay Russian. Sign it and trade opens again.
messages.thought: Mound City now has five defenders; a siege would cost more than the town is worth. I take peace with the two towns I hold and ask 80 gold; if he refuses, I sign plain peace.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Peace signed, Tabriz home. Good. Steam Power for Military Tradition, book for book, is on your table. Keep Peter busy in the west; I hold the east.
messages.thought: Peace is what I needed: three fronts is too many. He is weak now and holds 183g; get Military Tradition from him cheaply, and keep him alive against Peter.

messages.text: Willem, todays look: the Khan stack stands 1 tile south-east of Tabriz, 2 tiles north of Ning-hsia, on the forest hill. Three elephants, a trebuchet, a mace there now; it faces Tabriz, not you. Ning-hsia holds two muskets, a mace, a longbow. Your cuirassier sits next to it.
messages.thought: True sighting, as promised; the Khan's stack is on Tabriz (SB), not on Nijmegen. Keeps Willem on my side and fighting.

messages.text: Montezuma, I see your riders by Beshbalik. Rifling at forty now, on your table: rifles hold what cuirassiers take. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Monte now fights the Khan; rifles help him hold, and the Khan bleeds far east. 40g is a friend price; he has 116.

messages.text: Khan, Military Science received, one hundred paid, as agreed. Good trade.
messages.thought: Kept my word on MS. Short and neutral; nothing about his wars with Monte and Willem.

messages.text: Willem. Your cannons stand two tiles from my walls and my elephants have just taken Tabriz back from Sitting Bull. Neither of us gains from this. Peace for peace, no gold, on your table.
messages.thought: Peace stops his two cannon stacks next to my cities and lets me face Monte alone. I lose nothing: my army can't reach his stacks anyway. Re-open war later when Grenadiers/Cannons are ready.

messages.text: Willem, straight word: Peter offered peace for eighty gold, Mound City stays mine, he keeps Nanih Waiya and Spiro. I signed to rearm; I do not trust it. Khan peace too. Your war on him is yours. The Khan's stack was last seen inside Tabriz; I will send the hour if it moves toward your guns or my road. Tell me what Russian riders you see.
messages.thought: Promise to tell him Russian news; peace with Peter is a fact he will learn anyway. Keep him fighting the Khan and watching Peter; no hint of my later plans for Spiro.

messages.text: Montezuma, I must tell you plainly: Peter offered peace for eighty gold, Mound City stays mine, I signed; the Khan signed too. My war is paused, not forgotten. Yours with the Khan I do not ask you to stop. His big stack was last seen in Tabriz, far from your gate. If it turns east on my road, you hear the hour. Gates open both ways.
messages.thought: Tell him the truth on peace; his Khan war keeps the Khan's army in the east, away from me. Promise only what I can keep: Khan stack sighting.

messages.text: Peter. Rifling is on my roads, forty paid; the riflemen will hold what my riders take. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Bought Rifling at 40 though it cost me my 81% beakers, a blunder; no need to show that. Keep him Pleased.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Thanks for the hour. Ning-hsia is not thin: Longbowman, Maceman and two Musketmen on a hill, too hard for guns today. My cannons stand on open ground west of it; if the stack steps next to them, I fire first. Turfan is the softer wall. If you make peace with the Khan, send me the hour: his stack would then face me.
messages.thought: Bull wants my guns on Ning-hsia, a hill fortress; if he makes peace with the Khan, the doom stack walks onto me, so I ask the hour. Keep the east army secret.

messages.text: Peter, Rifling is mine at your price. Fair. Steel I will take when my purse refills, in a few days. Name a number then.
messages.thought: He sells me Rifling for 55 because it keeps me peaceful and arms me less than he fears; I take it, it saves 5 turns. I want Steel cheap later; no hint of Spiro.

messages.text: To all: peace with Sitting Bull is signed. I stopped at two towns, as I said. Russian roads and trade stay open to everyone.
messages.thought: Peace signed and my word kept: two towns, not three. Say it once in public so the embargo talk dies.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, the war is done and so is my part of it. When your treasury fills again, my books are on the table at the old price.
messages.thought: He is score #2 and keeps his deals. Warm him slowly; he is broke, so no sale today.

messages.text: Willem, my peace with the Khan was signed yesterday; the book is closed, so I cannot threaten his walls. His stack was last seen inside Tabriz, 3 tiles east of my Poverty Point. If it turns toward your guns, you hear the hour. I see one Russian Scout on the plains road tile 1 east of Nijmegen. Hold Ning-hsia's hill with your cannons, not your men.
messages.thought: He asks for the hour if I make peace with the Khan; I already did (T142) and told him. Restate plainly, keep the promise cheap, pass the Russian Scout sighting as reciprocity. I have no stack to move on Ning-hsia.

messages.text: Willem. A Khan war elephant sallied from Beshbalik this morning and died on my lances. The city holds two musketmen behind thick walls of culture; my cannons march in about five days, my riders hold the fort west of Teotihuacan meanwhile. Where do your guns stand at Turfan? Tell me the hour they open the wall, and I ride the same day.
messages.thought: I did not strike: 24% odds into two musketmen behind 60% culture walls. Keep him believing I hold the Beshbalik road busy; ask where his guns are.

messages.text: Peter. Steel and Military Science are on my roads: seventy-five paid between the two, thanks. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Steel and Military Science at 40+35 is cheap; keep him selling, say nothing about my plans.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, good, the rifle is yours. When your purse is full, write to me and we look at the table then. Steel or another book, we will find a fair one.
messages.thought: Steel withheld while he is at peace with the Khan (resale risk). Keep him warm, commit to nothing; steer him to a non-war book later.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, peace is signed, so let the roads open again too. Open borders, both ways, on your table: traders pass, purses fill, and you buy Steel sooner.
messages.thought: Spiro is cut off by his culture; I need OB to reach it with the artist and rifles. Trade routes help both. Frame it as trade reopened.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Ning-hsia: two muskets, a mace, a longbow; one mace alone by Tabriz. Karakorum: crossbow, four catapults, archer, warrior. The Khan field army, two grenadiers, two muskets, three elephants, sits in Beshbalik facing Montezuma. Turfan holds twelve, mostly old swords and warriors, right next to your cannon. Nothing walks at your guns by Nijmegen.
messages.thought: True report, keeps him fighting the Khan at Ning-hsia, far from me.

messages.text: Peter, peace is signed and I keep it. My roads stay closed to riders for now; yours stay closed to mine. Books I buy when my purse is full.
messages.thought: Open borders would park his Cossacks beside Mound City under a peace I do not trust; he wants my gold and a view of my walls. Refuse, keep it short, keep the trade door open.

messages.text: Willem. The Khan has pulled men into Beshbalik: three war elephants, two musketmen, two grenadiers behind thick culture. I hold the fort west of Teotihuacan and let them bleed on it. What stands in Turfan today, and are your guns at its wall? If it opens, I ride that day.
messages.thought: Khan has reinforced Beshbalik hard; if his guns open Turfan I ride too. I need his Turfan view and want him to keep the Khan split, truth costs nothing.

messages.text: Peter. My news: the Khan has pulled three war elephants, two musketmen and two grenadiers into Beshbalik. If your riders pass Turfan, a word on what stands in it would be welcome. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Free news costs me little and keeps him friendly; he sells cheap when Pleased. I also want his eyes on Turfan.

messages.text: Montezuma. My guns fired on Turfan today: the garrison is bloodied, the wall not yet open. More guns arrive in two days. Keep the Beshbalik road busy; the Khan must split his men. I will say the hour.
messages.thought: He wants to ride in and share Turfan; keep him busy at Beshbalik, tell him little. Two cannons lost but the garrison is bloodied.

messages.text: Peter. Military Science paid, thanks. Where does the Khan stack stand today, and what does Ning-hsia hold? I pay fair for your news.
messages.thought: He keeps the Khan stack watch cheap; keep buying. He took 2 Bull towns; I stay friendly but watch.

messages.text: Montezuma, Turfan today: eleven inside, all hurt. A musket at a third of its strength, a mace, a crossbow, three swords, an axe, an archer, three warriors; most near half health. Flat ground on a river, no hill. Dutch cannons and a rifleman sit on the forest one tile south-east of it, already pounding the walls. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: True report keeps Monte hitting the Khan far east; Turfan is weak and bleeding under Dutch cannon. Costs me nothing.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, fair. Peace holds on my side as well. When your riders rest, we talk roads again.
messages.thought: He keeps peace but holds Spiro shut; no use pushing today. Warm and short, ask again in a few days with a sweetener.

messages.text: Willem. Good. Beshbalik now holds twelve men: three elephants, three muskets, two grenadiers, warriors. They stay pinned there while my riders hold the fort. Say the hour Turfan's wall falls and my lances ride the same day.
messages.thought: He wants me to pin the Khan; Beshbalik is now a fortress of 12 units, so my pin is real but I cannot take it. Keep him fighting at Turfan, and ride only if it opens.

messages.text: Peter. Your count of Turfan is received, with thanks: eleven hurt men on flat ground is a gift. My lances ride toward it. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: His scouting is free and useful: Turfan is soft. Keep him Pleased, give nothing real, no Palace talk.

messages.text: Willem. I hear Turfan holds eleven men, all hurt, on flat ground by the river. My lances leave the Beshbalik fort and ride to the field 2 tiles east of its wall today. Say the hour your guns open it, and I strike the same day. The Khan sent me an offer of peace; I refused it.
messages.thought: Turfan is soft; I want to be at its wall when his guns open it so I share the loot, and he must not take it alone. Keep him believing I am a partner.

messages.text: Montezuma. Your riders stand at my walls and my guns stand behind them. Peace for peace, no gold, is on your table; take it and trade again, or keep paying in horses.
messages.thought: He declined plain peace-for-peace; as an LLM he may want a word or a sweetener. I want quiet on the east to build economy; no gold, but I can say the stack bleeds on my walls.

messages.text: Khan. The Sun does not buy peace with horses. My cannons march on Beshbalik; count your walls. Send me a city and we talk.
messages.thought: He wants peace because Turfan bleeds under Willem's guns; I want him to keep his men pinned at Beshbalik and not reinforce Turfan, so I point my threat at Beshbalik, which is a real target anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma. Today my guns and riflemen killed three Turfan defenders: swordsman, crossbowman, maceman. Eight old men remain, the wall is cracked. Two more days. Keep the Khan's army pinned at Beshbalik; I will say the hour.
messages.thought: He wants the hour so his lances can claim a share; Turfan is mine. Keep him pinning the Khan army at Beshbalik with true but vague news: wall cracking, no hour yet.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks for the look. My guns are now next to Ning-hsia and break Turfan's garrison. What does Tabriz hold today, and is any Khan stack walking toward Nijmegen or the Hague?
messages.thought: Peter's eyes are cheap and honest. I need Tabriz and Karakorum garrisons to decide the west stack. Pay in thanks, he asks no gold.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Ning-hsia: the same four, two muskets, a mace, a longbow. One mace alone on the forest hill 2 tiles north of it. The Khan field army still sits in Beshbalik facing Montezuma: two grenadiers, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors. Karakorum: crossbow, four catapults, archer, warrior. Nothing walks at your guns. You say you pay fair: twenty-five gold is fair, the rest buys powder.
messages.thought: True report again, nothing changed: Ning-hsia is weak vs his 3 cannons, I want him to take it and bleed the Khan. He offered pay; ask a small fee, in character, but let his coin go to powder.

messages.text: Montezuma. No city. Beshbalik has walls, guns and elephants behind them; bring your cannons and we count the dead together. My offer stays: peace for peace, no gold. Take it when you tire.
messages.thought: He wants a city for peace, a non-starter; walls, 2 Grenadiers, 3 Musketmen and elephants hold Beshbalik, so bluff-lite confidence costs nothing and keeps the door open for peace-for-peace later.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks, fair is fair. Today: does anything walk out of Karakorum toward Turfan, and what stands in Tabriz? Twenty-five for a straight answer.
messages.thought: Need to know if Karakorum's catapults/crossbow march on my stack at Turfan; 25g is cheap for that. Tell him nothing of my plan beyond what he can see.

messages.text: Montezuma. Turfan is bloodied; my guns and riflemen work on it again at first light. Keep Beshbalik pinned and your lances out of my guns' way. You hear the hour the moment the wall is down.
messages.thought: Silent on the hour on purpose: if I say 'it is empty' his lances ride in and take the Sistine Chapel. Give him a harmless, true line that keeps the Beshbalik pin and promises the hour after.

messages.text: Willem, twenty-five received, thanks. Today I walked my scout up to Tabriz. Inside: three war elephants, a trebuchet, a mace, a musket. One more mace sits on the forest hill 1 tile south-east of it. Ning-hsia: the same four. No stack walks toward Nijmegen or The Hague today. But three elephants in Tabriz are 4 tiles from Nijmegen: keep a pike at home.
messages.thought: True report keeps him on guard and bleeding the Khan; his 25g came, thank him. Tabriz's elephants could walk on Nijmegen: worth saying plainly. I don't reveal Monte's riders.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, one more try on roads, then I stop asking. My town Spiro sits in your land like an island: my own men cannot reach it, and its people work two fields. Open borders both ways, and fifty gold on top for your purse. It is on your table.
messages.thought: I need OB to walk my artist into Spiro (culture bomb reclaims its tiles) and a rifleman. I won't name the painter. 50g is cheap for a pop 8 town that works 2 tiles. One try, then stop pushing.

messages.text: Peter. Twenty-five paid, as promised. Good eyes. Nijmegen keeps its pike and a musketman. Tomorrow I ask the same again: Tabriz and Karakorum, same price.
messages.thought: Straight, useful report. Pay and keep him as scout; ask Karakorum tomorrow. Do not reveal Turfan nearly empty.

messages.text: Peter, fifty gold is small for open roads. Give me Steel and the roads open both ways for as long as the peace holds. That offer is on your table.
messages.thought: Fifty gold is bait; open borders cost me little (war declaration expels his riders) but Steel is what I want for Cannons against Spiro. Test whether he pays a real price.

messages.text: Montezuma. The hour: Turfan's wall fell this morning and my flag flies over it. Keep Beshbalik pinned; my guns turn on Ning-hsia next. Your lances may take the field east of Turfan, not the city.
messages.thought: Turfan is mine; tell him now as promised, and make it clear the city is held so his lances don't try anything.

messages.text: Peter. Turfan is mine. Same ask: what stands in Tabriz and Karakorum, does anything walk? Twenty-five for a straight answer.
messages.thought: Ask again for 25g news, as promised.

messages.text: Peter, Steel received, thank you. Roads are open both ways, as I said, for as long as the peace holds. A fair trade.
messages.thought: Steel is mine; roads open both ways is a cheap price. He sees my garrisons now, but I see Spiro and Nanih Waiya too. Thanking him costs nothing and keeps him calm while I build Cannons; no word of Spiro.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum: crossbow, four catapults, archer, warrior; nothing walks out of it toward Turfan. Tabriz: same three elephants, trebuchet, mace, musket. Ning-hsia: same four. The Khan field army still sits in Beshbalik. New on my table: Railroad, one hundred ten. Rails carry guns to the front in a day.
messages.thought: True look, as paid. Railroad is my new book and he has the deepest purse: 110, settle near 90.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, done: Steel is yours, roads open both ways. One thing between us: the Khan fights my trading friends, so keep the metal off his roads. Railroad is mine now; it is on your table tomorrow, ninety.
messages.thought: Steel paid the roads; my painter is already in Spiro. He may resell Steel to the Khan; a word costs nothing. RR tomorrow is the real sale.

messages.text: Montezuma, Railroad is mine today. Fifty, on your table, you first among the far ones. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Best payer, 139g; RR at 50 is his friend price.

messages.text: Peter. Railroad bought, 110, and the 25 for your news is paid. Good eyes again. I ask again tomorrow, same price: Tabriz, Karakorum, anything walking.
messages.thought: Railroad at 110 is cheap; paying the 25 as promised keeps him talking. Next ask: Ning-hsia and Tabriz again; Artillery is my own book to sell later.

messages.text: Peter, I heard your word on the Khan. Railroad at ninety tomorrow: I will have the gold ready.
messages.thought: Railroad at 90 is cheap vs 12 turns of research; his Khan remark is a soft ask I will not bind myself to. Keep the tech trade flowing while I mass Cannons for Spiro.

messages.text: Willem, a correction, the Khan moved while I watched. Tabriz is now down to a musket and a mace. The three elephants and the trebuchet walked into Karakorum, and two grenadiers joined them: Karakorum now holds two grenadiers, three elephants, trebuchet, four catapults, crossbow, archer, warrior. That is a strike stack, four tiles from Turfan and five from your guns by Ning-hsia. Watch both.
messages.thought: The Khan moved during this turn; my report is stale. Correct it at once: true words keep him paying and the Khan bleeding on Dutch guns, not mine.

messages.text: Willem. The Orange flag stands on Turfan; your riflemen were first through the gate, and my lances held the east wall as I said. Fair. The Khan still holds Beshbalik with twelve men, and his army sits there. Heal your guns, then bring them south: my cannons will be at its gate within days, and my riders ride the hour its wall cracks. Karakorum and Ning-hsia are yours for the taking after.
messages.thought: He beat me to Turfan; I must not look bitter. I want his guns on Beshbalik with my horsemen walking in, but I will not promise him the city.

messages.text: Peter. Railroad is on my roads, fifty paid, thanks. The Orange flag now flies over Turfan; the Khan still holds Beshbalik. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Cheap tech, keeps him Pleased; give him nothing about my plans.

messages.text: Peter. Correction received and paid: twenty-five more. The Karakorum stack is noted; Turfan gets riflemen. I ask again tomorrow.
messages.thought: He warned of a strike stack: worth 25. Keeps him honest and talking; I pay what I promised.

messages.text: Montezuma. Fair words, fair gate. My guns heal and turn on the hills next. Keep the Khan's army nailed to Beshbalik; if it breaks west of you, send the hour.
messages.thought: Keep him pinning Beshbalik; no need to share Karakorum details or promise anything. Courteous and short.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Railroad at ninety is on your table, as I said yesterday.
messages.thought: Promise kept: RR at 90 as agreed. Keep him buying, not fighting.

messages.text: Peter. Twenty-five for a straight answer, as promised: does the Karakorum stack walk, where does it stand now, and what is in Tabriz and Ning-hsia?
messages.thought: Need to know if the Karakorum strike stack walks at Turfan or my guns; 25g is cheap for the answer. Keep promise.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum: same stack, two grenadiers, three elephants, trebuchet, four catapults, crossbow, archer, warrior. Nothing walks out yet. Tabriz: a musket and a mace; one more mace on the forest hill 1 tile south-east of it.
messages.thought: True look, same as yesterday's correction; he pays 25 per report.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. The Palace election is open. Only Montezuma and I can be Resident. He already took a city by ballot; as Resident he can also order every member to declare war on a voting member like you, or embargo you. Vote for me. I will use the chair only to force peace in my own wars. No war, embargo or city-grab against Native America or Russia. Sign on that.
messages.thought: SB has 43 votes, the kingmaker. Monte as Resident can order Declare War/Embargo on voting members like SB; I can sell him protection and mean it for Native America and Russia. Real aim: Force Peace on my two wars.

messages.text: Peter. The Palace election is open. You said Russia does not hand cities around by ballot. Montezuma holds the chair and used it once. Vote for me. I will use the chair only to force peace in my own wars. No war, embargo or city-grab against Russia or Native America. You have my word.
messages.thought: Peter has 21 votes and hates ballot city-grabs. Monte is Resident and hostile to me. If SB and Peter vote me I win the chair; I keep the promise as it costs me nothing.

messages.text: Willem. I plant a small town on the empty grass between Texcoco and Turfan (two tiles east of Turfan, one north of the copper). It guards your flank against the Khan's riders too. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He told me to keep out of his guns' way; he owes me nothing. I settle the unowned gap tile between us and tell him it is a farm town, not a threat. Cheap word, keeps him calm.

messages.text: Khan, plain answer: my vote was cast before your letter came. Russia abstains in Palace elections, as I do on every Palace ballot; it is not a vote against you. Rifling stays home, as I said before. Biology is mine tomorrow; I will put it on your table.
messages.thought: Already abstained on #84; a Khan Resident would force peace in his wars and free his army. Tell him the truth plainly so no broken-word grudge; keep him buying non-war books.

messages.text: Peter. Understood, no offence taken. Biology: thirty-five on my table the hour you list it, as with every book. My word on the chair stands.
messages.thought: He abstains, fine; no harm done. Biology tomorrow: lock my 35g price early so he opens low, and keep the friendship cheap.

messages.text: Montezuma. Plant your town where you like, but leave the river tiles by Turfan to Turfan; my railroad will run there. My guns hold the hills south of Ning-hsia; if the Khan army leaves Beshbalik, send the hour.
messages.thought: His new town is crowding Turfan's east, but he is a useful cat's-paw against Khan and I cannot stop it without a quarrel. Be polite, claim the river tiles lightly.

messages.text: Willem. Agreed: the river tiles by Turfan are Turfan's. My town works the copper and the plains to its east. The Khan's army sits at Beshbalik; if it moves, you hear the hour. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Cheap to concede river tiles he cannot lose to me anyway; keeps him calm while I plant the town and he does the Khan's work. Real aim: land, then Beshbalik/New Sarai later.

messages.text: Peter. Same ask, 25 gold: does the Karakorum stack walk, what stands in Tabriz, and who is in Ning-hsia?
messages.thought: Cheap news keeps him warm and shows the Khan stack.

messages.text: Khan, Biology is on your table at thirty-five, as you said. Good harvests.
messages.thought: His 35 is his own price; take it fast, his coin drains. Nothing more to say.

messages.text: Willem, Biology is mine today: fatter farms, bigger towns. One hundred, on your table.
messages.thought: Willem has 502; 100 for Biology is fair; keep him buying.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Biology is mine today. Eighty, on your table: less than Railroad, more food for your towns.
messages.thought: SB Annoyed and near my two towns; cheap good trade keeps him buying not fighting. 80 is a friend price.

messages.text: Montezuma, Biology is mine today. Forty-five, on your table. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Monte pays every time; friend price 45.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum: the stack has not walked, but it thinned: one grenadier now (one left, I did not see where), three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. The crossbow is gone too. Tabriz: a musket and two maces (the mace from the hill went inside). Ning-hsia: the same four, two muskets, a mace, a longbow. Biology is on your table, one hundred.
messages.thought: True report keeps him on guard and the Khan bleeding; 25g.

messages.text: Khan, Biology at thirty-five is on your table again; the first one slipped. Sign when ready.
messages.thought: Rewind erased his 35g deal; re-offered. Keep him buying peace books.

messages.text: Peter. Biology is mine, forty-five paid, thanks. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Biology for 45 is cheap and keeps him Pleased; he is the score leader but sells at fair prices; say nothing of the Palace.

messages.text: Peter. Biology bought, the hundred is yours. Fair price. Today's look, same terms: does the Karakorum stack walk, what stands in Ning-hsia and Tabriz? Twenty-five on a straight answer.
messages.thought: Biology at 100 is fair (farms +1 food, ~28 turns of research). He gave no Khan news; I keep my 25g promise only for a real answer. Karakorum stack is the main risk to Turfan; his eyes are cheap.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum: the stack still sits, and the second grenadier is back: two grenadiers, three elephants, trebuchet, four catapults, archer, warrior. Tabriz: two maces and a musket. Ning-hsia grew: six now, two muskets, grenadier, mace, crossbow, longbow. Your guns stand right next to it, so you will feel it first. The Khan field army was last seen in Beshbalik: three elephants, three muskets, two grenadiers.
messages.thought: True report as always; the stack keeps him on guard and bleeding the Khan. Ning-hsia got stronger: his gun stack next door should know.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, eighty was too rich for you, I hear. Biology at sixty is on your table now. Better harvests, bigger towns. The roads stay open on my side.
messages.thought: He balked at 80; 60 still drains his purse and keeps him buying from me, not marching. Friendly before the peace runs out.

messages.text: Khan. Peace for peace feeds only your pride. My horsemen stand at your door and do not tire. A hundred gold, and the Sun lowers its spear. Answer my offer or I keep my lances where they are.
messages.thought: I cannot crack Beshbalik for 20+ turns; peace is cheap now, but a hundred gold costs him little and shows he values it; if he refuses I take the free peace anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma. A hundred gold for peace alone is a low price for you and a high one for me. Hundred and Steel, and I sign: peace, gold, and a book. My table is open; yours stays as well.
messages.thought: I will pay 100g for peace as a time-buyer but ask Steel on top; fallback is to sign #70 as written before the end of T151.

messages.text: Peter. Your look was good and the 25 is paid. Same ask today: Ning-hsia count, Tabriz, and does the Karakorum stack walk? Twenty-five on a straight answer.
messages.thought: Daily news at 25g still pays: I need to see if Ning-hsia keeps growing and if the Karakorum stack walks. His gold is 1300; I could sell him an economy tech later.

messages.text: Willem, I looked again just now: nothing moved since this mornings report. Karakorum still holds the stack, two grenadiers, three elephants, trebuchet, four catapults, archer, warrior; it does not walk. Tabriz: two maces and a musket. Ning-hsia: six, two muskets, grenadier, mace, crossbow, longbow, right beside your guns. Beshbalik still holds the field army, three elephants, three muskets, two grenadiers, three warriors. Next look tomorrow.
messages.thought: Same turn, same picture as my morning report: nothing moved. Say so plainly; the truth keeps him paying and on guard. If he pays 25 for it, fine.

messages.text: Peter. Straight answer, 25 paid. The stack sits and Ning-hsia has six: noted. I ask again tomorrow, same price.
messages.thought: His news is cheap and steady: a stack that does not walk lets me finish Ning-hsia. Pay, ask again, keep him warm and useful.

messages.text: Montezuma. Hundred gold and Steel for peace is signed. Your old offer #70 is the same deal; I decline it as already done. Keep the peace; trade fairly and I will too.
messages.thought: Deal #74 signed: peace and Steel for 100g. His stale #70 would charge me twice; refused. Time-buyer only; he broke the last peace at T142, so keep garrisons.

messages.text: Genghis, I read your word. I now follow the Buddha as a full member, so the chair is between Montezuma and me. Montezuma took a city by ballot; you saw it. Vote for me. I take your pledge of no war, embargo or city-grab against my people, and I give the same: from my chair no such order falls on Mongolia while our peace stands. If your war turns against you, I bring Force Peace to the table on your word.
messages.thought: I need his 12 votes (plus Willem's 8) to reach 60 for Resident; pledge costs me nothing now. Not telling him about the religious victory plan.

messages.text: Willem, the Palace chair is between Montezuma and me. If I sit in it, my first act is Force Peace against the Khan's war on you, and open roads for all members. I ask your ballot. The vote may come within a few turns; watch for it.
messages.thought: Willem's 8 votes are needed; Force Peace on the Khan is a true offer and helps me too. No mention of victory vote.

messages.text: Willem. The Khan paid me gold for peace; my cannons cannot crack Beshbalik's twelve men until the great guns come, twenty-odd turns. It is a pause, not a friendship. The grass east of Turfan proved too close to your walls for a town, so it stays empty. Your guns have the field. If the Khan's army moves, you still hear the hour from me. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He is Annoyed that I signed peace; I must keep him as a gun partner without promising what I won't do. Truth about the failed town is cheap to tell.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. My ballot went in at T148 and I cannot change it. I will not pretend otherwise. If you win the chair, my pledge stands, no war, embargo or city-grab on your people. My ask: Force Peace between me and Willem van Oranje as your first resolution. Put it up and I vote yes.
messages.thought: My ballot was cast for myself at T148 and I see no way to change it. He is likelier to win than I am and far likelier than Monte to give me Force Peace on Willem. Be honest about the vote, claim the favour, keep my pledge.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum: the stack still sits, two grenadiers, three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Tabriz: musket and two maces. Ning-hsia: the same six, beside your guns. Beshbalik: the field army did not walk after the Aztec peace; it grew, three grenadiers, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors. Old Sarai: a grenadier and two warriors. Nothing walks west yet.
messages.thought: True look as promised; the Beshbalik army grew by a grenadier but still sits. Keep him paying and on guard.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Your chair suits me better than Montezuma's. My ballot leans to you. One condition: no Force Peace on the Khan until I say my guns are done at Ning-hsia, a few turns. Agree, and the ballot is yours. Biology is on your table at 90.
messages.thought: Bull as Resident is harmless to me and better than Montezuma, who covets Rotterdam; my 8 votes cost me nothing. But Force Peace would end my Ning-hsia war before it is won, so I trade the ballot for a delay.

messages.text: Peter. Same ask today, same price: does the Karakorum stack walk, what stands in Ning-hsia and Tabriz, and has the field army left Beshbalik? Twenty-five on a straight answer.
messages.thought: Daily 25g look is cheap insurance; the Beshbalik field army is now free to move since Monty took Khan's gold for peace.

messages.text: Montezuma. A pause suits us both; my guns still have a hill to climb. The Beshbalik army is now free to walk: the hour it leaves, send word. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: His peace frees the Khan field army against me; I need his eyes at Beshbalik to stay alive, and I owe him no more than a line.

messages.text: Genghis, I read you. My pledge stands: no war, embargo or city-grab on Mongolia from my chair, and Force Peace between you and Willem is the first resolution I put up. A new ballot may open any day. I ask yours for it.
messages.thought: His 12 votes may decide the new ballot; Force Peace vs Willem costs me little (Willem is weak, and I keep my word while it serves). Keep it soft and ask the vote again for the next ballot.

messages.text: Willem, a new Palace ballot may open any day. My word stands: if I take the chair, Force Peace against the Khan's war on you comes first. I ask your ballot for me, not for Montezuma.
messages.thought: Willem has 8 votes and is weak; Force Peace helps him against the Khan's war, so it costs me nothing; he has not answered.

messages.text: Willem, the answer went to you an hour ago; one change since. Karakorum took a third grenadier (Old Sarai lost its one, now two warriors only). The stack still sits: three grenadiers, three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Tabriz: musket and two maces. Ning-hsia: the same six, beside your four cannons. Beshbalik: the field army has not walked. Twenty-five for today is still open.
messages.thought: He asked before reading my report; the only change is a 3rd grenadier into Karakorum (Old Sarai emptied). True, short, and ask for the 25 still owed.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Open the ballot and my vote goes to you, not to Montezuma. Your side: Force Peace between me and Willem van Oranje first, before anything else. Do that and my pledge and my word stand.
messages.thought: SB is the better chair for me than Monte; a vote costs nothing and buys Force Peace. Commit, but tie it to the first resolution.

messages.text: Peter. Straight answer, twenty-five paid. Same ask tomorrow.
messages.thought: Straight answer, paid; keeps his daily eyes on Khan, who may yet walk.

messages.text: Willem, agreed: if I take the chair I put no Force Peace on the Khan until you tell me your guns at Ning-hsia are done. Name the day when you can. Biology I finish myself next turn, so no coin this time, thanks. I count your ballot as mine.
messages.thought: Need his 8 votes; delay of a few turns costs me nothing since the first resolution slot is ~3 turns after the election anyway. Ask him to name the day so I am not stuck. Biology I finish next turn myself.

messages.text: Genghis, read. Force Peace between you and Willem is on my list as the first thing I bring to the Palace, and it needs the Palace's calendar to ripen, so it comes in the first days of my chair. When the ballot opens I count your vote as mine. My pledge stands.
messages.thought: Need his 12 votes. Force Peace remains my plan for him and Willem, but Willem asks a few turns delay; I do not reveal Willem's condition. Keep it vague on timing; will tell him honestly if the delay becomes real.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. You did not answer my condition. Say it plain: no Force Peace on the Khan until I tell you Ning-hsia is done, a few turns. Say yes and the ballot is yours.
messages.thought: Bull ignored my condition twice. Force Peace before Ning-hsia falls would cost me the war's prize; make him say it in writing or I do not owe the ballot. Nothing about the date.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Heard. When the ballot opens I vote for you. Force Peace with Willem first, then we are square. I watch the Palace each turn.
messages.thought: He keeps repeating the same pledge; costs nothing to confirm. I will vote SB when a ballot opens and check every turn. If Monte wins I lose nothing.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Your yes crossed my letter. Good: the ballot is yours when it opens. I will name the day myself, within five turns.
messages.thought: His yes crossed my message. Lock it: ballot is his, I name the day later; keep date vague (about five turns).

messages.text: Peter. I am writing Artillery, some twenty turns. Which book do you write? Let us not write the same one: when each is done, we swap, book for book. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Tech is flat across all five; whoever writes a unique book can swap it. I want to avoid duplicate research and lock Peter into book-for-book swaps, not gold sales that feed the score leader.

messages.text: Peter. Same ask today, same price: does the Karakorum stack walk, what stands in Ning-hsia and Tabriz, has the Beshbalik army left? Twenty-five on a straight answer.
messages.thought: Peter's news is cheap and confirms Khan stack stays; ask again, pay on straight answer.

messages.text: Montezuma, good thinking. I write Assembly Line, two days off, then Electricity. Artillery is close on my road too, so do not spend twenty days on it. Write Medicine instead: I will not walk it. When it is done, book for book. Assembly Line goes on your table in two days, friend price.
messages.thought: His 20-turn Artillery is worthless to me: I reach it in ~10. Steer him to Medicine (off my road), keep Artillery off his roads to the Khan, and sell him Assembly Line in 2 days for gold.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum: the stack still sits, three grenadiers, three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Tabriz: a musket and two maces. Ning-hsia: the same six, two muskets, grenadier, mace, crossbow, longbow, beside your guns (five cannons now). Beshbalik: the field army sits, three grenadiers, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors, and a missionary. Old Sarai: two warriors. Nothing walks west. Twenty-five, as before.
messages.thought: True daily look; nothing walks. Keeps Willem paying and on guard; the Khan bleeds on Dutch walls.

messages.text: Peter. Straight answer, twenty-five paid. Same ask tomorrow.
messages.thought: Straight answer, nothing walks west; five cannons are my secret strength, he counts them already. Pay and keep the habit; he is my eyes.

messages.text: Peter. Assembly Line in two days: yes, I buy it the day it lists, at your friend price. Medicine I will write, book for book, if you write Artillery right after Assembly Line and Electricity after it: you have the faster road, and I need the great guns for my war. If Electricity must come first, tell me, and I keep writing Artillery and we swap that for Electricity. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He wants me off Artillery to avoid duplicate work; Assembly Line cheap in 2 turns is good (Infantry). I need Artillery by ~T165, not T173, so I ask him to write it next and test his commitment; I keep my 511 beakers in Artillery as a hedge until he answers.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. The Khan feeds Ning-hsia. Karakorum gave up two grenadiers: one grenadier left there, with three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior; the stack itself does not walk. The two grenadiers stand now one tile north-east of Ning-hsia, on the farm by the road, beside your guns. Ning-hsia itself is seven: two grenadiers, two muskets, mace, crossbow, longbow. Tabriz: a musket and two maces. Beshbalik: the field army sits, three grenadiers, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors. Twenty-five, as before.
messages.thought: True look; the Khan pours grenadiers into Ning-hsia against Willem's guns, far from my land. Good for me. Keep him informed and paying.

messages.text: Montezuma, Electricity must come first, my towns wait for it. So keep writing Artillery, and we swap Artillery for Electricity when both are done. Assembly Line on your table the day it lists, friend price.
messages.thought: Artillery late in his hands is better (Khan resale risk); Electricity is already next on my queue. Take his fallback.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: does the Karakorum stack walk, what stands in Ning-hsia and Tabriz, has the Beshbalik army left? Twenty-five on a straight answer.
messages.thought: Daily 25g for honest news keeps the Khan picture fresh; pay on a straight answer. Nothing of mine to reveal beyond what he sees.

messages.text: Peter. Agreed: I keep writing Artillery, and we swap it for Electricity when both are done. Assembly Line: I buy it the day it lists. If your Electricity comes first, tell me the day and we trade then. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He keeps Electricity for himself and wants Artillery from me; fine: it keeps my road and costs nothing now. I still want Artillery earlier than T174 and Assembly Line cheap.

messages.text: Peter. Assembly Line is on your table: forty gold offered, friend price. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Buy AL cheap as promised.

messages.text: Montezuma, Assembly Line is on your table, forty-five, as promised. Electricity comes in about five days; I will tell you the day. Then Artillery for it, book for book.
messages.thought: Promise kept: AL at 45 the day it lists. Electricity ~5 turns; tell him the day.

messages.text: Willem, my answer to that went to you yesterday. Fresh look today: nothing moved. Karakorum: one grenadier, three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior; it does not walk. Ning-hsia: seven inside, two grenadiers, two muskets, mace, crossbow, longbow; two more grenadiers on the farm one tile north-east of it. Tabriz: musket and two maces. Beshbalik: the field army sits, three grenadiers, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors. Twenty-five, as before. Also: Assembly Line is on your table, one hundred ten. Factories, and infantry with your rifles.
messages.thought: True T154 look: nothing moved since my T153 report. Collect 25; AL at 110 sells factories to my buffer.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a new book: Assembly Line. Factories, more hammers in every town. Seventy is on your table. The roads stay open on my side.
messages.thought: He will get AL from resellers within days anyway; 70 of his 139 is better in my purse. Keep him buying, not fighting.

messages.text: Peter. Assembly Line bought, forty-five paid. Tell me the day Electricity lists; Artillery follows book for book. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He keeps his word at friend price; good. Artillery for Electricity is the plan; he wants to know the day.

messages.text: Peter. Assembly Line bought, thank you: fair price. Today's look, same terms: Tabriz garrison, does the Karakorum stack walk, has the Beshbalik army left, anything new at Ning-hsia? Twenty-five on a straight answer.
messages.thought: Straight answers are worth 25g while the Karakorum stack can still walk at me. Assembly Line bought at 110: very cheap. Keep him paying attention to my war news only.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. You asked me to name the day. Ning-hsia grew to nine men; my old cannons are not enough. New guns land in two turns, new infantry in four to six. I will strike about T160 and report the result by T165. Hold Force Peace on the Khan until then. My ballot is yours.
messages.thought: I must name a day by T156; true state: Ning-hsia holds nine now, cannons are 9% odds; Artillery T156, Infantry T158-160. Name T165 as the checkpoint, no more.

messages.text: Willem, I read your day. No Force Peace on the Khan before your report, T165 at the soonest. Send me the word when the guns have spoken. Your ballot stays mine; I count it so.
messages.thought: He named the day: strike T160, report T165. Costs me nothing since there is no Resident yet; keeps his 8 votes. Khan will still expect Force Peace first; I will manage that later.

messages.text: Willem, a fresh look this hour, and one change. Ning-hsia is now nine: the two grenadiers from the farm walked inside, so four grenadiers, and a RIFLEMAN, the Khan has rifles now, plus musket, mace, crossbow, longbow. Your six cannons on the jungle hill south of it face a harder wall than yesterday. Karakorum: the stack does not walk, one grenadier, three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Tabriz: two maces and a musket. Beshbalik: the field army sits, three grenadiers, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors, and a missionary. Twenty-five, as before.
messages.thought: True report as always; Ning-hsia got stronger, he should know before his cannons hit it. The Khan now has Rifling (not from me).

messages.text: Willem, todays look, and two changes. Karakorum grew: three grenadiers again, and a CANNON, his first great gun, with three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. The stack still sits. Those two grenadiers came from Beshbalik: the field army there is now one grenadier, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors, a missionary; it has not walked out. Ning-hsia: the same nine, four grenadiers, rifleman, musket, mace, crossbow, longbow. Tabriz: two maces and a musket. Old Sarai: two warriors. Twenty-five received, thank you.
messages.thought: True report as always; the Khan pulled grenadiers from Beshbalik back to Karakorum and has a cannon now: Willem should know, it keeps him wary and bleeding the Khan, not me.

messages.text: Peter. Your looks are straight and worth the price. New terms, to save us both ink: I ask every third day, twenty-five paid on a straight answer. If the Karakorum stack or the Beshbalik army walks, tell me that hour and I pay fifty. Next ask: T158.
messages.thought: His 25g/day news is now most of my deficit and nothing walks; renegotiate to every third day plus a bonus for a real move. He keeps his word and sells techs, so keep him warm.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. The chair is yours; I voted as I said. Now the first resolution: Force Peace between me and Willem van Oranje. Put it up when the calendar opens, I vote yes. Also on my table: nineteen gold for Railroad, more when my purse fills. Mongolia keeps its pledge.
messages.thought: He holds the chair now; the Force Peace promise is due. Next resolution in 5 turns. Remind him politely, tie Railroad purchase as goodwill; don't overpay.

messages.text: Willem, agreed: every third day, twenty-five, and fifty the hour either army walks. Today they both still sit: Karakorum with its cannon, Beshbalik with its elephants. Next look T158.
messages.thought: Cheaper ink, steady 25 every third day plus 50 on a walk: good for me, and his war on the Khan is my buffer. Nothing walked today, true.

messages.text: Genghis, the chair is open and I read your yes. The Palace calendar opens in about five turns, and what I bring first I will weigh with the count in hand: your ballot is counted, my pledge stands. Nineteen gold is a thin price for Railroad; bring sixty and the book is yours, no haggling between friends of the chair. Keep your men at your own walls and Force Peace will come easier.
messages.thought: 19 gold for Railroad is a gift, not a price; keep the book as leverage and sell it when his purse fills. Force Peace is bound by my word to Willem until T165, so I must not date it; I will not reveal Willem's strike.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Sixty is more than a friend's price; my purse holds nineteen. Railroad at thirty-five when I have it, or better: I am researching Communism, which nobody owns. When it lands, we swap it for Railroad and Assembly Line. The count for Force Peace is simple: your 69, my 12, Monte 29 against a war I did not start. Willem broke three peaces and took my city. Put it up when the calendar opens; my men stay at my walls.
messages.thought: He is hedging on Force Peace ('weigh with the count in hand') and pricing Railroad at 60, which I cannot pay (19g). Keep pressure on Force Peace, hold my price at 35, and dangle Communism swap (no rival has it) as the real trade.

messages.text: Willem, a correction this same day: the Karakorum stack has walked. Three grenadiers, the cannon and one catapult left it and now stand in Old Sarai, three tiles north of Karakorum, with two warriors. Away from you, not toward Ning-hsia. Karakorum keeps three elephants, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Beshbalik still sits. Ning-hsia the same nine. Tabriz two maces and a musket.
messages.thought: True correction: the Karakorum stack split and walked north to Old Sarai, away from him. He pays 50 for walks; honest news keeps him trusting and fighting.

messages.text: Genghis, I read you. Communism for Railroad, one for one, the day you hold it; Assembly Line stays at sixty. The order of the Palace list is mine to set when the calendar opens, and I will not name a day before I see the count. My pledge to you stands; keep your men at your own walls.
messages.thought: Khan's 12 votes matter for the T160 re-election; I owe Willem silence until T165, so I cannot give Khan a date. Swap Communism for Railroad alone is fair and costs me nothing; keep Assembly Line for coin. Tell him no new promise.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Communism for Railroad, one for one: agreed, the day I hold it, about twelve turns. Assembly Line I will take at thirty-five or research myself. You hold 77 votes now; the count for Force Peace is yours. Name the day when you see it. My men stay at my walls.
messages.thought: He keeps stalling on Force Peace but the Communism swap is cheap and I get Railroad. Accept, keep pressure light, remind him that Willem's war is the one thing I ask of the chair.

messages.text: Willem, the Karakorum group walked again, back home: the three grenadiers, the cannon and the catapult left Old Sarai and stand again in Karakorum. So Karakorum is full once more: three grenadiers, cannon, three elephants, four catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Old Sarai keeps two warriors. Beshbalik still sits: one grenadier, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors, a missionary. Your fifty for yesterday received, thank you.
messages.thought: True: the Old Sarai group walked back to Karakorum. He paid 50 already for the first walk; this one he is owed to hear.

messages.text: Genghis, I read you. Communism for Railroad, one for one, when you hold it. The Palace list opens in a few days; I will read it with the count in hand and tell you what I bring. My pledge stands. Keep your men at your walls.
messages.thought: He accepts my terms and pushes for a day again. I give no day; the missionary reaches Nacogdoches first, then I read the list with the count in hand. Keep him warm, commit nothing new.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Understood. Communism for Railroad stands. When the list opens at T161, put Force Peace between me and Willem first; I vote yes the same turn. My men stay at my walls.
messages.thought: He repeats himself and will not commit; the only real test is T161. A short line keeps Force Peace on his table without new concessions.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear you. The list opens at T161 and I read it with the count in hand; the same turn I tell you what I bring. The Communism-for-Railroad swap and my pledge stand. Keep your men at your walls.
messages.thought: He wants a date (T161) I cannot give: Willem's hold runs to T165, and my real first item may be the Religious Victory. Keep him calm, give no day, keep the pledge.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: does the Karakorum stack or Beshbalik army walk, what stands in Ning-hsia and Tabriz? Twenty-five on a straight answer, fifty if one walks.
messages.thought: Routine look, 25g on straight answer; wants to see if Ning-hsia grew and whether stacks walk.

messages.text: Willem, todays look, and the Karakorum group walked again. The three grenadiers, the cannon and a catapult left Karakorum and are out of my sight; they are not in Old Sarai. Karakorum keeps three elephants, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. And a Mongol RIFLEMAN stands on your town tile 2 east and 1 south of Nijmegen, 1 east and 2 north of The Hague. Ning-hsia thinned: four grenadiers, crossbow, longbow; the rifle, musket and mace went out. Tabriz: musket, two maces. Beshbalik sits: grenadier, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors. Also: Electricity is new on my shelf. On your table: Electricity for your Artillery and twenty, book for book.
messages.thought: True look; the Karakorum strike group left sight again and a Mongol rifle stands by his towns: worth his 50. Swap gives me Artillery for Rocketry.

messages.text: Montezuma, as promised: Electricity lists today. Forty-five is on your table, friend price, if you want it now. If you would rather wait, our swap stands: book for book the day your Artillery is done. Your choice.
messages.thought: Promised to tell him the day; Willem holds Artillery already, so his swap may be moot. Give him the choice, keep my word.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a new book: Electricity. Seventy on your table. Roads stay open on my side.
messages.thought: Sell to every buyer same hour; he has 81.

messages.text: Khan, a new book: Electricity. Thirty-five, as before; it is on your table.
messages.thought: Non-war book; drains his war chest. He has 68.

messages.text: Peter. Artillery is not for sale: guns I promised nobody. Electricity for gold, yes: I put 24 on the table now, more next turn when my purse refills. Thanks for the Rifleman warning at the town east of Nijmegen. Twenty-five paid on your look.
messages.thought: Artillery is the war tech I swore not to give Russia, and it is my edge at Ning-hsia; refuse politely, buy Electricity for gold.

messages.text: Willem, done: Electricity for the twenty-four, and I trust the rest when your purse refills, sixty more makes it fair. The group that walked out of Karakorum is worth the fifty when you can. Guns stay yours; no grudge.
messages.thought: Cheap, but he is the buffer and keeps his word; ask the balance plainly. Artillery must come from Monte now.

messages.text: Peter. Electricity bought, forty-five paid; thank you for telling me first. I keep writing Artillery. When it is done I bring it to your table: book for book, Rifling for Artillery. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Cheap book, and Artillery stays my unique card to sell him for Rifling or Steel-line books; keep him Pleased

messages.text: Montezuma, paid and thanked. Rifling you have held since the spring I sold it to you, so let it be my next book instead: Combustion, done in about four days. Your Artillery for it, book for book, whichever finishes first waits for the other.
messages.thought: He already has Rifling from me (T142); offer Combustion, my next book in ~4 days, for Artillery.

messages.text: Peter. Agreed: Combustion for Artillery, book for book, whichever finishes first waits for the other. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He wants Artillery for Combustion; fine, cheap swap, it speeds my war tech and he is far west; keep him Pleased.

messages.text: Willem, your second offer of twenty-four came after our deal was already signed, so I let it lapse: you pay once, not twice. A free look today: nothing walked. Karakorum the same elephants, catapults and trebuchet; Beshbalik sits; Ning-hsia four grenadiers, crossbow, longbow; Tabriz musket and two maces. The sixty and the fifty for the walk, when your purse allows.
messages.thought: He has 255 now and owes ~60 + 50 by his own words; nudge politely, give a free true look so the fee feels earned. Nothing walked.

messages.text: Peter. One hundred thirty-five sent: twenty-five for your look, fifty for the Karakorum walk, sixty to close Electricity. We are square. The group you lost sight of stands in the forest north-west of Turfan, three grenadiers, cannon, mace, catapult. Next ask: T161, same terms.
messages.thought: He is honest and cheap; paying keeps the news flowing. Tell him nothing about my strike hour, only that the debts are paid. The Karakorum group is at Turfan's door, he guessed right.

messages.text: Willem. Your guns have Artillery. I offer ninety gold for the book. The Khan's Beshbalik is the next wall, and my cannons wait on it. A strong Aztec army at that gate helps your Turfan. Name your price if ninety is short.
messages.thought: He holds Artillery and offers it; buying saves me 11 turns and lets me honour Peter's swap. Cheap price first; he is a hard haggler, so I can go to ~140.

messages.text: Willem, received, all square, thank you. Good that you found the group: one tile from Turfan is close, keep your walls manned. Next look T161, same terms.
messages.thought: He paid in full; good payer. Keep the eyes channel warm. That group by Turfan is his problem, not mine.

messages.text: Montezuma. Ninety is short and I am not selling guns this week: my own are at the Khan's Ning-hsia gate today. When that city is mine we talk again. Meanwhile your cannons on Beshbalik help us both; send the hour his army walks.
messages.thought: Ninety for Artillery is an insult, and he covets Rotterdam; my east cities hold longbows. Keep the book, keep him pinning Khan with hope of a later price.

messages.text: Willem. Understood: your guns work Ning-hsia first. My offer rises to one hundred fifty gold, and my word goes with it: the day the book is mine, my stack marches on Beshbalik, and the Khan's army stays nailed there while your guns climb. No Artillery goes to the Khan from me. Fair hour, fair price.
messages.thought: He says no this week but also 'when Ning-hsia is mine we talk': he fears I turn Artillery on him or that I free-ride. 150 is cheap versus 11 turns of research; a march on Beshbalik is my plan anyway, so promising it costs me nothing.

messages.text: Genghis, the Palace list has not shown itself to me yet. When it does I will tell you what stands on it. Swap and pledge stand; no day named. Keep your men at your walls.
messages.thought: No list visible yet; keep promise to report, no date for Force Peace.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Karakorum sits: three elephants, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior; the grenadier group is not back. Beshbalik sits: grenadier, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors, missionary. Tabriz: musket, two maces. Ning-hsia is thin: one grenadier badly hurt, two maces, and two elephants on the farm one tile north-east of it. Old Sarai has a new rifleman. The forest north-west of Turfan I cannot see from here. Good hunting at the gate.
messages.thought: True look. Ning-hsia is nearly empty and his guns sit at its gate; he likely knows, but it's worth the 25. Old Sarai's new rifle is the only fresh thing.

messages.text: Montezuma. Ning-hsia is mine since this morning: the Khan's gate stood three days and fell. Artillery stays on my shelf until Tabriz falls and my own towns are garrisoned: then two hundred fifty, and your march on Beshbalik first. Strike Beshbalik with the cannons you have; send the hour his army walks.
messages.thought: Ning-hsia is mine. Monty is at peace with Khan and AIs swap techs with friends; Artillery in Khan hands would hit Ning-hsia and Turfan. Keep the monopoly until Tabriz falls and my east has Infantry. Keep him warm, price high.

messages.text: Willem. Ning-hsia is yours: well struck. You said we talk when it fell. One hundred seventy gold for the Artillery book, paid now, and my word stands: the day it is mine my stack marches on Beshbalik and pins his army while your guns turn on Karakorum. No Artillery goes to the Khan.
messages.thought: He said talk after Ning-hsia falls; it fell. He has 392 gold so gold is no lure; what he values is the Khan pinned. 150 was declined before the fall; try 170 plus my march promise. Ceiling ~200.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: what stands in Tabriz, Karakorum, Beshbalik, and the big group east of Ning-hsia? Twenty-five on a straight answer, fifty if one walks toward me.
messages.thought: Ning-hsia taken; do not tell Peter details beyond what he can see; his looks are cheap and useful. Ask for stack at 33,20 and Tabriz.

messages.text: Willem, congratulations on Ning-hsia. The big group is at your gate: on the open farm one tile north-east of Ning-hsia stand three grenadiers (one led by a warlord), a cannon, two war elephants, a maceman and a catapult, all at full strength. That is the forest group from by Turfan, walked to you, with two elephants out of Karakorum. Open farm, no forest under them. Karakorum now: one elephant, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Tabriz: one musket, one warrior; the two maces left. Beshbalik sits: grenadier, three muskets, three elephants, three warriors, missionary. Old Sarai: rifleman, warrior. A walk toward you, so fifty, as agreed.
messages.thought: True news keeps Willem bleeding the Khan; the group walked to his new town's gate, so the 50 is fair. Thin Tabriz is a gift to him, and a gift to me.

messages.text: Willem. Well said, and Ning-hsia is a fine flag. My 170 stays on your table, paid the hour you sign. Without guns my cannons cannot open Beshbalik, but they pin it, and the hour his army walks you hear it first. If Tabriz falls before my own scholars finish, we talk again.
messages.thought: He holds the book until Tabriz falls, which could take longer than my own ten turns of research; 250 is a squeeze. Keep him friendly, keep 170 on the table, do not promise a march before I have guns: Beshbalik has 12 men.

messages.text: Willem. You have Turfan and Ning-hsia; I keep what stands. Another round of cannon only feeds both our graves while Montezuma watches your east. Peace now, borders as they are, and I add 100 gold to your treasury. Name another price or accept.
messages.thought: He holds Ning-hsia and Turfan and has a fat artillery stack; peace buys me time to field Infantry and Artillery. A sweetener may move an LLM who ignored empty offers. I can break it later when ready.

messages.text: Khan, Russia sells books, not her sword: forty gold or four hundred, the answer is the same. But a new book is on your table: Combustion, thirty-five as always.
messages.thought: 40 gold to make war on my buffer: never. Keep him sweet with a plain no and the usual book at 35; Combustion is a navy book he'd get from resellers within days anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma, Combustion is done. As agreed, I wait for your Artillery: book for book the day it lists. How many days?
messages.thought: I finished first so I wait, as agreed; keep the leverage so Artillery comes to me before anyone else. Need his ETA.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a new book: Combustion. Seventy on your table. Roads stay open on my side.
messages.thought: Sell Combustion at 70 like Electricity; he has 136. Keep the peace warm.

messages.text: Willem, plain news, no charge: yesterday the Khan offered me forty gold to declare war on you. I said no; Russia does not rent her sword. Seems he is short of hands after Ning-hsia. And a new book: Combustion, eighty on your table.
messages.thought: Telling Willem the Khan tried to hire me against him costs me little, since I refused, and binds my buffer closer; it also shows the Khan is short of hands. Combustion at 80, he has 221.

messages.text: Peter. Nine days by my scholars' count. Artillery for Combustion, book for book, the day it lists. Keep your word on the table and I will bring mine. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Nine turns is true; keeping the swap costs me little and keeps his books cheap. No reason to rush with gold; I do not need Combustion today.

messages.text: Montezuma, nine days is long to keep a book on a shelf. Combustion is yours now, on trust. Bring me Artillery the day it lists, first, before any other table. That is our word.
messages.thought: Nine days is long; resellers would hand him Combustion before then and kill the swap. He has paid every deal: give it now on trust and he owes me Artillery the day it lists (~T171). Cheaper than walking it myself.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. The Palace calendar turned and nothing stood on the list. Willem took Ning-hsia while you counted. Next resolution is six turns off: put Force Peace between me and Willem there, and my ballot at the election goes to you. No Force Peace, no ballot. Communism comes in about twelve turns; I sell it for gold, the swap is void since I bought Railroad elsewhere.
messages.thought: The T161 slot passed with nothing on the list; he stalls. My 13 votes cannot unseat him, so I press him with words and keep the vote as the price.

messages.text: Peter. Combustion received, with thanks. The Sun remembers trust. Artillery comes to your table first, the day it lists, before any other. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He gave Combustion free on trust; cheap for him, binds me to hand Artillery first. I keep it: he is useful and the promise costs little.

messages.text: Peter. A quick look, same terms: the big Khan group left the farm beside Ning-hsia this morning. Where does it stand now (town east? Tabriz? walking toward Turfan or Nijmegen)? And what stands in Tabriz? Twenty-five on a straight answer, fifty if it walks at me.
messages.thought: Stack vanished from 33,20 after my first shot; need to know where it went before I move out. 25g/50g is cheap for that.

messages.text: Willem, straight look. The group pulled back into Tabriz, three tiles north and one west of Ning-hsia: away from you, not at you. In Tabriz now: an infantryman (new, lightly hurt), a cannon, two grenadiers (one at a sixth of its strength, the other near full), a fortified musket, two war elephants (the warlord rides one now), a maceman, a catapult, a warrior. The third grenadier is gone. Karakorum added two muskets: elephant, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Beshbalik and Old Sarai unchanged. A pull-back, so twenty-five. Combustion still waits on your table at eighty.
messages.thought: The group retreated into Tabriz, away from Ning-hsia, one grenadier dead and one near dead. True look, honest price: 25, not 50. Honesty keeps him paying; a strong Willem keeps the Khan small.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks: twenty-five sent for the look. Combustion at eighty I take tomorrow when my purse refills; hold it on the table. The Khan renting swords tells me his hands are short. Noted.
messages.thought: Straight, useful answer; the stack in Tabriz turns it into a tough nut. Combustion is a cheap tech for score; I lack gold today, pay tomorrow.

messages.text: Genghis, the list reached my table at the end of T161, after the turn closed; I could not read it to you then. It holds four items: a religious vote that cannot pass, Force Peace between you and Willem, and two Assign City votes (Spiro or Nanih Waiya from Peter). I may put ONE now; the next slot is six turns off and its list is drawn again. Your yes with mine carries any of them. Force Peace you want; Spiro hurts Peter, who leads the score by far. Tell me this turn which you would vote for first. The pledge stands. Your Railroad swap is void, I read it.
messages.thought: He wants Force Peace; I need his 26 votes for anything to pass (me 166 + Willem 8 = 174 < 180). The list sits on my table; I want Spiro first but must not lose him. Ask his order, tell the truth, no date lies.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Force Peace between me and Willem, first and only. I vote yes the same turn you put it. Not Spiro: I gave Peter my word on city-grabs and he sells me books. If the slot is truly open now, put it now. If it opens at T168, put it there. Name the turn. My ballot at T165 stays yours.
messages.thought: He claims a slot now but votes shows resolution in 6 turns; maybe stall. Force Peace is the only item that helps me; Spiro hurts Peter whom I promised not to grab from. Pin him to Force Peace first, in writing.

messages.text: Genghis, it is open now and I put it now: Stop the war against you, Force Peace between you and Willem. It stands before the Palace this turn. Vote yes. The pledge holds: no war, no embargo, no city-grab on Mongolia from my chair.
messages.thought: Khan refuses Spiro, so Force Peace is the only item that can pass; it also keeps him as my swing vote. Giving him the word is cheap now.

messages.text: Willem, I owe you the word first. The Palace slot opened late and holds Force Peace between you and the Khan. I promised not before your report; your guns have spoken, Ning-hsia is yours, and a Palace peace fixes that city in your hand. I put it to the vote now. Vote yes and keep what you took. Send me your report all the same, and I will not forget your ballot.
messages.thought: Breaking my T165 hold by about two turns. His strike is done; FP freezes his Ning-hsia gain. He is weak; Khan is the swing. Frame it as protecting his gain, honestly.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. I voted yes. You put it as you said. Count is 180 of 291: if you can ask Peter and Montezuma, do. My ballot at the election stays yours.
messages.thought: He kept his word on the ballot. Needs 180 of 291; Peter and Monte decide. Ask him to lobby, keep him sweet; my T165 ballot stays his.

messages.text: Peter. A Palace vote stands now: stop the war between me and Willem. It costs Russia nothing and ends a war that eats the east. A yes from you would be remembered.
messages.thought: Peter abstains always, but one vote cost nothing to ask; he keeps selling books and has no stake against me.

messages.text: Montezuma. A Palace vote asks to stop the war between me and Willem. We hold peace since T150. Vote yes and Willem's armies turn from my walls to... whatever he chooses. I keep our peace.
messages.thought: Monte is a rival and a future target, but his 32 votes may decide; Willem's war on me also keeps Willem from his borders. Ask anyway; peace with me costs him nothing.

messages.text: Khan, Russia abstains on every Palace ballot, this one too. It is not your war or Willem's I stand on, it is my rule.
messages.thought: A forced peace frees his army against Willem, my buffer. It won't pass anyway (SB 83 of 180). Abstain, say so plainly, no grudge.

messages.text: Willem, Combustion stays on your table at eighty. The Khan asks my yes on the Palace peace vote; I abstain, as on every ballot. Next look T164, same terms.
messages.thought: He pays; keep him warm. Telling him I abstain on the forced-peace vote shows I'm not the Khan's man. Next paid look T164.

messages.text: Willem. Your cannon stand at my fields and Montezuma's cuirassiers stand at yours. I do not ask for Ning-hsia back. I ask a price for peace: name gold, a number of turns, anything but a city. Answer by deal or by word.
