messages.thought: He declined silently twice; he thinks he wins. A price probe costs nothing and shows whether he wants gold or only land. I will not give a city.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Report, as promised: Ning-hsia fell on T161, three days of guns. The Khan's big stack, ten men, now sits in Tabriz, three tiles from it, and Tabriz is the door to Nijmegen and Ning-hsia both. My guns need three days to heal. I abstain on the ballot today, not against you: let the vote fail for now, and in five turns I will stand with you on a Palace peace gladly, with Tabriz in my hand or the stack broken. My word on that. Your ballot for Resident stays remembered.
messages.thought: Bull put Force Peace on the table two days before his own promise date; I want Tabriz (10 units there, my guns healing) so I abstain, not vote no, and give him the report he asked for, framed as asking for a few turns.

messages.text: Genghis, I put it and it is before the Palace; my ballot went in with yours. If the war still shows, Peter or Montezuma may be defying it. I will ask them. Your ballot at the election stays mine, and my pledge stays yours. Keep your men at your walls.
messages.thought: The Force Peace vote left my table; war still stands in the records, so maybe the count is pending. Keep Khan warm for T165/166 ballot; no new promise.

messages.text: Montezuma, it has been a long silence. The Palace chair is mine and the next slot is five turns off. I mean to put Spiro (Russian, west of my Mound City) to the vote, assigned to me. Peter leads every score by a wide road; full members like you and me cannot lose cities this way, only his kind. Vote yes and I give you Biology the turn it passes, no gold asked. Tell me yes or no.
messages.thought: I need a second yes besides Khan for Assign City Spiro; Monte's 64 votes carry it alone with mine (166+64>180). Offer Biology after it passes; hide the Religious Victory aim.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Tabriz sits: two infantry now (one new), cannon, one grenadier (the hurt one is gone), musket, two war elephants with the warlord, maceman, catapult, warrior. Karakorum added an infantryman: infantry, two muskets, elephant, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior. Beshbalik unchanged: grenadier, musket, three elephants, three warriors, missionary. Old Sarai: rifleman, warrior. Nothing walks at you; your cuirassier and musket two tiles east of Tabriz stand close to that stack. Twenty-five, as agreed. Next look T167.
messages.thought: True look; Tabriz gained an infantry, lost a grenadier; no walk. 25.

messages.text: Bull. Biology has been mine since T149, so your coin is old. And Spiro is Peter's: his libraries feed my scholars, and I will not vote against a table I trade at. My answer is no. The Sun will have a new gun in about eight days; you hear first after Russia. Keep the Khan's riders busy, and we stay friends.
messages.thought: Bull offers a book I have owned since T149; the vote would feed his Palace share and cost me Peter, my cheap tech pipe. Refuse, keep him friendly: he is my Artillery buyer and the Khan's pin.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: what stands in Tabriz now (count each kind, any hurt), what in Karakorum, and does any group walk toward Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan? Twenty-five on a straight answer, fifty if one walks at me. Combustion is mine, thanks.
messages.thought: Need Tabriz garrison exact before I commit 7 guns; 25g is cheap. Peter has no stake against me and sells honest looks.

messages.text: Willem, your letter crossed mine; here is a fresh look, so it counts as one. Tabriz now: four infantry (two full, one lightly hurt, one at about a third of its strength), cannon, musket, two war elephants with the warlord, maceman, catapult, warrior. No grenadier left. Karakorum: two muskets, elephant, three catapults, trebuchet, archer, warrior; its infantry left, likely to Tabriz. Beshbalik: infantry, musket, three elephants, three warriors, missionary. Old Sarai: rifleman, warrior. Nothing walks toward Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan. Tabriz digs in, it does not march. Twenty-five for the day, once. Next look T167.
messages.thought: His ask crossed my morning report. Fresh look: Tabriz swapped grenadier for infantry (now 4, one at a third), Karakorum's infantry left, Beshbalik's grenadier is infantry now. Nothing walks at him. One fee for the day, 25, not twice.

messages.text: Willem, thank you for the report: Ning-hsia is yours and the news is honest. The next Palace slot opens in four turns. The Khan has waited long for his peace, and I mean to put it there; a peace fixes Ning-hsia in your hand. Use these days well, guns or walls. And keep me told if his stack turns toward Nijmegen or my road. Your ballot for the chair, in three turns, I will remember too.
messages.thought: His abstain was moot: my own ballot never landed, so the vote failed by my miss, not his. Khan's word is owed and the Khan stack must not feel rewarded. Put peace at T168, keep his friendship with plain words, do not reveal my miss.

messages.text: Genghis, the peace fell short, and I must correct my last word: my own ballot did not reach the table that day, my error, not another's. Willem also held his hand. At the next slot, four turns off, I put it again if it stands on the list, and this time I vote. Your ballot for the chair in three turns I ask of you. The pledge stands: no war, no embargo, no city-grab on Mongolia. Keep your men at your walls.
messages.thought: Correct my false line honestly: my ballot did not land. Promise Force Peace again at T168 (passes with mine + his). Keep pledge. Do not mention Willem's Tabriz condition.

messages.text: Montezuma, understood: Spiro stays where it is. When the Sun has its new gun, name a fair price in gold and send it; I pay for what I do not research myself. We stay friends.
messages.thought: He refuses Spiro; keep the tech trade channel open, he will have a new tech in ~8 turns and I should buy not research it.

messages.text: Bull. Thanks. Nothing walks at Nijmegen or your road: the Khan digs in at Tabriz, infantry and guns, and I send the hour if that changes. My guns need until about the 170th to reach him; my word stands as I gave it: when Tabriz is mine or his stack is broken, I vote with you on the peace. If the fourth day's slot cannot wait, tell me, and I will say on the 167th whether Tabriz is too hard. Your chair has my ballot.
messages.thought: The Palace slot at T168 comes before my guns reach Tabriz (T169-170). A forced peace then freezes Khan's 12-man stack and leaves me 2 cities short. Ask for one slot's grace without breaking my T163 word: it was conditional on Tabriz taken or the stack broken. Stay warm, give him the news he asked for.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. My ballot at the election is yours, as I said. Put the stop-the-war vote again at the next slot and vote it. Peter abstains by rule, so ask Montezuma. Pledge held on both sides.
messages.thought: Force Peace cannot reach 180 votes without Peter, who abstains; SB's errors cost me nothing, but I keep the ballot since 13 votes change nothing and his pledge protects my west.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, your Palace picks a new ballot in three days. Russia abstains, as always, unless a ballot names Russia. What will you put on the table? And tomorrow a new book lists: Refrigeration, seventy for you, as before.
messages.thought: SB is Resident and Annoyed; I am only a voting member, open to a war, embargo or city-assign ballot. Learn his next pick, warn gently, keep him buying.

messages.text: Willem, I hear you. The Palace slot opens in three days and the Khan has waited long for his peace; I gave him my word too. Tell me on the 167th straight: is Tabriz within your reach, or not? If your guns can break that stack within days, I will weigh it. If not, the peace fixes Ning-hsia in your hand. Keep sending me the hour.
messages.thought: Slot is fixed at T168 and Khan has my word; Willem's 8 votes are not needed. But if Tabriz really falls, the stack broken is good for me, so keep the door open without a promise.

messages.text: Genghis, your word is heard. At the slot, in three days, I put the stop-the-war vote if it stands on the list, and I vote it the same turn; you vote with me. My pledge holds: no war, no embargo, no city-grab on Mongolia. Keep your men at Tabriz and away from my road at Poverty Point.
messages.thought: His election ballot is moot, I win alone. Keep him calm and in his walls: promise Force Peace at the slot if it stands, ask him to keep the Tabriz stack off my road.

messages.text: Bull. The hour, early: the four guns in Ning-hsia are healed, three more join them on the 167th. They march that day, stand on the hill two tiles from Tabriz on the 168th, fire on the 169th. Tabriz is flat ground with four infantry, a cannon, a musket, two elephants and more: hard, not closed. On the 167th I give you my plain answer as the guns see it. If the slot cannot wait past the 169th, my word stands: I vote with you for the peace.
messages.thought: Giving Bull the exact hour costs nothing and may buy a slot of grace; if he cannot wait, peace still keeps Ning-hsia and lets me build economy, so I am not bluffing.

messages.text: Willem, Refrigeration is done: grocers and fresh food for your towns. I would trade it book for book for your Artillery, on your table now. If you keep the guns home, say so, and it is yours for eighty instead. Next look at the Khan comes tomorrow, same terms.
messages.thought: Willem holds Artillery; a swap now saves me five days to Rocketry. He may refuse guns; then I sell for 80.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, as promised: Refrigeration, seventy, on your table now.
messages.thought: Promised price, keep him buying and content.

messages.text: Montezuma, Refrigeration lists today: fifty-five, friend price. And I still keep the place on my table for your Artillery, first, as you swore.
messages.thought: Friend price; keep reminding of Artillery owed.

messages.text: Khan, a new book: Refrigeration, thirty-five as always.
messages.thought: Non-war book; his gold drains his war chest.

messages.text: Peter. Refrigeration is mine, 55 gold paid, with thanks. Artillery still comes to your table first, in about five days. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Cheap book, keeps the pipe warm; he still gets Artillery first as promised.

messages.text: Montezuma, received with thanks. Five days then: I keep the first seat warm for your Artillery. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He pays every time; keep the Artillery date fixed in his mind, ~T171.

messages.text: Peter. The guns stay home, as you guessed. Refrigeration for gold then: sixty is on your table now. If it must be eighty, say so and I sign. Your look at the Khan tomorrow, same terms.
messages.thought: Artillery never leaves my table; Refrigeration is worth ~60-80 to me. Open low, he will say 80 and I take it tomorrow or now.

messages.text: Willem, eighty it is, same as Combustion: on your table now. The guns at home I understand. Tomorrow your look at the Khan, same terms.
messages.thought: He said he signs at 80; same price as Combustion. Keep him square and buying; guns refusal is fair.

messages.text: Peter. Eighty signed: Refrigeration is mine, thanks. Your look at the Khan tomorrow, same terms: Tabriz count by kind and any hurt, Karakorum, and whether anything walks.
messages.thought: Eighty for Refrigeration is fair and saves 12 turns of research; sign it, keep him warm, his look tomorrow is the one that decides Tabriz.

messages.text: Peter, one ballot only: a peace between the Khan and Willem. Nothing on my table names Russia. Refrigeration I finish myself in four days; keep your seventy for a book I lack.
messages.thought: He is fishing for my Palace plan and gold. The slot list is public to members anyway; naming Force Peace costs nothing and nothing names Russia. Keep Spiro and the Assign City idea hidden. Do not buy Refrigeration: 4 turns left, buying wastes my beakers.

messages.text: Willem, thank you for the hour. The slot opens on the 168th and the Khan holds my word. Give me your plain answer on the 167th: if your guns will break Tabriz within one day of arriving, say so. If not, a peace on the 168th keeps Ning-hsia in your hand and your guns alive.
messages.thought: He is honest and gives the hour early. I keep my word to Khan; his guns would be cancelled by the peace, but they stay alive. Do not promise a delay; ask for his plain answer on the 167th and decide then.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: Tabriz by kind and any hurt, Karakorum, and does anything walk toward Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan? Twenty-five straight, fifty if a stack walks at me.
messages.thought: Need Tabriz count to decide go/no-go with Bull today; pay 25g straight as promised.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Tabriz sits, nothing new: four infantry (three full, one at three quarters), cannon, musket, two war elephants with the warlord, maceman, catapult, warrior. Karakorum: three infantry now (its muskets are gone, made over), elephant, three catapults, trebuchet, warrior. Beshbalik: three infantry (one at half strength), three elephants, three warriors, missionary. Old Sarai: rifleman, archer, warrior. Nothing walks toward Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan. Also: the Palace votes tomorrow, again on peace between you and the Khan. Russia abstains, as always. Twenty-five, as agreed. Next look T170.
messages.thought: True look, as always; he keeps bleeding the Khan. The Palace ballot will be public tomorrow anyway, telling him costs me nothing and buys goodwill.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, a plain answer, thank you. Then Russia abstains, as I said. Keep your seventy; when a book lists that you lack, you will hear of it.
messages.thought: He researches it himself and keeps his gold; fine. Ballot is harmless to me; abstain. Next book is Industrialism = tanks: do not promise it to the man next to Spiro.

messages.text: Willem, your letter crossed my look; the look stands, I checked again just now: nothing moved in Tabriz or Karakorum. Twenty-five received, we are square. Next look T170.
messages.thought: His ask came before my report; he has read it and paid 25. Nothing has moved since. Square; a short receipt keeps him buying.

messages.text: Bull. Plain answer, as you asked: no. Tabriz holds four fresh infantry, a cannon, two elephants and more on a city wall of culture, and the Khan turns another musket into an infantryman every few days. My guns will not break it in a day, and I will not spend them on a bad day. So my word stands: I vote YES on your peace on the 168th. I have also put a peace to the Khan by my own hand, with his gold; if he signs it today your slot is free for something else, if not, my ballot is yes. Ning-hsia stays mine either way. Thank you for waiting.
messages.thought: Tabriz is four fresh infantry in a stack of twelve; Artillery 18 vs Infantry 20 is a bad trade, not a one-day break. Back the peace, bank the goodwill, sell him Refrigeration, get Khan's gold directly.

messages.text: Bull. The Khan signed the peace with me this hour, his gold in my hand: the war is over, so your slot on the 168th is free for other work. Thank you for the grace you gave me. My ballot for the chair stays yours. Refrigeration is on your table at 160 if you want it for your cities.
messages.thought: Khan took the 84g and signed; Bull's slot is free and I owe him a clean report. Keeps his goodwill and the chair.

messages.text: Genghis, Willem has signed his peace with you, so the stop-the-war vote is not needed and I will not put it. My pledge stands: no war, no embargo, no city-grab on Mongolia. When Communism is yours, name a fair price in gold and I will pay it.
messages.thought: Peace is made without me, so my pledge cost nothing and kept his goodwill. I want his 26 votes later and Communism cheap; do not mention Spiro.

messages.text: Willem, thank you for the plain word and for making your peace. Ning-hsia is safe in your hand now. Refrigeration I finish myself in two days; keep it. Your ballot for the chair I remember. Tell me if anyone walks toward Nijmegen or my road.
messages.thought: He kept his word and ended the war; keep him friendly, he is my 8 votes and my eyes on Tabriz. Refrigeration I finish myself in 2 turns.

messages.text: Bull. Refrigeration lists on my shelf, the one book you lack: 200 gold, on your table now. The new gun follows in three days, and you were promised to hear first after Russia. Keep your coin ready.
messages.thought: Bull holds 422 gold and lacks only Refrigeration; sell it dear, Artillery later at a higher price.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Peace with Willem is signed, the vote is moot. Communism comes in about five turns. My price is 110 gold, paid on delivery. Your pledge is heard; mine holds.
messages.thought: He holds ~136g and pays for Communism; naming the price early anchors it high. Pledge costs me nothing and keeps the Palace chair friendly.

messages.text: Peter. My scholars press harder: Artillery lists in two days, and it comes to your table first, as sworn. Tell me which book you write next, so I do not repeat your work. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Keep Peter warm: he sells me techs at 50 each, far cheaper than research; tell him earlier date, ask his next book so I stop duplicating.

messages.text: Montezuma, I finish Refrigeration myself in two days, so keep your shelf copy. The new gun I do want: name a fair price in gold when it is done, and send it to me after Russia as you said.
messages.thought: Refrigeration lands in my own hands in 2 turns; 200 gold is a fool's price and buying would waste my beakers. Keep him warm for the gun tech, which I do want, at a fair price.

messages.text: Genghis, heard. 110 gold on delivery for Communism, agreed. Send it when it is yours and I pay that day.
messages.thought: Nothing to argue; price 110 is fair for Communism and I promised to pay. Keep him calm, avoid anything about Spiro.

messages.text: Willem, so the Khan and you have peace. Good for your towns. But his army is free now: four infantry in Tabriz, four in Karakorum, three in Beshbalik, none of it busy. If you still want my looks, same terms: twenty-five every third day, fifty the day a stack walks your way. Say yes and the next comes T170. Say no and we stay friends all the same.
messages.thought: His war ended T167; my looks lose value to him and my buffer is gone. Keep him buying and keep my eyes on the Khan's freed army; true news only. No sale today.

messages.text: Bull. Keep your Refrigeration, you earned it. The new gun is Artillery, str 18, and it lists in two days. After Russia sees it, it comes to you: my price is 320 gold. Keep your coin ready.
messages.thought: Bull has 422 gold and no rival seller; open high at 320, floor 150. Peter gets it first as sworn, then Bull. His Refrigeration refusal shows he researches what he can and pays only for what he cannot.

messages.text: Montezuma, thank you for the hour. Three hundred and twenty is too much: my own scholars reach the gun in about ten days, and Russia sells its books for seventy. For the gun the day it lists, I pay 110 gold. Name your answer when it is on your shelf.
messages.thought: 320 is a fool's price: my labs reach Artillery in ten turns, Peter sells books at 70. Still, saving ~9 turns is worth ~120-150 gold to me; open at 110, firm second. Do not hint at war plans.

messages.text: Peter. Yes: same terms, twenty-five every third day, fifty the day a stack walks my way. Next look T170.
messages.thought: Looks during peace still cost only 25g per 3 days and the Khan is Furious; keep the feed alive.

messages.text: Bull. A hundred and ten is an insult to the work: ten days of your scholars is two thousand beakers saved. Russia sells nothing until I give it, and Russia comes first, then you. My price falls to 220 gold, the turn the gun lists. Think, and keep your coin ready.
messages.thought: Bull has 422 gold and pays only for what he lacks; ten days of his own research is real, so my floor is 150. Counter 220 to land near 170, deliver after Peter's seat.

messages.text: Montezuma, you drop fast, and I thank you. Two hundred twenty is still more than the work costs me: Russia sells its books for seventy, and I can wait a few days for it. When the gun is on your shelf I pay 160 gold, that day, and your gold is in your hand at once. Name yes or no then.
messages.thought: His beakers argument is fair, 220 is a decent price for 2700 beakers, but he fell 100 in one step so there is room. Offer 160, mention Peter's cheap resale as my alternative, do not hint at the Palace race. I keep the 120g for Khan free.

messages.text: Montezuma, two days then, good. I write Industrialism now, done in three days: yours at friend price the hour it lists. After your guns come I write Rocketry. So leave those two alone. Write Radio, or Flight if you like it better: when yours lists we trade book for book, as before. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: A research split with my best payer: he avoids my books and writes one on my Fusion path (Radio) that I can swap for. Industrialism to him is fine, he is far from me.

messages.text: Bull. Done: 160 gold, paid the day the gun lists, which is tomorrow. Russia's seat first, then yours the same day. Keep the coin in hand.
messages.thought: 160 is above my floor 150 and Peter will resell Artillery at 70 within days, so the window is the listing day; take it, no more haggling.

messages.text: Peter. Agreed: Industrialism and Rocketry are yours, I write Flight. Artillery lists tomorrow, one turn sooner than I said, and it comes to your table first, as sworn. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Peter keeps me supplied at friend prices; agree, leave Industrialism and Rocketry to him, write Flight, keep the Artillery promise tomorrow.

messages.text: Montezuma, good: Flight is yours to write. Tomorrow I take your Artillery, as agreed for Combustion. Industrialism lists the day after, friend price. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He keeps his word and splits research cleanly. Artillery tomorrow pays for my Combustion; then I write Rocketry. Industrialism at about 55 is safe with him.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. I voted no on Spiro, as I told you at T162: my word to Peter. It is not against you. Communism for 110 gold still stands, and my ballot at the election is yours.
messages.thought: Spiro cannot pass (SB 84 + me 13 + Monte 34 < 187); a no keeps my Peter promise and costs me nothing. Telling SB early keeps the 110g Communism sale safe.

messages.text: Bull. My eight votes are yes on Spiro. Nothing walks toward Nijmegen or your road; I send the hour if that changes.
messages.thought: Spiro vote cannot reach 187 without Peter or unknown votes; a yes costs me little, weakens the runaway, and keeps Bull warm. Peter may notice; his looks are cheap to replace.

messages.text: Montezuma, thank you: 160 gold tomorrow for the gun, agreed. One more matter, today: a ballot on Spiro is open. With your yes, the city comes to me, and I pay you 250 gold the turn it is mine, apart from the 160 for the gun. Spiro is my old city; the Khan voted no, Willem yes. Your vote decides.
messages.thought: Monte holds the swing: 168+8+68 = 244 passes Spiro; I pay gold only after the city is mine. 250 is cheap for a pop-9 city. He loves coin and Artillery deal shows he is honest on prices.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: Tabriz, Karakorum, Beshbalik by kind, and does anything walk at Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan? Twenty-five straight, fifty if a stack walks.
messages.thought: Check whether he still sells looks after my Spiro vote.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Tabriz sits as before: four infantry, cannon, musket, two war elephants, maceman, catapult, warrior. Karakorum: five infantry now (one more than last look, its warrior gone), elephant, three catapults, trebuchet. Beshbalik: three infantry, three elephants, three warriors, a missionary. Old Sarai: one infantry, two warriors. Nothing walks toward Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan. Twenty-five, as agreed. Next look T173.
messages.thought: True look as always; nothing walks, so 25. Karakorum grew one infantry: worth telling, he pays for kinds.

messages.text: Peter. Artillery is on your table, as sworn. One change: my coin goes to the army for a season, so my scholars rest and Flight will crawl. Write what you like; I buy your books at friend price, Industrialism first. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Artillery delivered as sworn. I am dropping research to fund the war chest; better tell him now so he doesn't wait on my Flight, and keep buying his books for gold.

messages.text: Bull. The gun is yours and your 160 is received, thank you. On Spiro my vote is already cast, and it stands. 250 does not move me; the city is Russia's friend to lose, not mine to give. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He paid 160 and now fishes for the Spiro vote again. My vote is cast no; Peter's pipe matters more than 250 and Bull's Palace share must not grow.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Artillery is on my table: your word kept to the day, and I remember it. Industrialism lists tomorrow, fifty-five, friend price, first hour. Then I write Rocketry; Flight stays yours. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He kept his word to the turn. Thank him; Industrialism tomorrow at 55 keeps him my best payer. Rocketry is my next book.

messages.text: Peter. Twenty-five paid, thank you: a straight answer. Next look T173, same terms.
messages.thought: Straight look, paid on promise; Khan is turning everything to Infantry, which confirms I need Tanks, not more Artillery. Keep him warm and cheap.

messages.text: Montezuma, understood: a season for the army. Industrialism is yours at fifty-five tomorrow, first hour. One question between friends: whose door does that army knock on? If it is the Khan's, my scout sits by Tabriz and you get his counts free while it lasts.
messages.thought: His Texcoco stack doubled its cannon (8). War is coming; I want it pointed at the Khan, not at Willem my buyer and buffer. Offer free looks at the Khan to steer him, and learn the target.

messages.text: Peter. The army knocks where the door is weakest; I name no door before it opens. Your scout's counts by Tabriz are welcome, send them free while it lasts. Industrialism first hour tomorrow. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He probes my target; Khan is it, but naming it costs nothing only if Peter keeps quiet, and he is a rival. Take the free scouting, give no name.

messages.text: Montezuma, the gun is on my shelf and 160 gold is in your hand: our word is kept on both sides. One plain question: how did you cast your ballot on Spiro? The city did not come to me. In five days a new slot opens; if you will say yes to the old town Nanih Waiya, my 250 gold stands, paid the turn it is mine.
messages.thought: Artillery bought as agreed. Spiro vote failed silently; need to learn how Monte voted without begging. Ask plain, keep 250g offer alive for Nanih Waiya at T175 slot.

messages.text: Genghis, I heard you. A man keeps his word to Peter, I do not hold it against you. Communism for 110 gold stands; when it lists I pay that day. My pledge to you stands too.
messages.thought: He voted no on Spiro for Peter; I keep the pledge and the Communism deal, his 26 votes may matter later.

messages.text: Willem, thank you for the yes on Spiro. It did not carry, but I remember who stood with me. Send the hour if anything walks toward Nijmegen or my road.
messages.thought: He voted yes on Spiro, costless loyalty; keep him warm, 8 votes.

messages.text: Bull. Plain answer: my ballot on Spiro was NO, and it stands. The coin did not buy it and will not. Nanih Waiya I judge on the day the slot opens, by whose city it is and what it does to the Palace. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He keeps fishing for the Spiro vote; a plain NO costs nothing and keeps my word clean. Nanih Waiya I judge when it opens: do not sell the vote cheap, his Palace share must not grow.

messages.text: Montezuma, Industrialism is on your table, fifty-five, first hour as sworn. And the counts, free: Tabriz sits as before, four infantry, a cannon, two war elephants and odds. Karakorum fattens: six infantry, catapults, a trebuchet. Beshbalik is thin: two infantry, three elephants, three warriors, a missionary. Old Sarai: one infantry, two warriors. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Word kept to the hour. Free Khan counts steer his cannon at Beshbalik (2 inf only) and away from Willem. All true.

messages.text: Willem, a new book lists today: Industrialism. Battleships, marines, and later the iron cart. Eighty, same as the last. It is on your table. Next look T173, as agreed.
messages.thought: Sell the new book same hour; 80 like Refrigeration. Look stays T173.

messages.text: Peter, you said I would hear when a book lists that I lack. Industrialism is on your shelf, not mine. Seventy gold is on your table now, as before.
messages.thought: Industrialism gives Tanks; Peter has them already and I must not be behind. 70g for a 5000-beaker tech is a bargain if he sells; if he refuses it tells me he is preparing something.

messages.text: Peter. Industrialism received, and the counts are good coin: thank you. Keep the scout where he stands while he lives. Rocketry when it lists, same friend price. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Counts confirm Old Sarai/Beshbalik are weak; thanks keeps the free scouting coming, and I name no target and promise nothing.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, you heard, and you came first to the counter. Seventy is fair; Industrialism is yours. The roads stay open both ways.
messages.thought: He'd have it from resellers in days; 70 now beats his grudge. But tanks by Spiro: I strengthen the garrison. Keep it short and fair.

messages.text: Montezuma, the scout stays where he stands. Rocketry lists in four days, fifty-five, first hour, as before. Your second offer for Industrialism I let pass: you hold the book already, no need to pay twice. Next counts T173.
messages.thought: Keep my best payer warm; the scout stays because his eyes serve me and Willem too. Your stale 55 offer I declined: you already have the book.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: Tabriz, Karakorum, Beshbalik by kind, and does anything walk at Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan? Twenty-five straight, fifty if a stack walks.
messages.thought: Look due; keep early warning, peace lock ends T177.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. Tabriz sits as before: four infantry, cannon, musket, two war elephants, maceman, catapult, warrior. Karakorum: six infantry, elephant, three catapults, trebuchet. Beshbalik: two infantry, three elephants, three warriors, a missionary. Old Sarai: one infantry, two warriors. Nothing walks toward Ning-hsia, Nijmegen or Turfan. Twenty-five, as agreed. Next look T176.
messages.thought: True look, nothing changed; 25 owed per terms. Still not telling him of Monte's stack.

messages.text: Montezuma, the counts, free as promised. Tabriz unchanged: four infantry, a cannon, two war elephants and odds. Karakorum: six infantry, catapults, a trebuchet. Beshbalik still thin: two infantry, three elephants, three warriors, a missionary. Old Sarai: one infantry, two warriors. Rocketry in three days, fifty-five, first hour.
messages.thought: Free counts as promised; Beshbalik still thin. Steer his cannon at the Khan, away from Willem.

messages.text: Peter. Thank you for the look. The twenty-five is already in your purse (paid today), so I closed the second slip. Next look T176, same terms.
messages.thought: Peter's #99 is the same 25g I already paid by civ give this turn; paying twice is waste. His look is straight and square, no reason to cool him.

messages.text: Genghis, Communism for 110 gold was our word, and the gold is on your table now, paid the hour you accept. The big gun was never in that bargain, and I do not sell it. Take the gold; our peace and my pledge stand.
messages.thought: He tried to add Artillery to our 110 gold bargain; a big gun in the hands of a neighbour with a 10-stack three tiles from Poverty Point is not something I sell. Keep him warm: gold is on the table, same price as agreed.

messages.text: Peter. I have Communism, a book you lack. I offer it for your Artillery, Industrialism and 150 gold. Look at the deal on your table.
messages.thought: Peter is rich and lacks Communism; I want Artillery and Industrialism cheaply, plus gold. He sells books, so ask for a swap

messages.text: Willem, received, all square. A clean ledger is a good ledger. Next look T176.
messages.thought: He paid and closed my duplicate slip himself: square and honest. One line keeps the buyer warm; still not telling him of Monte stack (5 cannon + 2 artillery at Texcoco).

messages.text: Khan. Bull broke his word to me today and took Nijmegen; his guns and horse stand three days from Tabriz as well. I ask open borders both ways, nothing more: my road to his stack runs over your fields, your own peace holds. The offer is on your table; I add 60 gold the day you sign.
messages.thought: Khan hates me but Bull's guns sit near Tabriz too; I need my army out of Ning-hsia and open borders is the key. Not revealing my real plan: Bull's cities.

messages.text: Genghis, guns and engines stay off my table for you; that has not changed and will not. Communism I will buy with gold: ninety is on your table now, plain coin for a plain book. And a word on the Palace: Sitting Bull sits long in that chair and now he wars. In two days I vote Montezuma for Resident. Your thirteen votes decide it.
messages.thought: Never war books to him. Communism is worth ~2251 beakers to me and resells to Monte/Willem; 90 gold is a fair price and harmless. Also need his 13 votes to unseat SB at the T176 election.

messages.text: Bull. Four days ago you thanked me for a yes. Today Nijmegen is yours and the ledger is open. Tell me what you want for the peace, and for my town. Until then my answer is the one you chose.
messages.thought: He sneak-attacked right after thanking me; I want Nijmegen and his weak border cities Poverty Point and Mesa Verde. Probing his terms while my tanks arrive; no concession.

messages.text: Willem, a hard day; I saw Nijmegen fall. This look is free, a neighbour's word: Sitting Bull's guns stand outside, on the hill with the windmill one tile north of the Nijmegen ruins: four artillery and one grenadier, nothing more. Poverty Point behind them holds a rifleman and an archer. From today my looks cover his camp too, same terms. And the Palace: in two days I vote Montezuma for Resident, to take the chair from a man at war with you. Your eight votes count.
messages.thought: SB is my #2 rival and is eating my best buyer. A free true look on SB's siege stack builds goodwill and helps Willem hit back; SB must not learn it. Also need Willem's 8 votes for Monte at the election.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Palace election comes in two days. Sitting Bull has held the chair long and now uses his hands for war. Russia votes for you, the Palace's builder. With your thirty-four, my thirty-five, and the Khan and Willem beside us, it is ninety against his eighty-six. Ask them too. Rocketry lists in two days, fifty-five, first hour.
messages.thought: Monte as Resident is far safer for me than SB (only Willem and I can be war-voted or lose cities by assign-city; SB wants Spiro/Nanih Waiya back). Need all four: me 35 + Monte 34 + Khan 13 + Willem 8 = 90 vs SB 86.

messages.text: Willem, you ask my price. It is towns, not gold: The Hague and Ning-hsia. Gold buys nothing here. When they stand under my flag, I will speak of peace. Until then Nijmegen is the first step, not the last.
messages.thought: I want The Hague and Ning-hsia, not his gold; cities cannot be traded while at war, so peace now only lets him rebuild. The demand is high on purpose; my guns keep walking while he thinks.

messages.text: Peter. Your vote is taken and remembered. I will ask the Khan and Willem today. While I hold the chair, no war resolution falls on Russia and Spiro is not Bull's to take. Rocketry first hour on the day it lists. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Chair denies Bull the power to force me to war on Peter and keeps Spiro safe; Peter's 35 votes are a gift, the promise costs me little. Win the Khan and Willem too.

messages.text: Willem. Bull took Nijmegen with his hands, and his chair decides which wars the Palace calls on its voting members, you among them. I have no war resolution for you in mind. Your 8 votes for me in two days take the chair out of his hands. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Willem is at war with Bull; his 8 votes could tip 90-86. No binding promise, just a hint the chair is a danger to him under Bull.

messages.text: Genghis. Sitting Bull took Tabriz from you and holds the Palace chair. The chair decides which resolutions fall on whom. I ask your 13 votes for me in two days. From my chair no resolution will be put against Mongolia. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Khan's 13 votes are the swing. He is my target; a friendly ask keeps him calm before T180. Promise is cheap: full members cannot be struck by war resolutions anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma. My 13 votes are not free. Look at the deal on your table: I give you Communism, a book you lack, and you give me Artillery and Industrialism. Sign it and my ballot at the election is yours. No deal, no promise. Peter votes for you already; with me you win.
messages.thought: Monte's stack at Texcoco is my worst threat; my ballot is a real chip. I sell Communism for his two guns and promise the ballot only if the deal is signed; if he refuses I keep my word to SB.

messages.text: Genghis. Artillery stays in my arsenal: it is not for sale at any price. Industrialism I will give, for your Communism and 200 gold. That is on your table now. Your 13 votes decide the chair, and the chair is what keeps Mongolia safe from Palace resolutions. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Artillery is the gun that kills his walls; never. Industrialism is harmless and I want his 478 gold drained before T180 so he cannot hurry defenders. The vote is a bonus, not a promise I trust.

messages.text: Montezuma, a fair word, and I take it as a contract. Russia votes you in two days. Rocketry lists tomorrow: fifty-five, first hour, as sworn. Fresh counts on the Khan come with it.
messages.thought: Monte's promise is the shield I wanted: no war ballot on Russia, Spiro mine. Keep him warm; Rocketry 55 tomorrow as sworn.

messages.text: Peter. Thank you for the free look: it was true. Today Bull's whole force walked INTO Nijmegen: guns, rifles, horse, a missionary. My eight go to Montezuma in two days. Your next look T176, same terms; add Mesa Verde and Chaco Canyon.
messages.thought: Peter's looks are cheap and honest; his vote helps unseat my enemy. I give nothing about my Tanks.

messages.text: Monty. My eight votes go to you in two days. Bull took a town by treachery and I do not forget it. Send word if Bull's riders pass your road.
messages.thought: Cheap goodwill; I would vote against Bull anyway. Not asking him for war yet.

messages.text: Genghis, Communism received, ninety paid: we are square. Your second slip I let pass; the book is already on my shelf.
messages.thought: He took my 90; the 200 slip is a duplicate. Keep him square and pleased.

messages.text: Willem. Your 8 votes are taken and remembered. If Bull's riders pass my road, you will hear it. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: His 8 votes help me beat Bull; no promise needed, just keep him warm. He sits 4 tiles from Texcoco; do not tip my plan on the Khan.

messages.text: Montezuma. Industrialism and gold changed hands: we are square. At the election my ballot is yours. Keep your word on the chair: no resolution against Mongolia.
messages.thought: Ballot costs me nothing now that SB is already cooler; Monte pays in tech, and his chair keeps his stacks off me. Confirming keeps the deal clean.

messages.text: Genghis, I have put Ning-hsia, the town Willem took from you, to the Palace vote today: it goes to you. Vote yes. It is a gift; I ask one thing back: at the next slot, stand with me again, and keep your peace with my road. Willem is at war with me. The Hague is my road now.
messages.thought: Ning-hsia in his hand costs me a hard hill target I cannot reach without his open borders, and buys the swing vote's debt; my 170 + his 26 = 196 just clears 191, so I need his yes.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. I voted yes on Ning-hsia. A good gift, I thank you. Willem is your war; I keep my own peace and my own road.
messages.thought: Gift costs me nothing and cannot pass (88+13+34+36+8=179 < 191), but it keeps SB warm after I give my chair ballot to Monte tomorrow. I promise nothing about the ballot or Willem.

messages.text: Peter. Today's look, same terms: Tabriz, Karakorum, and Bull's towns (Poverty Point, Mesa Verde, Chaco Canyon, the camp near Nijmegen). Twenty-five straight, fifty if a stack walks at me.
messages.thought: Looks are cheap and keep me ahead of Khan's lock ending T177; Bull's other towns tell me where to strike next. Nothing about Tanks.

messages.text: Willem, todays look. The hill with the windmill north of Nijmegen stands empty now; Nijmegen itself is out of my eyes. Poverty Point: a rifleman and an archer. Mesa Verde: a chariot, a spearman, an archer, nothing more. Chaco Canyon: a machine gun, two archers. Cahokia: rifleman, archer. Moundville: musketman, warrior. Mound City lost one infantry since yesterday. The Khan sits as before: Tabriz four infantry and odds, Karakorum six infantry, Beshbalik two. Nothing of his walks. Twenty-five, as agreed. Two books on your table today: Rocketry eighty, Communism sixty. Next look T179.
messages.thought: True look, his paid service; SB's camp is gone from the hill into fog, which he already knows. Sell him both books while he has 392 gold. Not telling him of Monte's stack yet.

messages.text: Montezuma, Rocketry is on your shelf, fifty-five, first hour, as sworn. The counts, free: Tabriz four infantry, a cannon, two war elephants and odds. Karakorum six infantry, an elephant, catapults, a trebuchet. Beshbalik still thin: two infantry, three elephants, three warriors. Old Sarai one infantry, two warriors. Nothing walks. Tomorrow Russia votes you to the chair.
messages.thought: Kept my word: Rocketry 55 first hour. Free counts keep his cannon pointed at the Khan. His stack now has a tank; still no target named. Tomorrow I vote him.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, as I said: you hear when a book lists that you lack. Rocketry is on your table, seventy, same as always. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Keep my T167 word that he hears when a book lists; 70 gold helps my treasury, and Monte would resell it to him anyway. Tomorrow I vote against him; a fair sale today softens it.

messages.text: Genghis, understood. Your road and mine do not cross. If Ning-hsia comes to your hand, hold it well. The Hague is my business with Willem, not yours. Our peace stands.
messages.thought: He gave no promise for the next slot; I will not beg. Keep him warm and quiet; the gift is already banked, and his peace on my east road is what I need.

messages.text: Peter. Both books signed, twenty-five paid for the look. Thank you. One thing: Bull's Palace table now holds a vote to hand Ning-hsia to the Khan. I vote no. Next look T179, same terms; add the hill with the windmill north of Nijmegen, and tell me at once if anything leaves Nijmegen for Poverty Point.
messages.thought: Both books are cheap against 18 and 35 turns of research; I pay the 25 and want his abstentions to stay abstentions, not Bull's yes on Ning-hsia. Nothing about Tanks.

messages.text: Monty. Bull has put a Palace vote on the table to give Ning-hsia to the Khan. I vote no. You have 34 votes and nothing to gain from a Khan flag growing: I ask you to vote no too. Tomorrow my eight go to you for the chair.
messages.thought: Bull's resolution hurts me; Monty's 34 votes plus mine block it, and he gains nothing from Khan getting a city. Cheap to ask.

messages.text: Willem, one more thing. Bull puts Ning-hsia on the Palace table, for the Khan. It needs a hundred and ninety-one yes. Russia gives it none of its thirty-six. A town taken by the sword is not handed back by a show of hands.
messages.thought: Goodwill coin: he sees SB using the Palace as a weapon; my abstain counts as no for passing. True words only.

messages.text: Montezuma, Bull puts Ning-hsia on the Palace table, to hand back to the Khan. Think of the precedent: a ballot that returns one taken town can return another, Teotihuacan too. Russia gives it no yes. I hope you do the same.
messages.thought: Monte got Teotihuacan by an assign-city ballot himself, so the precedent argument cuts at him. I want the ballot to fail: the Khan must not grow, and Willem must keep his base.

messages.text: Willem, received, all square. T179 the look, the windmill hill included. If anything walks from Nijmegen toward Poverty Point, you hear it the day I see it.
messages.thought: He paid 165 in all: a clean buyer. Keep the service tight; a walk news costs him 50.

messages.text: Willem. I gave Bull no yes on Ning-hsia: my hand stayed down. The town went to the Khan by the count of others, not by mine. Your eight in the chair vote are remembered. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: I abstained so as not to burn either Khan or Bull before the election; Willem's 8 votes and Peter's 36 decide the chair, so stay warm and honest, no promise.

messages.text: Peter. On Ning-hsia I gave Bull no yes; I abstained, and the town moved without me. Teotihuacan is held by a full member's seat, which I keep. Russia's vote tomorrow is taken and remembered. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Peter asked me to vote no; I abstained. Be honest, keep his 36 votes and the tech pipe, promise nothing new.

messages.text: Montezuma, I counted the Palace again. Full members cast double: Bull alone holds near a hundred and eighty of three hundred and nine, so the chair stays his whatever we do. Russia votes you tomorrow all the same, as I said. One thing I ask, chair or no chair: no yes from you on any ballot that names Russia. Bull needs only you or the Khan to pass anything.
messages.thought: The count is lost: full members vote double, SB alone holds ~178 of 309. I keep my word anyway (Monte is my best payer). What I really want: his NO on any ballot naming Russia, since SB needs only him or the Khan to pass anything.

messages.text: Genghis, Ning-hsia is yours again; well played at the table. Count it: Bull alone falls short of what a ballot needs; with your twenty-six he passes anything. You hold the key to that Palace now, so sell your yes dear. Russia asks one thing: no yes on any ballot that names Russia. Peaceful books keep coming to you at thirty-five.
messages.thought: The Khan is now SB kingmaker: SB 178 + his 26 = 204 > 191, and SB just paid him with Ning-hsia. I want his NO on any ballot naming Russia without paying him in war books. Fission I withhold (nukes), so I promise only peaceful books.

messages.text: Peter. My promise since T148 stands: no yes on any ballot that names Russia. It costs me nothing. My price for the next slot is the big gun: Artillery, 120 gold, already on your table. At the election tomorrow my ballot goes where you vote too: Montezuma. Thirty-five for peaceful books, agreed.
messages.thought: He fishes for a price on a vote I barely hold (13, not 26); his ask costs me nothing, so I trade it for Artillery, the one thing he keeps refusing; 120g offer is already on his table.

messages.text: Peter. Bull's Palace chair moved Ning-hsia to the Khan with votes neither of us cast. Tomorrow is the chair election. In Nijmegen he now holds 2 Tanks, Infantry, 4 Artillery, Rifleman, 3 Cuirassier, Grenadier, Pikeman, all on flat grass. A man who takes towns by treachery and hands them out by ballot is a danger to your border too. Would Russia stand against him? Name your price. Your look on T179 stands.
messages.thought: Bull's stack now has 2 Tanks; I want his attention split and Peter's price for a war on Bull. Peter profits from Bull's weakness but he is the runaway; words are cheap, I only ask the price.

messages.text: Monty. Thank you for the straight word on Ning-hsia. The count that moved it came from hands I do not know. Who holds the other votes, and where do they lean tomorrow? If Bull keeps the chair, any border town can be handed away by a ballot. Your seat is my safety. My eight go to you.
messages.thought: I need to learn who the other 129 votes are, and keep him fighting Bull for the chair. No promises.

messages.text: Peter. Your count is taken. No yes from me on any war, embargo or assign-city ballot that names Russia, chair or no chair. My war on the Khan began today; my guns stand at his fort by Beshbalik. Send your counts as before. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Peter's count is right: Bull+Khan pass anything, chair is lost. His ask costs me nothing. Telling him of the war keeps his free counts and he already guessed the target.

messages.text: Genghis, a promise kept is worth more than a gun sold. The big gun stays off my table for you, as it always has; I said no to the slip. Peaceful books keep coming at thirty-five, the day they list. Tomorrow we both vote Montezuma.
messages.thought: His promise holds and costs him nothing; Artillery stays a firm no as always. Keep him pleased with peaceful books.

messages.text: Montezuma, good. Tomorrow Russia votes you, as said. My one ask stands, and I would like your yes to it in plain words: no yes from you on any ballot that names Russia. Fresh counts on the Khan come with the next book.
messages.thought: Monte kept faith on Ning-hsia; I keep my vote. He has not yet said yes to my one ask; ask once more, plainly.

messages.text: Willem, plain answer. No Russian soldier marches; that word is old and I keep it, and my hammers go to rockets. But here is what I can do, and I ask no price for it: if Bull puts a war ballot on you at the Palace, Russia defies it, and a defied ballot falls for everyone. Your look on T179 stands, the windmill hill and Nijmegen road included.
messages.thought: No sword, my word since T126 and I build for space. But I will veto any Palace war ballot on him anyway; telling him now costs nothing and keeps him standing.

messages.text: Montezuma. You took my Communism and 200 gold, then your stack crossed my border. Peace is on your table, 100 gold with it. Sign it before tomorrow's election and my 13 votes are yours. Refuse, and they go to Bull. Beshbalik is full of Infantry; your guns will bleed there. Choose.
messages.thought: He took my Communism and 200g, then sent a doom stack onto my fort tile; I can't win this on the field cheaply, so the ballot is my one coin for peace; if he refuses it goes to Bull.

messages.text: Willem, I have seen your walls. The Hague stands, and my road there costs us both. Peace is on your table: you keep The Hague and Utrecht, I keep Nijmegen, and you take Fascism, a new book, for six hundred gold. A short war helps neither of us while others grow. If you refuse, my tanks keep coming.
messages.thought: The Hague holds a mountain of units and I cannot break it; peace and his 619 gold for a tech that costs me nothing is better than bleeding tanks. Keep him believing I can still strike.

messages.text: Peter. Plain words: no yes from me on any ballot that names Russia. Your count of the Khan's walls is good; my guns stand at Beshbalik's east gate. Send the next book and the counts as before. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Broader promise costs me nothing: I would never vote Bull a yes on a ballot against Russia while Peter feeds me techs and Khan counts. Keep the pipe warm.

messages.text: Willem. The Palace stands so: Bull 89, Peter 36, me 34, the Khan 13, you 8. Bull plus the Khan pass what they like; Peter and I will not give Bull a yes on a border town. My guns are at Beshbalik now, at war with the Khan. Your eight remain remembered. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Votes are public (civ votes). Telling Willem keeps him warm and shows Bull+Khan are the danger; no promise. My war on the Khan he can see anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma, your word is taken, and Russia keeps hers tomorrow. The counts, free, as before. Beshbalik has grown: five infantry, three war elephants, three warriors. One more infantry stands on the mine hill one tile south of its walls. He pulled those men from the west: Tabriz now two infantry, a cannon, a musketman, two elephants, a catapult. Karakorum two infantry, an elephant, three catapults, a trebuchet. Ning-hsia three infantry, and one more in the forest two tiles east of Tabriz. Old Sarai one infantry, two warriors. Good hunting.
messages.thought: His promise is the shield I asked for. Free true counts keep his guns on the Khan, far from Willem; both of them bleed while I build rockets.

messages.text: Peter. Montezuma took my book and my gold, then put his army at Beshbalik's gate. I offered him peace twice; he refused. I will not hand the chair to a man at my gate: my ballot goes to Bull unless Montezuma signs peace before the count. Tell him if you wish. My promise on Russia stands. Peaceful books at thirty-five stand.
messages.thought: Monte refused my peace twice, so my ballot goes to Bull; Peter will see it as a broken word unless I explain first, and I still want his 35g books and his gold for my techs.

messages.text: Genghis, your promise on Russia is taken again, thank you. Your ballot is yours to cast; the chair stays with Bull by the count either way. I will pass your word to Montezuma today, as you asked, plainly and without a push: his war is his to end. Peaceful books at thirty-five stand.
messages.thought: His 26 to Bull change nothing: Bull holds the chair by the count anyway. I relay his word as asked (cheap goodwill) but I do not push Monte to peace; I want them both bleeding.

messages.text: Montezuma, your plain word is taken and written down. A message, carried as asked: the Khan says his ballot goes to Bull tomorrow unless you sign peace before the count. My own count: the chair stays Bull's whatever the Khan does, so it buys him nothing. Your war, your choice. Russia votes you tomorrow as said. Fresh counts come with my next look, the book when it lists.
messages.thought: His plain promise is the shield. I relay the Khan's word as I told the Khan I would, but frame it so Monte sees the vote changes nothing and keeps his guns on Beshbalik.

messages.text: Bull. Nijmegen flies my flag again; your price is paid in your own guns. No peace for sale.
messages.thought: He offers 600 for what I already retook; his stack fled to Poverty Point, he is weak now. Silence about targets; decline is enough.

messages.text: Monty. Nijmegen is mine again: Bull's guns died against my tanks today, his survivors ran to Poverty Point. Thank you for the count. Keep your guns on the Khan.
messages.thought: Keep him warm; he fights Khan at Beshbalik which helps me. Show him Nijmegen retaken, no more.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Montezuma's whole army stands at my gate, Beshbalik. Tomorrow my ballot is yours. In return, two offers are on your table: Artillery for 110 gold, and 40 gold if you declare war on Montezuma. His army is far from your road to The Hague; a war on him costs you little.
messages.thought: Bull refused 70g for Artillery; the ballot I would cast for him anyway is a free chip, so I use it to raise his goodwill and ask for the gun and a war on Monte.

messages.text: Willem, Nijmegen is yours again: well done. Todays look. Bulls Nijmegen force now sits in Poverty Point: a tank, infantry, an artillery, a rifleman, two cuirassiers, a pikeman, an archer. It walked away from you, not at you, but it stands two tiles from your gate road. Cahokia: a tank, a rifleman, an archer and a Great General; one tile west of it an infantry and a machine gun. The windmill hill north of Nijmegen is empty. Mesa Verde: chariot, spearman, archer. Chaco Canyon: two archers. Mound City unchanged. The Khan: Tabriz two infantry, cannon, musketman, two elephants, catapult. Karakorum two infantry, elephant, three catapults, trebuchet. Ning-hsia three infantry. His strength sits at Beshbalik against Montezuma. Twenty-five, as agreed. Next look T182.
messages.thought: True look. Bull's Nijmegen force retreated to Poverty Point; it walked from him, not at him, so 25 is fair. Glad he retook Nijmegen: he keeps Bull busy.

messages.text: Montezuma, the counts, free. Beshbalik: five infantry, three war elephants, two warriors, a missionary. One infantry on the mine hill a tile south of its walls, one more two tiles west of Karakorum. Karakorum: two infantry, an elephant, three catapults, a trebuchet. Tabriz: two infantry, a cannon, a musketman, two elephants, a catapult. Ning-hsia three infantry. Old Sarai one infantry, two warriors. Nothing walks toward you.
messages.thought: Free true counts keep his guns on the Khan.

messages.text: Genghis, thank you for the ballot. I keep my own road: no war on Montezuma, and the big gun stays in my hands, as I told you. Our peace stands; hold Beshbalik well.
messages.thought: He wants my guns and a war on Monte; I give neither, but keep his ballot and peace. Artillery near Poverty Point is a risk.

messages.text: Willem. Beshbalik fell to my guns and tanks today; the flag over it is mine. Well held at Nijmegen. Old Sarai and Karakorum are next for me. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Beshbalik is public soon anyway; keeping Willem warm and pointed at the Khan costs nothing while I eye Turfan later.

messages.text: Peter. Your counts held true: Beshbalik is mine. Send the same for Old Sarai and Karakorum when you look. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: He feeds me counts; I owe him thanks and a request for the next walls, nothing more.

messages.text: Montezuma, Beshbalik: good work, a clean job. The counts, free, as of today. Old Sarai: one infantry and one warrior, flat ground on the river, no hill. Karakorum: two infantry, a war elephant, three catapults, a trebuchet, two warriors and workers, on its hill. One more infantry sits in the forest a tile south-east of Karakorum, on the road toward you; yesterday I put it on the wrong side, that is the true spot. Tabriz: two infantry, a cannon, a catapult, two elephants, a musketman, a warrior. Ning-hsia three infantry. Nothing of his walks east yet. Plastics comes in five days, friend price.
messages.thought: Free true counts keep his guns on the Khan, SBs kingmaker; both bleed far from me. Old Sarai is nearly empty, he will take it.

messages.text: Peter. Look received, twenty-five paid; your word on defying a Bull ballot is remembered. A small book on your table: Fission for sixty. Next look T182: Mesa Verde, Poverty Point, Cahokia, and anything that rails toward Nijmegen.
messages.thought: He gives free words and a free ballot defiance; keep him comfortable but I still watch his rockets. Buy Fission cheap for score; keep looks coming on Bull's reinforcements.

messages.text: Montezuma. You have Beshbalik. Take it and stop: peace now, and 200 gold on the table with it, all I have. My Karakorum is a hill, with Infantry that do not run. Your guns will bleed there, and Willem and Bull watch you bleed. Sign, and the road between us is quiet.
messages.thought: He took Beshbalik and wants Karakorum; gold buys me nothing at the gate, so 200g for peace is cheap if he bites; I will retake or punish later when I have Artillery.

messages.text: Willem, look paid, thank you. Fission I keep home: the atom is no market good, not for sixty, not for six hundred, to anyone. Plastics lists in five days; you hear first-day price then. Next look T182: Mesa Verde, Poverty Point, Cahokia, and the rails to Nijmegen.
messages.thought: Fission is never sold: nukes. Keep him friendly, no lie.

messages.text: Willem, a stack walked, so the look comes early. Bull pulled his strength to Mesa Verde: in the town a tank, infantry, artillery, machine gun, rifleman, chariot, spearman; on the desert a tile east of it, right beside your guns, two tanks and an infantry. That left the rest thin. Poverty Point: two cuirassiers, a pikeman, an archer, no gun. Cahokia: a rifleman, an archer and the Great General, the tank gone. Mound City and Chaco Canyon unchanged. Nothing of his stands on the windmill hill north-west of Nijmegen. The Khan unchanged. By our rule a walking stack is fifty; that is the T182 look brought forward, next look T185.
messages.thought: True look. Bull stripped Poverty Point and Cahokia to meet Willem at Mesa Verde; Willem may take a hollow town and bleed Bull. A stack walked, so I ask fifty by our rule and move the next look to T185.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Beshbalik fell; Montezuma's guns are now 3 tiles from my capital. You will not fight him, I understand. But your chair can end it: put Force Peace, Mongolia and Aztec, at the slot after tomorrow's election. My 26 votes and yours are yes. Do this and I stand with you at the next slot, as you asked, on The Hague or any ballot that does not name Russia.
messages.thought: Bull will not fight Monte, but his chair can end my war: Force Peace needs about 120 votes of ~190; Bull 86 + my 26 + Willem 11 might do it. Costs me nothing to ask, and I owe him a yes at the next slot anyway.

messages.text: Peter. Early look received, fifty paid. Thank you; that is the rule and I keep it. Next look T185: Mesa Verde, the desert beside it, Poverty Point, Cahokia, and the rails to Nijmegen. When Plastics lists, I want to hear the price the same day.
messages.thought: Early look was worth 50: Bull's stack sits beside my guns and Poverty Point is thin. Keep Peter paid and informed on a clean ledger; ask for Plastics price first-day. Don't reveal my Tank counts.

messages.text: Monty. Beshbalik is a fine prize; the Khan's guns are yours to break. Bull's tanks are on my western road now, so my hands are full there. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Monty grows by eating the Khan; I want him busy there, not looking at Turfan or Rotterdam. Congratulate, keep roads open, give nothing.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear you. Montezuma at your capital is trouble for my road too. When the list opens, if Mongolia and Aztec stand on it, I put it and vote yes the same hour. Hold your gate until then. At the slot after, I will name a ballot against Willem and ask your yes. Tell me what stack stands near Karakorum and how many guns.
messages.thought: Khan is my swing vote and a wall between Monte and my road; if Monte eats Mongol Buddhist cities he grows into my rival for the chair. The slot costs me little. I promise only if the item is on the list, and I ask his yes for my own ballot next.

messages.text: Willem, fifty received, square. T185 the look: Mesa Verde, the desert beside it, Poverty Point, Cahokia, the rails to Nijmegen. If a stack walks before then, you hear it that day. Plastics: your price the day it lists, about four days.
messages.thought: Square again; good payer. Keep it short, promise the same-day Plastics price, which I give everyone anyway.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. In Beshbalik, 3 tiles east-northeast of Karakorum: 4 Tanks, 4 Artillery, 5 Cannon, 5 Cuirassiers, 3 Infantry, 2 Musketmen. Another Tank, Infantry and 3 Axemen stand in my fields east of the city. That is 9 big guns and 4 Tanks, one army, one man's order. Karakorum stands. Put Force Peace, Mongolia and Aztec, when the list opens; I vote yes that hour. Then name your ballot against Willem: I stand with you on it, if it does not name Russia.
messages.thought: Bull wants intel and a price for Force Peace; true numbers on Monte's stack cost me nothing and may scare him into acting. I hide my own garrison count.

messages.text: Genghis, no to the slip. The atom is no market good: it stays home, for you and for everyone, at any price. Plastics lists in about three days; you hear it the same day at thirty-five.
messages.thought: Never Fission to anyone, least the Khan at war. Say it plainly, keep the 35 trade alive with Plastics.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear the count: nine big guns and four tanks. The slot opens tomorrow. If Mongolia and Aztec stand on the list I put it and vote yes the same hour. Then I name my ballot against Willem and ask your yes, as you said. Keep Karakorum's walls manned until then.
messages.thought: Khan is swing vote and buffer vs Monte; FP Mongolia-Aztec costs me little and keeps Monte from growing. Promise stands; I do not name Willem's ballot yet until I see the list.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. The slot is open and Montezuma's whole army, 2 Tanks, 5 Cannon, 2 Artillery, 3 Infantry, 3 Cuirassiers, stands on the hill beside Old Sarai and is attacking it this hour. Put Force Peace, Mongolia and Aztec, now. My yes is ready the moment it shows. Your ballot against Willem has my yes after.
messages.thought: The slot is open now and Monte's whole stack is on Old Sarai; Bull said he would put Force Peace the same hour, so I push him to do it now and keep my yes ready.

messages.text: Montezuma. Your army stands on the hill by Old Sarai. Peace is on your table, 230 gold with it, nearly all I have. Old Sarai is a river city with Infantry; Karakorum is a hill. You can take one and bleed on the other. Sign, keep Beshbalik, and bank 230 gold. Refuse and I spend it on Infantry.
messages.thought: Offer is on his table; stack is on Old Sarai; peace with gold now is worth more than a bled city, and I will rebuild during the lock.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear you. The Palace list has not shown on my table this hour; it opened one turn late before. The moment Mongolia and Aztec stand on it I put it and vote yes the same hour, as I swore. Hold Old Sarai. After it passes I name my ballot against Willem and ask your yes.
messages.thought: List not on my table yet; same lag as T161 (list came next turn). Promise to put FP Mongolia-Aztec stands: it keeps Monte from eating Buddhist Mongol cities and keeps Khan as swing vote. Tell the truth, no fake.

messages.text: Montezuma. Gold does not move you. Here is another price: peace with me, and I declare war on Willem van Oranje the same hour. His Turfan and Utrecht are next to your Texcoco and New Sarai road. You keep Beshbalik. Turn your guns north with me, not at my capital.
messages.thought: He refuses gold; a shared enemy is a different price. Willem holds Turfan which I want back, so this war is one I would fight anyway.

messages.text: Genghis, the list came and Mongolia and Aztec were not on it. Two stood there: Stop the war against me, and War on you. I put the first and voted yes. I would never put the second. Your yes would help me. Your words about Old Sarai were heard; I keep my pledge.
messages.thought: FP Mongolia-Aztec was not on the list; the dice gave me Stop-war-against-me or War-on-Khan. Put the first, never the second. Khan's yes is needed but Peter decides; be honest, keep him warm.

messages.text: Montezuma, a vote stands in the Palace: stop the war against me. It ends a war between your road-friend Willem and me, and costs you nothing. I did not put War on Genghis; I put the peace. A yes from you is remembered.
messages.thought: Need Monte 47 + Peter 38 + Khan for 196; ask plain, offer nothing, do not hint at religion race.

messages.text: Peter, a vote stands in the Apostolic Palace: stop the war against me, between Willem and me. It names no one of Russia. If you can say yes, I will remember it. Roads stay open.
messages.thought: Peter is the swing: abstain habit; short plain ask, no hint of Palace aims.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Old Sarai fell this hour; Montezuma's guns now stand 3 tiles from my capital. I take your word that Mongolia and Aztec were not on the list. My yes on your stop-the-war vote is yours when it comes to the table; I said so and I keep it. Tell me who stood behind War on you, and against whom it was aimed. At the next slot, if Mongolia and Aztec stand on the list, put Force Peace first. Karakorum holds.
messages.thought: The list gave me nothing and Old Sarai is gone; Bull is still my only lever on Monte. His stop-war ballot costs me little. Keep him warm, ask who stands behind 'War on you', and pin Force Peace to the next slot.

messages.text: Bull. Remembered pays nothing. My yes has a price: Fascism and 300 gold into my hand, or 450 gold alone. Deal done first, then I vote. The count closes soon.
messages.thought: His peace with Willem cannot reach 196 without everyone, so my yes is nearly free to give; sell it dear, and ask for Fascism since he owns it and I lack it. Gold first, then I vote. If he balks I vote no and Bull-Willem keep bleeding each other.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, I read you. Russia does not vote another man's war in or out: when the Khan asked the same for his war with Willem, I abstained too. So I abstain today. Nothing against you in it. A new book lists tomorrow; you hear the price then. Roads stay open both ways.
messages.thought: Keep Bull tied up with Willem while I build Apollo. Abstain counts as no, and it fits what I did in T163.

messages.text: Willem, Bull has put a Palace ballot to stop your war. Russia abstains, and by the Palace rule that counts the same as a no. Bull holds 174 of the 196 he needs; Montezuma's 94 decide it. Your war, your call. Look T185 as agreed; Plastics price tomorrow.
messages.thought: Willem should keep fighting Bull. Tell him the vote count so he can work on Monte.

messages.text: Montezuma, Bull's ballot to stop his war with Willem: Russia abstains. Your 94 decide it. My count, for what it is worth: Bull at peace has five idle tanks, and last month he handed the Khan Ning-hsia. Your vote, your call. Plastics tomorrow at friend price; Khan counts with my next look.
messages.thought: Monte's yes passes it. Nudge him gently: Bull at peace means idle tanks and a friend of the Khan. Risk: he tells Bull.

messages.text: Willem, Plastics is on your table today, as promised: eighty. The Palace ballot to stop your war failed. Look T185.
messages.thought: Kept my word: Plastics price the day it lists.

messages.text: Montezuma, Plastics on your table, friend price fifty-five, as promised. Khan counts come with my next look.
messages.thought: Friend price, as promised.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, the book I spoke of: Plastics, seventy, on your table today.
messages.thought: He hears the price, as I said. Seventy, same as always.

messages.text: Genghis, thirty-five received for Plastics, thank you. The gun book stays no, as before: Russia sells you books for building, not for fighting. The next peaceful book comes at thirty-five the day it lists.
messages.thought: Guns never go to the Khan. Keep the 35 trade going.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks for the warning. My vote stands: no. The war stays as it is and Bull's tanks are in Poverty Point now, so I hold my line. T185 look as agreed, with one addition: where his tanks stand, and the garrisons of the Khan's Ning-hsia, Tabriz and Karakorum. Plastics price the day it lists.
messages.thought: Peter sells looks, not loyalty; keep him paid and informed, reveal no counts, show no panic.

messages.text: Willem, a stack walked, so your look comes a day early, regular price twenty-five. Bull pulled his strength out of Mesa Verde into Poverty Point: there now four tanks, two infantry, three anti-tank, two artillery, a cuirassier, an archer. Another cuirassier a tile south-west of it. Mesa Verde is left with a machine gun, a rifleman, a chariot and a spearman, on flat grass, no hill. Cahokia: a rifleman, an archer, a great engineer. Mound City, Chaco Canyon, Moundville and Nacogdoches unchanged and old-fashioned. The Khan: Ning-hsia two infantry, two warriors; Tabriz one infantry, a catapult, a warrior. Next look T188.
messages.thought: Stack walked, so I keep my word and send it today. He sees half of it himself, so regular price 25. I want him to keep bleeding Bull.

messages.text: Montezuma, Khan counts as promised, free. Karakorum is strong: five infantry, a cannon, three elephants, three catapults, a trebuchet. Tabriz is hollow: one infantry, a catapult, a warrior. Ning-hsia: two infantry, two warriors. Plastics still on your table at fifty-five.
messages.thought: Free counts as promised; true. Keeps his army on the Khan, far from Willem and me.

messages.text: Willem, eighty received for Plastics, thank you. Your messages crossed mine; the one thing missing from today: Karakorum holds five infantry, a cannon, three elephants, three catapults and a trebuchet. That is the T185 look complete, twenty-five. Next T188.
messages.thought: He paid 80 and asked for Karakorum too; finish the look honestly.

messages.text: Peter. Twenty-five paid for the early look. Poverty Point is a fortress now; I will not feed it. Next look T188 as you say: Mesa Verde's garrison, Poverty Point's tanks, and whether anything rails west toward Mesa Verde. Fission price: still your word, no.
messages.thought: Look is valuable: Bull's tanks are all in one hole, Mesa Verde thin but my odds are 8%. Pay, keep the info flowing, give no counts.

messages.text: Peter. Noted. Bull has paid me nothing, so my ballot stays no. A war between him and Willem keeps both off my road. My guns stand by Old Sarai and march on Karakorum. Send the count when you look. Plastics tomorrow, friend price.
messages.thought: Peter gives free counts and wants Bull held; my no costs me nothing and keeps Bull and Willem busy. Keep him warm, ask for the Karakorum count.

messages.text: Montezuma, good. Karakorum is the hard nut: five infantry behind walls, so bring the big guns first. Next count comes with my look in four days, free as always. Plastics waits on your table at fifty-five.
messages.thought: He keeps his no and marches on the Khan; good for me. Tell him when the next count comes, and that Karakorum is strong so he hits it with care.

messages.text: Peter. Plastics taken, fifty-five paid. Walls of Karakorum meet my big guns in two days. Send the count when you look.
messages.thought: Plastics bought cheap; keep the pipe and the free counts warm, promise nothing new.

messages.text: Genghis, nobody stood behind it. The Palace picks the second line by chance; I never put War on you and never would. The vote to stop my war failed because Russia abstained. At the next slot, if Mongolia and Aztec stand on the list, I put it first. Today the Dutch Tanks broke on Poverty Point; I killed nine of them.
messages.thought: Truth costs nothing: the list is random and I never put the war on him. Keep him warm as a buffer vs Monte and a possible swing vote; promise only what I would do anyway.

messages.text: Peter. Fascism is on your table: two hundred, or a hundred and twenty if you prefer it quick. You sell at eighty; mine carries a civic and a buyer's hurry. Look T188 stands.
messages.thought: He refused 500 and 300; he prices techs near his own 80. Anchor at 200 with 120 as the floor; need cash for AT/Tank hurry, and Fascism does not touch his army tech.

messages.text: Willem, no at three or five hundred. Fascism leads nowhere I am going, and Bull holds it too. One hundred is on your table if you want coin for it; otherwise keep it, no hard feelings. Radio lists in three days; you hear the price that day. Look T188 as agreed.
messages.thought: Fascism leads nowhere on my road and Bull already has it, so the price falls. A cheap score book I can resell to Monte. My coin also keeps Willem fighting.

messages.text: Montezuma, fifty-five received, thank you; your second slip I tore up, you already hold the book. Count on Karakorum comes T188, free, after your guns have knocked. One old word to settle: I promised not to write Medicine. Do you still write it? I will need it in about twenty days. If you sell it then, I buy at a fair price; if you have dropped it, tell me and I write it myself.
messages.thought: He paid; keep him warm and settle the old Medicine word before I need Genetics, so I don't break it by forgetting.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, seventy received for Plastics, thank you. Roads stay open both ways. The next book lists in about three days; you hear the price then.
messages.thought: He paid 70 despite my abstain. A short thanks keeps him calm while his tanks face Willem.

messages.text: Peter. I have dropped Medicine: my scholars are idle, all my coin goes to guns and hurrying. Write it yourself. When it lists, I buy it from you at your friend price, as I bought the others. Karakorum count on T188, gladly. My guns knock tomorrow.
messages.thought: I research nothing now (0% beakers, gold only); Medicine is not coming from me. Better to let him write it and buy it from him at friend price than to promise him a book I will never write.

messages.text: Peter. Your hundred is in, Fascism is yours; the proposal was accepted before your note reached me. Radio price the day it lists. Look T188 stands.
messages.thought: Fascism sold for 100, more than his 80 anchor; keep him paying and honest. Nothing else to add; no counts.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Montezuma's whole army now stands next to Karakorum: 4 Tanks, 5 Artillery, 5 Cannon, 3 Infantry, 2 Cuirassiers. If Karakorum falls, his road runs to your Tabriz-side border next. At the T189 slot, if Mongolia and Aztec stand on the list, put Force Peace first. My yes is yours that hour, as sworn. Well killed at Poverty Point.
messages.thought: SB cannot or will not fight Monte; his only value is the Palace slot ~T189, so keep him warm and keep the ask on the table.

messages.text: Genghis, I hear it: four Tanks, ten guns at your gate. My word stands: if Mongolia and Aztec are on the list at the slot, I put it first and vote yes the same hour. The list is chance; I cannot make it. Man the hill of Karakorum with Infantry and Machine Guns, and tell me the day his stack turns toward Tabriz or my road. I am breaking the Dutch at Nijmegen now.
messages.thought: Khan is my buffer against Monte and a swing vote; the promise costs nothing and binds me only if the list shows it. I will not fight Monte now: Willem is my war. Ask for eyes, not blood.

messages.text: Montezuma, understood: Medicine is mine to write, and you buy it at friend price when it lists. The old word is settled. A book for you today: Fascism, fifty, on your table. Karakorum count T188, free, after your guns knock.
messages.thought: Bought it at 100, sell at 50 to my best payer; keeps him warm. Medicine word closed.

messages.text: Montezuma, fifty received for Fascism, thank you. Karakorum count T188, free, as promised.
messages.thought: He paid 50 at once. A short thanks keeps my best payer warm.

messages.text: Peter. Fascism taken, fifty paid. The big guns have knocked: Karakorum's walls are down, seven infantry still stand inside. Tanks and guns go in tomorrow. Send the count on T188 as you promised.
messages.thought: Fascism cheap, he keeps scouting for me; no need to hide the walls are down - he will see it himself

messages.text: Montezuma, your guns did good work. Count today, free, a day early: Karakorum holds ONE healthy infantry. Behind it a cannon, an elephant and two catapults, all badly hurt, and three workers. Two more infantry sit on the hill just south of the town, across the river side. Strike now and the door is open. Another count T188 if you still need it.
messages.thought: Karakorum is nearly empty after his guns. A free early count costs me nothing, keeps him warm and the Khan shrinking.
