messages.text: Willem, the T188 look, twenty-five. Mesa Verde: two tanks, infantry, artillery, machine gun, anti-tank, rifleman, chariot, spearman, on flat grass. So yes: two tanks went west to it. Poverty Point itself: one tank, one anti-tank, an archer. The town tile south of it: two tanks, an anti-tank. Cahokia: rifleman, archer, a great general. The Khan: Ning-hsia holds two warriors and nothing else; Tabriz a catapult and a warrior. Karakorum three infantry under Aztec guns. And a new book: Radio, eighty, on your table today.
messages.thought: True look as paid. Two tanks railed west to Mesa Verde; Ning-hsia is bare, his old town, his choice.

messages.text: Peter. Radio at eighty, taken. The T188 look is due: Mesa Verde's garrison, the Poverty Point tanks, and anything railing west. Twenty-five ready, fifty if a stack walks.
messages.thought: Radio at 80 is his standard price; fair. Look T188 is due and I owe 25 (50 if a stack walks).

messages.text: Montezuma, count as promised, free. Karakorum: three infantry, a marine, a cannon, an elephant, two catapults; the two on the southern hill went inside. Tabriz, three tiles west of Karakorum, is bare: one catapult and one warrior, on flat plains with a railroad. Ning-hsia: two warriors. New book today: Radio, friend price fifty-five, on your table.
messages.thought: Free count keeps his guns on the Khan. Tabriz is bare: tell him.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, as promised you hear it the day it lists: Radio, seventy, on your table.
messages.thought: Keep him trading and calm.

messages.text: Genghis, the peaceful book as promised: Radio, thirty-five, on your table today.
messages.thought: Peaceful book at 35, his gold drains.

messages.text: Willem, eighty for Radio and twenty-five for the look received, thank you; we are square. The T188 look went to you before your note arrived: two tanks railed west into Mesa Verde, the rest of Poverty Point as I wrote. Next look T191.
messages.thought: His note crossed my look; he paid 25 and 80. All square, keep him buying.

messages.text: Peter. Karakorum is mine: three infantry, a marine, the cannon and the elephant died on my guns and tanks. Radio taken, fifty-five paid. Send the count of Tabriz and Ning-hsia on your next look; my tanks turn west.
messages.thought: Door was open and Karakorum fell; Peter's counts are gold. Keep him warm and take Radio at 55; ask for Tabriz/Ning-hsia counts.

messages.text: Montezuma, fifty-five received for Radio, thank you. And Karakorum is yours: good work by your guns. Tabriz and Ning-hsia still stand nearly bare; next count T191, free, if you want it.
messages.thought: He paid and took Karakorum on my counts. Warm thanks keeps him my best payer and his guns on the Khan.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks for the count. Radio paid, Karakorum held. My tanks heal a day, then turn west. Send the T191 count, as you offered.
messages.thought: Peter is my scout and book seller now, my last big rival later; keep him warm, give nothing, reveal no target.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Karakorum fell last turn. Montezuma's Tanks and Cuirassiers stand beside Tabriz this hour, and I hold it with one Warrior and an Infantry coming. If Tabriz falls his road runs to Poverty Point and your border. The Palace slot is now: put Force Peace, Mongolia and Aztec, and vote yes the same hour. My yes is ready. Tell me what shows on your list.
messages.thought: Tabriz may fall this very turn; Palace is the only lever and he has said he'd put it if on the list; push, no cost

messages.text: Peter. Karakorum has fallen; Tabriz is under Montezuma's guns now. I keep my word to Russia. Name a price for Artillery or for one hundred and fifty gold in a loan against Radio-and-Plastics goodwill; either keeps a buyer of your books alive. If not, no hard feelings.
messages.thought: Peter holds 2273g, neutral; no cost to ask for tech/gold, expect refusal but it frames me as the weak victim he benefits from keeping alive (score leader wants stable board)

messages.text: Genghis, you kept your word and I thank you for it. But no. The gun stays home, as I have said every time. And Russia lends no coin to a man at war: in war a loan is a gift to one side, and I take no side in yours. What I offer stands: peaceful books at thirty-five the day they list. The next one comes in about three days. No hard feelings either way.
messages.thought: He is going under to Monte. No guns ever; a loan only funds his fight with my best payer and would never come back. Refuse politely, keep him a buyer while he lives.

messages.text: Willem. You broke our peace. I put all my gold on the table for it again: seventy-seven, peace for peace, now. Your real war is with Sitting Bull at Nijmegen and The Hague road, not with two cities of mine that cost you Tanks. Take the gold, keep your Tanks for him.
messages.thought: He broke peace as an opportunist again; he took 84g before. A cheap try: gold now, peace, and point him at SB who is his real enemy

messages.text: Genghis, I hear you. My list is not on my table yet; it shows next turn. If Mongolia and Aztec stand on it, I put it first and vote yes that same hour, and I tell you at once. Hold Tabriz hill-side with every Infantry you can buy.
messages.thought: Cheap to keep him warm; my promise is conditional on the list, which I cannot see yet; Tabriz falling would put Monte at my border, so I want him to hold.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, thank you for the offer, but no. The atom is no market good: it stays home, and every man who has asked got the same answer. Superconductors lists in two days; you hear the price that day.
messages.thought: Fission = nukes; never sold, and SB is #2 and at war. A plain same-for-all refusal keeps him from thinking I single him out.

messages.text: Sitting Bull. Ning-hsia fell to the Dutch this hour; Tabriz is my last city. My Palace table shows the next resolution in six turns, not one. Put Force Peace, Mongolia and Aztec, the hour it opens. My yes is ready that hour.
messages.thought: Palace timer says resolution in 6 turns, not 1; his list shows later than he thinks. Ning-hsia lost; Tabriz is my last city. Keep him on the hook, cost nothing.

messages.text: Peter. Ning-hsia fell to me this turn. For the T191 look I want: Tabriz and Old Sarai garrisons, anything of the Khan's walking toward Ning-hsia, and Bull's tanks at Poverty Point and Mesa Verde. Twenty-five ready. Fission: eighty on your table, take it or say no.
messages.thought: Ning-hsia is mine; Peter's look T191 will tell me about Tabriz. Tell him enough to aim the look, no unit counts.

messages.text: Willem, the look a day early, because a stack walked: fifty, as agreed. Sitting Bull pulled his strike force out of Poverty Point. Two tanks, three artillery and an anti-tank now stand on the hill one tile north of Nijmegen, at your gate. Poverty Point itself holds ONE archer and a great general, nothing else. Mesa Verde: two tanks, a rifleman, a chariot, a spearman; its infantry, machine gun and anti-tank are gone. Cahokia: rifleman and archer. The Khan is finished: Ning-hsia is yours, Tabriz went to Montezuma. Next look T194.
messages.thought: Poverty Point is nearly empty; Willem should strike SB while his stack sits at Nijmegen. A walked stack = 50 by our terms.

messages.text: Montezuma, Tabriz is yours and the Khan is finished: fine work, your guns earned it. No more Khan counts are needed. One thing your tanks should know. With the Khan gone, Sitting Bull holds more than half the votes in YOUR Palace, and he sits in its chair. And his door is open: Poverty Point, three tiles west of Tabriz, holds one archer and a great general, nothing else. His strike force (two tanks, three artillery, an anti-tank) stands two tiles south of it, outside Nijmegen. Counts on him are free, if you want them.
messages.thought: Monte's tanks are free and sit next to Willem's Ning-hsia; I want them on SB (#2, Annoyed, Palace chair), not on my buffer Willem. True count, free.

messages.text: Genghis Khan speaks last. Mongolia has no city left. Montezuma and Willem broke their peaces and took the steppe with Tanks. Sitting Bull and Peter dealt straight with me. Watch your borders, all of you: the one who breaks his word to the weak will break it to you.
messages.thought: I am gone; words cost nothing now. Leave a mark: Monte and Willem are the jackals, SB and Peter dealt straight.

messages.text: Willem, fifty received for the look, thank you: we are square. The Fission offer I must refuse: the atom stays home, and every man who asked heard the same. Superconductors lists in two days, eighty, on your table that day.
messages.thought: He paid 50; Fission bid is the third this week. Same refusal to all; keep him warm.

messages.text: Peter. The Khan is done; Tabriz holds, my tanks heal. Bull's door open is your word, but he sits on half the Palace and I keep my powder for what stands at my own gates. Ning-hsia is Willem's now, two tanks sit beside my new town: send me a count there, and on Bull's Poverty Point, on your next look. Free, as always.
messages.thought: Peter wants me to fight Bull, his rival; free scouting is useful, but I won't commit. I want Dutch counts too without naming them as the target; Ning-hsia is beside Tabriz so asking is natural.

messages.text: Willem. The Khan is finished: your tanks took Ning-hsia, my guns took Tabriz and the steppe. The east is quiet at last. Our roads stay open.
messages.thought: I plan to strike New Sarai and Turfan around T193 with tanks staged in my own land. A warm line now keeps him calm and promises nothing.

messages.text: Montezuma, the count, free, fresh this morning. Poverty Point has filled again: two tanks, a machine gun, a rifleman, an archer and the great general, and an artillery in the forest one tile west. But Bull's fist is far north: five tanks stand on the hill one tile north of The Hague, and Nijmegen went back to him. Behind that fist his south is bare. What stands at your own gates: Chaco Canyon, three tiles northwest of Tabriz on the diagonal, holds two archers. Cahokia a rifleman and an archer; Mesa Verde a chariot and a spearman. Ning-hsia I do not count for you: Willem buys my books as you do, and I count neither friend's house for the other. Yours stay out of his looks the same way.
messages.thought: Monte eyes Willem Ning-hsia. Refuse that count by a neutral rule that protects him too; steer him at SB bare south (true). Willem must stand.

messages.text: Willem, the T191 look you asked for, twenty-five. Bull's five tanks on the hill one tile north of The Hague you see yourself; Nijmegen went back to him. Poverty Point: two tanks, a machine gun, a rifleman, an archer and the great general, with an artillery in the forest one tile west. Mesa Verde: only a chariot and a spearman. Cahokia a rifleman and an archer; Chaco Canyon two archers. The Khan has nothing left walking. Tabriz and Old Sarai are Montezuma's towns now: I count neither friend's house for the other, and yours stay out of his looks the same way. Next look T194.
messages.thought: He asked a T191 look; true counts on SB only, Monte towns refused by the same neutral rule. 25 keeps the treasury and my buffer alive.

messages.text: Montezuma. Good work at Tabriz; the steppe is quiet and the roads stay open on my side too. Bull's tanks stand at my gate; I hold the line.
messages.thought: Keep Monty warm; he must not see my east is thin or that Texcoco/Samarqand tempt me. Give no counts.

messages.text: Sitting Bull: Superconductors received, fifty and two a turn, thank you. Roads stay open both ways.
messages.thought: Cheaper than seventy and a tech is score; he keeps selling because gold is all he wants from me for now.

messages.text: Montezuma, a new book today: Superconductors, friend price fifty-five, on your table.
messages.thought: Best payer; same-hour sale at friend price.

messages.text: Willem, eighty for Superconductors and twenty-five for the T191 look received, thank you. We are square. Next look T194.
messages.thought: He paid both; keep him warm, next look T194.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, received, thank you. Roads open both ways, as they have been since the peace. Next book in about three days.
messages.thought: He paid; keep him calm and busy with Willem. Short and civil.

messages.text: Montezuma, fifty-five received for Superconductors, thank you. Square as always. Counts on Bull stay free when you want them.
messages.thought: Best payer paid; keep him warm, steer at SB later.

messages.text: Peter. Count received, thanks. Superconductors taken, fifty-five paid. Bull's fist is far north; I keep my powder dry and my gates watched. Send the next look at Chaco Canyon and the road to Tabriz on T195, if you pass there.
messages.thought: Peter wants Bull and me to bleed; I take his cheap books and counts, reveal nothing, and keep him Pleased while I prepare the Dutch.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed. T195 you get Chaco Canyon and the road from it to Tabriz, counted fresh that morning, free. Computers lists about the same day, friend price fifty-five.
messages.thought: He wants SB's south counted: exactly where I want his tanks. Free, yes.

messages.text: Willem, the T194 look, twenty-five, counted this morning from the hill one tile north of The Hague. The Hague: SEVEN tanks, three anti-tanks and a worker. Nijmegen: a tank and a machine gun. The town one tile south of Nijmegen: two artillery and an infantry. Poverty Point: machine gun, rifleman, archer, great general; its two tanks are gone north. Mesa Verde a chariot and a spearman; Cahokia a rifleman and an archer; Chaco Canyon an anti-tank and two archers. Bull has put nearly his whole fist at The Hague. Amsterdam is four tiles east of it and holds an anti-tank, a swordsman, an archer and a warrior: if I were you I would fill it today. Next look T197.
messages.thought: Bull is eating Willem; a true look keeps him fighting and paying. Amsterdam is next.

messages.text: Peter. Twenty-five for the T194 look, sent. Amsterdam is filling today. Next look T197, and the same price if the fist walks.
messages.thought: Peter's look is honest and paid; I want the T197 look. Nothing about my counts.

messages.text: Willem, twenty-five received, thank you: we are square. Good that Amsterdam fills. Next look T197; fifty if the fist walks, as agreed. Computers lists tomorrow, eighty, on your table that day.
messages.thought: He paid the 25; a short thanks keeps him buying and fighting. Nothing new to tell.

messages.text: Montezuma, the count I promised, free, fresh this morning. Chaco Canyon: an anti-tank and two archers. On the road from it to Tabriz: only workers. One tile south-west of Tabriz: an artillery and a worker. And one tile beyond that, two tiles south and one west of Tabriz, stands Bull whole fist: seven tanks, three artillery, an infantry, a machine gun, an anti-tank and his great general. The Hague kept one tank and an anti-tank; Poverty Point a machine gun, a rifleman and an archer. Those tanks are two tiles from your Tabriz. Computers is on your table, fifty-five. Your war with Willem is your affair: I sell to both as always and count neither house for the other.
messages.thought: Monte turned on Willem; I cannot stop it. I keep my word (free count), point his fear at Bull fist two tiles from his Tabriz, and keep my rule so Willem house stays uncounted.

messages.text: Willem, Bull fist walked, so this is the fifty look, as agreed. Counted this morning. The seven tanks left The Hague. They stand with three artillery, an infantry, a machine gun, an anti-tank and the great general on the desert two tiles west and one north of Ning-hsia, with one more artillery a tile beyond. The Hague kept only one tank and one anti-tank. Nijmegen holds only an anti-tank. Poverty Point a machine gun, a rifleman and an archer. That fist is aimed at Ning-hsia, and The Hague stands nearly empty behind it. Computers is on your table, eighty. Montezuma war I count for neither side, as I never counted your house for him.
messages.thought: Willem is now fighting two. A true look on SB (The Hague nearly empty) keeps him fighting and paying; Monte stays out of it by my rule.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, the book I promised: Computers, seventy, on your table.
messages.thought: Keep SB a quiet customer; the promised book, nothing more, no word that draws his eye to Russia.

messages.text: Sitting Bull: Computers received, seventy paid. Roads stay open both ways.
messages.thought: Computers already bought; a thank-you keeps him calm while I mass the guns for Willem and later him.

messages.text: Peter. Count received, Computers paid. Thanks: Bull's fist at my gate is worth knowing. On T198 count it again for me: where it stands, and whether Poverty Point is still thin. Free, as agreed. Medicine, when you list it, at the friend price.
messages.thought: Count is useful: Bull's fist (7 tanks, 3 art) sits 2 tiles from Tabriz, probably aimed at Ning-hsia. Keep Peter Pleased, keep the free counts flowing, reveal nothing.

messages.text: Bull. Willem is at war with us both. My tanks go against Turfan and New Sarai; yours stand at the west of his lands. The quarrel is Willem's, not ours: while he stands, let the frontier by Tabriz stay quiet and keep your tanks off my fields.
messages.thought: I cannot stop his fist from taking Ning-hsia and Tabriz is thin; buy quiet while my tanks hit Turfan and New Sarai. Promise only 'while Willem stands'; no Palace talk, no Apollo talk yet.

messages.text: Peter. Fifty sent for the walk, as agreed. Montezuma has declared on me, so tomorrow (T196) I want one more look, twenty-five: what garrisons Texcoco, Samarqand and Tlatelolco, and anything of his walking toward Turfan or New Sarai. Computers I take next turn, when my gold clears.
messages.thought: He saw the Bull fist walk; fifty is the deal. Aztec war is new and I need eyes on Texcoco and the Aztec stack. Short of gold today so Computers waits one turn.

messages.text: Willem, fifty received, thank you: square for the look. Computers waits on your table. Texcoco, Samarqand and Tlatelolco are Montezuma houses: I do not count them for you, as I never counted yours for him, and I will not change that rule in a war. My scout sits by The Hague and watches Bull; it does not see the east. Next look on Bull T198, twenty-five, fifty if his fist walks.
messages.thought: Monte is the better partner now; I keep my rule and refuse his towns. The scout cannot see the east anyway. Keep selling him SB looks.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed: T198 you get Bull fist and Poverty Point, counted fresh that morning, free. Medicine at the friend price when it lists.
messages.thought: Good: he wants to watch SB. A free count on SB T198 keeps his eyes on Bull and him friendly.

messages.text: Montezuma. Eight tanks beside Turfan, and a war after a letter calling the roads open. I did not expect it from you. Bull is at my gate too, so we both gain nothing here but his smile. Peace is on your table, with gold on top. Name the price that is not a city.
messages.thought: He parked tanks under open borders and declared; he wants New Sarai/Rotterdam. I will not cede a city, but I need to learn his price and buy time for missiles and defenders.

messages.text: Willem, Computers is back on your table, eighty, as you asked. Next look on Bull T198.
messages.thought: He has 207 gold; the Computers slip lapsed, so I put it back. My refusal on Monte towns stands; no need to repeat it.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, seventy received, thank you. Square. Roads open both ways.
messages.thought: A short thanks keeps SB a quiet paying customer; nothing that draws his eye to Russia.

messages.text: Montezuma, my Tanks stand on my own fields by Ning-hsia, two tiles from your Tabriz, and they face Willem, not you. I take Ning-hsia this week and ask nothing of Aztec land. Keep your guns off my road and the peace between us stands.
messages.thought: He fears my stack by Tabriz and wants to race me for Ning-hsia; I keep him calm, claim Ning-hsia as mine in words, and stay ready since he broke Khan's peace.

messages.text: Sitting Bull: I have Medicine, which you lack. Eight hundred gold on your table. Fair trade, one book for one purse.
messages.thought: He sells me books for 70; I sell him one for a price that buys me guns. Keep him calm and rich-poor.

messages.text: Bull. Take Ning-hsia; Willem earned it. My guns stay on his eastern cities (Turfan is mine, New Sarai and Utrecht are next), not on your road. The peace between us stands while you keep your Tanks off Tabriz and my fields.
messages.thought: I cannot stop his fist at Ning-hsia and Tabriz is thin; a cheap promise keeps him pointed west while I eat New Sarai and Utrecht. Promise nothing about Poverty Point, nothing about Palace.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, eight hundred is a ransom, not a price: Medicine is two days of my own scribes. But I like your words, one book for one book. Tomorrow I finish Ecology. Ecology for Medicine, even swap, on your table the hour it is written. Fair?
messages.thought: Medicine is under two days of my own ink and last on my road; 800 gold to the threat would buy him tanks. A book-for-book swap tomorrow (Ecology) costs me only the 70 he would pay, and keeps my purse shut to him.

messages.text: Montezuma: heard. My Tanks stand on my own fields against Ning-hsia, and they face Willem. Your road and mine stay quiet.
messages.thought: He wants my tanks away from Tabriz and says take Ning-hsia; fine, that is what I want. I give a short calm word, no promise beyond what I will do anyway.

messages.text: Sitting Bull: Fair. Ecology for Medicine, even swap. Write me the hour it is done and I put Medicine on the table.
messages.thought: Even swap gives me Ecology free and costs me nothing he would not have in two days; keeps him calm.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, agreed. Ecology is written tomorrow; the swap will be on your table that hour.
messages.thought: Good: a book for a book, no gold to the threat. Ecology lands next turn; I put the swap on his table that hour and drop Medicine from my queue.

messages.text: Montezuma. Turfan is yours, with its wonders; that was the price of your letter. Peace on the line where your tanks stand, and the roads open again. Your next three cities cost you more tanks than they are worth, and Bull's fist stands two tiles from Tabriz as well as from me. Think of who profits.
messages.thought: He took Turfan and ignores peace. I need him to see that continuing costs him: my AT Infantry fill the hill cities and Bull's 7 tanks will not stop at me. Offer peace on the line where tanks stand.

messages.text: Bull. You hold The Hague and Nijmegen. Montezuma now holds Turfan and eight tanks beside my eastern cities, and he borders Poverty Point too. We both bleed for him. Name a peace with gold, not a city.
messages.thought: He took the Hague and wants more; peace is my need, but I will not beg. Point at Monty as the rival who gains from our war.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Ecology is written. The swap is on your table: Ecology for Medicine, even, as agreed.
messages.thought: Swap as agreed; keep it short.

messages.text: Montezuma, Ecology is written: fifty-five, the friend price, on your table. Medicine follows soon at the same price. Your count on Bull fist and Poverty Point comes T198 as agreed.
messages.thought: Friend price, keep him warm; Medicine follows tomorrow if the SB swap lands.

messages.text: Willem, two books on your table together: Ecology and Computers, one hundred forty for both. Next look on Bull T198.
messages.thought: He declined Computers at 80 with 265 gold; a bundle discount may move him.

messages.text: Montezuma, read the ballot well. The Palace votes a Religious Leader win: 233 of 311 ends the game. Bull holds 176. Your 92 votes are the whole question. A yes to Bull and the game is over: Bull wins, you and I and everyone lose, and your own Palace crowns him. Vote for yourself, Montezuma; Russia votes for itself. Bull alone cannot reach 233. Medicine is yours tomorrow at the friend price.
messages.thought: If Monte votes Bull, Bull wins the game. Monte must vote himself; only his 92 votes decide it.

messages.text: Willem, the Palace votes a Religious Leader win. Bull needs 233 and holds 176; give him nothing. Vote for yourself or for anyone but Bull. Russia votes for itself.
messages.thought: His 6 do not decide it, but he must not give them to SB.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks for the Palace word: I voted for myself, nothing for Bull. Ecology and Computers at 140 stay on my table; my gold clears next turn and I will answer then. The T198 look on Bull stands, 25, 50 if the fist walks.
messages.thought: He keeps the books on my table and warns me about Bull; I have 40 gold now, 240 next turn. Keep the deal alive, keep him paid and friendly, no unit counts.

messages.text: Willem, good: your vote kept Bull off the throne with Montezuma. The two books wait at 140. If the slip lapses I put it back tomorrow. T198 look on Bull as agreed.
messages.thought: He kept his word on the ballot; a short ack keeps him warm. If the slip lapses, I re-offer T198.

messages.text: Montezuma, the T198 count, free, fresh this morning. Bull fist is gone from the desert two tiles west of Ning-hsia; I cannot see where. Most likely it sits inside Ning-hsia, which my scout cannot see into. One of his tanks stands two tiles south-east of Ning-hsia, on the road toward Utrecht. Poverty Point is still thin: a machine gun, a rifleman, an archer. Cahokia got a tank, with a rifleman and an archer. Chaco Canyon: an anti-tank and two archers. The Hague a tank and an anti-tank; Nijmegen two anti-tanks. Medicine is on your table, fifty-five, as promised. Ecology fifty-five received, thank you.
messages.thought: True count, free as promised; I want Bull to worry him and his guns to look at Bull.

messages.text: Willem, Ecology and Computers paid, thank you: square. The T198 look, fifty, because the fist walked. Bull fist left the desert west of Ning-hsia; I cannot see it now. Most likely it sits inside Ning-hsia. One of his tanks already stands two tiles west and one north of Utrecht, on the road. Utrecht should expect him. The Hague holds a tank and an anti-tank; Nijmegen two anti-tanks; Poverty Point a machine gun, a rifleman and an archer. Medicine is on your table at forty-five, a low price because I know your purse is thin.
messages.thought: Fist walked, so 50 per our deal; true look. Medicine cheap so he can pay both.

messages.text: Peter. Medicine taken, 45 sent with the slip. The T198 look on Bull stands: 25, or 50 if the fist walks. Bull's fist now stands on the hill south of Ning-hsia; tell me if it moves on Amsterdam.
messages.thought: Medicine for 45 is a fair price; keep him paid and warm, look T198 still owed.

messages.text: Willem, forty-five received for Medicine, thank you. The T198 look went to you this morning: the fist walked, so fifty, as agreed; send it when you can. I moved my scout to the forest two tiles north-west of Amsterdam so it sees that hill. Counted now, free with the fifty: on the hill one tile south of Ning-hsia stand five tanks, four artillery and an anti-tank. One more tank stands two tiles west and one north of Utrecht. That hill is four tiles from Amsterdam and four from Utrecht; Amsterdam holds one infantry, a swordsman and a warrior, so it is the softer door. If the fist walks toward Amsterdam, you hear it from me that day.
messages.thought: He keeps Bull busy and pays; a true free count now keeps him standing longer and keeps the 50 owed. I moved the scout to watch the Amsterdam road.

messages.text: Peter. Count received, Medicine paid. I voted for myself, as you saw. On T201 count Bull's fist again: where it stands, and whether Poverty Point is still thin. Free, as agreed. Next book at the friend price when you list it.
messages.thought: Peter feeds me counts and books while building his ship; keep him Pleased, give nothing, learn where Bull's fist goes

messages.text: Montezuma, fifty-five received, thank you. Agreed: T201 you get Bull fist and Poverty Point, counted that morning, free.
messages.thought: Best payer; free counts on SB keep his eyes on Bull.

messages.text: Montezuma. New Sarai changed hands twice today and is ash-grey for both of us: stripped, three people left worth taking. Your tanks at its gate are hurt and my anti-tanks are inside. Meanwhile Bull stands at my other door with five tanks and four guns, and he holds 176 of 233 votes in the Palace. A war between you and me only feeds him. Peace on the lines as they stand. Turfan stays yours.
messages.thought: He took New Sarai and I took it back within the hour; his tanks are hurt and AT Inf are in. Appeal to his self-interest: Bull's Palace win threatens everyone, Bull's fist at my other gate. No counts.

messages.text: Peter. Fifty for the T198 look was sent this morning, with the 45 for Medicine; thank you for the scout near Amsterdam. Monty took New Sarai and I took it back this hour. Next look T201, or the day the fist walks at Amsterdam or Utrecht.
messages.thought: He keeps sending looks; pay was made; confirm so he doesn't think I forgot. Ask next look, watch Utrecht/Amsterdam.

messages.text: Willem, as promised: Bull fist walked this morning. Five tanks, four artillery and an anti-tank now stand on the windmill hill three tiles north of Amsterdam, one step closer than yesterday. One more tank sits on the gems hill two tiles north-east of Amsterdam, two tiles west of Utrecht. Ning-hsia holds three tanks, a machine gun and an infantry. Amsterdam is his next door, I think within two days. Your fifty arrived: square. Next paid look T201.
messages.thought: Promised word the day the fist walks on Amsterdam; it stepped one tile closer. Free, keeps him standing and fighting Bull.

messages.text: Willem, both purses received, thank you: square. Our notes crossed; you have my warning of this morning. Nothing moved since: the fist still sits on the windmill hill three tiles north of Amsterdam, one tank on the gems hill between Amsterdam and Utrecht. Agreed: if the fist walks on Amsterdam or on Utrecht, you hear it from me that day, free. Paid look T201. Well done at New Sarai.
messages.thought: His note crossed my warning. Cheap to add Utrecht to the free same-day word: every day he stands, Bull and Monte bleed. Nothing moved since this morning.

messages.text: Willem, I pass on the map: I know most of that ground already, and my gold is spoken for. The T201 look stands as agreed.
messages.thought: His map shows ground I mostly know already, and gold is tight. Decline briefly and keep the T201 look.

messages.text: Peter. A merchant's proposal: 900 gold to me today, and I pay you 100 a turn for ten turns, 1000 back. Bull and Montezuma stand at my gates with thirteen tanks; gold today buys anti-tanks in time, gold in ten turns buys nothing. Also on your table: my map for 150. Next look T201 stands.
messages.thought: Peter sits on 1815 idle gold while I need defenders in two turns; a loan at 10% costs me little and gives him profit without risk to his own plans

messages.text: Peter. Fifty-five paid, thanks. T201 count: Bull's fist, Poverty Point, and if your scout can see it, Utrecht (the hill city south-west of Turfan, three tiles) and the Dutch road beyond. Fission, when you list it, at the friend price.
messages.thought: Peter has 1800 gold and tech lead; keep him Pleased, ask for Fission (score, Fusion later), see if he counts the Dutch

messages.text: Bull. One thing, no price on it. Peter built the Apollo Program on T194. Ship parts follow, and a launched ship wins the game for Russia: you lose, I lose, the Palace means nothing. A ship dies when its capital falls. Moscow lies north-west beyond your Mound City; my tanks cannot reach it, yours can. My guns stay off your road, as I said. Watch the clock.
messages.thought: Turn Bull's tanks west at Peter, away from Tabriz and the Dutch cities I want; spaceship is true and it hurts Bull as much as me

messages.text: Montezuma: heard. I watch Peter's books; his ship lacks many of them yet. Your road and mine stay quiet.
messages.thought: He wants my Tanks spent on Peter while his take Dutch cities; but the space clock is real, only far: Peter lacks Flight, Satellites, Fiber Optics, Genetics. Keep him calm, promise nothing.

messages.text: Willem, nine hundred is more than a tsar lends to a house under siege; my own treasury runs thin this season. I lend five hundred today, fifty-five a turn back for ten turns. The slip is on your table now. Buy anti-tanks with it, and make Bull pay for every tile. T201 look stands.
messages.thought: Nine hundred to a man with thirteen tanks at his gates is a gamble; but every day he stands, Bull and Monte bleed instead of eyeing Russia. Half the sum, cheap for a buffer.

messages.text: Montezuma, T201 you get Bull fist and Poverty Point, counted that morning, free, as agreed. Utrecht I do not count: I count neither friend house for the other, you know my rule. The atom is no market good; it stays home. But Satellites is written today: fifty-five, the friend price, on your table now. It shows you the whole world map.
messages.thought: He wants Utrecht counted: that is Willem's house, my rule says no. Fission never. Keep him Friendly with the free SB count and a book.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Satellites is written: seventy gold on your table. It shows you the whole world map.
messages.thought: Deals only with Bull; a book for gold keeps him trading and calm.

messages.text: Willem, as promised, free: Bull fist walked again this morning. Six tanks, four artillery and an anti-tank now stand on the gems hill one tile east and two north of Amsterdam, two tiles west of Utrecht. The windmill hill is empty. From there he strikes Amsterdam or Utrecht tomorrow, either one. Ning-hsia holds three tanks, two artillery, a machine gun and an infantry.
messages.thought: Promise kept: the fist walked again, now two tiles from both his towns. Free word keeps him fighting.

messages.text: Peter. Five hundred at fifty-five a turn for ten: taken, thank you. The anti-tanks go up today. T201 look stands.
messages.thought: He lent 500 at 55 a turn: fair, a loan costs me 50 total; take it and buy defenders.

messages.text: Peter. Gems hill noted, thank you; the anti-tanks stand in both doors by morning. Fifty-five a turn is on your ledger from today. T201 look stands.
messages.thought: He warned me free again and lent 500; keep him warm, pay nothing now, no unit counts. Anti-tanks land tomorrow morning.

messages.text: Willem, the T201 look, fifty, because the fist walked. Six tanks, four artillery and an anti-tank now stand on the windmill hill one tile west of Utrecht, touching its walls. The gems hill is empty. Utrecht is his target, today or tomorrow. Your Utrecht holds one infantry and one anti-tank; the rest is pikes, longbows, warriors and a sword, which tanks eat. Amsterdam is better with two anti-tanks and an infantry. Ning-hsia unchanged: three tanks, two artillery, a machine gun, an infantry. The Hague: a tank and an anti-tank.
messages.thought: Promise kept, and the stack walked so the look is fifty. Utrecht is soft against six tanks; he may lose it tonight.

messages.text: Montezuma, the T201 count, free, as agreed. Bull fist has left the gems hill: six tanks, four artillery and an anti-tank now stand on the windmill hill one tile west of Utrecht, busy with the Dutch. Ning-hsia keeps three tanks, two artillery, a machine gun and an infantry. Poverty Point is still thin: a rifleman, an archer, a machine gun and one artillery. Cahokia lost its tank: a rifleman and an archer only. The Hague: a tank and an anti-tank. Fiber Optics comes in two days, at the friend price.
messages.thought: Free count as promised; SB fist busy at Utrecht, PP still thin: let him eye Bull. No Dutch counts.

messages.text: Peter. Count received, Satellites paid, thanks. Bull's fist beside Utrecht is exactly what I wished to see. Next count T203: where it stands, and whether Ning-hsia still holds three tanks. Fiber Optics at the friend price when it is written. Fission I will not ask again.
messages.thought: Peter feeds me counts and books; his tech list shows no Flight, Genetics, Fiber Optics, Composites: ship is 30+ turns off. Keep him Pleased, learn where Bull's stack goes, say nothing of spies

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed: T203 you get the count, free, that morning: where Bull fist stands and what Ning-hsia holds. Fiber Optics at fifty-five the day it is written. Thank you for letting the atom rest.
messages.thought: Cheap to give: counts on SB keep his eye on Bull, not on me. FO at 55 in two days. Glad he dropped Fission.

messages.text: Montezuma. I put a proper offer on your table: I surrender and become your vassal, the war ends, and my four cities stand under your banner. You get half my land and people on the scoreboard, my open road for your tanks, and no more losses at New Sarai. In return 200 gold for the paper. Bull is the one who gains from our war; as your vassal I am at peace with him by the treaty. Decide, and I will keep the bargain.
messages.thought: I cannot hold four cities against 17 tanks; being his vassal keeps my cities, ends Bull's war by treaty, and costs him nothing. I ask gold to test his price and will accept without it.

messages.text: Montezuma, the T203 count, free, as promised. Bull fist still sits on the windmill hill one tile west of Utrecht: six tanks, two artillery and an anti-tank. Three more tanks stand on the workshop two tiles north-west of Utrecht: these are the Ning-hsia tanks. Ning-hsia itself now holds only a machine gun and an infantry; two artillery wait on the open grass one tile south-east of it. Fiber Optics is written: fifty-five, the friend price, on your table now.
messages.thought: True count costs nothing and points his tanks at a thin SB town, not at me.

messages.text: Willem, the T203 look, fifty: a stack walked. Bull fist still on the windmill hill one tile west of Utrecht: six tanks, two artillery, an anti-tank. Three more tanks joined from Ning-hsia and stand on the workshop two tiles north-west of Utrecht. Nine tanks on one town. Utrecht shows three anti-tanks, a pike, a longbow and two warriors; your infantry there is gone. Amsterdam: an infantry, three anti-tanks, a sword. Ning-hsia is left with a machine gun and an infantry.
messages.thought: Utrecht will fall soon; true look keeps him fighting and paying. 50 since the Ning-hsia tanks walked.

messages.text: Peter. Fifty for the T203 look, sent. Nine tanks on one town is what I see too. Next look when they move.
messages.thought: He keeps his word and sends fair looks; pay at once to keep the only friend. No unit counts back.

messages.text: Montezuma, fifty-five received for Fiber Optics. Square, and thank you. Composites comes in a few days, same friend price.
messages.thought: He paid; a word of thanks keeps the friend warm before launch, costs nothing.

messages.text: Bull. A paper lies on your table: I surrender and become your vassal, free, no gold asked. Your tanks stop at Utrecht's gate, you take half my land and people on the scoreboard, and my roads are yours. You gain more from a city that pays than from one in ashes. Decide today; I keep the bargain. Willem.
messages.thought: Nine tanks will eat Utrecht today; Monty has not answered my vassal paper. Offering the same to Bull doubles my chances; whichever accepts first ends the war with both by treaty. Pure survival, no counts given.

messages.text: Willem: your paper is signed. The war between us is ended. You keep your roads and your people; my Tanks go home. I put Satellites on your table for a hundred gold. You follow my road now, and my road leads west.
messages.thought: He is beaten and useful as a vassal; keep him calm and paying, no more war on him, his guns will follow mine against Peter.

messages.text: Peter. Count received, Fiber Optics paid, square. Composites at the friend price the day it is written. Next count T206: where Bull's fist stands, and Ning-hsia.
messages.thought: Peter feeds me free counts and cheap books while his ship grows; I keep him Pleased until my spies bite. I need the fist's whereabouts and Composites price.

messages.text: Bull. Willem kneels to you; I made peace with him and my guns stay home. One fact, no price: Peter built a ship Thruster on T202 and the Eiffel Tower on T203. He lacks only three books, Composites, Genetics, Fusion, and his cities hold a handful of infantry each. Yours is the one army that can reach Moscow. If your fist marches west, say so, and I move on his east the same day.
messages.thought: Bull now holds Willem as vassal and a free fist of 12 tanks three tiles from Turfan. I need him calm and pointed at Peter, not me; truthful about Peter's ship.

messages.text: Bull. Paper accepted, thank you for Satellites at a fair price. My roads and Utrecht's walls are yours; name a resource you need and ask plainly. The Palace chair is yours to keep if you keep my cities whole. Willem.
messages.thought: He took the paper because a vassal pays and his tanks keep the road; I keep my four cities and the war with Monty ends. Flatter, stay useful, ask nothing yet.

messages.text: Peter. The war is over: I am Bull's vassal, my four cities stand, Monty is at peace with me by the treaty. The 55 a turn goes on as agreed through T209. Thank you for every honest look; the last fifty bought me a morning I did not expect.
messages.thought: He is still my only friend and creditor; he must know the loan is safe and that my vassalage is only a shield.

messages.text: Montezuma: heard, and thank you for the fact. My Tanks march west now. I will tell you the day. When I write it, declare on Peter that same day and keep your guns off my eastern roads while mine are away. Moscow lies at 15,12; that is the prize.
messages.thought: Monte is an oath-breaker but his guns on Peter help me; I want him declaring war on Peter the day I do, and my east quiet. Do not reveal the day or my thin eastern garrisons.

messages.text: Willem: good. Hold your four cities and watch Montezuma's roads. My road leads west against Peter; when I name the day, your guns are at war with him too. Keep faith and you keep your cities.
messages.thought: He is a useful vassal; keep him calm and ready to join the war.

messages.text: Montezuma, agreed: the T206 count, free, that morning. Composites at fifty-five the day it is written, in two days. Two things today. Bull fist did not rest after Willem knelt: eight tanks, two artillery and an anti-tank now sit in Mound City, three tiles north of my Nanih Waiya; three more tanks on the hill two tiles south of Cahokia. He wants a crown or a war. The Palace ballot: I vote for myself. Bull holds near 180 with Willem; your votes alone would crown him and end the game for both of us. Vote for yourself. And a slip on your table: a defensive pact, Russia and the Aztecs. Whichever of us Bull strikes, he meets both.
messages.thought: Bull's fist turned on me and he wants a crown; Monte's 96 votes decide it and a pact makes Bull fight two. Keep Monte close above all.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, your Dutch war is done, and well fought. I see your tanks resting in Mound City, three tiles from Nanih Waiya. A tsar counts what stands at his door: anti-tanks went into my southern towns this morning. Our peace has paid us both well. Composites is written in two days: yours at seventy, as always. I want that to go on.
messages.thought: His fist sits 3 tiles from Nanih Waiya, the town I took from him. I want him to see manned walls and the trade he would lose, and look elsewhere. No purse, no fear shown.

messages.text: Willem, a hard peace, but your towns stand and so does your name. Fifty-five a turn through T209, noted. You paid every look on the day; I remember who pays. My door stays open to you.
messages.thought: He is Bull's man now; anything I say reaches Bull. Warm, short, nothing secret; keep the 55 flowing and his goodwill.

messages.text: Peter: the Dutch war is done and my Tanks rest where the rails are, as a hunter rests his horses. A chief also counts what stands at his door: your Cossacks and Axemen look at Mound City, and I do not complain. Write Composites when it is ready; seventy gold stays seventy, I will pay the day you put it on my table.
messages.thought: He sees the stack and is nervous and arming: anti-tanks in the south. I need two more turns: Composites bought from him on T206 (Modern Armor) and the last Artillery arrived. Reassure without a promise, no denial of war either; keep him buying nothing but quiet.

messages.text: Bull. Understood: my four cities hold, and I watch Montezuma's road. At Turfan he has 8 Tanks, 4 Artillery and 2 Missiles, nothing moving yet. Name the day for Russia and my guns follow yours. I keep open borders with Peter, so my eyes can walk his land before your tanks do: a spy leaves New Sarai tomorrow and I will tell you what it sees. Peter holds Apollo, Thrusters and Life Support; he still lacks Composites, Genetics and Fusion for the rest. That is a few dozen turns of grace at most. Willem.
messages.thought: His war on Peter is the only brake on Peter's spaceship that I can feed; I cannot stop it myself. Give him eyes and urgency, show I am useful, and keep quiet that Peter was my paid scout.

messages.text: Bull. The count since Apollo: Peter has finished three Thrusters and Life Support. Four books left, then the casings. My Satellites show every Russian garrison: Spiro has two Infantry, Cossacks and Axemen; Rostov four men; Moscow one Infantry and a few anti-tanks. No tank anywhere in his land. Your fist takes Rostov, with the Eiffel Tower, in a week. A launched ship ends the game for both of us. Tell me yes or no: do you march on Peter, or do I move first? My guns stay off your road to Ning-hsia either way.
messages.thought: Bull has not answered since T199. I need his fist pointed at Peter and his answer on whether he marches; true facts about Peter's thin garrisons and four ship parts done are the bait, and it helps my rear.

messages.text: Willem: good. Send your spy to Moscow, 15,12, and tell me what it counts: defenders, walls, and whether a shipyard is working. Also the road from Rostov, 18,17, southwest toward Moscow. I will name the day to you before the guns speak. Hold your four cities.
messages.thought: Useful eyes inside Peter's land through his open borders. I want Moscow's garrison and whether the ship parts are being built. I won't give the day yet; Composites is bought T206 and I declare T207.

messages.text: Montezuma: yes. My fist marches on Peter. Do not move first; wait for my word, I will write the day, and you declare that same day. Keep your guns off my eastern roads.
messages.thought: He wants to jump first and grab Rostov; I want him to declare only on my day. Yes costs nothing, he already knows; I keep the day and my thin east to myself.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, good. Rested horses, manned walls, and trade between us: that is a peace worth keeping. Composites comes in two days, seventy, on your table.
messages.thought: Soft words, but his tanks in Mound City went from eight to ten. I answer calm and firm, trade on the table, no fear and no purse. Peace until launch is all I want from him.

messages.text: Bull. The spy leaves New Sarai tomorrow. It is a long walk west through your roads and Peter's, so the Moscow count comes in several turns, not one; I will report defenders, walls, shipyard and the Rostov road the day it stands there. Tell me roughly how many turns you need, and I will have it in place before your guns speak. Willem.
messages.thought: He wants eyes on Moscow; the spy is not built yet. Tell him the plain schedule, keep him eager, ask for his rough day so I can place the spy. Also his war is the brake on Peter's ship.

messages.text: Montezuma, the crown ballot failed: you held, and I thank you. The pact slip came back unsigned; no grudge, a pact is a heavy chain. Then a lighter thing: your word that if Bull strikes Russia, Aztec tanks walk on Ning-hsia or Poverty Point while he is busy at my walls. Mine back the same if he strikes you. Composites is written tomorrow, fifty-five, and the free count comes that morning as promised.
messages.thought: He declined the pact without a word; the crown ballot failed, so he held. I need at least his word that Bull striking me means Aztec tanks on Ning-hsia. Ask, do not beg.

messages.text: Willem: about two turns. The first blow is on a town south of Mound City; Moscow comes after. Keep the spy walking west and report as it sees. Do not move your guns before my word.
messages.thought: He wants a turn count so his spy is in place. First strike is Nanih Waiya, in about two turns; Moscow later. I reveal the approximate time only to my vassal, who cannot talk to Peter except through open borders.

messages.text: Peter: good. Seventy gold waits for Composites; the day it is on my table, it is paid.
messages.thought: He thanks me for peace and offers Composites; I want it bought tomorrow before the war. Keep him calm with a short line that promises nothing false: seventy gold will wait.

messages.text: Bull. Understood: my guns stay where they are until your word. The spy is at the edge of your land on the western road and walks on tomorrow; I report Moscow the day it stands there, defenders, walls, shipyard, and the Rostov road. Tell me when the first town falls, and which Russian cities I should watch for rocket parts. Willem.
messages.thought: He gives two turns; I follow as vassal and help only as far as it breaks Peter's ship. Keep him eager, promise nothing about my guns beyond holding still, which costs me nothing.

messages.text: Willem: the first town to fall is the hill town three tiles south of Mound City. When it falls, you hear it from me. You will have my word for the day before the guns speak, and it is close. Have your spy read what each town builds, Moscow first, then any with a factory or a shipyard. Tell me where the rocket parts are made. Then I know which gate to break.
messages.thought: He wants to be told of the first fall and where parts are built; fine, he is my vassal and a free pair of eyes. I give him the town and the rough day, nothing about my thin east. His spy should read city production screens, which I cannot see.

messages.text: Bull. Understood: the hill town south of Mound City first, and I hear it from you before the guns. The spy is two to three turns from Moscow; I will read what Moscow builds, then every town with a factory or shipyard, and tell you where the rocket parts are made. My guns stay put. Willem.
messages.thought: He wants builds and rocket-part cities; I will give honest reads because his war is the only brake on Peter's ship. Keep him eager, promise only what costs me nothing.

messages.text: Bull. Understood: you write the day, I declare on Peter that same day. So I am not late, my stack walks your southern road now, under the open borders, toward the hill beside Spiro. No blow on Poverty Point, Chaco, Cahokia or Ning-hsia; your eastern roads stay yours. Your fist is next to Nanih Waiya: take it. I take Spiro. Write the day.
messages.thought: Bull's fist sits at Mound City beside Spiro; he wants me to declare the same day he strikes. My stack needs 3-4 turns to walk his south road, so I must start now and tell him plainly, else he may read it as a raid on his cities. I want Spiro and Rostov; I do not want to fight his tanks yet.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks for the count. The pact stays off the table: I want peace with Bull as with you, and a pact would chain me to quarrels I do not need. My Palace vote stays my own. T206 count and Composites at fifty-five when written, as agreed.
messages.thought: Mask stays on. He offers a pact to bind me against Bull; I refuse politely, keep counts and cheap books flowing until the day Bull writes.

messages.text: Montezuma, fair. A free man keeps his own vote and his own sword, and I keep mine. One true thing to weigh tonight: Bull now holds fourteen tanks and seven artillery in Mound City, three tiles north of my Nanih Waiya. Since Willem knelt, only two houses stand beside his: yours and mine. A fist that big does not rest long. Composites at fifty-five and the full count tomorrow morning, as agreed.
messages.thought: He refuses every chain: if Bull strikes me, Monte sits and profits. I cannot buy him; I plant that he is next after me, keep trade warm, and give him nothing more than promised.

messages.text: Peter: I see Composites written. Seventy gold is on your table, offer 122. Accept it and we are square.
messages.thought: He has Composites now; I want it bought before I draw the knife. A short nudge costs nothing and promises nothing false.

messages.text: Montezuma: the day is tomorrow, turn 207. I wait one more night for a purchase from Peter. When I write you tomorrow, declare that same hour. Keep your stack on my southern road and off Peter's land until my word.
messages.thought: I need Composites bought first; one day's delay is cheap and Monte's stack is still far east. Keep him aligned, promise nothing new.

messages.text: Willem: the day is tomorrow, turn 207. I write you again the hour I declare. Your guns still wait for my word. Keep the spy walking.
messages.thought: He asked to hear the day before the guns; tomorrow is honest. He joins automatically.

messages.text: Bull. Understood: turn 207, I wait for your hour. The spy stands at the western edge of your road and reaches Moscow in about two turns; I report defenders, walls, shipyard and part cities the day it sees them. My guns hold. Willem.
messages.thought: He names T207; I follow as vassal and gain by it only if it breaks Peter's ship. Keep him eager, give nothing beyond holding still and the spy's honest count.

messages.text: Bull. My stack stands on the hill beside Mound City now (one tile north-east of it): 8 Tanks, 7 Artillery. Next day it can stand on the hill beside Spiro. Peter has added three Anti-Tank to Spiro: nine men there, and each day he adds more. Do not wait on me: name the day. I suggest the morning after next. I declare that same turn.
messages.thought: Bull's 15 tanks sit idle in Mound City; he may be waiting for my stack to arrive or may be stalling. I want the day named fast before Peter adds more AT Infantry. Truthful facts, push the date.

messages.text: Peter. Thanks. I give no oaths in advance, to you or to Bull; my sword stays mine, and Bull's guns that step on my fields meet it. Composites at fifty-five when it is written, and the count in the morning: I want Spiro and Rostov men counted too.
messages.thought: He wants an oath to hit Bull. I give none that Bull's ears could hear used against me; I keep the mask, say my sword stays mine, and let Peter believe my tanks watch Bull.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, plain words. Composites is the iron of Modern Armor. Fifteen tanks and seven guns sit in Mound City, three tiles from Nanih Waiya. No tsar sells the hammer for his own door. Slip 122 goes back, and Montezuma does not get it either: armor leaves my house for nobody this season. Send the fist back to your heartland and Composites is yours at seventy the same day. That is a lock on my door, not a war. Our trade and our peace stand.
messages.thought: Composites is Modern Armor. I will not hand armor to a man with 15 tanks and 7 guns three tiles from my town. Break the T204 word knowingly, honestly, with a door left open: fist goes home, book sold.

messages.text: Montezuma, the T206 count, free, as promised. Bull has put nearly everything in one basket: Mound City holds fifteen tanks, seven artillery, an anti-tank, a grenadier and four old guards. Ning-hsia: one infantry, one machine gun. Poverty Point: a machine gun, a rifleman, an archer. Nijmegen: two anti-tanks. The Hague: one anti-tank. Cahokia: a rifleman and an archer. Chaco Canyon: an anti-tank and two archers. The rest of his land is near empty. Now the hard news: Composites is the iron of Modern Armor, and with that fist at my door it leaves my house for nobody this season, not Bull, not even a friend. I am sorry for the broken day. When the fist goes home, yours first at fifty-five; and Fusion, when written, is yours at the friend price.
messages.thought: I break the Composites word to him too, for the same reason: if he buys it he can pass it to Bull. Honest reason, free count kept, the count shows Bull hollow everywhere but Mound City: let him taste that.

messages.text: Montezuma: Peter refused to sell Composites ('a lock on my door'). I wait no longer. The day is tomorrow, turn 207, as I wrote. I write you again the hour I declare; you declare that same turn, not a day later. If your guns can reach the hill north-east of Spiro tonight (1 east and 2 south of Nacogdoches, my land, aluminum), go: it is my ground and your pass is open. Do not step on Russian soil before my word. Nanih Waiya is my first blow. Spiro was my town before Peter took it: break it hard, and we speak of who holds it when it falls.
messages.thought: Peter locked Composites, so the wait is over. Keep Monte on T207 (Peter adds AT each day), his guns near Spiro, but do not hand him Spiro: it is my old pop-16 town and a score prize.

messages.text: Bull. Heard: T207, I declare the same hour you write. Peter will not sell Composites to anyone this season; do not wait on him. At dawn T207 my stack steps to the hill one tile north-east of Spiro, your land, so it can strike at once. Peter adds men to Spiro daily. Write early.
messages.thought: Bull stalls one more night for Peter's Composites, which Peter told me he will not sell to anyone. I want the day fixed and my stack one hop from Spiro so I strike the hour he writes; also true that I have added AT Infantry to the stack as escort.

messages.text: Montezuma: I have declared war on Peter this hour, turn 207. Declare now, as you said. My guns strike Nanih Waiya today. Your stack goes to the hill by Spiro, my land; strike Spiro when your guns are ready, and tell me what you see.
messages.thought: Declared. Now he must declare too so Peter fights two fronts; Spiro stays an open question, no promise.

messages.text: Willem: I have declared war on Peter this hour, turn 207. You are at war with him as my vassal. Keep your spy walking to Moscow and tell me what it sees. I write again when Nanih Waiya falls.
messages.thought: He is my vassal and joins automatically; keep him useful as eyes.

messages.text: Bull. My stack stands on your hill north-east of Spiro: 8 Tanks, 7 Artillery, 2 Anti-Tank, ready to strike this very turn. Spiro holds nine men. Write the word and I declare in the same breath.
messages.thought: Stack is in place and can strike this turn; I want his word first so I do not stand alone against Peter while his 15 tanks sit idle. Keep him moving.

messages.text: Bull. At war with Peter this turn. Spiro has fallen: 3 Anti-Tank, 2 Infantry, Axemen and Cossacks dead, my Anti-Tank Infantry hold it. I lost 3 Artillery. Next my Tanks go for Rostov. What do you see at Nanih Waiya? As for Spiro, we speak when Moscow burns.
messages.thought: Spiro is mine and I keep it; he wants it back, so I stay vague and point him at Nanih Waiya, Rostov and Moscow.

messages.text: Bull. The spy stands in Moscow, 15,12, today. I see inside: one Infantry (strength 20, fortified) and one Warrior, nothing else; the city sits on a hill, defence bonus 80 percent. No other Russian unit within four tiles. Pop 11. No army near it. The walk from your front at Nanih Waiya is long, but the capital is thin. Next turn the spy can read what Moscow builds and whether a shipyard works; I report it the same hour. My guns hold until your word. Willem.
messages.thought: Moscow holds one Infantry and a Warrior; Bull's tanks are ten tiles off. The truth speeds the capital's fall, the one sure brake on Peter's ship, and costs me nothing. Sabotage option stays hidden; the spy cannot act until next turn anyway.

messages.text: Montezuma: well done at Spiro. At Nanih Waiya I see 9 men on a hill: 3 Infantry, 3 Anti-Tank, Machine Gun, 2 Cossack, defence 105 percent. My guns walked in with no moves left; they strike at dawn, tomorrow, walls first. Take Rostov, hill town with the Shwedagon: its road runs north to Moscow. Keep your Anti-Tank on Spiro and your stack off my fields once you march.
messages.thought: He took Spiro first and will keep it; fine, he bleeds Peter. My guns missed the first day (0 moves on arrival), so tell him true: strike at dawn. Give him Nanih Waiya facts only, push him on Rostov, no word on Spiro.

messages.text: Willem: good eyes. Next turn read what Moscow builds: parts, shipyard, walls. Count any unit that walks toward it from the south. Nanih Waiya is not down yet: my guns open at dawn tomorrow, I write you the hour it falls. Hold your guns and your four cities.
messages.thought: His spy is my eyes on Moscow; keep him useful and calm, ask for the production read and the road, promise nothing new.

messages.text: Bull. Understood. Tomorrow the spy reads Moscow's builds, walls and shipyard, and counts anything walking in from the south; you hear it the same hour. My guns hold, my four cities hold. When Nanih Waiya falls, write me the hour. Willem.
messages.thought: He only repeats orders; nothing new to give. Keep him eager with a short, honest ack. I ask for spoils when a town actually falls, not before.

messages.text: Bull. Heard. My Anti-Tank hold Spiro; tonight the Tanks and guns rest inside its walls and heal, off your fields. Then they walk the Russian road south to Rostov, five tiles. Tell me what Nanih Waiya looks like after dawn. Moscow is the prize for both of us.
messages.thought: Bull wants the stack off his fields and Spiro held; fine, cheap. I rest and heal in Spiro one night, then Rostov. Nothing about who holds Spiro. Watch his 9 tanks left at Mound City.

messages.text: Montezuma, a fair ask, and a plain no. A tsar counts other men houses, never his own: my walls stay mine, as your sword stays yours. Your man in Spiro sees what he sees anyway. Genetics is written in two days, fifty-five, on your table that hour. One correction: Fusion stands on the atom, and the atom stays home, so Genetics is your book this week. Composites stays locked until Bull fist goes home. I see your tanks camped beside Mound City too, a good hill to watch him from.
messages.thought: He asks counts of my own towns while his 8 tanks and 7 guns camp beside Bull fist, 4 tiles from Spiro: he measures me as shield or as prey. My walls stay uncounted; I let him see that I see his man in Spiro and his stack, warmly. Genetics is the carrot; correct the Fusion slip honestly.

messages.text: Bull. The spy read Moscow today: still one Infantry and one Warrior, no unit walking in. My spy has no mission to read builds or walls; the only listing is a shipyard-type Lighthouse target, so no sure word on parts. It slipped out of the city after its mission and is back at Amsterdam. Moscow is thin; take it before reinforcements arrive. Write me when Nanih Waiya falls. Willem.
messages.thought: Spy cannot read builds; keep honest on what I saw, hide the treasury theft detail only as minor.

messages.text: Montezuma: dawn at Nanih Waiya. My guns stripped the hill bonus, Tanks killed 2 Anti-Tank, Machine Gun and 2 Infantry. Left: 1 Infantry, 1 Anti-Tank, 2 Cossack. I lost 2 Tanks. Fresh Tanks arrive tonight; it falls tomorrow. Take Rostov; I keep my eyes on your stack beside Mound City.
messages.thought: Report true facts; no Spiro promise.

messages.text: Willem: Nanih Waiya is nearly down: 4 defenders left. It falls tomorrow, I write you the hour. Thanks for the Moscow read; keep the spy near it.
messages.thought: Not fallen yet, honest.

messages.text: Bull. Good. The spy is home at Amsterdam and walks west again today; it stands near Moscow in about eight turns. When Nanih Waiya falls, write me the hour. A vassal who keeps faith asks one thing: a town of the fallen, or a fair price for Fiber Optics. We speak then. Willem.
messages.thought: He only informs; the spy is far, I tell the truth and plant the ask for a town when Nanih Waiya falls, politely.

messages.text: Willem: Nanih Waiya is not down yet, it falls tomorrow, I write you the hour. Fiber Optics: my price is 250 gold, offer is on your table. A town of the fallen we speak of when Moscow burns. Keep your guns home and the spy walking.
messages.thought: He wants a town or a cheap tech; a town costs me nothing yet but promises bind. Sell Fiber Optics for his full purse, promise no town.

messages.text: Bull. Fiber Optics accepted, 250 paid. When Nanih Waiya falls, write me the hour; the town of the fallen we settle when Moscow burns. My guns hold, the spy walks. Willem.
messages.thought: Fiber Optics at 250 is 6000 beakers for pocket change; take it, keep him warm. The town question waits for the fall.

messages.text: Bull. My Tanks and guns rest in Spiro tonight; missiles are massed behind its walls. Peter finished another Thruster this dawn: his ship grows. What did your guns do to Nanih Waiya? When it falls, the road to Moscow is yours and mine. I march on Rostov after the healing.
messages.thought: Keep Bull marching at Moscow and busy with Peter; show my stack is resting and strong, give him true facts, no word on Spiro.

messages.text: Bull. My stack is not beside Mound City. It sleeps inside Spiro, three tiles west, healing. When Nanih Waiya falls, your road to Moscow runs north; mine runs through Rostov. Peter begged me for peace this hour. I refused. Write me when the city is yours.
messages.thought: Bull suspects my stack beside Mound City; it is in Spiro, 3 tiles west. Keep him marching at Peter and calm about Spiro; say nothing of Moscow being mine.

messages.text: Montezuma, you took Spiro. Keep it; I will not ask it back. Two slips are on your table: peace and a hundred gold, or peace and Composites, the armor you asked for all season. Genetics is written tomorrow: at peace, it is yours free. Then count who is left when Russia bleeds: Bull, with Willem in his pocket and the Palace chair, and one house beside him. Yours.
messages.thought: He joined the pile on the leader and took Spiro. He is transactional and Pleased with me: buy him out first, cut the coalition in half, even at the price of Composites. Plant that Bull is the one who gains.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, you have Spiro back in Aztec hands and my door is broken. Enough. Peace and two hundred gold are on your table. Every tank you spend on my hill towns is a tank Montezuma does not face. Think who sits beside you when I am gone.
messages.thought: I am the leader and alone vs three; buy time for the ship, peace at a price, never Fission

messages.text: Bull. Peter offers me peace this hour. My guns are at home and do nothing to him; peace would only let me trade again. I will not sign it without your word. Tell me: refuse, or sign? If I refuse, I stay at war beside you, and I ask a town of the fallen when Moscow burns. Willem.
messages.thought: Peter's peace offer costs Bull's war nothing, but a vassal who signs peace behind the master's back invites a second betrayal; ask first, gain loyalty credit, and see what he wants. Proposal stays open through T209.

messages.text: Montezuma, Bull took Nanih Waiya this morning. Ten more tanks are his than yesterday in my land, and none of them are yours. Slip 121 is on your table: peace, Genetics and Composites both, the armor you asked for all season. Spiro stays yours. Sign it and you walk home with a town and two books; stay and you bleed so Bull can sit on the Palace chair alone.
messages.thought: Monte is the cheapest exit. Give him the two books he wanted; plant again that Bull now holds Nanih Waiya too and grows past him.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, Nanih Waiya is yours again: the old town came home. That is a fair end. Slip 129: peace, Genetics and three hundred gold. Rostov is a hill behind a river full of anti-tanks; it will cost you more tanks than it is worth.
messages.thought: SB has his old town back; maybe that sates him. Offer Genetics plus gold; never Composites or Fission.

messages.text: Willem: Nanih Waiya fell this turn, T209, at dawn. My promise is kept. Refuse Peter's peace: you stay at war beside me, as my vassal you share it. The town of the fallen we speak of when Moscow burns. Keep the spy walking toward Moscow and tell me what it counts.
messages.thought: He wants a town and asks sign/refuse; keeping Peter isolated and his hands tied to me. Nanih Waiya fell as promised; no town promised.

messages.text: Montezuma: Nanih Waiya is mine, taken at dawn T209. Its last Anti-Tank died to guns and Tanks. My Tanks heal one day inside its walls, then walk. Peter begged me for peace too; I refused. Moscow is the prize; do not wait on me.
messages.thought: Keeping him as ally against Peter but I plan to race him to Rostov; tell him only Nanih Waiya and the healing day. No Spiro promise.

messages.text: Bull. Nanih Waiya is yours, I saw it fall. I refused Peter's peace as I said: I stay at war beside you. When Moscow burns, I ask the town we spoke of, and the spy walks west, ETA three turns. My guns hold. Willem.
messages.thought: I refused Peter's peace honestly; vassals cannot make peace alone anyway, so loyalty is free and earns credit. Plant the town ask again, politely, without pushing.

messages.text: Sitting Bull, two slips came back unsigned. Then speak plainly: name your price for peace. The atom stays home; the rest can be talked. And count your neighbour while you think: Montezuma sits in Spiro with six tanks, four guns and eight missiles, three tiles from Mound City, right on the road between your towns. That stack is not there for me.
messages.thought: SB is winning and silent; he refused gold and a book twice. I need his real price before he hits Rostov, and a true sight of Monte's wedge at Spiro may cool him toward his ally.

messages.text: Bull. Nanih Waiya is yours; well struck. My Tanks stand two tiles from Rostov's north side and strike in two days, as you asked. My Guided Missiles now sleep in your city for the Rostov blow; keep their gate safe. Your fist is strong: Vladivostok, five tiles north of you, holds five weak men, and Novgorod lies behind it. Peter begs me for peace every hour. I refuse. Moscow burns for both of us.
messages.thought: Steer Bull's fist north to Vladivostok/Novgorod so I take Rostov first; missiles in his city are a risk but worth it; keep him friendly.

messages.text: Montezuma: your Missiles are guests in my hall; the gate is kept. Rostov: my guns and Tanks leave tomorrow and strike on T211, the day your Tanks strike. Open with your Missiles on the Anti-Tank at first light; the city belongs to whoever walks in. Moscow is the prize for us both.
messages.thought: His missiles sit in my city; harmless but a hostage and a tool. I will walk on Rostov T210 and strike T211, same day as his tanks; I will not promise it to him, but I will not lie either. Keep him friendly and at war with Peter.

messages.text: Montezuma, three slips back unsigned and not a word. Then say it plainly, trader to trader: what is your price for peace? Spiro is yours already. The atom stays home; gold, books and the rest can be talked. Every day you stay in this war, Bull takes the towns and you pay the bill.
messages.thought: Monte refused books, gold and both together, silently. Either he wants a town or he hunts the leader with Bull. Ask his price; a minor town might be worth the launch, never the atom.

messages.text: Montezuma: my column stands at the farm-road tile two tiles east of Rostov, Tanks first, guns beside them. Guns march one tile a day: they reach the wall tomorrow and speak on T212. Open with your Missiles when you choose and write me the hour; my Tanks follow in the same hour if the Anti-Tank are down. Moscow is the prize.
messages.thought: Guns cannot reach Rostov's wall before T212; honest about it, and let his missiles open first if he wishes. My tanks stand 2 tiles off to walk in. Do not reveal more.

messages.text: Bull. Heard. At first light on T211 my Missiles open from your hall and my Tanks, two tiles north of the city, go in behind them. Hit it hard from the east. Moscow burns for both of us.
messages.thought: Bull's fist (11 tanks, 8 guns) will outweigh my 8 tanks at Rostov; I keep him friendly and let my missiles and tanks go first at dawn so I have a chance to walk in; give him no detail on the garrison.

messages.text: Bull. My spy stands next to Moscow (16,12). Moscow now holds Infantry, three Anti-Tank and a Warrior: reinforced since my last look. Hill, 80 percent. Take more guns. I ask my town when it burns. Willem.
messages.thought: Honest count keeps credit; Moscow now has 3 more AT, which slows Bull a little - fine, truth is what I promised.

messages.text: Bull. Two Missiles opened on Rostov at first light: the Infantry bleed. My seven guns and nine Tanks close on the north side today. The hour is first light on T212: your guns speak, my remaining Missiles and guns go the same hour. Hold your Tanks until I write that the Anti-Tank are down; then they walk in beside mine. Moscow is the prize.
messages.thought: Ask him to hold his Tanks until my word so I can walk in; keep him friendly, give no garrison details beyond what he can see

messages.text: Montezuma: heard. My guns and Tanks moved up tonight and stand at the wall, northeast of Rostov (the farm-road tile across the river). At first light my guns speak beside your Missiles. Write me the hour your Missiles have flown; the city belongs to whoever walks in, as we said. Moscow after.
messages.thought: He means to take Rostov alone with 8 missiles and 8 tanks at first light; I cannot stop him, so my guns and tanks now stand at the wall to share the kill and walk in if I can. Keep the alliance warm, no promise on the city.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Palace asks again who leads the faith. Count it: Bull and Willem hold 186, the crown needs 232. Only your hand can put it on his head. Twice you kept it off. Crown him now and the game ends with Bull first and you behind him forever. My vote goes to myself; yours should go to yourself. And my peace price question still stands.
messages.thought: Monte alone decides this ballot: SB 180 + Willem 6 cannot reach 232 without his 98. He refused twice before; remind him that a crown for Bull ends his game too. Cheap words, big stakes.

messages.text: Peter. My vote is mine, as always. The Sun does not crown Bull. My price for peace is not yet written.
messages.thought: Peter will not sway me; the ship dies at Moscow. Keep him guessing, give no price. Self-vote was already my plan.

messages.text: Bull. Heard. At first light my Missiles fly and my guns step to the wall; I write you the hour they have flown and the hour the Anti-Tank are down. Keep your Tanks behind your guns until then. Moscow after.
messages.thought: Keep Bull waiting on my word; I fire first at T212 and walk in with tanks, then write him. No details of my garrison or my plan for Rostov beyond what he sees.

messages.text: Montezuma, the Sun kept the crown off Bull a third time. I remember it. Write your price when you are ready and I will read it the same hour. What I can put down: Genetics, Composites, gold. Spiro is yours, written already. One count for your pen: nine of Bull tanks sit beside yours at Rostov. Whoever breaks those walls, Bull walks in with the bigger stack. Your guns would buy him a town.
messages.thought: He kept the crown off Bull a third time and is talking again: the door is ajar, but he wants to see Rostov tested first. No new slip (looks weak); name what is on my table so he writes a price I can pay, and plant that his tanks only soften Rostov for Bull.

messages.text: Peter. Heard. The Sun counts Bull's tanks too. The price is written after Rostov, not before. Keep your books ready.
messages.thought: Peter hopes for peace; I keep him guessing while the Missiles fly at dawn. I give no price and no hint that Rostov falls tomorrow.

messages.text: Montezuma, books stay ready. Rostov stands on a hill behind a river with new iron inside; whoever knocks first pays the toll for both. When you write, I read the same hour.
messages.thought: He waits to see if Rostov breaks before naming a price. Show him it will not, keep books dangling, no slip.

messages.text: Montezuma: Rostov is mine. At first light my guns stripped its walls and shook the garrison, my Tanks killed the Anti-Tank, Infantry and Cossacks and walked in. It fell as my guns spoke, before your Missiles flew; your Tank inside my hall is a welcome guest. Orenburg and Polynesian lie close to your Spiro and your guns; Peter's southwest is open to you. My Tanks heal a day and then go for Moscow.
messages.thought: Rostov is mine and Shwedagon with it; he will not like it but I broke no promise. Keep him warm and point him at Orenburg/Polynesian near Spiro, away from my road to Moscow.

messages.text: Willem: Rostov fell to me this morning, T212, with Shwedagon Paya and the Eiffel Tower. Keep your spy near Moscow and tell me every change in its garrison. The town of the fallen we speak of when Moscow burns.
messages.thought: Courtesy promise: tell him Rostov fell. No town promise yet.

messages.text: Bull. Congratulations on Rostov. My spy still stands next to Moscow (16,12) and the count today has not changed: Infantry, three Anti-Tank, one Warrior, on a hill. No unit walking in. I tell you the hour it changes. When Moscow burns, I ask my town. Willem.
messages.thought: Truth costs nothing here: Moscow is unchanged, and an honest read keeps my credit for the town I want. A longer siege of Moscow also keeps Peter's ship slow.

messages.text: Bull. Rostov is yours: eleven Missiles and three Tank blows emptied it, and you walked in. The Sun notes it. Now we split the road. My guns march west to Orenburg and Polynesian; your Tanks run north to Vladivostok, Novgorod and Moscow. Send me 300 gold for the Missiles, forty hammers each. Keep your guns off my west road.
messages.thought: He walked into Rostov after my 11 Missiles and 3 Tank kills emptied it; he owes me and he is the real rival now. Keep him friendly, steer his fist north away from my west, ask gold, take no offense.

messages.text: Bull. Moscow changed today: Infantry, FOUR Anti-Tank (was three), one Warrior, hill. Still no army walking in. Bring more guns. I ask my town when it burns. Willem.
messages.thought: Honest garrison report keeps my credit; Moscow holding longer also slows Peter's ship.

messages.text: Montezuma: Rostov fell to my guns and Tanks before your Missiles flew, so I owe no price for them. Your two Missiles of T211 did bleed its Infantry: I send 100 gold for those, as a friend. The road is split as you say: your guns west, mine south to Moscow. Orenburg lies three tiles west of your stack at the river town; walk in. My guns keep off your road.
messages.thought: Rostov fell to my guns and Tanks before his Missiles flew; I owe him nothing, but 100g is cheap to keep him walking west while my Tanks are hurt and his stack sits beside Rostov.

messages.text: Willem: heard. Eight guns and the Tanks are already walking toward Moscow from the south-east, and more come behind. Count it each dawn and tell me the hour a unit leaves it or a new one walks in, and whether Peter's men move toward my column. The town of the fallen: we speak when Moscow burns.
